notes.aatrox-combo-basic: The basic trade combo is Q1 → E to reposition → basic attack → W → Q2 → Q3. Use E immediately after pressing Q to reposition during the cast and land the blade's sweet spot.
notes.aatrox-combo-w: The W combo is Q1 → W → Q2 before the pull → Q3 immediately after the pull. W also reaches targets within Q1's knockup range. If Q1 misses, hold W to avoid wasting it. Land W immediately after Q1's knockup to limit the opponent's time to walk out of the chain area.
notes.aatrox-combo-ult: The teamfight combo is R → Q1 → E → W → Q2 → Q3. R increases attack damage. R increases self-healing. R's duration can only be extended through takedowns. Since R has a short duration, use it just before engaging when you are sure you can force a fight.
notes.aatrox-skill-q-tip: Q must hit with its sweet spot to deal full damage. Q knocks up opponents hit by its sweet spot. Prioritize landing Q1, which has the longest range of the three casts. Q2 and Q3 have visible windups, making them easy for opponents to dodge. Try to land the tip of every Q to reduce the passive cooldown as much as possible and keep empowered autos cycling.
notes.aatrox-skill-passive: The passive's empowered auto deals damage based on the target's maximum health. The passive's empowered auto restores health. Each ability hit reduces the passive cooldown. Save the empowered auto to pressure melee opponents instead of wasting it on minions.
notes.aatrox-skill-e: E can be used to move even while other abilities are in progress. Use E during Q's cast to adjust the position of its sweet spot. E's passive restores health based on damage dealt to champions. Use E to close in and land abilities, bringing the next passive empowered auto sooner. Avoid saving E solely for disengaging, so your abilities and empowered basic attacks keep cycling.
notes.aatrox-laning: At levels 1–2, farm safely near your turret, even if you have to give up some CS. From level 3 onward, farm with Q. From level 3 onward, stick to short trades in lane. Use Q3 and W after the opponent has used their tools for fighting back. In losing matchups, Q's damage alone lets you trade, so choose health and regeneration over attack damage to sustain in lane.
notes.aatrox-laning-q-timing: Harass melee opponents with Q as they step forward to last-hit. Land Q's sweet spot during the opponent's basic attack windup to prevent them from dodging or fighting back. Wait for the opponent's last-hit animation before using Q instead of using it on cooldown.
notes.aatrox-phase: Aatrox is often weak at levels 1–2, when Q has a long cooldown. From level 3 onward, with points invested in Q, Aatrox gains strong trading power. Aatrox reaches his peak in the mid game as he builds up ability haste and items. Aatrox often struggles against duelists in late-game 1v1s.
notes.aatrox-situational-armor: If the opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Cloth Armor or Bramble Vest first. If the opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Plated Steelcaps earlier. In matchups where you keep getting pushed back, switch to a build that prioritizes armor and health to survive.
notes.aatrox-situational-antiheal: If the opponent's healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner's Calling to reduce it. Buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
notes.aatrox-teamfight: In teamfights, use W to group opponents and try to hit multiple targets with Q's sweet spot. Avoid accepting 1v1 duels during teamfights. Engage once you and your allies have created a numbers advantage. Follow up allied immobilizing crowd control with Q to reliably land its sweet spot.
notes.vs-aatrox-q: Aatrox relies on Q for most of his damage. Avoiding Q's sweet spot greatly reduces the damage you take. When you see Aatrox cast Q, move outside or inside the blade's tip area. Aatrox's attacks have pronounced windups, giving opponents time to react.
notes.vs-aatrox-passive: Aatrox's empowered auto deals heavy damage early on. Try to trade right after Aatrox uses his empowered auto on a minion.
notes.vs-aatrox-r: Aatrox gains increased attack damage when he uses R. Aatrox gains increased self-healing when he uses R. R's duration can only be extended through takedowns. When Aatrox activates R, create distance to avoid taking a 1v1. Wait out Aatrox's R, then look to fight again.
notes.vs-aatrox-early: Aatrox turns early advantages into much larger leads. Focus on securing CS without giving up kills early so the matchup improves as the game goes on.
notes.vs-aatrox-w: If W hits you, leave its area within the allotted time before it pulls you to the center. W's area is a circle centered where the chain hit you. Within W's area, the distance to get out is the same in any direction. If W hits you, walk out immediately instead of hesitating over which direction to take. Save your mobility ability to get out of W.
notes.ahri-combo-basic: The basic combo is E → W → Q. Land E first to focus all three W flames on one target. Landing E first guarantees that the follow-up W and Q will hit.
notes.ahri-combo-q: Q hits on both the outward and return paths. Q's orb returns toward Ahri after being thrown. To hit both parts of Q, throw it past the enemy, then immediately move in toward them. Q's return damage is true damage, so the enemy's magic resistance does not reduce it.
notes.ahri-combo-ult: R is a mobility ability that links your combo together. You can use other abilities while dashing with R.
notes.ahri-skill-e: E only affects the first target it hits. Minions block E, preventing it from reaching enemies behind them. To hit an enemy behind minions with E, move around the side or use R to cross the minion line. Ahri's combat effectiveness drops sharply while E is unavailable. Do not waste E.
notes.ahri-skill-w: W deals greatly increased damage to low-health minions. Use W to last-hit minions and clear waves. Using W increases movement speed. Use W's movement speed boost to chase and disengage.
notes.ahri-skill-r: R lets you dash multiple times. Champion takedowns while R is active increase your remaining dashes. Champion takedowns while R is active extend its duration. Save at least one R dash to disengage. If you can secure a kill, use the extra R dash from the takedown to go after the next enemy.
notes.ahri-skill-passive: P restores health each time you kill a set number of minions. Ahri's lane sustain effectively depends on P's healing. Keep up your CS so P's healing can support your trades. P heals more from champion takedowns than from minion kills. Champion takedowns restore R dashes.
notes.ahri-phase: Ahri is weakest without R because she has no mobility ability available. Do not overextend in lane while R is on cooldown. From the mid game onward, as Ahri builds ability power, landing E gives her stronger single-target kill potential.
notes.ahri-laning: Use Q as your main poke tool in lane. Throw Q so it clips the enemy backline minions to clear the wave and poke at the same time. Save E unless you have a kill opportunity or are following up on a gank. When you run out of mana, stop poking and focus on farming.
notes.ahri-laning-roam: After unlocking R, push the lane and roam. Only enter another lane when both E and R are available. If either E or R is unavailable, farm instead of roaming. Ahri's roams depend on landing E.
notes.ahri-teamfight: Ahri is classified as an assassin, but she is also strong in teamfights. Q is easier to land when enemies are grouped together. Use E to draw one enemy toward your allies so they can follow up. Poke with Q from outside the enemy's range without engaging head-on first. While poking, use E when you have an angle to land it.
notes.ahri-teamfight-cleanup: As the fight winds down, use R to chase fleeing enemies. Use W for movement speed while chasing. Decide how far to chase by calculating how many R dashes takedowns will restore.
notes.ahri-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing offsets your combo damage, use Morellonomicon to reduce it. Buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.vs-ahri-e: Standing behind minions lets them block Ahri's E. Ahri's damage potential drops sharply without Charm. During laning, keep the minion wave between you and Ahri.
notes.vs-ahri-ult: Ahri has no mobility ability available when R is down. Track when Ahri's R will be available again. Time your ganks or engages for when Ahri's R is unavailable.
notes.vs-ahri-q: Ahri's Q hits on both the outward and return paths. After dodging Q's first hit, keep moving out of its return path. Q's return damage is true damage, so magic resistance cannot reduce it.
notes.vs-ahri-fight: Ahri is most vulnerable right after she uses E. Close in and attack as soon as you dodge Ahri's Charm. Ahri can create distance with an R dash. Ahri can create distance with W's movement speed boost.
notes.akali-combo-passive-ring: Akali's combos rely on moving around her passive ring. Hitting an ability creates a passive ring around the target. Cross the edge of the passive ring and return to use an empowered basic attack with twice the range. Practice quickly moving back and forth across the passive ring to keep dealing damage.
notes.akali-combo-basic: Land Q, step back across the ring, then finish the trade with an empowered basic attack. The empowered basic attack's extra range lets you attack from outside the enemy's retaliation range. Crossing the ring and returning to poke with an empowered basic attack costs no energy.
notes.akali-combo-e-double: Land the first E, cross the ring, and hit an empowered auto. Then close in with the second E and hit another empowered auto.
notes.akali-combo-allin: Use the first R to get past the target and close in, chip away with Q and an empowered basic attack, then finish with the second R. The second R deals more damage the more health the target has lost. Save the second R until the end of the combo. Cast Q during the second R dash to land both hits at once.
notes.akali-combo-r-flash: You can combine Flash with either R dash to extend its reach. Combine R with Flash to chase down a fleeing target from farther away.
notes.akali-skill-q: Q spreads in a cone and slows targets hit at its maximum range. Landing Q at maximum range also readies the passive ring immediately. Aim for the edge of Q's range to poke more efficiently.
notes.akali-skill-w: W's smoke grants Akali stealth. W's movement speed boost helps Akali continue her combo quickly. You can be hit by skillshots during the brief moment you appear just after entering the smoke. Avoid using W only to escape in open areas. Use W just before engaging or to interrupt targeted enemy abilities.
notes.akali-skill-e: The second E dash follows the marked target no matter how far they go. Before using the second E, check whether the target has moved under a turret or into the enemy team. You can also place an E mark on W's smoke. Use an E mark left on the smoke as an escape route.
notes.akali-skill-r: You can use R to get past an enemy and escape when caught in a bad position. Save the first R if you are unsure you can secure the kill. If the first R misses, Akali loses a way to close in and cannot complete the combo.
notes.akali-phase: At levels 1–2, Akali lacks the energy to trade effectively. Akali can start poking as she levels up Q. Kill opportunities open up as soon as you learn R at level 6. After completing one core ability power item, Akali can kill a backline target in one combo. Throughout the game, Akali is likely to die if she fails to finish the kill.
notes.akali-laning: Statistically, Akali ranks near the bottom in CS. Even if you give up some farm, build a health advantage with max-range Q hits and empowered basic attacks. Once you have a health advantage, push the wave and move to another lane to build on it.
notes.akali-teamfight: Do not start teamfights. Enter after your allies start the fight, draw the enemy's attention, and force out their crowd control. In teamfights, dive the backline and kill a squishy target. Before engaging, check whether the enemy has used their targeted crowd control.
notes.akali-situational-antiheal: If the enemy survives through healing, buy Morellonomicon to apply Grievous Wounds. Akali must secure a kill during her brief engage, so she loses out if the enemy still has healing available.
notes.akali-situational-mercurial: If the enemy has crowd control that can lock you down, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items to have a way to cleanse it. If Akali is caught by crowd control right after engaging, she is likely to die before using the second R.
notes.vs-akali-shroud-entry: Akali briefly appears when she enters the smoke. Cast skillshots during the brief moment Akali appears as she enters the smoke.
notes.vs-akali-shroud-reveal: Turrets and true sight reveal Akali inside the smoke. Place a Control Ward in the smoke to remove Akali's stealth advantage. Draw the fight near a turret to remove Akali's stealth advantage.
notes.vs-akali-e-mark: If you are marked by E, Akali's second dash follows you wherever you run. Dodging the first E takes away one of Akali's ways to close in. Make dodging Akali's first E, a skillshot shuriken, your top priority.
notes.vs-akali-r: If the first R misses you, Akali cannot close in to start her combo. Save your mobility ability or cleanse while Akali is close to you. Use the mobility ability or cleanse you saved to stop Akali as she engages with R.
notes.vs-akali-early: Akali is weak in close-range trades before level 6. Wait for Akali to leave the smoke and attack, then fight back. Build a health and CS lead while Akali's ultimate is unavailable.
notes.akshan-combo-q: Hit with Q's boomerang on both the way out and back to poke. Q's boomerang travels farther each time it hits an enemy. After throwing Q, move in the direction your opponent dodged the first hit so the returning boomerang hits them.
notes.akshan-combo-passive-cancel: Cancel the second shot after your first basic attack by moving to gain movement speed. Fire both shots when you need to deal all your damage. To control your spacing, fire only the first shot and move immediately to cancel the second.
notes.akshan-combo-passive-third: The passive deals bonus damage on every third hit from basic attacks and abilities combined. If the passive's third hit lands on a champion, you also gain a shield. Hit with Q on the way out and back, then land one basic attack to trigger the passive's third hit. Start a trade when you can land the passive's third hit.
notes.akshan-combo-e: E is a movement ability that hooks onto terrain and swings around it. While swinging with E, Akshan automatically shoots the nearest enemy. Use E to swing around your opponent and close in. Cast E a third time to land where you want and fire the final shot. Take a wide swing away from your opponent's path so hitting a champion or terrain does not end E.
notes.akshan-skill-e-reset: A takedown resets E's cooldown. Use E to engage if the takedown is certain. After a takedown, use the reset E to reach the next target or escape. If the takedown is uncertain, avoid engaging with E so you keep a way out.
notes.akshan-skill-w-revive: An enemy who kills an ally is marked as a Scoundrel. Killing a Scoundrel revives the allies they killed. Killing a Scoundrel grants bonus gold. If an ally dies in a teamfight, look for a chance to finish off the Scoundrel. Stay alive as Akshan to secure the ally revive.
notes.akshan-skill-w-camo: W's camouflage lasts longer near terrain or brush. W's camouflage ends quickly in open areas. Plan roaming and escape routes along river or jungle walls. While camouflaged, you are revealed if you enter an enemy champion's detection range. When there is a Scoundrel, a trail toward them appears and you gain movement speed.
notes.akshan-skill-r-target: R's bullets hit the first enemy or structure in their path. R's bullets execute minions instantly. Use R to finish off a low-health enemy fleeing at long range.
notes.akshan-skill-r-channel: Akshan is rooted in place while aiming R. Aiming R also shows the target an aiming indicator. Aim R for a long time only when there is no wall along the target's escape route. You can fire R's stored bullets without fully charging it. Stop aiming and fire R before the target reaches a wall.
notes.akshan-laning: In lane, trade from a distance where Q can hit on both the way out and back. Before trading, check whether you can gain the passive shield.
notes.akshan-laning-roam: After pushing the wave, use E to cross terrain and roam to another lane. When roaming, approach with W's camouflage along river and jungle walls. After roaming, check E's cooldown before choosing your return route.
notes.akshan-phase: Akshan is weak at levels 1–2. Even if you learn E first, early trades depend on chances to land Q. Kill opportunities increase sharply once level 6 R and your first core item come together. As you build critical strike items in the mid to late game, both R's finishing power and your basic attack damage increase.
notes.akshan-teamfight: Do not start a teamfight from the front. After the fight starts and the enemy has used their immobilizing abilities, enter from the side with E. In teamfights, finish off low-health targets. If an ally falls first, prioritize the Scoundrel.
notes.akshan-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing targets, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. When an enemy heals, R has less chance to finish them because its damage scales with their missing health.
notes.vs-akshan-w: Killing one of Akshan's allies marks you as a Scoundrel. If Akshan kills you while you are marked as a Scoundrel, the enemies you killed are revived. While marked as a Scoundrel, avoid facing Akshan alone. If you are marked as a Scoundrel, fight outside Akshan's finishing range in teamfights.
notes.vs-akshan-camo: W's camouflage lasts longer only near terrain and brush. Establish vision around river and jungle walls to track Akshan's roaming routes. In open areas, Akshan's W camouflage ends on its own. Stay grouped to stop Akshan from approaching under camouflage.
notes.vs-akshan-e: Akshan must hook onto terrain to use E. Push Akshan into open areas to prevent him from engaging or escaping with E. Walk into the path of Akshan's E swing to interrupt his movement. A takedown resets Akshan's E cooldown.
notes.vs-akshan-r: Akshan is rooted in place while aiming R. When Akshan aims R, an indicator appears on the target. If R targets you while you are low on health, move behind terrain. Someone in front can take Akshan's R bullets for you. Do not flee alone through an open area while Akshan is aiming R.
notes.vs-akshan-q: Akshan's Q boomerang travels farther each time it hits an enemy. Do not stand behind the minion wave to dodge Q. Dodge both Q's outgoing and returning paths. If Akshan moves sideways, Q's return path shifts with him.
notes.vs-akshan-early: Akshan is weak in early basic attack fights. If you can pressure at close range, play aggressively at levels 1–2 to gain an advantage. After the early pressure, farm outside Akshan's Q poke range.
notes.alistar-combo-wq: Right after W Headbutt, use Q Pulverize to knock up the opponent you pushed away. To send an enemy toward your allies, first get behind them and use W.
notes.alistar-combo-qw: Knock the target up with Q, then use W to push them in the direction you want. Use Q → W to peel enemies off your backline. Use Q → W to push enemies away rather than toward your allies.
notes.alistar-combo-flash: Using Flash during Q's cast moves Pulverize's area toward the target. Land Q with Flash, then immediately use W to push the target toward your allies.
notes.alistar-skill-e: While E is active, you can move through units. Activate E when moving through minions. Activate E when escaping through a narrow path. Deal enough damage to a champion with E, and your next basic attack stuns them. Build up E damage during a trade to prepare the stun.
notes.alistar-skill-r: Activating R immediately removes impairing effects already on you. Activating R greatly reduces the damage you take. Activate R right after enemy crowd control catches you or as focused fire begins. R does not prevent new crowd control applied after you activate it.
notes.alistar-skill-passive: Your passive gains a stack each time you stun, knock up, or push back an enemy. At full stacks, your passive heals you and nearby allies. In lane, if your passive stacks are almost full, engage once more after a trade to trigger the heal, then back off.
notes.alistar-phase: Alistar is strong in early trades. His kill pressure is strongest at levels 2–3, when he has his crowd control. He deals very little damage late in the game. Late in the game, focus on starting fights and protecting your allies.
notes.alistar-laning: Alistar is a support who pressures the lane. Look to land Q as an enemy steps forward to last-hit. If you use both Q and W but fail to engage, you leave yourself open to a counterattack while they are down. Engage with Q and W only when your allied marksman can follow up.
notes.alistar-laning-mana: His abilities cost a lot of mana, so you cannot use the combo repeatedly early on. One failed engage costs you both mana and lane control. If the engage angle is uncertain, trade with E and wait for the next opportunity.
notes.alistar-teamfight: In teamfights, push an enemy damage dealer toward your allies. In teamfights, peel enemies off your backline. In teamfights, activate R and charge through the enemy team to break their formation.
notes.alistar-dive: When an enemy is under their turret, use W to push them deeper under it. When diving, take turret shots first, activate R, and go in. Before a dive, check whether your allies have enough damage to finish the target.
notes.alistar-situational-boots: Movement speed increases your engage range, so generally choose Boots of Swiftness. If the enemy team deals mostly physical damage, choose Plated Steelcaps to survive lane and teamfights.
notes.vs-alistar-r: Alistar takes much less damage while his R is active. When Alistar activates R, back off and fight again after it expires.
notes.vs-alistar-r-cc: Alistar's R only removes impairing effects already on him when he activates it.
notes.vs-alistar-turret: When defending by your turret, do not give Alistar room to get behind you.
notes.vs-alistar-cooldown: Alistar's threat comes from his close-range Q and W. Counterattack right after Alistar uses Q and W. Push the lane or reposition while Alistar's Q and W are on cooldown.
notes.ambessa-combo-dash: If you issue a move or attack command during a cast, Ambessa dashes in the commanded direction when the cast ends. If you issue no move or attack command during a cast, Ambessa uses the ability in place. When engaging, issue a move command toward the opponent. When using an ability to disengage, issue a move command backward.
notes.ambessa-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use an E dash and its extra strike, a basic attack, Q at the blade’s edge, the second Q, then another basic attack. Weave basic attacks between abilities during a combo to consume passive stacks and restore resources.
notes.ambessa-combo-q-recast: The first Q must hit an enemy to briefly ready Sundering Slam. Minions can also be hit by the first Q to ready Sundering Slam. If a champion is out of range of the first Q, hit a minion with it, then use Sundering Slam on the champion. If the first Q misses completely, the second strike is lost, so set up a hit before trading.
notes.ambessa-combo-ult: R sends Ambessa to the farthest enemy champion along the targeted line. Before using R, check that your intended target is farthest along the targeted line. After R lands, attack with E, a basic attack, Cunning Sweep, then Sundering Slam while the suppression and stun continue.
notes.ambessa-skill-passive: Passive stacks build whenever Ambessa starts a dash and disappear after a short time. While Ambessa has passive stacks, her basic attack range and attack speed increase. Weave basic attacks between abilities to consume passive stacks. Use the extra basic attack range to land another hit from a distance the opponent thinks is safe.
notes.ambessa-skill-q: Cunning Sweep and Sundering Slam deal full damage at the edge of their hitboxes; hits closer in deal half damage. If you are close to the opponent, dash back or sideways to create space, then hit with Q at the blade’s edge. Q deals damage based on maximum health, so it also works against opponents who build health.
notes.ambessa-skill-w: W grants a shield first, then slams the area around Ambessa after a brief windup. If Ambessa takes damage from an enemy champion, large monster, or structure during W’s windup, the slam’s damage increases greatly. Damage from minions does not empower W’s slam. Use W just before the opponent uses an ability or during a tower dive.
notes.ambessa-skill-e: E’s slow is strong enough to nearly stop its target, but wears off quickly. Follow E’s slow immediately with Q to hit at the blade’s edge. If E starts a dash, its extra strike lands when the dash ends. E is an important way to close the gap, so do not spend it on farming unless you have a chance to get a kill.
notes.ambessa-skill-r: Once you learn R, its armor penetration and healing based on ability damage apply even when you do not use it. Use R to engage when you have a sure kill or a chance to reach the backline. Ambessa is unstoppable during R, so crowd control cannot interrupt it.
notes.ambessa-laning: As a melee champion in mid, Ambessa takes early poke from ranged opponents. Do not force your way onto a ranged opponent. Use Q at the blade’s edge to last-hit and poke while keeping up in levels. When the opponent steps forward to last-hit, close in with an E dash, land both Q strikes, then leave immediately. After pushing the wave, get vision at an entrance to the enemy jungle or join a side lane.
notes.ambessa-phase: Ambessa is weakest at levels 1–2: with only one or two abilities, she struggles to chain dashes. From level 3, once you have both Q and E, you can trade by chaining combos. At level 6, R’s passive gives her a major power boost. Almost all her damage ratios scale with bonus attack damage, so she is strongest in the mid game as she builds core items. If the opponents group up late in the game, do not engage alone; look for someone isolated on a flank.
notes.ambessa-teamfight: After your allies draw the opponents’ attention, use R from a flank to reach the backline and target one opponent. Engage after the opponents have used their key crowd control and defensive abilities. If burst damage is coming just before you engage, use W first to block it and empower the slam. Before engaging, plan a route out with an E dash after you take down one opponent.
notes.ambessa-situational-antiheal: If the opponent sustains through their own healing, buy Executioner’s Calling early so you can finish them after your combo.
notes.ambessa-situational-cleanse: If the opponent has crowd control that restricts movement, consider Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar so you can dash and line up Q after R lands.
notes.vs-ambessa-w: When Ambessa gains a shield and briefly winds up, she has used W. Damaging Ambessa with an ability or basic attack during W’s windup greatly empowers its slam. When you see Ambessa wind up W, stop attacking and walk out of its range.
notes.vs-ambessa-q: Both of Ambessa’s Q strikes deal full damage at the edge of their hitboxes; hits closer in deal half damage. If you cannot easily run far enough from Q, move close to Ambessa to reduce its damage. If you dodge the first Q, Cunning Sweep, completely, the second slam will not be readied.
notes.vs-ambessa-passive: Ambessa can follow her abilities with short dashes. While she has stacks remaining, her basic attack range and attack speed increase. Step forward only while Ambessa’s abilities are on cooldown. Counterattack right after Ambessa has used all her abilities and spent her passive stacks.
notes.vs-ambessa-r: Ambessa’s R moves her to the farthest enemy champion along the targeted line. Ambessa is unstoppable during R, so crowd control cannot interrupt it. During a standoff, position so Ambessa and your backline aren't in a straight line.
notes.vs-ambessa-e: Ambessa’s E slow is strong enough to nearly stop you, but wears off quickly. Immediately after E hits you, use a mobility ability or cleanse to avoid the Q attack at the blade’s edge that follows.
notes.vs-ambessa-phase: Exploit Ambessa’s weakness at levels 1–2, when she has only one or two abilities. Exploit Ambessa’s weakness right after she uses all her abilities. Ambessa is strongest in the mid game as she builds core items. Avoid giving up kills early and keep up in levels. Once Ambessa learns R, its armor penetration and healing apply even when she does not use it.
notes.amumu-combo-engage: The basic engage is Q in, then R, E, W, and an auto attack. Right after Q hits, you can land R while the target is stunned. Use R before E so allies can attack during the stun.
notes.amumu-combo-flash-r: If enemies are grouped but you have no Q angle, Flash and immediately use R. After engaging with Flash, save both Q charges for disengaging or chasing. If you engage with Q first, you may be pulled toward one target and hit fewer enemies with R.
notes.amumu-combo-double-q: Q stores up to two charges. After closing in with the first Q, use the second to catch the target if they escape with a mobility ability. When an ally ganks, save Q and throw it right after the target Flashes.
notes.amumu-skill-passive: Cursed Touch makes targets hit by your auto attacks take more magic damage. W continually reapplies the curse, and R applies it too. Weave in auto attacks after engaging to increase your allied magic damage dealers' damage.
notes.amumu-skill-q: Q is narrow and stops at the first target it hits. Against a target behind minions or jungle monsters, look for a Q angle from the side. Throw Q from a brush or behind a wall to give the target less time to react. If the Q angle is uncertain, hold it so you keep a way to close in.
notes.amumu-skill-w: When W is on, it continually deals damage based on nearby enemies' maximum health and reapplies the curse. Turn W off while moving to save mana, and turn it on during fights and jungle clears. In teamfights, stay beside high maximum health enemy frontliners to deal W damage.
notes.amumu-skill-e: E's passive reduces physical damage taken. Each auto attack you take reduces E's cooldown. E deals area magic damage and reduces armor and magic resistance. Use E as your main damage source when clearing the jungle.
notes.amumu-skill-r: R is an instant area stun around Amumu, so you need to get close to land it. As a rule, use R on multiple grouped enemies. If it can turn the fight around, use R even on a single enemy diving your allied damage dealer. Avoid aiming for multiple enemies only to miss everyone with R.
notes.amumu-jungle: Clear the jungle mainly with E, and use W briefly to manage mana. The first jungle clear costs a lot of health, so avoid risky invades. Take auto attacks from monsters to reduce E's cooldown while clearing. Turn W off while moving to save mana for ganks and objectives.
notes.amumu-gank: Before level 6, ganks depend entirely on landing Q. Before level 6, gank when the lane is pushed toward your side and nothing blocks Q. When ganking, approach from the river or brush for a side angle on Q. After level 6, you can finish a gank with Flash and R even if Q misses.
notes.amumu-objective: The narrow terrain around Dragon or Baron groups enemies, making Q and R easier to land. Establish vision around the objective early and look for the moment enemies enter a narrow passage.
notes.amumu-teamfight: Amumu starts teamfights, but has little he can do if he engages alone without R. Wait on a flank outside enemy vision, then engage when their formation narrows. Use R when your allies are ready to follow your engage. After engaging, turn on W and stay among enemy frontliners to keep dealing damage and applying the curse.
notes.amumu-phase: Amumu is weak before level 3 and loses a lot of health while clearing the jungle. Once he gets R at level 6, he becomes much stronger in ganks and objective fights. His peak is in mid to late game teamfights, when he has built magic penetration and damage over time items. His solo fighting remains weak throughout the game, so he is unsuited to fighting alone in a side lane.
notes.amumu-situational-antiheal: If enemies sustain through healing, build Morellonomicon between core items. W's continuous magic damage makes it easy to keep Grievous Wounds on multiple enemies at once.
notes.vs-amumu-r: Amumu's R is an area stun around him. When Amumu has R available, don't stand close together with your allies. Against Amumu's R, fight in open areas rather than narrow passages. Keep your distance before Amumu gets close enough to use R.
notes.vs-amumu-q: Amumu's Q is narrow and stops at the first target it hits. Keep minions or jungle monsters between you and Amumu to block his Q engage. In lane, move unpredictably and stand behind minions to avoid Amumu's ganks.
notes.vs-amumu-w: Amumu's W continually deals magic damage based on the maximum health of nearby enemies. Against Amumu, build magic resistance as well as health. Even as a frontliner, adjust your spacing so you don't stay beside Amumu for long.
notes.vs-amumu-e: Amumu's E passive reduces physical damage taken. The more auto attacks Amumu takes, the shorter E's cooldown becomes. If you deal physical damage against Amumu, build armor penetration. When attacking Amumu, combine your damage with your allies' magic damage.
notes.vs-amumu-cleanse: Make Amumu use R before starting a full fight. Once Amumu has used R, his teamfight threat drops sharply. A key damage dealer can neutralize Amumu's R with Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar.
notes.vs-amumu-early: Before level 6, Amumu is weak because his jungle clear is slow and costs a lot of health. Invade Amumu's jungle early to delay his level 6. Push lanes that offer early gank opportunities in advance to delay Amumu's level 6. Exploit Amumu's weak period before he gets R.
notes.anivia-combo-basic: The basic trade is to land Q, reactivate it to detonate, then use E. E deals double damage to enemies chilled by Q. If Q misses, save the cooldown and mana by holding E.
notes.anivia-combo-r: In teamfights, place R first, let it grow to full size, then use Q and E. A fully grown R chills enemies, doubling E damage even without Q.
notes.anivia-combo-wall: Block their escape with W, detonate Q in front of the wall, then use E. Enemies trapped against the wall have a hard time dodging Q's explosion stun. Land E and R while the enemy is stunned by Q.
notes.anivia-skill-q: As Q travels, it deals damage through enemies and slows them. Q stuns in an area when reactivated or when it reaches the end of its range. If the opponent dodges Q sideways, predict their direction and detonate it a little early. When farming without needing the stun, you can let Q pass through without detonating it.
notes.anivia-skill-w: The W wall gets longer as the skill levels up. Low-level W blocks jungle paths; high-level W divides teamfight terrain. To block an enemy's path, place the W wall perpendicular to their direction of travel. The W wall also blocks allies. When allies are engaging, position the W wall so it doesn't trap them.
notes.anivia-skill-e: E is Anivia's main damage skill and her only instant damage skill. E has a short cooldown, so you can use it repeatedly while an enemy is chilled. To increase E damage, chill the enemy with Q or R first. To save mana for trades, don't waste E on clearing minions without chilling them.
notes.anivia-skill-passive: When Anivia takes lethal damage, her passive turns her into an egg; she revives with full health. The egg must survive for a set time with altered defensive stats to revive. The egg is more likely to survive near allies or under a turret than when attacked alone. When her passive is available, you can position aggressively while accounting for the chance to revive. After reviving, position safely until the passive cooldown ends.
notes.anivia-skill-r: R continuously consumes mana while active. The storm ends on its own if Anivia moves too far from R. Turn off R as soon as you've pushed the wave or blocked the area you intended. Anivia relies heavily on mana; keeping R active too long can leave too little mana for E in the next fight.
notes.anivia-laning: In lane, focus on surviving and scaling instead of forcing a win. Save Q for stopping ganks and guaranteed chances to attack rather than poking. Last-hit with basic attacks and E to keep up in levels. Anivia scales through CS more than kills.
notes.anivia-laning-gank: Anivia has no mobility skill, making ganks hard to escape. If you've pushed the lane, keep W ready for a gank. When escaping a gank, place the W wall to block the path behind you as you flee.
notes.anivia-laning-wave: Learning R greatly speeds up wave clear. Use R to clear waves when you plan to push and roam or establish vision. To save mana for the opponent's next engage, don't push waves with R without a purpose.
notes.anivia-phase: Anivia is weakest at levels 1–5 because she lacks mana and damage. At level 6, learning R strengthens both her wave clear and sustained damage. Anivia gains strength in the mid game once items ease her mana problems. In the late game, her role in controlling terrain with W and R grows.
notes.anivia-teamfight: In teamfights, position well behind your frontline. Place R where the fight will start so the storm has time to grow. When the enemy engages, use W to separate their follow-up, then clear the enemies trapped in front with Q and E. Draw teamfights toward narrow passages to increase the impact of the W wall.
notes.anivia-situational-antiheal: If an enemy's self-healing offsets R's sustained damage, reduce their healing with Morellonomicon. Anivia's damage is sustained rather than a short burst.
notes.vs-anivia-egg: When Anivia takes lethal damage, she becomes an egg and revives with full health. To make sure the egg is destroyed, attack it with your jungler or another ally. After Anivia revives, look for a kill while her passive is on cooldown.
notes.vs-anivia-q: Anivia can reactivate her straight-traveling Q to detonate it in place and stun. If you're a ranged champion, stay outside Anivia's Q range. If you're a melee champion, close in on Anivia and move past Q's explosion radius.
notes.vs-anivia-e: If Q hits you or you're chilled inside a fully grown R, E deals double damage to you. Right after Q hits you, watch out for the empowered E. If Q hits you, stop fighting and immediately leave R or use a mobility skill to dodge the next E.
notes.vs-anivia-wall: Even a low-level W blocks a jungle path. Fight Anivia in a wide lane when possible so W cannot block your escape. When engaging, save Flash in case W separates you from your allies.
notes.vs-anivia-early: Anivia has no mobility skill. Before level 6, pressure Anivia with your jungler to force her egg or look for a kill. A lead gained before level 6 weakens Anivia's late-game terrain control.
notes.annie-skill-passive: After using abilities a set number of times, Annie's next damaging ability stuns. Do not move forward unless the stun is ready.
notes.annie-skill-passive-e: Using E does not consume a ready stun. Learn E early to stack the stun safely during a standoff.
notes.annie-combo-ult-engage: Ready the stun, then use R for an area stun, followed by W and Q. Before engaging with R, check that the stun is fully stacked. Do not consume a ready stun with another ability before engaging with R.
notes.annie-combo-solo: Against one target, open with a stunning Q, then follow with W and a basic attack. Do not start a single-target combo with the short-range W.
notes.annie-skill-q: Killing a target with Q refunds its mana cost. Killing a target with Q halves its cooldown. Last-hit minions with Q to save mana and build stun stacks.
notes.annie-skill-w: W hits a cone in front of Annie. Early on, use W to push the wave or secure a clear kill opportunity. Do not waste the costly, short-range W on single-target poke.
notes.annie-skill-e: E grants a shield and increases movement speed. Use E just before engaging to get within range for W and R. Use E to absorb enemy poke. E can also be used on allies. Summoned Tibbers also receives E's effects. Use E right after summoning Tibbers if you want him to survive longer.
notes.annie-skill-r-tibbers: Learning R grants magic penetration as a passive effect. Cast R again to control summoned Tibbers directly. Control Tibbers to chase fleeing enemies. Control Tibbers to check vision in a bush. When Annie stuns an enemy, Tibbers becomes enraged and moves faster. Tibbers also becomes enraged and moves faster when Annie dies.
notes.annie-laning: When the stun is unavailable, stay back and last-hit minions with Q. When the stun is fully stacked, start a combo as the opponent steps up to last-hit a minion. Do not start a fight unless your stun is ready as the opponent goes for a last hit.
notes.annie-laning-roam: Ready the stun, push the wave, then move to a side lane. Do not consume a ready stun while clearing the wave before roaming.
notes.annie-phase: Annie can stun from level 1, giving her kill opportunities early. Annie's first strong point is her level 6 R and stun combo. Annie's burst is strongest in the mid game with two or three ability power items. Late in the game, Annie's short range and lack of mobility make engaging harder. Use leads gained before the late game to close out the game.
notes.annie-teamfight: Do not use R in a teamfight unless the stun is ready. Engage with R when two or three opponents group together. Start a teamfight with R only where your allies can follow up immediately.
notes.annie-teamfight-peel: If there is no opening to engage, stay back and protect your allied carry. Stun enemies who get onto an ally. When stopping an enemy who gets onto an ally, shield that ally with E.
notes.annie-situational-tenacity: After engaging with R, Annie has no mobility ability to escape. If the opponents have a lot of immobilizing crowd control, use Quicksilver Sash to cleanse one crowd control effect after engaging.
notes.vs-annie-passive: A white swirl around Annie means her stun is ready. Do not enter Annie's ability range while her stun indicator is visible. Pressure Annie right after she uses her stun, before she rebuilds the stacks.
notes.vs-annie-no-mobility: Annie has no mobility ability. Approach Annie when her stun is unavailable. If you have forced Annie to use Flash, look for a jungle gank.
notes.vs-annie-tibbers: Summoned Tibbers deals continuous damage to nearby enemies. Keep your distance from summoned Tibbers even after killing Annie. When Annie dies, Tibbers becomes enraged and moves faster. Summoned Tibbers can be killed with Smite.
notes.vs-annie-teamfight: If Annie is out of sight or her stun is ready, don’t group up in twos or threes. Decide in advance who will take down Annie immediately when she moves forward with R.
notes.vs-annie-range: Annie's ability range is relatively short for a mage. Poke Annie from long range. Look for the moment Annie pushes forward through your poke.
notes.vs-annie-mr: All of Annie's damage is magic, and learning R also grants her magic penetration. Get enough magic resistance to survive one burst from Annie. Counterattack after surviving Annie's combo.
notes.aphelios-skill-weapon-cycle: Aphelios carries one main weapon and one off-hand weapon. Basic attacks and abilities consume ammo. When the main weapon runs out of ammo, it moves to the back of the rotation. Using ammo on minions can change your weapon combination for the next fight.
notes.aphelios-skill-e-preview: The E slot shows which weapon is coming next. Check the E slot to anticipate your weapon combination for the next wave, gank, or objective.
notes.aphelios-skill-w: W swaps the main and off-hand weapons. Q is the current main weapon's ability. Use W to bring out the weapon you want, use Q, then swap back with W. Swapping weapons with W does not restore ammo.
notes.aphelios-skill-calibrum: Calibrum Q marks the target. Consuming a Calibrum mark lets you attack once more from beyond your normal range. During the Calibrum phase, avoid direct fights because your immediate damage is low.
notes.aphelios-skill-gravitum: Gravitum Q roots all enemies slowed by Gravitum. Apply Gravitum's slow first, then root with Q. Slow multiple enemies with off-hand Gravitum, then use W and Q to root them all. Time your team's engage around the Gravitum rotation.
notes.aphelios-skill-infernum: Infernum Q attacks in a cone. After Infernum Q, you attack once more with the off-hand weapon. Time your wave push and preparations for a roam or objective around the Infernum phase.
notes.aphelios-skill-crescendum: Crescendum Q places a turret. The Crescendum turret uses the same weapon as your off-hand weapon. Use W to choose the off-hand weapon for the turret, then use Crescendum Q.
notes.aphelios-skill-severum: Severum Q lets you move quickly while attacking nearby enemies. Severum Q attacks with both the main and off-hand weapons.
notes.aphelios-combo-ult: R attacks each champion it hits once more with the main weapon. The additional attack from R applies the main weapon's on-hit effects. Before using R, choose your main weapon with W. With Gravitum as the main weapon, R leads from an AoE slow into a root. R with Infernum as the main weapon greatly increases area damage.
notes.aphelios-phase: Instead of leveling abilities with skill points, Aphelios gains permanent stats. Q unlocks at level 2. R unlocks at level 6. Aphelios gains a lot of power when he completes items. Farm while avoiding losses early, then look for fights after completing a core item.
notes.aphelios-laning: During the Calibrum phase, poke enemies to lower their health. During the Infernum phase, clear the wave to gain control. During the Gravitum phase, follow your support's or jungler's engage with a root. With an unfavorable weapon combination, avoid forcing a fight and manage your ammo.
notes.aphelios-teamfight: In teamfights, attack from behind your frontline and make use of your range. If you have Gravitum, look for a chance to root multiple enemies. If you have Infernum, deal area damage to grouped enemies. When your weapon combination is poor, do not force a role in the fight.
notes.aphelios-situational-cc: If the enemy has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash early. Outside the Severum phase, you have no way to escape on your own.
notes.aphelios-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Mortal Reminder. Mortal Reminder's healing reduction applies when you attack with any weapon.
notes.vs-aphelios-weapon-read: You can see Aphelios's next weapon in his E slot. Trade with Aphelios when he has a weapon with low immediate damage.
notes.vs-aphelios-gravitum: If Aphelios uses Q while you are slowed by Gravitum, you will be rooted. If a Gravitum basic attack slows you, immediately retreat out of range. Do not group with allies while slowed by Gravitum.
notes.vs-aphelios-mobility: Aphelios has very little mobility. When Aphelios does not have Severum, he has no way to escape other than Flash. Look for a chance to catch Aphelios when he does not have Severum.
notes.vs-aphelios-ult: Aphelios's R must hit a champion to trigger. Every champion hit by R takes one additional attack from the main weapon. If Aphelios can use R, spread out from your allies before engaging.
notes.vs-aphelios-calibrum: If you are marked by Calibrum, you can be attacked once more from beyond Aphelios's normal range. If you are marked by Calibrum, retreat immediately to preserve your health.
notes.ashe-combo-w-reset: W can also reset the basic attack timer. Use W right after a basic attack to follow up quickly with the next one. Use W to safely apply Frost Shot's slow to multiple enemies.
notes.ashe-combo-q-prestack: Build stacks with basic attacks to activate Q. Build Q stacks on minions beforehand so you can start the fight with empowered basic attacks. Although Q's empowered basic attack fires multiple arrows, on-hit effects count it as one basic attack.
notes.ashe-combo-engage: When engaging, stun with R, land W, then activate Q and follow up with basic attacks. R's stun lasts longer the farther it travels. Before engaging, try to land R from as far away as possible.
notes.ashe-skill-passive: Frost Shot applies a slow through basic attacks and abilities. Ashe's critical strikes strengthen Frost Shot's slow instead of dealing extra damage. Keep attacking the same target, and Frost Shot's slow stacks and grows stronger. Focus your attacks on one target to strengthen Frost Shot's slow.
notes.ashe-skill-e: E is a scouting tool that stores charges. Use E to check unwarded objective areas and the enemy jungler's path ahead of time. Use E so it doesn't sit at full charges. E grants vision along its flight path as well as at its destination. Aim E to sweep paths where enemies may gather.
notes.ashe-skill-r: Use R to stun targets across virtually the entire map. Predict where enemies will move before firing R. If it isn't urgent, create distance before using R to increase its stun duration. Save R for plays in other lanes instead of wasting it on lane poke.
notes.ashe-skill-w-poke: Ashe relies almost entirely on W for lane poke. At low ranks, W's long cooldown and high mana cost make it costly to use. Use W only when you're sure it will hit, such as when the enemy support steps forward. W's cooldown drops significantly as it gains ranks.
notes.ashe-phase: After level 6, Ashe puts strong pressure on the lane because R creates kill opportunities. Ashe has no way to escape on her own, making poor positioning especially dangerous. With midgame items, Ashe's slow and range make her strong in teamfights. Ashe has less late-game burst damage than other marksmen.
notes.ashe-laning-wave: Avoid pushing the lane too far, since Ashe has no mobility ability. Keep the lane pulled back and use Frost Shot's slow to discourage enemies from approaching. Always account for the routes the enemy jungler can use to engage. Check inside bushes with E before moving forward.
notes.ashe-laning-trade: After your support engages, add slows with W and basic attacks. Avoid stepping forward to start a fight, so you don't get caught by a counter-engage.
notes.ashe-laning-tower: Use Q to take down turrets faster. While attacking a turret, build stacks on nearby minions to use Q repeatedly. Push the lane, then look for a chance to attack the turret.
notes.ashe-teamfight: Stay behind your allies and keep slowing enemies who engage, giving your team time to close in. Stay behind your frontline so your allies can protect you. Move with your allies when your team starts grouping.
notes.ashe-teamfight-r: Before a fight, decide whether to use R to start the teamfight or stop an enemy engage. If your team has no other way to engage, save R to start the fight.
notes.vs-ashe-mobility: Ashe has virtually no mobility or defensive tools, leaving her vulnerable to enemies who get close. Focus your resources on creating chances to get close to Ashe in lane and teamfights.
notes.vs-ashe-slow: Once Frost Shot's slow stacks up, it becomes hard to escape by walking alone. Avoid staying within Ashe's basic attack range for long, or Frost Shot's slow may keep you pinned down. Use a mobility ability to close the gap in one move before Frost Shot's slow traps you.
notes.vs-ashe-r: R travels in a straight line. Keep changing direction to make it harder for Ashe to predict R's path. When Ashe's R is ready, avoid initiating small skirmishes from outside vision.
notes.vs-ashe-w: Move sideways to dodge W's fan-shaped spread. Try to trade damage right after Ashe uses W.
notes.vs-ashe-q-window: When Ashe builds stacks with basic attacks and activates Q, her damage rises sharply for a short time. Keep your distance while Ashe's Q is active. Move in after Ashe's Q ends.
notes.asol-skill-passive-stardust: Aurelion Sol's growth depends heavily on his Stardust count. Stardust stacks permanently and is not lost on death. Gain Stardust by keeping Q on the same enemy for a while, holding champions inside E, and hitting champions with R. Minions and monsters that die inside E also grant Stardust. Collect Stardust from every wave, even if you cannot win lane.
notes.asol-skill-q: Q deals full damage to the first enemy hit and half damage to nearby enemies. Keep Q on the same target for a while to gain bonus damage and Stardust. Avoid switching targets repeatedly while using Q. If you cancel Q right after casting it, you cannot use it again for a short time.
notes.asol-skill-w: During W flight, Q's cooldown and maximum channel duration limit are removed. Q's base damage increases during W flight. If you help secure a takedown soon after damaging a champion, you recover almost all of W's cooldown. Use W when you have a chance to secure a takedown. When using W to escape, leave Q off so your flight speed does not drop by half.
notes.asol-skill-e: Lane minions and jungle monsters inside E have zero movement speed. Champions inside E are slowly pulled toward its center. As Stardust stacks, E's area and execute threshold grow. E cannot execute epic monsters.
notes.asol-skill-r: After collecting enough Stardust, R changes from Falling Star, which stuns, to The Skies Descend, which knocks enemies up. Empowered R also adds a wide shockwave and a slow. Use unempowered R to follow up on ganks or block escapes. Use empowered R to start teamfights.
notes.asol-combo-poke: In trades, place E first, then layer Q over it. While E pulls enemies in, keep Q on one target to gain bonus damage and Stardust. If you use Q before E, the enemy may walk sideways and break Q's contact.
notes.asol-combo-fight: In a full fight, use R to restrict movement, place E, then approach with W while maintaining Q. Q has no channel duration limit during W flight. Your damage is most concentrated while maintaining Q during W flight. If an enemy remains inside E when your flight ends, they may fall below its execute threshold.
notes.asol-laning-early: At levels 1–5, focus on catching waves over trading. The first minion hit blocks Q, preventing it from dealing full damage to the champion behind it. Try to poke with Q when your opponent steps beside the minion wave.
notes.asol-laning-wave: To clear a wave, hold the minions in E, then layer Q over it. Minions inside E have zero movement speed, so they do not spread out. Each unit that dies inside E grants Stardust. Think carefully before giving up a wave to roam.
notes.asol-phase: Aurelion Sol is weakest at levels 1–8, when he has little Stardust. At levels 1–8, stay alive and farm waves. He becomes much stronger in mid game once R is empowered and he has one core item. In late game, E's area and execute threshold, along with R's impact area, keep growing with Stardust. Buy time to stack Stardust.
notes.asol-teamfight: In teamfights, hold the frontline in place and keep dealing damage with Q. Q deals damage based on maximum health, making it effective against durable enemies too. Do not overextend to reach the backline. Turn on Q after your allies draw the enemy's attention or R restricts their movement.
notes.asol-teamfight-objective: Low-health enemies struggle to cross E's center because they risk being executed. Before an objective fight starts, place E in a passage the enemy must cross.
notes.asol-situational-zhonya: If the enemy can dive onto you, get Zhonya's Hourglass early to withstand their engage. You stay in place while channeling Q. Without a takedown, W remains on cooldown for a long time.
notes.asol-situational-antiheal: Choose Morellonomicon if the enemy's healing is a problem. Q and E's damage over time can apply healing reduction for an extended period.
notes.vs-asol-stardust: Aurelion Sol's strength scales with his Stardust count. Aurelion Sol does not lose stacked Stardust when he dies. Stay out of range to avoid unnecessary Q poke.
notes.vs-asol-q: Q deals full damage to the first enemy hit and half damage to nearby enemies. Q must stay on the same target for a while to trigger bonus damage and Stardust. Move out of Q's line of fire quickly.
notes.vs-asol-e: Enemies below the health threshold are executed at E's center. If you are low on health, avoid even the edge of E. E pulls slowly, so you can walk out right after entering it. If you enter E, keep moving outward immediately.
notes.vs-asol-w: If Aurelion Sol helps secure a takedown after entering with W, he recovers almost all of its cooldown. Fight back when he enters with W and deny the takedown. Counterattack right after he uses W.
notes.vs-asol-r: Once enough Stardust has stacked, R knocks enemies up and sends out an area shockwave instead of stunning. If several of you are grouped up when empowered R hits, you will be knocked up and slowed. Do not bunch up in narrow passages.
notes.vs-asol-early: Aurelion Sol is weak early, and W, his mobility tool, has a long cooldown. If your champion can close the gap, engage hard when his W is down. Stop Aurelion Sol from scaling before he stacks Stardust.
notes.aurora-combo-q-recall: Q's first hit applies a curse. Recasting Q retrieves it and damages enemies along its path again. After landing Q, don't retrieve it immediately. Lower the target's health with an auto attack or E first. Line up Q's return path before it returns automatically when its duration ends.
notes.aurora-combo-allin: When going all in, use Q's first hit, W to approach, an auto attack, E, then Q's return. While approaching with W, stealth and increased movement speed give the opponent less time to react. Weave one auto attack into your all-in combo to build passive stacks. You can still deal damage along Q's return path after E hops you backward.
notes.aurora-combo-teamfight: In teamfights, enter with R to slow enemies, use E inside the area, then retrieve Q. Enemies entering or leaving R's area are slowed. Aurora can travel between opposite sides of R's area.
notes.aurora-skill-passive: The passive triggers after you damage the same target multiple times, dealing damage based on their maximum health. When the passive triggers on a champion, a spirit follows Aurora and restores her health. Weave auto attacks between abilities to build passive stacks. In lane, take short trades: move in, build passive stacks, then back off.
notes.aurora-skill-q: Q's return damage is greatly reduced against minions and monsters. When clearing a wave, calculate around the damage from Q's first hit. When chasing a fleeing champion, delay Q's return as long as possible so their health drops further.
notes.aurora-skill-w: W gives Aurora a hop, stealth, and a movement speed boost. A takedown resets W's cooldown. Decide whether to engage with W based on whether you can reset its cooldown with a takedown.
notes.aurora-skill-e: E deals area damage and applies a strong slow, then hops Aurora backward. Use E as your opponent engages to counterattack and create distance. Before casting E, check where you'll land when you hop opposite the cast direction. E's slow fades over time, so use your follow-up abilities immediately.
notes.aurora-skill-r: Use R to trap opponents. Use R to stop opponents from engaging. You can recast R to end it early. Keep R's area active if enemy reinforcements are outside it. If your team needs to retreat, end R's area early and leave with them. Choose your entry point knowing you can cross to the opposite side of R's area.
notes.aurora-laning-trade: Land Q as your opponent steps forward for a last hit. Apply Q's curse, build passive stacks with an auto attack, then retrieve Q. An opponent cursed by Q may move to avoid its return path, disrupting their farming. Use the passive's healing to take repeated short trades.
notes.aurora-laning-roam: Push the wave, then use W to cross terrain and roam. When roaming, use W's stealth to hide the final part of your approach. Poke safely in lane, then spend your spare time in other lanes.
notes.aurora-phase: Aurora is weak at levels 1–2 because Q is her only available ability. At level 3, W lets Aurora trade and roam. Learning R at level 6 lets Aurora dive and initiate teamfights. Aurora's win rate rises after she completes three core items. Early on, use safe poke and farming to complete three core items instead of forcing kills.
notes.aurora-teamfight: Don't engage first with R while your opponents still have their engage abilities. Engage with R after your opponents have used their initiation abilities or your team has applied crowd control. Trap opponents with R, slow them with E, then retrieve Q. Move more aggressively after W's cooldown resets.
notes.aurora-situational-zhonya: If opponents have a lot of immobilizing crowd control, buy Zhonya's Hourglass between core items, since escaping with W and E will be difficult. Use Zhonya's Hourglass to survive being trapped inside R's area after engaging.
notes.aurora-situational-antiheal: If opponents have a lot of healing, buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.vs-aurora-q: Q applies a curse on hit. You take return damage when Aurora recasts Q or its duration ends. If Q curses you, move off the straight line between you and Aurora to reduce the return damage.
notes.vs-aurora-missing-hp: Q's return damage increases with the target's missing health. If you're below half health, staying in range while cursed by Q can quickly put you within kill range. If your health is uncertain, back off before Q's curse returns.
notes.vs-aurora-w: When Aurora suddenly disappears, it's W's brief stealth. When Aurora uses W's stealth, cast an area ability in advance where she might land. W's stealth is brief, so wait a moment for Aurora to reappear.
notes.vs-aurora-w-reset: When retreating from a teamfight, don't leave a low-health ally behind where Aurora can chain another engage.
notes.vs-aurora-r: Enemies entering or leaving R's area are slowed. To leave without being slowed by R's area, retreat before the area appears. If you remain inside R's area, commit to fighting Aurora. Aurora can cross from one side of R's area to the opposite side.
notes.vs-aurora-dive: Once an opponent gets close to Aurora, her E hop is her only way to create distance. Engage once to draw out Aurora's E, then catch her with a second engage. After level 6, account for R when engaging on Aurora. If Aurora has used both E and W, look for a chance to catch her while she has trouble escaping.
notes.azir-skill-w-projection: Azir's effective attack range depends on where he places his W soldiers. Calculate your damage angles from the soldiers' positions, not Azir's. If enemies line up along a soldier's attack path, one attack hits multiple targets. When multiple soldiers hit the same target, damage drops sharply from the second soldier onward, and on-hit effects apply at half strength. Spread two soldiers apart at different angles instead of overlapping them.
notes.azir-skill-w-charges: W can hold up to two charges. Place two soldiers at once only when you can secure a kill. Save one W charge so you can place a soldier to escape. Place a soldier over a wall with W, then dash to it with E to escape.
notes.azir-skill-q: Q moves soldiers to the targeted location. Soldiers moving with Q damage and slow enemies in their path. Even if multiple soldiers pass through the same enemy with Q, they deal damage only once. Use Q when you need to reposition soldiers. Early on, Q has a long cooldown, so using it carelessly can cost you the next trade.
notes.azir-skill-e: E dashes to a soldier and grants a shield. If E collides with an enemy champion, Azir stops there and regains one soldier charge. When placing a soldier, also choose where you want E to take you. Use E to create distance and escape, or to engage an enemy and regain a soldier charge.
notes.azir-skill-r-defense: Use R to push enemies away as they engage on your allies. The soldier wall left by R briefly blocks enemies' path. Allies can pass through the soldier wall created by R. In narrow passages, use R to block enemies trying to follow up.
notes.azir-skill-passive: Azir's passive can raise a Sun Disc where a turret has fallen. Use the Sun Disc to defend an area where an allied turret has been destroyed. Use the Sun Disc to hold the position after taking an enemy turret. The Sun Disc has armor and magic resistance and remains for a short time. Remember where destroyed turrets are near places where objective fights may happen.
notes.azir-combo-poke: To poke, place a soldier in front of the enemy with W, attack with it, then send it toward the enemy with Q. Keep the attack command active while the soldier moves with Q so it attacks again as soon as it arrives. Attack with the soldier first, then move it with Q.
notes.azir-combo-shuffle: Place a soldier behind the enemy with W, use E to get past them, then use R toward your allies to push the enemy back. Place the soldier at an angle that lets E carry you past the enemy without colliding with them. Attempt the combo that pushes an enemy toward your allies only when your allies are close enough to follow up.
notes.azir-laning-soldier-position: During laning, place soldiers between the enemy minions and the enemy champion. A soldier between the minions and the enemy champion lets you last-hit while pressuring the enemy's approach. If you place soldiers only behind the minions, you can farm but lose your poke. If you place soldiers right next to the enemy champion, you can poke but miss last hits.
notes.azir-laning-mana: Placing a soldier costs mana, and the soldier disappears when its duration ends. Place a soldier only when the enemy enters range or you need to last-hit. Don't keep replacing soldiers when there is no fight or last hit to take. Aim to farm safely during laning.
notes.azir-phase: Azir is weakest early on. Early on, Q's long cooldown leaves gaps between trades. In the mid game, Q's cooldown gets shorter, letting you use soldiers more often. Azir becomes strong in the late game as he builds attack speed and ability power. Early on, minimize losses instead of looking for an advantage. Don't stand forward in lane when you don't know where the enemy jungler is.
notes.azir-teamfight: In teamfights, keep Azir back and use soldiers to attack the enemy frontline continuously. Use R to push enemies away as they dive your backline. Use R to push an enemy toward your allies only when your team is clearly winning the fight. Azir has strong sustained damage but lacks burst damage. Avoid facing an enemy alone.
notes.azir-situational-antiheal: If the enemy frontline sustains through healing, buy Morellonomicon between core items so your soldiers' sustained attacks can keep Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.azir-situational-banshee: If the enemy's main damage is magic and they have a targeted ability that starts an engage on Azir, buy Banshee's Veil to block that first ability and buy time to place soldiers.
notes.vs-azir-soldier-window: Azir's damage depends on his sand soldiers. Avoid the line where a soldier stands, and approach Azir himself from behind or beside the soldier.
notes.vs-azir-burst: Don't trade damage with Azir for long; concentrate your attacks in a short burst. When you catch Azir, don't let him go; kill him immediately.
notes.vs-azir-e: Azir can escape by using E to dash to a soldier placed over a wall. If Azir places a soldier near a wall, block that escape route or engage before he uses E. Stand in the path Azir would take with E to stop his dash.
notes.vs-azir-r: Azir's R pushes enemies away and creates a soldier wall that remains briefly. Azir's allies can pass through the soldier wall created by R. When engaging Azir's team, spread out and approach from multiple directions in an open area.
notes.vs-azir-early: Approach when his soldiers expire or Azir is low on mana. Azir cannot use R before level 6. Before level 6, pressure Azir with your jungler to slow his growth.
notes.bard-combo-q-wall: Q stuns only if it hits a wall or a second enemy after passing through the first target. Fire Q at an enemy with a wall behind them. Fire Q when an enemy lines up with a minion. Hitting an isolated enemy with Q in open space only slows them.
notes.bard-combo-q-angle: If the enemy is away from a wall, Q cannot stun them. Before firing Q, move sideways to line up yourself, the enemy, and a wall.
notes.bard-combo-r-setup: R also affects allies. Aim R so your allied damage dealer does not get caught in it.
notes.bard-combo-r-defense: Use R to save an ally just as a finishing ability is about to hit them. Use R to put an enemy who dives in into stasis, separating them from your allies.
notes.bard-skill-chime: Collecting more chimes strengthens Bard's meep attacks and increases his movement speed. Collect chimes when the wave is pushed out and the lane is safe. Collect chimes along your path back to lane. Do not leave your lane partner alone to chase chimes.
notes.bard-skill-meep: Basic attacks with meeps are one of Bard's ways to harass. When you have meeps, approach the enemy and harass them with basic attacks. Do not waste meep attacks on minions. With enough chimes, meep attacks spread to nearby targets. With enough chimes, meep attacks slow nearby targets.
notes.bard-skill-w-charge: W shrines heal more as they charge over time. If healing is not urgent, place a W shrine in advance and step on it later. An enemy champion destroys a W shrine by walking over it. Place W shrines behind your allies.
notes.bard-skill-e-both: Enemies can also use E portals. Before opening an E portal to escape, check whether an enemy can follow you. Allies travel through E portals faster than enemies.
notes.bard-skill-e-entry: Travel through an E portal with your jungler or mid laner to start a fight from an unexpected angle.
notes.bard-phase: Bard is ordinary at levels 1–2 because he needs time to collect chimes. As chimes build up, stronger meep attacks and increased movement speed make Bard's roams faster. From level 6, R can turn an objective fight around. Later on, Bard's main roles are catching enemies out and intervening in teamfights.
notes.bard-laning-absence: If Bard stays away from lane too long, his marksman has to hold the lane alone. Leave lane after the enemy has used their engage ability. Leave lane when the wave is moving toward your turret. Place W shrines before leaving lane.
notes.bard-laning-trade: Slow the enemy with Q, then trade damage with a meep attack. Fight near brush by a wall or at the river tri-brush to set up a Q stun.
notes.bard-teamfight: In teamfights, Bard catches enemies out and cuts them off. Use Q to pin an engaging enemy against a wall. Use R to briefly take the enemy's main damage dealer out of the fight. Use R to stop an enemy arriving late to the fight. Bard is not a champion who absorbs damage at the front.
notes.bard-teamfight-objective: R also affects Dragon and Baron. As the enemy jungler prepares to Smite, use R to freeze both the objective and the enemy. Before using R at an objective, coordinate its timing with your jungler's Smite.
notes.vs-bard-shrine: Bard's W shrines disappear when stepped on. If you see a W shrine in lane, change your path if needed to step on it and remove it.
notes.vs-bard-portal: The enemy team can also use Bard's E portals. If Bard opens an E portal to escape, follow him through and chase when it is safe. Bard can enter through an E portal, so do not leave your flank open.
notes.vs-bard-ult: Bard's R affects allies, enemies, monsters, and turrets alike.
notes.vs-bard-q: Bard's Q must hit a wall or a second target to stun. When facing Bard, do not stand with your back to a wall. Position yourself so you do not line up with an ally or minion.
notes.vs-bard-roam: Bard often leaves lane to collect chimes. When Bard disappears from view, you can create a 2v1 in bot lane. When Bard disappears from view, signal on the minimap that he may appear in another lane.
notes.vs-bard-mobility: Bard's only escape tool is his E portal. After Bard uses his E portal, look for an opening to engage him again.
notes.belveth-combo-basic: In a standard fight, use Q to close in and auto attack, knock them up with W, then re-engage with the reset Q. If W hits a champion, it resets Q's cooldown in the direction W was cast. Right after W lands, you can use Q once more in the same direction.
notes.belveth-combo-e-timing: Activate E when the enemy starts their burst combo. While E is active, Bel'Veth takes much less damage and gains lifesteal. Using another ability or pressing E again ends E immediately. Do not press Q or W while using E to survive. If you need to hold out for a while and then escape immediately with Q, cancel E on purpose.
notes.belveth-skill-q-direction: Q has a separate cooldown for each direction. You cannot use Q twice in a row in the same direction, but you can use it again immediately in a different direction. When escaping, use Q in different directions.
notes.belveth-skill-q-onhit: Q applies on-hit effects to the first target it hits. If you have on-hit items, line up Q to pass through the enemy during fights. Q's cooldown gets shorter as attack speed increases.
notes.belveth-skill-w: W is Bel'Veth's only reliable crowd control and her way to reset Q. When ganking, draw out the enemy's mobility ability or Flash before using W. If the enemy is on the opposite side of their escape route, use W to cut off their path.
notes.belveth-skill-passive: Lavender stacks from Death in Lavender grant permanent attack speed. A takedown on a large minion or large monster grants one Lavender stack. A takedown on a champion or epic monster grants two Lavender stacks. Bel'Veth's late-game strength depends on her Lavender stacks. Secure takedowns on large jungle monsters to keep scaling. Join team fights to earn takedowns. After using an ability, Bel'Veth briefly gains bonus attack speed and ghosting. When you need to pass through minions, use Q once and move through them.
notes.belveth-skill-r-coral: Void Coral drops only after a takedown on a champion or epic monster. Bel'Veth must consume Void Coral to transform into her true form. Right after a kill in a fight, check where the coral dropped. Transforming increases maximum health, attack range, and attack speed. If you have secured coral, transform just before the next fight or objective contest.
notes.belveth-skill-r-voidling: If you transform using coral left by a Void epic monster, nearby minions that die become Void Remora. Void Remora push the lane. After taking a Void objective, choose a lane to pressure and transform near it.
notes.belveth-jungle-clear: When clearing the jungle, use Q to move between camps and keep your rotation going. Q deals bonus damage to monsters. At camps where you lose health, use E's lifesteal to heal while clearing.
notes.belveth-jungle-gank: Bel'Veth cannot gank with W alone. Gank lanes where an ally has reliable crowd control. Gank when the enemy has pushed the lane and has a long way to escape. If ganks are uncertain before level 6, clear large monsters to build stacks. If ganks are uncertain before level 6, establish vision around objectives.
notes.belveth-phase: Bel'Veth is weakest at levels 1–3. At levels 1–3, avoid encounters with the enemy jungler. Duels become viable in the mid game, after maxing Q, completing your first core item, and starting to build stacks. Bel'Veth peaks in the late game once she has enough Lavender stacks.
notes.belveth-teamfight: Bel'Veth is not suited to leading the front line in team fights. After your tank absorbs the enemy engage, flank with Q into the backline, kill one enemy, and escape with Q. If targeted enemy abilities focus you right after you engage, activate E. After a kill, transform with the dropped coral to prepare for the next fight. E does not require a target; it automatically targets the enemy with the lowest health. Use E to finish enemies in chaotic fights.
notes.belveth-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing makes it hard to secure a kill with sustained damage, buy Executioner's Calling first and upgrade it to Mortal Reminder. Auto attacks and Q's on-hit effects can keep applying Grievous Wounds.
notes.belveth-situational-mercurial: If the enemy has several immobilizing crowd control abilities that can lock down Bel'Veth, buy Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar between core items. Bel'Veth survives more easily only while she can move with Q.
notes.vs-belveth-early: Pressure Bel'Veth with jungle invades or early encounters at levels 1–3. Take large monsters and camps from Bel'Veth before she builds stacks to slow her growth.
notes.vs-belveth-w: W is Bel'Veth's only reliable crowd control. Dodging W prevents the Q reset and slows Bel'Veth's chase. When Bel'Veth closes in, sidestep to dodge W.
notes.vs-belveth-e: Bel'Veth takes much less damage while casting E. Use burst abilities after Bel'Veth's E ends. Interrupt Bel'Veth's E with immobilizing crowd control.
notes.vs-belveth-q: Bel'Veth's Q has a separate cooldown for each direction. Bel'Veth cannot immediately dash again in the direction she just used Q. When escaping or using a skillshot, use the line Bel'Veth just dashed along as your reference.
notes.vs-belveth-coral: Bel'Veth needs a takedown on a champion or epic monster to get coral and transform. Giving Bel'Veth one kill makes the next fight much harder. If you lose an ally in a fight, retreat before Bel'Veth picks up the coral. Delay team fights while Bel'Veth is transformed.
notes.blitz-combo-basic: The basic combo is to pull with Q, knock up with E, and finish with R. Chain Q, E, and R without gaps to prevent a squishy target from fighting back. Try the combo within your turret's range so the turret attacks too.
notes.blitz-combo-e-prefire: Activate E just before Q hits to immediately knock up the pulled target. Pressing E after Q pulls the target gives them a window to escape with a mobility ability.
notes.blitz-combo-w-e-first: If you are unsure you can land Q, approach with W, knock up with E, then use Q. Use Q while the target is knocked up by E or when they start fleeing. Check that the enemy has used their crowd control before approaching with W. Start your W engage from brush to make your approach less visible.
notes.blitz-combo-e-reset: E resets the basic attack timer. When harassing, use E immediately after a basic attack to land both attacks in quick succession.
notes.blitz-skill-q: Q pulls only the first enemy it hits along its path. Target enemies when they move away from minions so minions cannot block Q. Hide in brush to conceal your Q reach. Avoid spamming Q early, given its high mana cost and long cooldown. If the Q angle is uncertain, hold it to pressure the enemy into retreating.
notes.blitz-skill-w: Use W to approach and escape. W slows you when it ends, making escape harder. W's attack speed boost contributes greatly to attacking objectives. Use your saved W when starting to attack Dragon or Rift Herald.
notes.blitz-skill-r: R has a relatively short cooldown for an ultimate. Use R to push waves. Use R to disrupt enemy sieges. Clear minions with R to create a Q angle. When sneaking up, keep in mind that R's automatic lightning may unintentionally hit an enemy.
notes.blitz-skill-r-hold: Avoid using R immediately in an extended one-on-one fight with no minions. After several hits, R's passive lightning deals more total damage than its active. Use R when you need immediate burst damage. Use R when you need a silence. Use R when you need to remove enemy shields.
