notes.blitz-phase: At level 1, using Q leaves you unable to apply much pressure for a while. Blitzcrank starts applying serious grab pressure at levels 2–3. Blitzcrank stays strong throughout the early and mid game. As the game progresses, Blitzcrank relies on allied follow-up to kill targets. In the late game, avoid grabs without allied follow-up.
notes.blitz-laning: Blitzcrank's grab opportunities in lane depend heavily on securing brush vision. Control the brush to conceal your grab range. When Q is on cooldown, fall back and protect your ally as they farm.
notes.blitz-laning-invade: Q is especially effective in narrow jungle chokepoints. Join early invades and try to catch the enemy jungler with Q at chokepoints. Look for chances to steal enemy camps with Q during early invades. If your lane is stable, pressure enemy jungle routes with your allies.
notes.blitz-teamfight: Blitzcrank struggles to kill healthy targets alone and relies on allied damage. Engage with Q only when allies can follow up immediately. After engaging, use E and W to stick to the target and maintain pressure.
notes.blitz-situational-thornmail: If the enemy's main damage is physical and they also have healing, choose Thornmail for both armor and healing reduction.
notes.vs-blitz-minion: Q pulls only the first target it hits along its path. Stand behind minions rather than beside them so they block Q.
notes.vs-blitz-cooldown: Q costs a lot of mana at level 1. Q has a long cooldown at level 1. Use the window immediately after a missed level 1 Q to pressure the lane or trade.
notes.vs-blitz-mana: Q costs a lot of mana. Watch Blitzcrank's mana bar to identify safe windows when he cannot use Q.
notes.vs-blitz-peel: Blitzcrank lacks the damage to finish off targets with crowd control alone. Bypass Blitzcrank and engage on his allies behind him. When enemies bypass Blitzcrank to attack his allies, his ability to protect only one ally becomes a limitation.
notes.vs-blitz-shield: P creates a shield that scales with mana when health gets low. Account for P's shield, secure a way to finish the kill, then try to kill him in one go.
notes.vs-blitz-vision: Giving up brush vision makes it harder to judge grab range. Use Control Wards to secure brush vision. Stay well away from brush when moving through areas without vision.
notes.blitz-skill-passive: When Blitzcrank's health falls below 30%, his passive shield activates. The passive shield scales with maximum mana. Spending mana does not reduce the passive shield's strength. Choose items that increase maximum mana to strengthen the passive shield. After the passive shield activates, look for an opening to engage while accounting for its cooldown.
notes.brand-skill-passive-blaze: Brand's damage depends heavily on Blaze stacks. Landing an ability adds Blaze stacks to the target. When Blaze reaches maximum stacks on a champion or large jungle monster, it explodes shortly afterward, dealing area damage based on maximum health. Build combos around stacking Blaze. When farming, apply Blaze before last-hitting to restore mana.
notes.brand-skill-q: Q is a single-target projectile that stops at the first enemy hit. Q stuns only if the target is already burning. Use Q when the target is burning and no minions block its path.
notes.brand-skill-w: W detonates after a warning, so enemies can walk out of it. Place W ahead of the enemy's movement. Use W during an ally's immobilizing effect or your Q stun. W deals more damage to burning targets. To increase W's damage, set the target on fire first. W is Brand's only long-range poke that minions cannot block.
notes.brand-skill-e: E spreads around the targeted unit. E has twice the spread range when used on a burning target. Set a minion on fire, then use E to poke the enemy champion beside it. Set minions on fire to make it hard for enemies to stand near their minions.
notes.brand-skill-r: R prioritizes bouncing toward champions with fewer Blaze stacks. The fewer targets R can bounce to, the more often it hits the same target. Count the targets R can bounce to before casting it. In fights with many champions, use R to spread stacks across the area. In smaller fights, R concentrates damage on one target.
notes.brand-combo-stun: At range, set the target on fire with W, then stun them with Q. If the enemy is already close, use E then Q for a quick stun. The enemy must have Blaze before Q reaches them for it to stun.
notes.brand-combo-burst: For single-target burst, use W, Q, E, then W. Land W, which has a warning, during the Q stun. If Blaze reaches maximum stacks during this combo, the explosion also deals damage. E has twice the spread range when used on a burning target.
notes.brand-combo-aoe: When several enemies are grouped, set them on fire with W, then spread Blaze with E. For an area combo, build stacks with W and E, then use R.
notes.brand-laning: Poke with W during the laning phase. Place W as the enemy marksman steps forward to last-hit. After poking with W, do not stay within the enemy's range. Brand uses a lot of mana and has low health, making him vulnerable to dying in lane.
notes.brand-laning-allin: Go all in when the enemy has Blaze and Q is available. Before going all in, check that the enemy has Blaze. Landing Q on a burning enemy lets your allies land basic attacks and lets you use W and E during the stun.
notes.brand-phase: Brand's damage depends heavily on the Blaze explosion rather than individual abilities. His trades become stronger from levels 3–6, when he can chain at least two abilities. Brand is strongest in the mid game as he builds ability power. Brand struggles to contribute to late-game teamfights if he gets picked off first. In the late game, position yourself to avoid getting picked off first.
notes.brand-teamfight: Stay in the back during teamfights and deal area damage. When enemies group up, set them on fire with W, spread Blaze with E, then use R. Blaze's explosion damages the frontline too, so do not move forward to target the backline.
notes.brand-teamfight-choke: If enemies are spread out, R stops bouncing early. Use R in narrow passages near objectives or when the enemy formation tightens. Save R if the enemies have already spread out. If enemies are spread out, use E and W to keep Blaze on the frontline.
notes.brand-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, choose Morellonomicon to keep Grievous Wounds active longer through damage over time.
notes.vs-brand-blaze: Brand's threat comes from Blaze stacks more than individual abilities. Getting hit by consecutive abilities builds Blaze stacks until they explode. Dodge the first Q or W to break Brand's combo.
notes.vs-brand-q: Brand's Q stuns only burning enemies. If you are on fire, move out of Q's path or hide behind a minion. Move after Blaze wears off.
notes.vs-brand-cluster: Brand's E spreads twice as far around a burning target. Brand's R bounces between targets. Space out from your allies before engaging. Do not stand beside a burning ally.
notes.vs-brand-r: Brand's R has a slow initial projectile, giving you time to spread out after you see him cast it. Move away from your allies when you see R cast. If you are on fire, move earlier to account for R's slow.
notes.vs-brand-minions: Brand uses E on burning minions to poke nearby enemies indirectly. Do not last-hit beside a burning minion. Where minion waves meet, step to the side before moving in.
notes.vs-brand-punish: Brand has very low health and no mobility abilities. Engage when Brand's W is on cooldown. Without Blaze, Brand cannot stun an enemy who gets close with Q.
notes.braum-skill-passive: Concussive Blows starts when Braum applies the first mark. After that, allied basic attacks also add stacks. The final stack triggers a stun and magic damage. Agree with your allies on a target before starting a trade.
notes.braum-skill-passive-window: Stacks cannot build again for a short time after the stun triggers. Braum's basic attacks deal bonus damage immediately after the stun. If allies do not attack in time after the first stack, the mark expires.
notes.braum-skill-q: Q is a projectile that hits only the first enemy. Q slows the enemy and applies a Concussive Blows stack. In lane, throw Q through gaps between minions. Q is Braum's only way to start a fight from range.
notes.braum-skill-w: W can leap to allied champions and minions. When W lands, Braum and the target gain armor and magic resistance. Braum gains more armor and magic resistance from W than the target does. Use W to reach an ally just before they take damage.
notes.braum-skill-e: E intercepts and destroys projectiles coming from the direction Braum faces. E negates damage from the first projectile it intercepts and reduces damage from later ones. E cannot block projectiles coming from behind or beside Braum. Stand in front of your ally, putting your body between them and the enemy marksman. Raise E when you see the enemy begin casting a key skillshot.
notes.braum-skill-r: After a long cast animation, R sends a fissure forward in a straight line. The farther R's first target is from Braum, the longer they are knocked up. Aim R's first hit at a key target farther away. The fissure left by R is a strong slowing zone.
notes.braum-combo-engage: Apply the first stack with Q, close the gap with W, then build stacks with basic attacks to stun. Allied basic attacks build Concussive Blows stacks faster. Tell your allies whom to attack right after Q hits.
notes.braum-combo-ult-chain: After knocking an enemy up with R, hit Q just before they land to follow up with a slow and a stack. Enemies knocked up by R cannot use movement abilities while airborne. Follow R with Q and basic attacks to extend the crowd control into a stun.
notes.braum-combo-peel: Hit a nearby enemy with Q, leap to the ally you need to protect with W, then raise E toward the threat.
notes.braum-phase: Braum is fairly strong in lane because he can start trades with Q from level 1. From level 6, Braum can use R to force an engage and control terrain. Braum stays strong through the mid game as he builds defensive items. In the late game, Braum's impact drops sharply if his allies have fallen behind.
notes.braum-laning: Throw Q when a gap opens between minions or an enemy steps up to last-hit. When Q hits, move in with your allies to build Concussive Blows stacks. If Q misses, back off and wait for it to come off cooldown. Use your positioning to limit the enemy marksman's space and keep them from stepping forward.
notes.braum-laning-vision: W requires an ally or minion, so Braum has trouble moving quickly on his own. Protect your marksman in lane while maintaining vision of the river and bushes. When the enemy jungler comes in, slow their engage with Q and E.
notes.braum-teamfight: In teamfights, stand between your backline and the enemy damage dealers. Stay beside your marksman, then use R on enemies who dive in to break up their formation. Place R's fissure along the enemy's path for follow-up.
notes.braum-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has an ability that can immobilize and burst down your marksman, buy Mikael's Blessing earlier. Braum has no way to remove crowd control already applied to an ally.
notes.vs-braum-stacks: Braum's stun triggers only after the mark gains multiple stacks. Once marked, move out of range before the remaining stacks build up.
notes.vs-braum-q: Braum must hit Q or a basic attack to apply the first Concussive Blows mark. Stand behind minions to block Braum's Q. Avoid lining up with Braum when a gap opens between minions.
notes.vs-braum-e: Projectiles cannot get through from the direction Braum faces with E raised. Wait for the shield to drop before using projectiles. Move around Braum's side and look for an angle to attack from a direction his shield does not face.
notes.vs-braum-r: Braum's R has a cast animation that gives you time to dodge. Dodge sideways out of R's straight-line fissure. Position early to avoid stepping into the slowing zone R leaves behind. If you are in the backline, stay out of R's straight path.
notes.vs-braum-damage: Braum's own damage is very low. Target the ally Braum is protecting. Find another route past Braum to the backline.
notes.briar-combo-gank: When ganking, stun with Q, activate W, land a basic attack, then recast W. When W is active, Briar can no longer choose her target herself. To attack a specific enemy, lock onto them with Q before activating W.
notes.briar-combo-r: In teamfights, land R, then after landing, use Q to stun, land a basic attack, recast W, and use E. Interrupt enemies using channeled ultimates with R's bloodstone. If the enemy's escape route leads toward a wall, fully charge E at the end to stun them against it.
notes.briar-skill-passive: Briar has no base health regeneration and spends current health each time she uses an ability. To heal, keep attacking and maintain bleed stacks. The more health Briar is missing, the more she heals.
notes.briar-skill-w-control: When Briar activates W, she is taunted toward the nearest enemy and loses control. Choose your target before activating W. Use Q to close in on your target first. If the enemy frontline is in front, don't activate W first.
notes.briar-skill-w-recast: Recasting W makes Briar's next basic attack deal damage based on the target's missing health and heal her. To deal more damage, recast W after the enemy has lost health. If Briar is in danger, recast W immediately to heal.
notes.briar-skill-w-jungle: Using Q on a minion or monster during Blood Frenzy removes the priority on attacking champions. When you need to chase a champion, don't use Q on a monster.
notes.briar-skill-e: E is Briar's only way to end Blood Frenzy herself and regain control. While charging E, Briar takes less damage and heals based on her maximum health. Fully charging E knocks enemies back and stuns those who hit a wall. Fully charge E against an enemy with a wall behind them. In open space, use a short E for damage and a slow.
notes.briar-skill-r: The first champion hit by R's bloodstone becomes the prey. To make your intended target the prey, fire R from an angle where the frontline cannot block it. When Briar lands with R, nearby enemies other than the prey are feared. Land R where enemies are grouped to split up those nearby.
notes.briar-jungle-clear: At jungle camps, use Blood Frenzy's area basic attacks, then charge E to heal when your health drops.
notes.briar-jungle-gank: Briar's kill participation at 14 minutes ranks among the highest of all champions. Try ganking where an ally has guaranteed crowd control or the enemy has pushed the lane. If there is no gank opportunity, don't activate W, which is hard to undo.
notes.briar-phase: Once Briar has Q, W, and E and learns R at level 6, she gains solo kill opportunities. Briar is strongest in the mid game when she has both attack damage and health. If Briar engages first in a late game teamfight, she may fall before she can heal. In the late game, enter after your allies start the fight and finish it.
notes.briar-teamfight: Choose an R prey that your allies can immediately attack with you. Enter teamfights after your allies land their first crowd control. If things go badly during Blood Frenzy, use E to end it and regain control.
notes.briar-situational-antiheal: If the enemy is surviving through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Briar can easily maintain healing reduction by spreading damage with her bleed and area basic attacks.
notes.briar-situational-qss: If the enemy has a long root, consider Mercurial Scimitar. Briar cannot heal while a root prevents her from landing basic attacks, leaving her vulnerable to losing health.
notes.vs-briar-w: Put your frontline in Briar's path when she dives with W to protect your backline carry. When Briar engages with W, the backline carry should not stand in front.
notes.vs-briar-e: Crowd controlling Briar while she charges E can stop her healing and wall stun. When Briar starts charging E, use a stun or knockup. Don't fight with your back to a wall, where Briar's fully charged E can stun you.
notes.vs-briar-passive: If you encounter Briar in the jungle, damage her to delay her next move.
notes.vs-briar-r: When Briar fires R, have your frontline stand in front to keep your backline carry from becoming the prey. If you become R's prey, Briar chases you with increased resistances and movement speed. If R marks you as its prey, move toward your allies and fight back together.
notes.vs-briar-early: Push the lane and secure vision to prepare for Briar's ganks. Without vision, don't stand in the middle of the lane for long.
notes.caitlyn-combo-trap-q: Place W under enemies or where they will retreat. When an enemy triggers W, use Headshot, then Q. Headshot range increases greatly against enemies caught in a trap. Apply the rule that Q damage is not reduced against enemies caught in a trap. Use the moment right after a trap triggers to deal maximum damage.
notes.caitlyn-combo-e-headshot: Headshot range increases against targets hit by E. After landing E, use Headshot, place W where the enemy will retreat, then use Q. Use E to create Headshot opportunities.
notes.caitlyn-combo-e-reposition: Use E's recoil movement to create distance. Use E's recoil movement to escape over walls.
notes.caitlyn-skill-passive: Headshot activates after a set number of basic attacks. Basic attacks from brush charge Headshot faster. Use the Headshot charged while moving in and out of lane brush on champions. Avoid attacking minions when Headshot is fully charged.
notes.caitlyn-skill-w: W stores multiple trap charges. Place W in advance so its cooldown finishes during the fight. Place W where enemies must pass, such as brush entrances, jungle entrances, or behind you.
notes.caitlyn-skill-e-keep: E is Caitlyn's only escape ability. Using E to poke first leaves you without a way to respond to an enemy engage. Save E until you confirm the enemy has used their engage ability.
notes.caitlyn-skill-r: Another enemy champion can take the hit from R instead of its target. Avoid using R in chaotic fights. Use R to finish off a fleeing target, a duel opponent, or an enemy in another lane only when no champion can block its path. Caitlyn stands still while casting R.
notes.caitlyn-phase-early: Caitlyn's long range lets her pressure enemies from level 1, even without items. Caitlyn excels in the laning phase. Build an early lead through CS and turret pressure.
notes.caitlyn-phase-late: In the mid to late game, Caitlyn has less raw damage output than other marksmen with strong sustained damage. Caitlyn reaches her power peak when she converts her lane lead into turrets and objectives. After her power peak, use her range advantage to attack from a safe position.
notes.caitlyn-laning-push: Caitlyn ranks among the best in CS and turret plating metrics. Use your range advantage to push the wave first and keep enemies pinned under their turret. Destroy turret plates while enemies are pinned under their turret. While the wave is pushed, place W at river approaches to defend against ganks.
notes.caitlyn-laning-trade: Only attempt trades when Headshot is ready. Poking with basic attacks without Headshot gives enemies an opening to close in. Back out of range immediately after trading to deny enemies an engage opportunity.
notes.caitlyn-teamfight: Attack from the edge of your maximum range in teamfights. Place W along enemy approach routes and around your feet to block their approach. Secure your position before the teamfight starts. In teamfights, save E exclusively for interrupting enemy engages.
notes.caitlyn-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Caitlyn's range lets her attack throughout teamfights and continuously apply Executioner's Calling's healing reduction.
notes.vs-caitlyn-r: R hits an allied champion of the target instead if they block its path. If an ally is targeted by R, step into the bullet's path to protect them.
notes.vs-caitlyn-rooted-cast: Caitlyn stands still while casting Q. Caitlyn stands still while casting R. When you see Q or R's cast animation, close in or find an angle to attack. The moment after Caitlyn uses Q to clear the wave is the best time to engage.
notes.vs-caitlyn-trap: Stepping on a W trap roots the target. Caitlyn's Headshot range increases against targets caught in a trap. Assume there are traps in bushes and narrow paths, and change your approach. Send minions ahead into bushes and narrow paths where you expect traps.
notes.vs-caitlyn-e: E is Caitlyn's only escape ability. E moves Caitlyn through recoil. Engage after Caitlyn uses E, when she has no way to create distance.
notes.vs-caitlyn-phase: Caitlyn is strongest during the laning phase and becomes relatively weaker as the game goes on. Avoid taking excessive risks early and giving Caitlyn kills.
notes.caitlyn-skill-q: Q deals reduced damage to targets after the first. Caitlyn stays in place while aiming Q. Do not fire Q at a champion behind minions. Use Q as soon as the enemy steps away from the minions. Use Q the moment your opponent is caught in a trap.
notes.vs-caitlyn-q: Caitlyn's Q passes through targets. Caitlyn's Q deals reduced damage to targets after the first. Stand behind allied minions when Caitlyn pokes with Q.
notes.camille-combo-trade: Trade in lane with an auto attack → first Q → wait → second Q. Waiting before recasting Q increases its bonus damage and converts part of the damage to true damage. If there’s no rush, weave another auto attack between Q casts to buy time. Hit with W’s outer edge during trades to slow the enemy and heal yourself.
notes.camille-combo-engage: Engage with E to a wall → W while moving → recast E to collide → auto attack → first Q → second Q. Camille can cast W while traveling on E’s hook. Time W’s windup to end as E’s leap finishes so you slow a distant enemy. Start a fight with an auto attack on an enemy champion to activate your passive shield.
notes.camille-combo-ult: For a guaranteed kill, use W’s outer edge → R → auto attack → first Q → auto attack → second Q. To make up for R’s short range, lock the enemy down first with E’s stun or W’s slow. While casting R, use its untargetability to ignore enemy crowd control and close in.
notes.camille-skill-q: Q acts as an on-hit ability that empowers your next basic attack. Both Q attacks can trigger Spellblade effects, such as Trinity Force, for two procs. The second Q converts part of its damage to true damage, bypassing enemy armor. Chain E’s stun, W’s slow, or allied crowd control to land both Q attacks. Basic attack negation, blinds, and dodges can block Q, so use it after those counters are spent.
notes.camille-skill-w: W deals bonus damage only with its outer edge. W slows only with its outer edge. Hitting with W’s outer edge heals Camille. Camille relies on W’s outer edge for lane sustain and engage opportunities. Account for W’s windup: step back before casting so the enemy is caught by its outer edge.
notes.camille-skill-e: E’s movement requires the hook to latch onto a wall. Firing E’s hook is not movement, so Camille can use it while rooted. When E pulls Camille to a wall, it shows the direction of nearby enemies. E’s leap gains range when aimed toward a visible enemy champion. E’s leap stops at the first enemy it hits, so adjust your approach if another enemy is in front of your target. Camille relies on E to engage. Choose your target before using E.
notes.camille-skill-passive: Camille’s passive shield activates only when a basic attack hits an enemy champion. Her passive creates either a physical or magic shield based on the enemy’s damage type. Basic attacks against minions do not activate her passive shield. Start a fight with an auto attack before using abilities to gain the passive shield. Camille relies on her passive shield for defense.
notes.camille-item-vs-physical: If the enemy’s main damage is physical, her passive shield will be physical. Against physical damage opponents, buy Plated Steelcaps early to pair armor with the shield. To strengthen side-lane 1v1s against physical damage opponents, follow up with Dead Man’s Plate or Randuin’s Omen.
notes.camille-item-vs-magic: If the enemy’s main damage is magic, build magic resistance to pair with the magic shield. Against magic damage opponents, choose Ionian Boots of Lucidity for ability haste. If burst damage is the problem, choose Banshee’s Veil to block the opening ability. Against a team with long chains of crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash first.
notes.camille-phase: Camille is at her weakest during the first two levels. Start trading once you have Q and your passive shield available. After learning R, Camille gains control over jungle skirmishes and gank follow-ups. Camille is strongest in midgame with two core items. Late game, avoid trading head-on with ranged carries and force 1v1s in the side lane.
notes.camille-laning: Start lane by chipping away at the enemy with W’s outer edge. Save E while poking in lane. Lure the enemy near a wall to set up an E engage. If the enemy stands far from walls behind minions, farm instead of engaging. While E and your passive shield are on cooldown, avoid trades and preserve your health. Camille farms slowly. Focus on CS and wait for a chance to join your jungler instead of forcing an early engage.
notes.camille-teamfight: R traps one target inside its area. When R’s area appears, it knocks back enemies other than the target. Get onto the enemy’s main damage dealer and trap them with R to give your team time to kill them. Time your teamfight engage with your allies’ engage. If the teamfight setup is bad, push a side-lane turret to draw enemies out.
notes.vs-camille-e: Camille’s engage relies on E latching its hook onto a wall. Against Camille, stay away from walls and position among minions. Because Camille can use W while traveling on her hook, count areas far from walls as within her threat range too.
notes.vs-camille-e-interrupt: Knockbacks and pulls interrupt Camille’s E leap. If E’s leap is interrupted, Camille loses both the collision stun and the attack speed increase. Save knockbacks or pulls until Camille’s hook latches onto a wall.
notes.vs-camille-r: A target trapped by R has virtually no way to leave its area. Camille becomes untargetable as she enters with R, allowing her to ignore crowd control. Don’t waste your counter ability as Camille enters with R; fight back after the area expires. Avoid the W slow or E stun that lets Camille get into R range. Use Flash to create distance before Camille reaches you, escaping R’s short cast range.
notes.vs-camille-passive: Camille’s passive creates only a physical or magic shield, based on the enemy’s damage type. Since the shield blocks only one damage type, attack alongside an ally who deals a different type. Avoid trading right after Camille’s passive shield activates; approach once it has worn off.
notes.vs-camille-q: Camille relies heavily on Q-empowered auto attacks for damage. Armor does not reduce the true damage portion of her second Q. Use basic attack negation, a blind, or stealth to neutralize her Q-empowered auto attack. Create distance while Camille waits for her second Q to avoid the empowered auto attack.
notes.vs-camille-early: Camille is at her weakest before completing her first core item. Camille clears waves slowly. Take lane control before Camille completes her first core item and deny her farm to delay it. Camille takes down turrets quickly from midgame onward. From midgame onward, defend the side lane to stop Camille from taking turrets.
notes.cass-combo-poke: For basic poke, land Q, then use E. When Q hits a champion, Cassiopeia gains a large movement speed boost. After landing Q, use the movement speed to stay within E range and follow the target. If Q misses, do not walk forward to trade.
notes.cass-combo-allin: For a guaranteed combo, stun with R, land Q, then repeatedly use E. Use E on a poisoned target whenever it comes off cooldown to maximize damage.
notes.cass-skill-q: Q detonates at the targeted spot after a short delay. Aim Q ahead of where the opponent is walking, rather than where they are standing. If the hit is uncertain, place Q ahead of time on the opponent's path or where they will step up to last-hit.
notes.cass-skill-e: E deals bonus damage and heals Cassiopeia only when used on a poisoned target. To save mana, poison the target before using E. Keep using E while Q's poison lasts. Last-hitting with E refunds mana.
notes.cass-skill-e-stationary: Use E repeatedly on a target that cannot move. Right after stunning with R, save your other abilities and use E repeatedly.
notes.cass-skill-w: Enemies inside W's poison cloud cannot use movement abilities. Place W under an opponent who has dashed in to stop their movement. W has a long cooldown, so do not waste it on poke.
notes.cass-skill-r: R stuns only enemies facing Cassiopeia. Cassiopeia’s R only slows enemies facing away from her. Use R when the opponent charges straight at you. Do not use R on a fleeing opponent's back or from an angle after moving behind them.
notes.cass-laning-farm: In lane, apply poison with Q, then last-hit with E. Early on, stand behind minions to avoid giving the opponent an angle to poke with basic attacks.
notes.cass-laning-wave: To keep enough mana for W in case of a gank, do not use Q to push the entire wave. If you do not need lane priority, keep the wave in the middle and clear it with E last-hits. Do not push the lane forward while the enemy jungler's location is unknown.
notes.cass-phase: Cassiopeia is weakest at levels 1–2 because trading with only one ability is difficult. From mid game, once E has been leveled up and Cassiopeia has mana items, her sustained damage rises sharply. Late game, Cassiopeia has some of the highest teamfight damage as long as she is not caught. Early on, focus on scaling rather than fighting.
notes.cass-teamfight: In teamfights, do not engage yourself; stand behind your frontline. From behind your frontline, apply poison with Q, then keep using E on the poisoned target. Use W on the path enemies take toward your backline or under an enemy who has already dived in. Save R for the moment several enemies charge straight at you.
notes.cass-situational-zhonya: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier, between your core items. Cassiopeia has no mobility ability, so getting caught is dangerous, but if she survives briefly, her sustained E damage can turn the fight around.
notes.cass-situational-mercurial: If the enemy's finishing blow comes from a magic damage composition that starts with a long stun, use Quicksilver Sash to remove the stun. Every moment Cassiopeia spends under crowd control is time she cannot deal damage.
notes.vs-cass-r: Cassiopeia's R stuns only enemies facing her. When you see R's cast animation, turn away to take the slow instead of the stun. When close to Cassiopeia, do not keep attacking while facing her R head-on.
notes.vs-cass-e: Cassiopeia's E deals more damage to poisoned targets and heals her.
notes.vs-cass-w: You cannot use movement abilities inside Cassiopeia's W poison cloud. If you are approaching with a dash, close the distance before W is placed. If W is already placed, take a route around the poison cloud.
notes.vs-cass-early: Cassiopeia has no mobility ability and is vulnerable to early ganks. At levels 1–5, keep pressuring Cassiopeia with basic attacks and short trades. Build an early lead before Cassiopeia becomes strong in the mid to late game.
notes.vs-cass-teamfight: Late game, Cassiopeia can win teamfights with sustained damage as long as she is not caught. Establish vision to cut off Cassiopeia's path. Engage right after Cassiopeia uses W elsewhere. When you have an opening to engage, apply guaranteed crowd control before Cassiopeia gains movement speed.
notes.chogath-combo-basic: Activate E in advance, close in with a basic attack, knock them up with Q, silence them with W, then land the remaining E empowered attacks. Activating E has no cast time. If Q misses, back off.
notes.chogath-combo-q-timing: Q shows a warning at the target location before it activates, so opponents can walk out of it. Place Q as the opponent steps forward to last hit with a basic attack. Place Q right after an ally's crowd control lands. Silence the opponent with W to lock out their mobility ability, then place Q.
notes.chogath-combo-wq: If the opponent looks likely to dodge Q with a mobility ability, lock it out with W before placing Q. W's silence does not stop opponents from walking.
notes.chogath-skill-r-stacks: Killing a target with R grants a Feast stack. Feast stacks increase Cho'Gath's maximum health and size. Feast stacks increase Cho'Gath's attack range and Feast range. There is a cap on Feast stacks gained from minions and normal jungle monsters. During the laning phase, reach the cap on Feast stacks from minions and normal jungle monsters. To gain Feast stacks beyond that cap, kill champions or epic monsters.
notes.chogath-skill-r-execute: R's true damage ignores the opponent's armor and magic resistance. Even against a tanky opponent, lower their health enough before finishing them with R. If the kill is uncertain, save R so you do not lose a chance to grow and a way to finish the target.
notes.chogath-skill-e: E adds spikes to the next three basic attacks. E's spikes pierce enemies in a straight line ahead and slow them. E deals damage based on the opponent's maximum health, making it strong against frontliners who build health. E's maximum health damage increases with Feast stacks. Against monsters, E's maximum health damage is replaced by a fixed amount.
notes.chogath-skill-w: W silences enemies in a cone. Use W just before a skill reliant assassin or mage casts a key ability. W costs the most mana of Cho'Gath's abilities. Early on, avoid using W too often so you have enough mana to stay in lane.
notes.chogath-skill-passive: Carnivore restores health and mana whenever you kill a unit. Carnivore restores more health and mana as you level up. Last hit consistently to sustain in lane with Carnivore. When your health is uncertain, heal by killing minions instead of forcing a trade.
notes.chogath-laning-ranged: Q is your only way to start a trade against a ranged opponent. Against ranged opponents, use E's spikes through minions to clear the wave and stay in lane. Call for a jungle gank when the opponent has pushed the wave. After level 6, look for a kill when the opponent forgets about your increased Feast range.
notes.chogath-laning-antigank: Cho'Gath has no mobility ability, making him vulnerable to ganks. When a gank comes, place Q as the enemies close in and commit to a direction. To turn a gank around, place Q in the opponent's path, then use W to lock out their pursuit ability. Pull the wave toward you and draw in the enemy jungler.
notes.chogath-phase: Cho'Gath is vulnerable at levels 1–2 because he lacks mana and abilities. You can start trading at level 3, once you have Q and W. Learning R at level 6 opens up chances to get kills and build Feast stacks. Cho'Gath relies on Feast stacks for durability in the late game.
notes.chogath-teamfight: In teamfights, stand in front of your allies. Place Q in the opponent's path to slow their engage. Silence the enemy initiator with W just as they are about to use an ability. Because you cannot use a mobility ability to return, do not stray too far ahead of your frontline in teamfights.
notes.chogath-teamfight-ult: In teamfights, use R on a low health enemy carry. A kill with R during a teamfight immediately increases your maximum health through a Feast stack. If R will secure the kill, finish the target yourself to gain a stack for the next fight.
notes.chogath-situational-antiheal: If the opponent survives through healing, choose Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Dealing damage consistently with Q and E can keep healing reduction active throughout a fight.
notes.vs-chogath-q: Q activates after a warning appears beneath your feet, giving you time to react. Move sideways immediately when you see Q's indicator. Save your mobility ability to dodge Q. Cho'Gath's combo depends on landing Q.
notes.vs-chogath-w: W silences enemies in a cone in front of Cho'Gath. If W silences you, you cannot escape with a mobility ability and may be hit by the follow-up Q. When trading with Cho'Gath, move around his side to avoid W's cone in front of him. Once silenced, walk out first instead of trying to use abilities.
notes.vs-chogath-r: Defensive items cannot block R's true damage. Do not stay near Cho'Gath when your health falls to half or less. Feast stacks increase Cho'Gath's R range.
notes.vs-chogath-stacks: Cho'Gath's late-game durability relies on Feast stacks. There is a cap on Feast stacks gained from minions and normal jungle monsters. When your health is uncertain, avoid giving Cho'Gath a kill to limit his Feast stack growth.
notes.vs-chogath-e: E's spikes deal damage based on the opponent's maximum health. E's spikes pierce enemies in a straight line in front of Cho'Gath. Standing behind minions in the path of E's spikes lets Cho'Gath poke you while clearing the wave. Stand away from the line of Cho'Gath's basic attacks.
notes.vs-chogath-mobility: Cho'Gath has no mobility abilities at all. During the laning phase, stay outside Q's range and poke Cho'Gath. Look for a gank right after Cho'Gath uses Q on the wave.
notes.corki-combo-poke: When poking, land Q before firing R. Q reveals the area it hits and any champions there for a while. Repeatedly poke with Q and R at max range.
notes.corki-combo-allin: When going all in, enter with W, activate E, land an auto attack, then finish with R. Corki can move and auto attack while firing E. Reducing armor and magic resistance with E increases the damage of your following auto attacks and R.
notes.corki-combo-bigone: Every third R shot deals heavy damage. Count your R charges and time the third shot to finish the target. Before a fight where you need the big missile, do not use the first two shots to clear the wave.
notes.corki-skill-r: R stops gaining charges when it is full. Do not use every R charge and leave yourself without missiles for a fight. Landing an auto attack on a champion reduces R's charge time. Weave in auto attacks while poking to recharge missiles sooner.
notes.corki-skill-e: E reduces enemies' armor and magic resistance in a cone. The defenses reduced by E also affect your allies' damage. In teamfights, aim E at the target your allies are actually attacking. Corki can move and auto attack while firing E.
notes.corki-skill-w: W is Corki's only mobility ability. W can cross terrain. Corki has trouble escaping when W is down. Use W to enter only after the enemy's engage ability is down.
notes.corki-skill-q: Throw Q into bushes or unwarded paths to check for an ambush. Hit a fleeing enemy with Q to reveal their position. Use Q to check the enemy jungler's position before an objective.
notes.corki-skill-passive: Corki's passive converts part of his auto attack damage to true damage. The passive's true damage conversion also applies to Spellblade effects. Weave in auto attacks even against enemies with high armor. As of the 26.17 tooltip, Corki's passive does not include the Package. Do not count on the Package as a way to engage.
notes.corki-laning: In lane, build small advantages by poking with Q and R. Corki is vulnerable to ganks. When you lack vision, do not push the wave toward the enemy turret. Save W to escape during the laning phase.
notes.corki-laning-farm: When the enemy pokes you, farm the wave safely instead of trading back.
notes.corki-phase: Corki is very weak at levels 1–5. At level 6, R and your first core item give you strong poke. Corki is strongest in the mid to late game with two or three items. Get through the weak early game without falling behind.
notes.corki-teamfight: In teamfights, fire R from the back. Use E on the target your allies are attacking. Enter with W only after the enemy's engage abilities and targeted crowd control are both down. Corki has trouble escaping once caught.
notes.corki-objective: In objective fights, deal damage with R from beyond a wall or outside enemy vision. Reveal the enemy team with Q, then fire R.
notes.corki-situational-antiheal: If the enemy sustains through your poke, buy Executioner's Calling between core items to keep that damage from being healed.
notes.vs-corki-r: Corki's R also damages enemies around the first target hit. Move out of Corki's R range instead of hiding behind minions. Corki's third missile deals heavy damage. Reposition to avoid being hit by consecutive missiles.
notes.vs-corki-w: Engage right after Corki uses W. Corki can escape over terrain if W is available.
notes.vs-corki-mobility: Corki is vulnerable to slows and targeted dashes. Corki is especially vulnerable to ganks. Pressure Corki during his weak first five levels to slow his growth.
notes.vs-corki-e: Corki's E reduces both armor and magic resistance when it hits you. Move sideways out of the direction Corki aims E.
notes.vs-corki-q: Corki's Q reveals your position for a while if it hits you. If Q hits you while you are escaping, immediately use a mobility ability to create distance.
notes.vs-corki-scaling: Corki grows stronger as he gets more items. Use early lane pressure and ganks to disrupt Corki's farm.
notes.darius-combo-basic: The basic trade combo is E → auto attack → W → Q. Landing E guarantees an auto attack and W. Use W's auto attack reset to quickly reach three Hemorrhage stacks. Finish the combo with Q, taking half a step back to land the blade.
notes.darius-combo-execute: The execution combo is E → auto attack → auto attack → W → Q → auto attack → R. R damage scales with the target's Hemorrhage stacks. Use R after reaching maximum Hemorrhage stacks. E's slow keeps the enemy in range while you add auto attacks.
notes.darius-skill-passive: Hemorrhage stacks up to five times. Reaching maximum Hemorrhage stacks greatly increases attack damage. Alternate auto attacks and abilities to build Hemorrhage stacks quickly. Darius grows stronger as fights drag on and he builds Hemorrhage stacks. Back off from fights that started with no Hemorrhage stacks.
notes.darius-skill-q: Q deals full damage only to enemies hit by the blade. Q's healing scales with the number of enemy champions and large monsters hit by the blade. In lane, step back as you use Q to hit the enemy champion with the blade. Using Flash during Q's cast moves the blade's hitbox.
notes.darius-skill-w: W resets the auto attack timer. W applies a strong slow to the target. Use W immediately after an auto attack to build Hemorrhage stacks quickly. Slow fleeing enemies with W to keep them in Q and R range. Avoid spending W on minions so you don't miss out on Hemorrhage stacks on champions.
notes.darius-skill-e: Use E right after the enemy uses their mobility ability. You cannot use Flash during E's cast. For a surprise engage, use Flash before E. E's passive grants armor penetration. Give lower priority to penetration-focused items whose effects overlap with E's armor penetration.
notes.darius-phase: Darius is weak at levels 1–2, when he has few abilities available. Darius gets stronger at level 3 with W and Q available, and at level 6 when he gains R. Darius has low item dependence and stays strong through the mid game. Darius is vulnerable in prolonged wars of attrition against ranged poke opponents. Darius falls off in standard late-game teamfights where he struggles to engage. Use your lane advantage during your strong periods to secure gains.
notes.darius-situational-armor: Buy Plated Steelcaps early if the enemy deals mostly physical damage. If the enemy deals mostly physical damage, choose Dead Man's Plate or Randuin's Omen for armor and slows that help you chase.
notes.darius-situational-magic: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buy Mercury's Treads to reduce the time you spend immobilized. If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buy Force of Nature after Mercury's Treads. Roots and stuns can easily disrupt Darius's combo. Prioritize tenacity over magic resistance when roots or stuns interrupt your combo.
notes.darius-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing turns fights around, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Darius relies on extended brawls and can easily lose his edge against sustained enemy healing.
notes.darius-laning: Freeze the wave on your side to lure the enemy into E range when they go for minions. Land E from brush or in narrow terrain to follow up with your combo. After pushing the wave, secure vision against ganks before moving forward.
notes.darius-teamfight: Darius struggles to reach backline damage dealers, putting him at a disadvantage in head-on teamfights. In narrow terrain, pull multiple enemies with E, then hit them together with Q's blade to heal. Getting a kill with R resets its cooldown. Start a kill chain by targeting enemies you can reliably finish with R. If you cannot make use of narrow terrain, apply pressure in a side lane through 1v1s.
notes.vs-darius-e: Poke Darius from outside his E range. Save mobility abilities and Flash to respond to Darius's E. Start a trade when Darius misses E or it is on cooldown.
notes.vs-darius-passive: Darius's attack damage rises sharply when Hemorrhage reaches maximum stacks. Create distance from Darius if Hemorrhage stacks are building up. Hemorrhage stacks expire over time. Stay away from Darius until Hemorrhage stacks expire, then reengage.
notes.vs-darius-q: Darius heals more based on the number of enemies hit by Q's blade. When you see Q being cast, move outside the blade's range to prevent damage and healing. When you see Q being cast, move close to Darius to get hit by the handle and reduce damage and healing. Poke Darius right after he uses Q to clear minions.
notes.vs-darius-r: Darius's R deals true damage. Darius's R damage increases with the target's Hemorrhage stacks. If Darius gets a kill with R, its cooldown resets. If you have several Hemorrhage stacks and your health is dangerously low, move completely out of R range.
notes.vs-darius-phase: Repeat short, hit-and-run trades to deny Q healing and maximum Hemorrhage stacks. Darius relies on W's slow to disengage. Once you gain a favorable position against Darius, keep pressuring him, as he relies on W's slow to escape. Darius is strong in early skirmishes and dives. Watch out for skirmishes and dives when the enemy jungler joins Darius.
notes.diana-combo-basic: In a basic trade, land Q, close in with E, auto attack, then activate W. Using E on a target marked by Moonlight immediately resets E's cooldown. Save the reset second E for an escape instead of using it right away.
notes.diana-combo-allin: For an all-in after level 6, use Q, E, W, an auto attack, R, then the remaining E. Activate W right after closing in with E. W's orbs only burst when they touch an enemy. R pulls enemies in, then deals damage after a short delay. To stack the damage with R, use R first, then land Q and an auto attack before its damage hits.
notes.diana-combo-r-engage: When several enemies are grouped, enter with E, pull them together with R, then use Q and W. R deals more damage the more champions it pulls in. Don't start a fight with R when there is only one opponent.
notes.diana-skill-q: Q travels in a curve, so it catches opponents who try to dodge in a straight line. Diana's combo depends on landing Q. Q has a short cooldown and low mana cost, so keep trying even if it misses. A target hit by Q is briefly revealed.
notes.diana-skill-w: W's orbs only burst when they touch an enemy. W's orbs last briefly and disappear if you activate W too far from an enemy. Bursting the last W orb grants another shield and extends its duration. Stay close to enemies and burst every W orb to increase damage and survivability.
notes.diana-skill-e: E's cooldown resets only when used on a target marked by Moonlight. If you enter with E without a mark, you lose your way back out. If you aren't confident you'll land Q, land it before using E. If the opponent still has crowd control available, land Q before using E.
notes.diana-skill-passive: Every set number of attacks, the passive also slashes nearby enemies for area damage. Right after using an ability, the passive briefly gives a large attack speed boost. Weave auto attacks between abilities to make use of the passive damage.
notes.diana-skill-r: R deals damage while pulling opponents toward Diana. Use R to catch fleeing opponents. Use R to stop an engaging champion who dives onto your allies. Don't use R if you can't withstand the opponents you pull in.
notes.diana-phase: Diana is weakest at levels 1–2, when she has melee range and no combo. At level 3, with Q, W, and E available, Diana can trade damage. Diana's first kill opportunity comes right after learning R at level 6. Diana is strongest in the mid game once she has at least two ability power items. In the late game, Diana's value depends on whether she can kill one target and get out alive.
notes.diana-laning: In mid lane, farm with Q while waiting for level 6. Clear caster minions with W to push the wave. After pushing the lane, look for gank opportunities with your jungler. After level 6, an opponent who stays after getting hit by Q presents a kill opportunity.
notes.diana-jungle: In the jungle, clear camps with W's orbs and the passive's area damage. When ganking, approach from an unwarded brush or behind the opponent to line up Q. If you enter with E during a gank without landing Q, you can't get back out.
notes.diana-teamfight: In teamfights, approach from the side and dive toward the enemy damage dealers. Enter after the enemy's key crowd control has been used. Enter after an ally engages and draws the enemy's attention. Use R when you can pull several enemies together. If you can't pull several enemies together, save the reset E, kill one damage dealer, then get out.
notes.diana-situational-cc: Diana is vulnerable if she is caught by an unavoidable root as she enters. If the enemy has an unavoidable root, get Quicksilver Sash after one core item to remove the root right after you enter.
notes.diana-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents a kill in one combo, reduce their healing with Morellonomicon.
notes.vs-diana-q: Diana's combo starts with Q. Dodge Diana's curving Q by sidestepping instead of moving straight back. If Q hits you and applies Moonlight, move away because E can hit you twice.
notes.vs-diana-w: Diana's W orbs disappear after a few seconds. Start the fight after Diana's W orbs disappear and her shield wears off.
notes.vs-diana-e: If Diana enters with E without landing Q, she has no way back out. If Diana enters with E without landing Q, catch her with a slow or stun. If Q hits you, keep your distance from Diana because E will reset.
notes.vs-diana-r: Diana's R deals more damage the more champions it pulls in. Establish vision to deny Diana an angle to enter from the side. In teamfights, spread out based on the angle Diana can enter from.
notes.vs-diana-early: Diana is weakest before level 6, when she has melee range and no finishing tool. Build a CS lead over Diana before level 6. As Diana reaches level 6, push the lane ahead of time or stay near your turret to weather her first all-in.
notes.drmundo-combo-basic: For a basic trade, slow them with Q, close in, activate W, and land an E-enhanced basic attack. W stores the most damage taken during the brief window right after activation. Activate W just before the enemy's combo hits.
notes.drmundo-combo-w-recast: An enemy champion must be nearby when W explodes to fully restore the stored gray health. Reactivate W yourself when an enemy champion is within its explosion range. If the enemy is retreating, delay reactivating W slightly until they are within its explosion range.
notes.drmundo-combo-e: E empowers your next basic attack, so you need to get within basic attack range. E deals more damage the more health you are missing. A minion killed with E is knocked back and damages enemies in its path. To clear the wave and harass with E at the same time, line it up so the minion is knocked toward your opponent.
notes.drmundo-skill-q: Q deals damage based on the target's current health, so it is strong against full-health targets but weak for finishing them off. Q hits only the first target, so minions can block it. Hitting a minion or monster with Q can also restore health. Before throwing Q, decide whether you want a kill opportunity or healing.
notes.drmundo-skill-passive-bag: The passive ignores the first immobilizing effect, but costs health and drops a canister nearby. Picking up the dropped canister restores health and reduces the passive's cooldown. If an enemy champion steps on the dropped canister, it breaks. When a canister drops, consider picking it up before continuing the trade.
notes.drmundo-skill-passive-timing: While the passive is available, you can ignore the enemy's first immobilizing effect and close in. Without the passive, immobilizing effects will stop you. If the enemy jungler is missing and your passive is down, do not push the lane forward.
notes.drmundo-skill-r: R's immediate heal scales with missing health, so it is stronger when your health is low. As your ultimate gains ranks, R heals more based on the number of nearby enemy champions. To increase the healing, activate R when several enemies surround you instead of while running away. Do not rely only on R's immediate heal; account for its healing over time too.
notes.drmundo-skill-r-engage: R's movement speed boost helps you engage. After joining a teamfight with Teleport, activate R and walk into the enemy backline. Choose when to fight with the difficulty of reaching the enemy backline without R in mind.
notes.drmundo-phase: Dr. Mundo has virtually no early kill pressure. In lane, survive and collect minions. From the mid game, once you have level 6 R and your first core item, your one-on-one sustain rises sharply. In the late game, stacking health items also increases the attack damage E grants.
notes.drmundo-laning-sustain: Healing from Q hits, passive regeneration, and canister pickups lets you stay in lane for a long time. To stay in lane, use canister and Q healing first. Time your recall for after the wave pushes toward the enemy turret. The longer Dr. Mundo stays in lane, the more he scales.
notes.drmundo-laning-ranged: Against a ranged opponent, getting into Q range is itself a losing trade. Against a ranged opponent, farm from behind minions and use Q to heal. Look for a chance to close in on a ranged opponent when your jungler ganks or just after the opponent uses an ability on the wave.
notes.drmundo-teamfight: Dr. Mundo is not a champion who starts teamfights. After enemies engage your allies, activate R and move in, slow an enemy damage dealer with Q, then hit them with E. If enemies attack Dr. Mundo, his healing makes them spend time on him.
notes.drmundo-situational-mr: Against a magic damage composition, buy Spirit Visage earlier. Spirit Visage increases magic resistance and healing received, working with the healing from Q, W, and R.
notes.drmundo-situational-attackspeed: If the enemy marksman relies on attack speed, buy Frozen Heart. Frozen Heart provides armor and slows nearby enemies' attack speed, buying time to reach the backline.
notes.vs-drmundo-passive-bait: Dr. Mundo's passive ignores the first immobilizing effect. Trigger Dr. Mundo's passive with weaker crowd control before using your key engage ability.
notes.vs-drmundo-bag: An enemy champion can break a canister Dr. Mundo drops by stepping on it. When backing off after a trade, step on the canister to deny Dr. Mundo its healing and passive cooldown reduction.
notes.vs-drmundo-q: Dr. Mundo's Q hits only the first target. Keep minions between you and Dr. Mundo to block his Q. Dr. Mundo's Q scales with current health, so it hurts most when your health is full.
notes.vs-drmundo-r-window: Look for a dive or force an objective while Dr. Mundo's R is down. If Dr. Mundo's R is available, look for an advantage in another lane or at an objective.
notes.vs-drmundo-early-mr: If magic damage is your main source of damage, pressure Dr. Mundo hard in the early laning phase while his magic resistance is low. Secure an advantage before Dr. Mundo levels up and gains much more magic resistance.
notes.draven-combo-juggle: Activate Q, auto-attack, then move to the axe landing marker to catch it and land your next auto-attack. Keep two axes going so one is in the air while you catch the other. Keeping two axes going empowers every auto-attack.
notes.draven-combo-w: Use W just before catching an axe. Catching an axe resets W's cooldown. Activate W before catching an axe to keep the movement speed boost going without interruption.
notes.draven-skill-q-uptime: If you stop auto-attacking for a while, you drop all the axes you're holding. If you won't be fighting soon, don't activate Q early. If you expect a fight, activate Q before your first auto-attack.
notes.draven-skill-q-give-up: Give up an axe if its landing spot is dangerous.
notes.draven-skill-q-control: If you throw an axe at a target that's too close, its bounce direction is hard to control. An axe bounces behind the target you attack, so your attack direction determines its next landing spot. To move forward, attack while facing your opponent. To fight while retreating, attack with your back toward the direction you're retreating. Axes don't bounce when you attack a turret, ending your axe rotation.
notes.draven-skill-w-collision: You can move through units during W's movement speed boost. Use W when you need to pass through minions to catch an axe. Early on, save mana for fights instead of using W repeatedly just to move.
notes.draven-skill-e: It's hard to control the direction E knocks an opponent. Save E to interrupt an opponent's dash or a skill they're casting. Use E when you urgently need space to catch an axe.
notes.draven-skill-r: R travels out and then returns. R deals less damage each time it passes through a unit, but the damage reduction resets on its return. If you think your opponent will dodge R, recast it just before it reaches them. R's execute threshold scales with League of Draven stacks.
notes.draven-skill-passive: Catching an axe, killing a minion or monster, or destroying a turret grants passive stacks. Killing a champion grants bonus gold based on your passive stacks. Dying costs you half your passive stacks. When you have many passive stacks, look for a reliable kill participation instead of forcing a solo fight.
notes.draven-laning: Draven is strong at trading damage in lane while holding axes. Move alongside the enemy marksman and auto-attack when they hit a minion. Account for a gank from the enemy jungler when moving forward to catch an axe.
notes.draven-laning-vision: Chasing an axe landing marker can easily narrow your awareness of your surroundings. Check the minimap every few seconds. Keep wards in the brush and river along the path you take to catch axes.
notes.draven-phase: Draven is strongest during the laning phase. Later, safe spots to catch axes become scarce and enemies have more ways to engage, making him relatively weaker. Quickly turn your early gold lead into turrets and objectives.
notes.draven-teamfight: Don't engage first in a teamfight. After your allies initiate and the enemies use their engage abilities, move in and secure space to catch axes. When space is tight, keep just one axe going and auto-attack from a safe position. Save E to interrupt enemies engaging on your allied damage dealers.
notes.draven-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has several forms of immobilizing crowd control, take Cleanse instead of Barrier so you can catch axes. If Cleanse isn't enough for the matchup, buy Mercurial Scimitar between core items.
notes.vs-draven-axe-spot: Aim skillshots at Draven's axe landing spot rather than at Draven. Attacking the axe landing spot forces Draven to get hit by the skill or miss the axe.
notes.vs-draven-disrupt: Draven's damage depends heavily on keeping his axes going. Use knockbacks, slows, and immobilizing crowd control to stop Draven from catching axes.
notes.vs-draven-two-axes: Early on, avoid trading damage with Draven when he has two axes. Move in when Draven has only one axe or none.
notes.vs-draven-safe-farm: If trading is difficult, farm safely without giving Draven a chance to kill you. If farming safely lets the wave push toward you, your jungler gets room to engage on the overextended Draven.
notes.vs-draven-snowball: Draven uses the gold he earns early to build momentum. Even after the laning phase, look for Draven when he's alone.
notes.vs-draven-r: Draven's R returns after passing through, with its damage reduction reset. Even after dodging R once, move completely out of its outbound and return path. If you're low on health, move out of Draven's R range.
notes.ekko-combo-fast: For a quick damage combo, throw Q, then use E to close in as Q returns. If Q hits on the way out and back alongside an E-enhanced basic attack, the third P hit triggers immediately.
notes.ekko-combo-full: For a full combo, place W first, slow with Q, then go in with E to stun, use basic attacks, and use R if needed. W takes time to set up, so place it first in a full combo. If you use W after closing in, the enemy can escape while it sets up.
notes.ekko-combo-e-cast: You can use other abilities while dashing with E. You can throw Q while dashing with E. Place the W sphere, then use E to enter it quickly and set up a stun. Use E to extend the reach of other abilities.
notes.ekko-combo-r: R returns you to where you were a few seconds ago. R deals area damage where you return. Before going in, deliberately set up a place to return to with R. Use R in the middle of a group of enemies to deal damage and get out.
notes.ekko-skill-passive: P triggers on the third hit against the same target. Triggering P on a champion increases your movement speed. Q hitting on the way out and back, plus one basic attack, can complete the third P hit. One ability hit and two basic attacks can complete the third P hit. Build your combos around landing the third P hit. Use the movement speed from P to get out.
notes.ekko-skill-q: Q deals more damage on its return than on its way out. Push the enemy toward a wall to improve your chances of landing both Q hits. Use Q to clear minion waves and jungle monsters. Do not overuse Q; save enough mana for a combo in a fight.
notes.ekko-skill-w: Casting W leaves a signal the enemy can see. W takes time to set up after you cast it. W triggers only when Ekko enters the sphere. Place W ahead of time along the enemy's escape route or approach path. W has a long cooldown, so missing it puts you at a major disadvantage in a fight.
notes.ekko-skill-w-passive: W's passive makes basic attacks against low-health enemies deal bonus damage based on their missing health. When finishing an enemy, confirm the kill with one or two basic attacks even after using all your abilities. If basic attacks can finish the enemy, do not waste R to confirm the kill.
notes.ekko-skill-r: R can be used to escape. R can be used to deal damage. R heals more the more health you lost during the few seconds it rewinds. If you only consider R's healing, it is better to hold out as long as possible before using it. In a teamfight, you may need to use R before crowd control or burst damage stops you.
notes.ekko-phase: Jungle Ekko's early clear is not especially fast. Jungle Ekko has a high gank success rate thanks to W's stun. You can start fights often from level 6, when you learn R. You can start fights often later on, when your ability cooldowns become much shorter. As you build ability power, your damage, W shield, and R healing all grow, making you strongest in the mid to late game.
notes.ekko-laning-gank: When ganking, place W along the enemy's escape route first, slow them with Q, then go in with E. Time W to land as an ally's crowd control takes effect. Placing W where the enemy can see it makes them back away from the lane.
notes.ekko-laning-split: Q's wave clear and E's damage to structures make Ekko strong at split pushing. His high mobility lets him escape enemies who come to catch him. If a teamfight is not an option, pressure a side lane to draw enemies out.
notes.ekko-teamfight: Do not go in first in a teamfight. After the enemy has used their engage abilities and crowd control and your allies have started the fight, jump into the backline. Before going in, set up a safe place to return to with R. In a teamfight, decide where R will return you before deciding where to go in.
notes.ekko-situational-tenacity: Choose Mercury's Treads if the enemy has a lot of hard crowd control. Ekko needs to keep moving; if crowd control holds him in place, he may die before using R.
notes.vs-ekko-ult-ready: Ekko is weakest while R is on cooldown after he uses it. If you can see a trailing afterimage behind Ekko, his R is ready. Do not overcommit to chasing Ekko when his R is ready, even if he looks low on health.
notes.vs-ekko-w: When Ekko casts W, it leaves a signal the enemy can see. Ekko's W takes time to set up. Remember where the W signal appeared and stay out of its area to deny the stun and shield.
notes.vs-ekko-q: Ekko's Q hurts more on its second hit as it returns. Watch the direction of the thrown Q and move out of its return path to reduce the damage you take.
notes.vs-ekko-cc: Ekko is vulnerable to crowd control. Right after Ekko closes in with E, his dash is unavailable. Right after Ekko closes in with E, stun or root him to force out R or stop him.
notes.vs-ekko-chase: If a low-health Ekko has R ready, place a skillshot in advance at the position of his trailing afterimage. When Ekko uses R, he returns to the position of his trailing afterimage. Ekko often chooses to use R to turn a fight around instead of running away.
notes.vs-ekko-bait: With both W and R on cooldown, Ekko is an ordinary melee champion. Bait out Ekko's W and R with a decoy fight, then start the main fight.
notes.elise-skill-form: Elise can transform into Spider Form from level 1. She fights by switching between human form and Spider Form within a single fight. Each time a human form ability hits an enemy, she stores a dormant spiderling. When she transforms into Spider Form, all stored spiderlings are summoned at once. Land a human form ability, then transform into Spider Form.
notes.elise-skill-q-threshold: Human form Q is stronger the more current health the target has. Spider Form Q is stronger the more health the target is missing. Open with human form Q and finish with Spider Form Q. Using Spider Form Q while the enemy still has plenty of health deals less effective damage.
notes.elise-skill-e-cocoon: Human form E, Cocoon, is Elise’s only source of hard crowd control. Cocoon affects only the first target it hits along its path. Throw Cocoon from behind or to the side of the lane so it does not hit the minion wave. Cocoon reveals stealthed enemies, so it can be used to check bushes. Do not waste Cocoon carelessly; it can decide whether a gank succeeds.
notes.elise-skill-e-rappel: Elise cannot be targeted while airborne with Spider Form E, Rappel. Use Rappel to dodge targeted abilities or turret attacks. Rappel can cross a wall by landing on a nearby enemy unit. If there is no enemy unit to land on, Rappel drops Elise where she started. To escape over a wall with Rappel, first check for a minion or jungle monster on the other side.
notes.elise-skill-w-spiderlings: The human form W spiderling walks to the chosen location and explodes. Use human form W after the enemy is caught or their escape direction is clear. Spider Form W increases the attack speed of both Elise and her spiderlings. Spiderlings attack the target Elise bites with Spider Form Q.
notes.elise-skill-mana: Spider Form abilities cost no mana. When mana is low, save human form abilities and clear camps in Spider Form. Spider Form basic attacks deal bonus magic damage and heal Elise.
notes.elise-combo-gank: For a gank, land human form E, then use W, human form Q, transform, use Spider Form Q, and basic attack. Confirm that Cocoon lands before continuing the rest of the gank combo. Transforming before using Cocoon costs you the hard crowd control needed for a gank. Landing all human form abilities before transforming lets you summon and send in the maximum number of spiderlings.
notes.elise-combo-escape: During a turret dive or countergank, use Rappel to dodge targeted abilities and turret attacks as Elise rises. After landing on a unit across a wall with Rappel, return to human form to get into range. You can use Spider Form Q to reach a fleeing enemy, then escape with Rappel. If Rappel is on cooldown, do not attempt a Spider Form Q engage that relies on it to escape.
notes.elise-laning-clear: Clear jungle camps mainly in Spider Form. Healing from Spider Form basic attacks reduces health lost while clearing the jungle. When entering a camp, build up spiderlings with human form abilities, then transform immediately to clear it. Health-based damage has a cap against monsters. Do not spend too long fighting a large monster alone.
notes.elise-laning-gankpath: After clearing the first few camps, shift to ganks and invades. Look for ganks as soon as you learn Cocoon. Gank lanes pulled toward your side, where the enemy has pushed forward, first.
notes.elise-phase: Elise is strong from the time she learns Cocoon through the mid game. Elise’s ability to transform from level 1 gives her high damage for her level. A single early gank can be especially valuable. Late in the game, health-based damage matters less, and her teamfight contribution falls because Cocoon is her only hard crowd control. Turn early leads into objectives and turrets to end the game quickly.
notes.elise-teamfight: In teamfights, look for an angle to land Cocoon instead of standing on the front line. Before a fight, stay back in human form and catch a key enemy with Cocoon. After an ally engages, close in with Spider Form and finish off a weakened target. Go in after an ally lands area crowd control or a key enemy loses health. Fight where there is a nearby unit you can land on with Rappel.
notes.elise-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Morellonomicon adds healing reduction while maintaining magic damage. Buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.elise-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has burst engage, buy Zhonya’s Hourglass early. Elise is exposed to counterattacks immediately after throwing Cocoon. Use Zhonya’s Hourglass to avoid a counterattack right after throwing Cocoon.
notes.vs-elise-form: Elise’s human form Q hits hard when its target is at full health. When Elise transforms into Spider Form, use mobility and defensive abilities.
notes.vs-elise-cocoon: Elise’s gank depends on landing human form Cocoon. The first minion or jungle monster Cocoon hits along its path blocks it. In lane, stand behind your minion wave to avoid Cocoon. When moving near the jungle, stay away from walls and move through areas with clear vision.
notes.vs-elise-rappel: If there are no nearby enemy units, Rappel brings Elise back down where she rose. When chasing Elise, clear nearby minions and jungle monsters to limit how far she can escape with Rappel. Do not use targeted abilities while Elise is airborne with Rappel. Aim skillshots at Elise’s Rappel landing spot in advance.
notes.vs-elise-cooldown: Rappel has a long cooldown, leaving Elise with few escape options right after she uses it. Attack Elise after confirming that both Rappel and Cocoon are on cooldown.
notes.vs-elise-phase: Elise is a jungler who tries to end games early with leads from early ganks. Avoid giving Elise kills early and draw out the game. Keep plenty of vision early in lane to prepare for Elise’s ganks. Do not push the lane too far when the enemy jungler’s location is unknown.
notes.evelynn-combo-gank: For a gank, cast W from outside vision, then use Q, empowered E, Q, and R in that order once the mark is ready. Trigger the W mark with Q to charm the target. Q has longer range than E. Use empowered E after the charm holds the target in place.
notes.evelynn-combo-execute: R deals much more damage to targets below a certain health threshold. Use Q and E to bring the target into execute range, then finish with R. After casting R, Evelynn retreats backward.
notes.evelynn-skill-passive: Demon Shade activates after Evelynn goes a while without basic attacking or using abilities. Demon Shade grants camouflage starting at level 6. Taking damage from an enemy champion or turret briefly disables Demon Shade. While Evelynn is camouflaged, a yellow eye appears above an enemy champion who comes close. If that enemy champion comes closer, Evelynn is revealed. When the yellow eye appears, adjust your distance from the enemy. When low on health, recover through Demon Shade in a brush before using a potion.
notes.evelynn-skill-q: The first Q hit leaves a mark that increases the damage of subsequent attacks against the same target. Recast Q to fire several more spikes. The spikes from Q recasts target the nearest enemy. To hit a champion among minions, move beside the minion wave to get a clear angle for Q.
notes.evelynn-skill-w: Once the W mark is ready, it adds a charm and reduces magic resistance. Triggering the W mark early applies only a slow. Listen for the heart filling up, then trigger the W mark. Cast W before approaching to give the mark time to become ready.
notes.evelynn-skill-e: Use E when it is empowered. Empowered E dashes to the target and hits every enemy along its path. Unempowered E has short range and does not dash. When Demon Shade activates, E's cooldown resets and E becomes empowered again. Step out briefly between fights to activate Demon Shade and regain E. If the charm wears off, use Q instead of chasing the target just to land empowered E.
notes.evelynn-skill-r: Evelynn cannot be targeted while casting R. Do not use R, which sends Evelynn backward, to engage. Using R briefly prevents Demon Shade from activating again.
notes.evelynn-laning-clear: At jungle camps, cast W on the large monster first and trigger it once the mark is ready. W charms monsters for longer. W deals more bonus damage to monsters. Deal damage with Q while clearing camps. At camps where multiple monsters line up, use empowered E to pass through them.
notes.evelynn-laning-path: Before level 6, clear both sides of the jungle to level up. After level 6, approach through an unwarded river or from behind a lane. Camouflage ends where Evelynn enters combat. Clear wards along your gank path first.
notes.evelynn-laning-target: Gank lanes pushed toward the enemy turret. In a pushed lane, the enemy has farther to retreat, giving the W mark time to become ready. Against enemies with several mobility abilities, choose a lane where an ally can land crowd control first.
notes.evelynn-phase: Evelynn's ganks are weak before level 6 because she lacks camouflage and struggles to give W time to become ready. After level 6, Evelynn gets far more kill involvement by approaching while camouflaged and using her charm. After level 6, Evelynn gets ahead through kills more than farming.
notes.evelynn-teamfight: Do not stand at the front in teamfights. Activate Demon Shade, flank or circle behind, and position yourself behind the enemy backline damage dealers. Go in when the enemy's key crowd control has been used on your frontline. Angle empowered E to pass through a grouped enemy team.
notes.evelynn-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps taking targets out of execute range, reduce their healing with Morellonomicon. Buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.evelynn-situational-zhonya: Buy Zhonya's Hourglass sooner if an enemy assassin immediately counterattacks when you engage. Use R's untargetability and Zhonya's Hourglass at separate times.
notes.vs-evelynn-ward: Buy Control Wards when facing Evelynn. A regular ward beside your jungle camp also spots Evelynn when she starts a fight there. Place vision where Evelynn starts fights as well as along her gank paths.
notes.vs-evelynn-early: Before level 6, Evelynn lacks camouflage and needs time for W to become ready, making it hard for her to start fights herself. Evelynn is especially vulnerable to early jungle invades. If you can win the fight, take Evelynn's jungle camps early to delay her level 6.
notes.vs-evelynn-w-tell: If you get a W mark, Evelynn is nearby preparing to charm you. Back away before the W mark is ready. When you see a W mark, immediately alert your team with a minimap ping and chat. While marked, use area abilities ahead of time on Evelynn's likely approach path.
notes.vs-evelynn-e: Empowered E after the charm accounts for most of the damage. Position yourself to dodge before the charm lands. Avoid narrow paths along walls and leave room to retreat within your team's vision.
notes.vs-evelynn-r: Evelynn's R deals much more damage to targets below a certain health threshold. If your health is in execute range, do not stay somewhere without vision. Do not use targeted abilities on Evelynn while she casts R.
notes.vs-evelynn-teamfight: Evelynn targets backline damage dealers in teamfights. Backline damage dealers should stay inside areas their team can see. Save immobilizing crowd control for Evelynn.
notes.ezreal-skill-q-engine: Landing Q reduces the cooldown of all abilities. Ezreal relies on landing Q to use E again quickly. Hold Q if you don't have an angle to land it.
notes.ezreal-skill-q-onhit: Q applies on-hit effects. Against enemies who are hard to approach, use Q to apply on-hit effects from outside basic attack range.
notes.ezreal-skill-w-order: W attaches an orb to a target that you can detonate with a follow-up attack. Detonating the W orb with an ability refunds the mana spent on that ability. To manage mana, land W and detonate the orb with Q.
notes.ezreal-skill-w-objective: W attaches to structures and large jungle monsters as well as champions. When attacking a turret or objective, attach W and detonate it with a basic attack or Q. Save W at an objective and use it as soon as a fight starts.
notes.ezreal-skill-e: E is Ezreal's only escape. E has a long cooldown. Use E aggressively only after the enemy has used all their engage abilities.
notes.ezreal-skill-e-lineup: Use E to move a short distance sideways and open a Q angle blocked by minions. The homing bolt fired just after E lands prioritizes targets with a W orb attached. Attach W before using E to direct its bolt at the target you want.
notes.ezreal-skill-r: R travels in a straight line, piercing and hitting multiple minion waves or jungle monsters. R deals reduced damage to minions and regular monsters. Use R to finish off a fleeing enemy you can see from long range. Before a teamfight starts, use R where the enemies are grouped.
notes.ezreal-combo-poke: When poking, use W, then Q, then a basic attack. Detonating the W orb with Q deals damage from both abilities. Passive stacks increase attack speed, making follow-up basic attacks faster. Use W to poke when the enemy is away from the minion wave.
notes.ezreal-combo-allin: When going all-in, use W, a basic attack, Q, E to adjust your angle, then another basic attack. Finish with R if needed. During an all-in, use E to move into position to cut off the enemy's escape route. Before going all-in, judge whether Q's cooldown reduction will let you use a second Q.
