notes.ezreal-phase-early: Ezreal is most vulnerable at levels 1–2. At levels 1–2, survive by last-hitting minions with Q. At levels 1–2, keep a safe distance instead of looking for a kill. Even after learning R at level 6, avoid stepping forward.
notes.ezreal-phase-scaling: Ezreal gains an advantage through CS and accumulated damage rather than early kills. Ezreal comes into his own from mid game onward, once he has completed two core items. Before completing two core items, focus on minimizing losses.
notes.ezreal-laning: Last-hitting minions with Q pushes the wave. If you don't know where the enemy jungler is, farm less with Q and use basic attacks to let the lane push toward you. If the enemy jungler appears on the other side of the map, push the lane with Q, then recall or establish vision.
notes.ezreal-laning-mana: Ezreal's ability to stay in lane depends on mana management. To keep poking, attach W and detonate it with an ability to recover mana. Judge when to recall by your remaining mana rather than your health.
notes.ezreal-teamfight: In teamfights, stay at the back and keep using Q. While your frontline holds the enemy in place, build up damage with Q and W from the edge of your range. Save E so you can escape after an enemy diver reaches you.
notes.ezreal-situational-antiheal: Buy Executioner's Calling early to apply Grievous Wounds from afar with Q against enemies who sustain through healing. Upgrade Executioner's Calling to Mortal Reminder to maintain Grievous Wounds throughout teamfights.
notes.vs-ezreal-minions: Ezreal's damage depends on landing skillshots. Minions between you and Ezreal block his Q and W. When facing Ezreal, move within the minion wave. Avoid facing Ezreal in open ground without minions.
notes.vs-ezreal-fragile: When fighting Ezreal, establish vision and find an approach angle to close the distance. Avoid trading poke with Ezreal from afar.
notes.vs-ezreal-e: Look for a chance to kill Ezreal right after he uses E. Force Ezreal to use E with a short engage, then go all-in. If Ezreal keeps landing Q, E's cooldown drops quickly.
notes.vs-ezreal-move-speed: If you have a slow or a movement speed boost, chase Ezreal after he uses E. When ganking Ezreal, approach from an angle that blocks his escape route first.
notes.vs-ezreal-w: Ezreal's basic attacks or abilities deal extra damage when they hit a target with a W orb attached. If a W orb attaches to you, briefly move out of Ezreal's range.
notes.vs-ezreal-r: If you flee at low health along a visible straight path, R can finish you off. When low on health, turn along the terrain as you retreat to avoid R's straight path. Don't retreat in a straight line with your allies, or R may hit you together.
notes.fiddle-skill-passive-scarecrow: The passive replaces trinkets with effigies. Effigies are used for scouting. When revealed, an effigy briefly mimics Fiddlesticks. From level 6, effigies reveal nearby wards. Just before a teamfight or objective, use an effigy to check vision at the entry point, then choose where to cast R. Fiddlesticks mimics an effigy when standing still for a short time. Stand still in a brush and wait to ambush passing enemies.
notes.fiddle-skill-q: Casting Q directly fears the target and deals damage based on their current health. Casting Q on a target recently feared by Fiddlesticks deals increased damage. After entering with an automatic fear, use Q to finish the target.
notes.fiddle-skill-w: Completing W's channel without interruption greatly reduces its remaining cooldown. Do not start W if its channel is likely to be interrupted. W's bonus damage based on missing health lands at the end of its duration. Lower the enemy's health before using W.
notes.fiddle-skill-e: E silences only enemies in the center of its area. Hit with the center of E to interrupt an enemy's channel or cast. To prevent an escape, aim for E's wide slow area. Use E to start an attack from outside enemy vision.
notes.fiddle-skill-r: R's channel is visible before the blink follows. Cast R from outside enemy vision, such as behind a wall or in a brush. Choose a narrow area where enemies will have trouble spreading out as R's landing spot.
notes.fiddle-combo-gank: When ganking, save Q until just after the enemy uses a mobility ability. When ganking, save Q to finish the target.
notes.fiddle-combo-ult: In a teamfight, enter with R, hit E as you land, and complete W. If someone can counterattack right after R lands, use Q on that target. During the teamfight combo, keep W's channel from being interrupted.
notes.fiddle-laning-clear: At jungle camps, group the monsters with E, then complete W. Completing W on monsters increases its damage and healing. Completing W without interruption reduces its remaining cooldown, making it easier to move on to the next camp. Jungle routes where W gets interrupted hurt clear speed and health management.
notes.fiddle-laning-gank-path: When ganking, approach by circling through the brush behind the lane or a blind spot near the river. If a lane has a control ward, ask an ally to clear the vision. If you must avoid a lane with a control ward, gank another lane.
notes.fiddle-laning-objective: Before an objective, use an effigy to check enemy vision and positions, then take a spot in a brush.
notes.fiddle-phase: From mid game, once R and core ability power items are ready, a single engage can turn a teamfight around. In late game, Fiddlesticks still initiates fights over objectives with R. Fiddlesticks is vulnerable if enemies spread out after the engage.
notes.fiddle-teamfight: Cast R after an ally's immobilizing effect lands. Cast R after the enemy uses a key counter ability. Choose an R landing spot where several enemies are grouped and have no room to retreat. W and R's channels can be interrupted by immobilizing effects.
notes.fiddle-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has strong burst physical damage, get Zhonya's Hourglass early to survive the focus fire right after engaging with R.
notes.fiddle-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, choose Morellonomicon to keep Grievous Wounds applied through W and R's damage over time.
notes.vs-fiddle-r: Fiddlesticks' R channel is visible before the blink follows. If you see R being cast, interrupt it with an immobilizing effect or a slow. If you cannot interrupt R, move out of its range and wait out its duration.
notes.vs-fiddle-ambush: If Fiddlesticks has been out of sight for a while, watch for an R ambush from a brush. Place control wards in brushes and along entry paths near objectives. Do not enter an unwarded narrow passage grouped together.
notes.vs-fiddle-q: During jungle gank windows, keep vision in the brush behind the lane. Do not walk past a motionless effigy until you confirm whether it is the real Fiddlesticks.
notes.vs-fiddle-w: If Fiddlesticks completes W without interruption, its remaining cooldown is greatly reduced. If Fiddlesticks completes W without interruption, it heals a lot. When Fiddlesticks starts channeling W, interrupt it with crowd control you have saved.
notes.vs-fiddle-cluster: Fiddlesticks' W, E, and R can hit several enemies at once. Spread out from your allies before Fiddlesticks engages. Do not face off against Fiddlesticks in narrow terrain. Fiddlesticks' E silences only enemies in the center of its area. Do not stand in the middle of your team when facing Fiddlesticks.
notes.vs-fiddle-punish: Fiddlesticks is fragile and has no mobility abilities. Counterattack as soon as Fiddlesticks lands with R. Save an instant immobilizing ability to counter R. Save a spell defense tool to counter R. Focus your damage on Fiddlesticks' R landing spot.
notes.fiora-combo-basic: For short trades, Q toward a vital → auto → E. E empowers the next two basic attacks. E's second basic attack is a guaranteed critical strike. When a new vital appears while E is active, hit it with the second empowered auto attack.
notes.fiora-combo-vital-angle: If a vital appears on the opponent's back or side, use Q to dash in that direction and hit it. Hit front-facing vitals with auto attacks and E, and save Q to chase or disengage. Hitting a vital grants movement speed, making it easier to move toward the next vital. Look for an angle to hit two vitals in succession during a single fight.
notes.fiora-skill-vital: Hitting a passive vital deals true damage based on the opponent's maximum health. Hitting a passive vital restores health. Vitals reappear in a different position after a set time or when hit. If the current vital is at a difficult angle to hit, wait for the next one instead of forcing an engage. The true damage from vitals is not reduced by the opponent stacking armor.
notes.fiora-skill-q: Q dashes in the chosen direction and attacks the nearest enemy. Q prioritizes hitting a vital if one is within its hit area. Hitting an enemy with Q greatly reduces its cooldown. Using Q without hitting anything does not reduce its cooldown. When using Q to move, make sure to hit something, even a minion or ward.
notes.fiora-skill-riposte: W blocks all attacks during its brief cast time. W blocks immobilizing effects during its brief cast time. If W blocks an immobilizing effect, its counterthrust stuns instead of slowing. Save W until the opponent has to use immobilizing crowd control. Simply having W available discourages the opponent from using abilities.
notes.fiora-skill-e: E increases attack speed. E's first empowered auto slows the opponent. E's second empowered auto is a guaranteed critical strike. Hit a vital with E's second empowered auto attack. Use E after setting up a situation where you can stay close enough to land both empowered autos.
notes.fiora-phase: Fiora gets stronger in 1v1s as she gains items. Avoid reckless fights early, looking ahead to 1v1s after scaling. Fiora is weak in large teamfights. Fiora excels at gaining advantages through split pushing.
notes.fiora-situational-antiheal: Fiora fights by hitting vitals one after another, gradually wearing down her opponent's health. Fiora struggles to duel opponents who use sustained healing to recover the damage between vital hits.
notes.fiora-laning: After hitting a vital, use the increased movement speed to create distance. Trade to bait out the opponent's mobility ability first and gain an advantage in mobility usage.
notes.fiora-laning-vs-physical: If the opponent has strong physical damage trades, focus on minimizing early losses rather than winning lane. In unfavorable physical damage trading matchups, stay in experience range even if you have to give up some minions. In unfavorable physical damage trading matchups, let the wave come toward your turret. Starting in the mid game, once your items come together, force 1v1s in a side lane. Once Fiora scales, she can turn around matchups that were unfavorable early.
notes.fiora-teamfight: Choose side lane pressure over large fights. R reveals four vitals on the target. Use R in 1v1s or skirmishes where it provides the most value.
notes.fiora-teamfight-ult: R's vitals deal true damage based on the opponent's maximum health. Hitting all four R vitals or killing the target heals you and nearby allies.
notes.vs-fiora-riposte: When facing Fiora, bait out W first. Fiora's W blocks all incoming attacks and immobilizing effects during its cast. If Fiora blocks an immobilizing effect with W, her counterthrust stuns. Avoid using immobilizing abilities such as roots or stuns while Fiora's W is available. Sidestep when using key abilities to avoid getting hit by Fiora's W.
notes.vs-fiora-riposte-aatrox: Fiora will try to block Aatrox's third Q cast or W pull with W. Use Aatrox's first and second Q casts to bait out Fiora's W. After baiting out Fiora's W, use Aatrox's third Q cast and W. Save Aatrox's W while Fiora's W is available.
notes.vs-fiora-vital: The vital marked on your body signals the direction Fiora intends to attack from. Position on the opposite side from the marked vital to narrow Fiora's approach angles. Counterattack the moment Fiora dashes toward the vital. Do not overcommit to chasing Fiora after a short trade.
notes.vs-fiora-ult: When Fiora uses R, hug a wall. Covering one vital with a wall can prevent Fiora from hitting all four R vitals. If Fiora hits all four R vitals, she and her nearby allies heal.
notes.vs-fiora-late: Fiora is strong in late-game 1v1s. In the late game, take down Fiora in a side lane with at least two players instead of facing her alone. In the late game, force teamfights instead of dueling Fiora in a side lane. The true damage from vitals is not reduced by stacking armor.
notes.fizz-combo-ult: Land R first, then use Q to close in as the shark knocks the target up and hit them with a W empowered attack. Use the time between the fish attaching and the shark appearing to close the gap. In an assassination combo that starts with R, save E to get out.
notes.fizz-combo-e-entry: Close in with E, slow the target with the landing, then use a W empowered attack followed by Q. If the enemy still has key abilities or you have no allied support, they can counterattack after you engage with E.
notes.fizz-combo-q-entry: Use Q to dash through and close in, land a W empowered attack, then dodge the counterattack with E. You are not untargetable during the Q dash, so you can be hit. Engage with Q after the enemy has used their skillshots and crowd control.
notes.fizz-skill-passive: Your passive lets you move through units. In lane, walk between minions and poke with W. Your passive reduces damage taken from every attack by a fixed amount.
notes.fizz-skill-q: Q is a dash that passes through its target and can target enemy minions. Using Q on an enemy minion to dodge a skillshot or escape a gank lets you save E. You can use Q on an enemy minion to get closer to your opponent. Q applies on-hit effects, so it can trigger items.
notes.fizz-skill-w: A W empowered attack deals magic damage and applies a bleed. If a W empowered attack kills the target, it refunds mana and greatly reduces W's cooldown. Last-hit minions with W to preserve mana and use your abilities more often. If you miss a last hit with W, its full cooldown applies.
notes.fizz-skill-e: E's untargetability can dodge skillshots and enemy ultimates. Early on, E costs so much mana and has such a long cooldown that you can only use it once or twice in lane. Save E and use it cautiously in the early laning phase. Avoid putting yourself in a position where E is your only escape.
notes.fizz-skill-e-recast: Pressing E again while untargetable makes you leap forward and ends the effect early. Recasting E narrows its area of effect and removes the slow. Recast E when you need to increase or close the distance. If you need to dodge enemy crowd control or a delayed explosion, do not recast E; use the full untargetable duration.
notes.fizz-skill-r: Even if R misses, an enemy who moves to dodge the shark can lose time and leave their formation split. Throw R where the enemy is going, rather than where they are standing. To scatter the enemy formation, throw R into a clustered group.
notes.fizz-phase: Fizz can threaten kills starting at level 2 or 3. If you close in aggressively the moment you level up before your opponent, you can force their Flash or kill them. Fizz reaches his full burst potential when level 6 R coincides with his first core item. He remains strong at assassinating a single target in the late game. With effectively only one way to engage, he struggles when enemies group up.
notes.fizz-laning-trade: Fizz has no built-in healing, so even a winning trade can leave him low on health.
notes.fizz-laning-roam: Fizz is a melee mage who does not rely on attack speed, so his tower pressure is weak. If you push your opponent out of lane, spend the time joining fights in a side lane or the jungle. Before roaming, push the wave toward the enemy tower.
notes.fizz-teamfight: In teamfights, use R from the flank to target one enemy in the backline. Engage when the enemy has used their targeted crowd control and your E is available. Before engaging in a teamfight, do not use E to poke or move around. If your assassination target is hiding behind their team, give up the engage and use R to scatter their formation.
notes.fizz-situational-antiheal: If your assassination target has healing, it may offset Fizz's burst and prevent the kill. Against an assassination target with healing, buy the inexpensive Oblivion Orb early; it suits Fizz's magic damage. When you can afford to delay a core item, upgrade Oblivion Orb to Morellonomicon. Executioner's Calling only gives attack damage, which does not suit Fizz's scaling.
notes.vs-fizz-e-cooldown: The moment Fizz's E goes on cooldown is a clear window to counterattack. Save crowd control and burst damage for the moment Fizz uses E. Early on, Fizz's mana limits him to using E only once or twice in lane.
notes.vs-fizz-entry-read: When Fizz comes in with E, he has to land an auto attack and then wait for W's bleed to trigger. To engage with Q, Fizz has to walk into its range. Counterattack right after Fizz applies W.
notes.vs-fizz-w-lasthit: If Fizz misses a last hit with a W empowered attack, W goes on its full cooldown. Trade with Fizz the moment he misses a last hit with W.
notes.vs-fizz-group: Stay close to your allies, make Fizz use E first, then focus him down. Do not walk alone or chase Fizz alone.
notes.vs-fizz-r: If R's fish attaches to you, move away from your allies before the shark erupts. Fizz uses Q to engage as the shark knocks his target up. Place damage or crowd control in Fizz's path as he engages with Q to force him to use E.
notes.galio-combo-qe: For a basic trade, place Q, then use E to knock the enemy into it. Q's vortex forms only where the two gusts overlap. Aim Q where E will knock the enemy.
notes.galio-combo-e-windup: E steps back before dashing forward, giving it more range than it appears to have. You can dodge enemy skillshots while E steps back. E's dash stops when it hits terrain.
notes.galio-combo-w-charge: You can press W again at any point during the charge to release it. The longer you charge W, the longer its taunt lasts. Charging W reduces incoming damage but slows Galio. Charge W as the enemy's combo comes in to reduce its damage, then counter with a taunt.
notes.galio-combo-full: For a full combo, knock the enemy up with E, briefly charge W to taunt them, then place Q on that spot. Start charging W before E's knockup ends so the enemy cannot walk away.
notes.galio-skill-r-shield: R grants its shield to an ally when cast, before Galio arrives. Starting R as soon as an ally is caught helps them survive while Galio flies in. Galio cannot move from his position while casting R.
notes.galio-skill-r-timing: R knocks up all enemies around its landing point. R's cast is visible to enemies, giving them time to spread out. Use R where an ally's crowd control is holding the enemy in place.
notes.galio-skill-w-passive: W's passive grants a shield after Galio has gone a while without taking damage. In lane, one hit of poke removes W's shield. Step forward only while W's shield is up. If it breaks, back off and wait for it to recharge.
notes.galio-skill-passive: Hitting a champion with an ability reduces P's cooldown each time. After landing an ability, use one empowered basic attack. P's damage scales with magic resistance.
notes.galio-phase: Levels 1–2 are Galio's weakest: his mana costs are high and he does not have E yet. Galio can start trading at level 3, when he learns E. Galio becomes much more valuable at level 6, when he can start using R to help other lanes. Later on, focus on engaging and crowd control rather than damage, and survive with magic resistance.
notes.galio-laning: Hit both the wave and the enemy with Q to manage mana. As a melee champion, Galio is easy for ranged opponents to poke. Against ranged opponents, save E to disengage instead of using it to engage first. Close in right after the enemy uses their main ability on minions, then follow up with W's taunt.
notes.galio-laning-roam: Push the wave into the enemy tower, then use R to help another lane. Calculate whether Teleport can make up for the farm lost while using R to help another lane.
notes.galio-teamfight: In teamfights, arrive with R to knock enemies up, then use W's taunt to pull their key threats away from your allies. Taunt the champion positioned to kill an ally right now.
notes.galio-teamfight-zone: Place Q's vortex in a narrow passage to cut off the way in. Use E to block the direction the enemy damage dealer will escape. Stagger your taunt and knockup to keep enemies locked down.
notes.galio-situational-mr: If the enemy's main damage is magic, build Spectre's Cowl or Spirit Visage earlier. P's damage, W's damage reduction, and R's damage all scale with magic resistance.
notes.vs-galio-w: Galio takes much less damage while charging W. When you see Galio charging W, hold your damage and walk out of taunt range. The longer Galio charges W, the longer its taunt lasts.
notes.vs-galio-q: Q's vortex forms only where the two gusts overlap. Avoid the point where Q's gusts overlap to avoid its damage over time. Q's damage over time scales with maximum health, so champions with more health take more damage.
notes.vs-galio-r: Galio's R has a visible cast animation, and its landing area is marked in advance. When you see R's marker, immediately walk out of its area. While Galio's R is ready, do not start a skirmish with his team in another lane.
notes.vs-galio-e: Galio's E stops when it hits terrain. Stand near a wall to shorten the distance Galio can close with E. Dodge when you see E's initial step back.
notes.vs-galio-lane: Galio is melee, so he is vulnerable to ranged poke, and his mana costs are high. Make Galio use his abilities to clear the wave. When Galio is low on mana, push the lane to leave him less room to use R to help another lane.
notes.vs-galio-armor: Building magic resistance increases both Galio's damage and defense. Include physical damage when attacking Galio. Pressure Galio with physical damage early, when his armor is low.
notes.gangplank-combo-barrel-chain: Powder Kegs with overlapping blast radii explode in a chain. Detonate the front Powder Keg with Q to set off the one behind it and extend your reach. A chain explosion does not damage the same target multiple times. Use a Powder Keg chain to extend your reach and keep the slow on your target.
notes.gangplank-combo-basic-trade: Place a Powder Keg behind or beside your opponent in advance, detonate it with Q, then follow up with Q. Place a Powder Keg behind or beside your opponent in advance, detonate it with Q, then follow up with an auto attack. To land a melee auto attack, approach after the Powder Keg's slow takes effect.
notes.gangplank-combo-barrel-prime: A Powder Keg cannot be detonated with one Q immediately after placement. A Powder Keg loses health over time. Place a Powder Keg where you expect to fight and let it age until one hit can detonate it. Do not use Q on a Powder Keg that has not aged enough.
notes.gangplank-skill-passive: Trial by Fire's burn applies only to melee basic attacks, not Q. Destroying a Powder Keg resets Trial by Fire's cooldown and grants movement speed. Detonate Powder Kegs in succession to chase or disengage.
notes.gangplank-skill-q: Q applies on-hit effects and can critically strike. Use Q to last-hit from range or harass your opponent. Check your remaining mana before deciding whether to use Q for poke or last hits.
notes.gangplank-skill-w: W restores health and removes crowd control effects. Use W right after a key enemy crowd control effect lands to break their combo. W cannot answer crowd control applied after you use it.
notes.gangplank-skill-r-global: R can strike anywhere on the map. Use R in fights in other lanes. Watch the minimap for low-health enemies and finish them with R. Cast R ahead of a fleeing enemy's expected path to cut them off.
notes.gangplank-skill-r-upgrade: Spend the Silver Serpents earned with Q to upgrade R at the shop. Depending on the R upgrade, it adds more bombardments or true damage and a strong slow. Recall before an expected teamfight to update your R upgrade.
notes.gangplank-phase: At levels 1–2, Gangplank is weak because Powder Kegs have little time to age and each keg deals little damage. Gangplank grows stronger in the mid game, when his Powder Keg combo starts landing all at once. From level 6, R lets Gangplank influence the entire map. Powder Keg range and bombardment keep Gangplank strong in the late game. Get through Gangplank's weak early game while avoiding bad trades.
notes.gangplank-laning-farm: Use Q to last-hit safely and hold the lane without pushing. In an unfavorable matchup, farm with Q in front of your turret.
notes.gangplank-laning-barrel-zone: Place Powder Kegs at brush entrances or river paths to block jungle entry routes. You can spot an opponent's position when they move to destroy a Powder Keg. A Powder Keg destroyed by an enemy disappears without exploding.
notes.gangplank-laning-mana: Overusing Powder Kegs and Q together drains mana quickly. Decide in advance how many Powder Kegs to use in a trade. Save Powder Kegs you will not use in a trade for farming. If an opponent closes in while you are out of mana, you lose both your means of fighting back and escaping.
notes.gangplank-teamfight: Do not stand at the front in teamfights. Place a Powder Keg beside the enemy team in advance, then detonate it with Q from behind to maintain an area slow.
notes.gangplank-teamfight-entry: Move in yourself after the opponent has used their key targeted abilities. W can clear crowd control only once, so overlapping crowd control can easily kill you. If the opening to move in is uncertain, place a Powder Keg and back away.
notes.vs-gangplank-barrel: A Powder Keg destroyed by an enemy disappears without exploding. Destroy nearby Powder Kegs yourself from outside their blast radius. The older a Powder Keg is, the greater the risk that one hit will detonate it.
notes.vs-gangplank-timing: Gangplank cannot properly execute his Powder Keg combo before the kegs have aged. Close in and trade right after Gangplank places a Powder Keg. Back away if an aged Powder Keg is nearby.
notes.vs-gangplank-w: W removes all crowd control effects and heals based on missing health. Save the key crowd control needed to secure a kill until after Gangplank uses W. If the fight looks likely to drag on, get Executioner's Calling or Morellonomicon for Grievous Wounds.
notes.vs-gangplank-ult: Do not cross a wide area alone when low on health. Time objective fights around whether Gangplank has used R.
notes.garen-combo-basic: For a basic trade, silence with a Q-empowered auto attack, then use E. Q's movement speed boost helps you close in on your opponent. Deal damage with E while Q's silence prevents your opponent from retaliating with abilities.
notes.garen-combo-ult: To finish your opponent, use a Q-empowered auto attack, then E, recast E to end it early, and use R. R deals true damage proportional to your opponent's missing health. If your opponent shows no sign of escaping, let E deal its full damage before using R. If your opponent shows signs of escaping, recast E to stop it and immediately use R.
notes.garen-skill-q: Q removes all slows affecting Garen. Garen has no mobility ability, so he relies on Q to chase. Use Q right after your opponent slows you to remove the slow. Q's empowered auto attack remains available briefly after activation. You can activate Q outside attack range, then approach and silence with the empowered auto attack.
notes.garen-skill-w: W's shield and tenacity apply only for a very brief moment right after casting. W's damage reduction lasts longer than its shield and tenacity. Time W for the moment an enemy ability comes at you. W's passive permanently increases armor and magic resistance whenever you kill a unit. Secure last hits in lane to build up W's defenses.
notes.garen-skill-e: E hits more times during its spin with higher attack speed. E's damage can critically strike. To increase E's total damage, mix in attack speed and critical strike chance instead of building only attack damage. E reduces the armor of champions it hits multiple times. To support allied physical damage dealers, let E spin for its full duration to reduce enemy armor. E deals bonus damage to the nearest enemy. During trades, position so only the enemy champion is within E's range.
notes.garen-skill-passive: P restores health after some time without being hit by a champion. Minion attacks do not interrupt P's healing. After a trade, briefly retreat into a brush or behind a turret to heal with P. P's healing lets Garen hold his lane even in unfavorable matchups.
notes.garen-phase: Garen's base health and P healing make him strong in early melee trades. Garen peaks in the mid game when Q's duration increases and R reaches rank 2. In the late game, as enemies become more durable, Garen relies on R's execute more than E's damage. Use lane pressure and split pushing to secure your advantage in the mid game.
notes.garen-situational-onhit: E's spin damage does not apply on-hit effects. Items whose value centers on on-hit effects, such as Blade of the Ruined King, are less efficient because those effects do not apply to E. For the same cost, choose attack speed and critical strike items that work well with E.
notes.garen-situational-boots-slow: If the enemy team has many slows, choose Boots of Swiftness over Berserker's Greaves to close in more easily while Q is on cooldown. You cannot use Q to remove slows while it is on cooldown.
notes.garen-situational-mr: If enemy magic damage is a threat, swap your boots for Mercury's Treads, which provide magic resistance and tenacity. Garen is vulnerable to being locked down by crowd control while E spins without hitting anyone.
notes.garen-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Mortal Reminder earlier to get healing reduction. If healing reduction is more urgent, buy Executioner's Calling first. Without healing reduction, Garen struggles to trade against opponents who heal through E's sustained damage.
notes.garen-laning: Let the wave push toward you instead of pushing it. Garen has no mobility ability, leaving him vulnerable to ganks when his lane is pushed. Always keep wards available to prepare for ganks. Trade when your opponent steps forward to last-hit a minion. After pushing the wave with E, retreat into a brush to activate P's healing.
notes.garen-teamfight: Garen cannot take the initiative in starting teamfights. Once your allies start the fight, move in while timing W. In teamfights, hold the front line and use E to reduce enemy armor. Use R in teamfights when an enemy's health drops. To avoid being kited, look for an opening to reach the enemy backline from the flank or out of vision. If there is no opening for a teamfight, split push and sustain with P without recalling to keep one enemy tied down in a side lane.
notes.vs-garen-q-cooldown: Garen's Q-empowered auto attack silences you, preventing retaliation with abilities. Start a trade right after Garen uses Q on a minion or consumes its empowered auto attack. Avoid approaching Garen while his Q is active.
notes.vs-garen-silence: Garen's Q silence interrupts abilities with long cast times and channeled ultimates. Use abilities with long cast times or channeled ultimates after Garen has used his Q silence.
notes.vs-garen-e: Garen's E deals continuous damage while he spins. Garen's E deals bonus damage to the nearest enemy. Avoid extended fights with Garen and keep taking short, hit-and-run trades. If you cannot leave E's range, move among allied minions so a minion becomes the nearest enemy. Avoid approaching Garen in a brush so you do not take the full damage of E's spin.
notes.vs-garen-w: Right after using W, Garen briefly withstands burst damage and crowd control with a shield and tenacity. When you see Garen activate W, delay your combo slightly.
notes.vs-garen-r: Garen's R deals true damage proportional to his opponent's missing health. Armor and magic resistance cannot reduce Garen's R damage. Stay outside Garen's R range when your health falls below half. Champions who fight while recovering from low health through life steal must be especially wary of Garen's R execute.
notes.vs-garen-mobility: Garen has no mobility ability. Garen has limited ability to leave his lane and influence other lanes. Push the wave hard to expose Garen to jungle ganks. After pushing the wave in, create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
notes.garen-combo-e-first: If the enemy is already in melee range, use E before Q. Using Q during E does not interrupt the spin. Q's silence applies to the first basic attack after E's spin ends. Save Q until the enemy uses a counterattack ability.
notes.gnar-skill-rage: Gnar gains Rage when he deals or takes damage. Once Rage is full, Gnar transforms into Mega Gnar when he uses his next ability. If it is not time to engage, hold your abilities even at full Rage to control when you transform.
notes.gnar-skill-rage-window: After Mega Gnar returns to Mini Gnar, he cannot gain Rage for a while. Gnar is most vulnerable just after transforming back, while he cannot gain Rage.
notes.gnar-combo-mini: For a Mini Gnar trade, use Q, then E to bounce off a unit and move forward, and finish with an auto attack. Catching the returning boomerang greatly reduces Q's cooldown. Aim your E movement along the boomerang's return path. When Mini Gnar hits the same target repeatedly, W triggers and deals bonus damage. When Mini Gnar's W triggers, his movement speed increases greatly.
notes.gnar-combo-transform: For a transformation all-in, approach with E at full Rage and transform. Mini Gnar's E bounces farther if he lands on a unit. Transform during the E bounce, then land, stun with W, auto attack, and follow with Q. In a transformation all-in, do not use another ability to trigger the transformation before closing in with E.
notes.gnar-combo-wall-r: Use R to finish Mega Gnar's combo. R stuns enemies only if they hit a wall. Enemies knocked into a wall by R take bonus damage. Before using R, position Gnar, the enemy, and the wall in a straight line. After stunning an enemy against a wall with R, follow with W to keep them controlled. If R does not knock an enemy into a wall, its only crowd control is the knockback and slow.
notes.gnar-combo-flash-r: If you lack an angle to knock enemies into a wall, use Flash to reposition and aim R toward the wall. R throws enemies around Gnar in the direction he is facing.
notes.gnar-skill-q: Mini Gnar's Q returns after hitting one enemy. Mini Gnar's Q deals reduced damage to enemies it hits after the first. Catching Mini Gnar's boomerang greatly reduces Q's cooldown. Mega Gnar's Q deals area damage. The boulder from Mega Gnar's Q (Boulder Toss) stops where it hits an enemy. Throw Mega Gnar's Q where you can pick up the boulder to reduce its cooldown.
notes.gnar-skill-w: Mini Gnar's W is a passive that triggers when he hits the same target repeatedly. Mini Gnar's W deals damage based on maximum health, making it useful against tanks. Mini Gnar gains movement speed when his W triggers. When poking as Mini Gnar, focus auto attacks and Q on the same target to trigger W. Mega Gnar's W slams the area in front of him and stuns enemies. As Mini Gnar, be careful not to waste passive stacks by pressing W.
notes.gnar-skill-e: Mini Gnar's E bounces when he lands on a unit, extending its travel distance. Mega Gnar's E does not bounce, so it covers less distance when escaping than Mini Gnar's E. Mega Gnar's E deals area damage where he lands. Before engaging with E, check its cooldown to see whether you can use it to escape after returning to Mini Gnar.
notes.gnar-phase: Gnar gains an advantage at levels 1–2 by poking with ranged auto attacks and Q. Early on, avoid extended close fights even as Mega Gnar. Look for kills once you learn R at level 6. Gnar is strongest in the mid game when he completes his first core item. Late-game Gnar relies heavily on terrain where he can knock enemies into walls.
notes.gnar-laning: As Mini Gnar, poke with ranged auto attacks and Q. Back away before entering the opponent's retaliation range. When clearing a wave, catch Mini Gnar's Q to reduce its cooldown. Commit to a close-range all-in only when you transform into Mega Gnar. Finish the trade before the transformation ends.
notes.gnar-laning-rage: Taking damage also builds Rage, so being hit without trading back can make you transform at an unwanted time. Manage your transformation so you do not waste it under the enemy turret or where you have no allied support. Choose where to transform with recalls, level-ups, and jungle involvement in mind. Adjust how much you trade to match your planned transformation timing.
notes.gnar-teamfight: Gnar's teamfight impact depends heavily on finding an angle to knock enemies into a wall. Choose the fight location in advance and position so opponents have a wall behind them. Engage as Mega Gnar and start the teamfight with R. As Mini Gnar, stay back and poke with Q while building Rage. Do not force an engage to start a teamfight as Mini Gnar.
notes.gnar-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing makes it hard to finish the fight during Mega Gnar's duration, buy Executioner's Calling first to reduce healing. Mega Gnar has a fixed duration, so longer fights put him at a disadvantage.
notes.vs-gnar-rage: Check Gnar's Rage bar to decide when to fight. Right after returning from Mega to Mini, Gnar cannot gain Rage for a while, so he cannot transform again. Go all-in or start a teamfight with your allies while Gnar is back in Mini form and cannot gain Rage.
notes.vs-gnar-wall: Gnar's R stuns only enemies who hit a wall. Hitting a wall from Gnar's R deals bonus damage to you. Position yourself so you are not between Gnar and a wall. Gnar has an advantage in teamfights in tight spaces.
notes.vs-gnar-mini: If you have a way to close the gap, fight Gnar up close while he is in Mini form. If you cannot close the gap, farm near your turret and wait for Gnar's transformation cycle.
notes.vs-gnar-q: The boomerang from Mini Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw) can hit enemies both on its way out and on its way back. When Gnar catches his boomerang, Q's cooldown is greatly reduced. Move away from the boomerang's path to make it harder for Gnar to catch it. If Gnar misses his boomerang, there is a longer gap before his next Q poke.
notes.vs-gnar-mega: Mega Gnar excels at dealing heavy damage in a short burst. Unlike Mini Gnar's E, Mega Gnar's E does not bounce and travels a shorter distance. Right after Gnar transforms into Mega, avoid fighting him head-on and keep your distance to wait out the transformation. Watch Gnar's appearance and Rage bar to tell when a transformation is near.
notes.gragas-combo-eq: While dashing with E, roll Q to the landing spot, then recast Q to detonate it while the target is knocked up by E. An enemy knocked up by E cannot walk out of the barrel's radius.
notes.gragas-combo-qe: Roll Q out first, then when the opponent comes near, engage with E and detonate Q as E hits. The longer the barrel stays out, the more damage and slow it gains, so do not detonate it immediately. Look for a Q-E combo in lane ganks where the opponent's retreat path is predictable.
notes.gragas-combo-full: For the full combo, press W after E hits, then detonate Q. W takes time to drink, so press it during E's knockup to land the empowered basic attack before the knockup ends. Use R to move the opponent where you want when needed.
notes.gragas-skill-q: The longer Q's barrel stays out, the more damage and slow it gains. In fights, detonate Q when the opponent cannot move. Q deals reduced damage to minions, so save it for fights rather than farming.
notes.gragas-skill-w: W's damage reduction applies from the moment Gragas starts drinking. If you see an opponent's burst coming, press W before it hits. W's empowered basic attack also deals damage based on maximum health around the target. Use W's empowered basic attack against jungle camps and high-health opponents.
notes.gragas-skill-e: E's cooldown is greatly reduced when Gragas collides with an enemy. If E misses, you must wait out its full cooldown. E can cross terrain. Before engaging, decide whether to use E to initiate or save it to escape.
notes.gragas-skill-r: R pushes opponents outward from the explosion point. To push an opponent toward your team, land R behind them. Landing R between an opponent and your team pushes them away from your team. R cannot push opponents over walls.
notes.gragas-skill-r-split: Land R between the enemy front line and back line to split their formation. Pushing the back line away with R gives your team time to clear the front line with a numbers advantage.
notes.gragas-skill-passive: Use abilities at each jungle camp to stay healthy and manage your mana.
notes.gragas-jungle: While jungling, wear down camps with W's empowered basic attack and stay healthy with passive healing. Watch the lanes and gank when an enemy is within E's reach.
notes.gragas-jungle-gank: For a gank, circle behind the lane, place Q on the opponent's retreat path, and knock them up with E as they try to back away. If you engage with E from the front, the opponent can walk toward their turret.
notes.gragas-phase: Learning E at level 2 or 3 makes ganks possible. Learning R at level 6 creates reliable kill opportunities. Burst damage is strongest in the mid game after building one or two ability power items. In the late game, sustained damage is lacking, so focus on burst damage and disrupting enemy formations.
notes.gragas-teamfight: In teamfights, activate W, knock up the back line with E, follow with Q, and split the enemy formation with R. Before engaging, check whether the opponent has used their targeted crowd control. Before engaging, check whether your team is close enough to follow up.
notes.gragas-situational-tenacity: If the enemy has a lot of immobilizing crowd control, buy Quicksilver Sash earlier so you can detonate Q after engaging.
notes.vs-gragas-r: Gragas's R pushes enemies outward from the explosion point. When Gragas has R available, do not stand with your back to an enemy turret or the enemy team. Standing against a wall shortens the distance Gragas's R pushes you.
notes.vs-gragas-e: Gragas's E cooldown is greatly reduced when he collides with an enemy. Only chase a fleeing Gragas when you are certain you can kill him.
notes.vs-gragas-q: A Q barrel that rolls in does not detonate immediately. If you see a barrel, leave its radius right away. The longer a barrel stays out, the more damage and slow it gains. If E hits you near a barrel, you will also get hit by Q's explosion.
notes.vs-gragas-w: Gragas takes reduced damage from the moment he starts drinking with W. When Gragas drinks with W, wait until the damage reduction ends before dealing burst damage.
notes.vs-gragas-position: Gragas's engage depends on E. Avoid narrow paths and bushes without vision. Do not let your back line stand alone within range of Gragas's E. If E hits you, move out of the barrel's radius to avoid Q's explosion.
notes.vs-gragas-late: Gragas has strong burst damage and formation disruption in the early and mid game, but weak sustained damage in the late game. In early and mid game objective fights, hold your formation and survive to play for the late game.
notes.graves-combo-engage: Close the gap with E, then basic attack at point-blank range. E loads one shell into the magazine. Use E just before reloading to keep attacking without interruption. At point-blank range, cut off their vision with W, then use Q.
notes.graves-combo-q-wall: Q explodes immediately when it hits terrain. Against an opponent with their back to a wall, hit the wall with Q to land the explosion quickly. Against an enemy across a wall, fire Q right against the wall to land the explosion.
notes.graves-combo-r: R explodes again in a cone behind the champion it hits. Line up R when other enemies are lined up behind the target. Casting R knocks Graves backward. Use R's recoil to cross a wall while escaping.
notes.graves-skill-passive: After using both shells in the magazine with basic attacks, you start reloading. Each basic attack fires a spread of pellets. Basic attack pellets are all blocked by the first unit they hit. Find an angle with no units between you and the target, then get close.
notes.graves-skill-q: Q's follow-up explosion deals much more damage than its outgoing projectile. Aim Q slightly ahead or to the side so the opponent stays in the explosion area even if they dodge the projectile. At jungle camps, hit a wall with Q so the explosion covers the entire camp.
notes.graves-skill-w: When ganking, place W on the opponent's escape route to help your allies chase.
notes.graves-skill-e: Using E toward an enemy champion grants twice as many armor stacks. Each basic attack hit reduces E's cooldown. Keep landing basic attacks so you can use E twice in one fight. Do not carelessly spend E on an early escape and lose your engage tool and armor.
notes.graves-phase: Graves is strong in level 2–3 fights. Learning R at level 6 gives you a finishing tool, increasing your gank success rate. Graves is vulnerable to being taken down easily if caught first in the late game. Graves reaches his peak strength in the early to mid game. Secure objectives and vision in the early to mid game to cement your lead.
notes.graves-laning-route: Graves farms efficiently thanks to his fast jungle clears. At camps with plenty of walls, hit a wall with Q to clear faster. If a gank opportunity is unclear, clear camps to widen the level and gold gap.
notes.graves-teamfight: In teamfights, do not initiate from the front. Once your allies draw the enemy's attention, use E to move in from the side or rear and get close to their damage dealers. Maintain a position with no units between you and the target.
notes.graves-situational-antiheal: Against opponents who sustain through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items to reduce healing. Graves concentrates his damage into a short window.
notes.graves-situational-boots: If the enemy's damage is mostly magic, choose Mercury's Treads over Plated Steelcaps to bolster your magic resistance.
notes.vs-graves-block: Graves's basic attacks are fully blocked by the first unit they hit. In chaotic fights, keep minions or allies between you and Graves to block his basic attacks.
notes.vs-graves-reload: After emptying his magazine, Graves cannot basic attack while reloading. Counterattack or create distance right after Graves fires both shells.
notes.vs-graves-smoke: Vision is limited inside W's smoke. Movement speed is reduced inside W's smoke. Leaving W's area immediately removes its harmful effects. Take the shortest route out of W's smoke, then reengage.
notes.vs-graves-q: Q explodes immediately when it touches terrain. Fight in open terrain so you have room to dodge Q's explosion.
notes.vs-graves-armor: Graves deals almost entirely physical damage, making him vulnerable to armor. Buy Plated Steelcaps earlier to counter his early to mid game physical damage.
notes.graves-laning-gank: Gank when the enemy is past the middle of the lane and an ally can lock them down. Use E to close the angle, then throw W on the enemy's escape path. W's smoke only blocks the vision of enemies inside it; it doesn't block allied vision. Use W's smoke to create an opening for allied abilities to land.
notes.gwen-combo-basic: Stack Q with auto attacks, then use E to close in, land an empowered auto attack, and cast Q. Q has fewer snips without stacks, greatly reducing its damage. Before trading, hit even a minion to build Q stacks.
notes.gwen-combo-q-center: Enemies in the center of Q's cone take some of its damage as true damage and are affected by Gwen's passive. Position so your target is in the center of Q's cone. Landing the center of Q matters more against targets with high armor and magic resistance.
notes.gwen-combo-w-cancel: Enemies outside the mist cannot target Gwen while she is inside it. Activate W as an enemy starts a targeted ability or auto attack to make it miss. W does not block turret attacks.
notes.gwen-combo-w-reposition: Recast W to move the mist toward Gwen. If you try to leave the mist with E, W automatically recasts. Recast W yourself before leaving the mist with E to stay untargetable while moving.
notes.gwen-skill-e-reset: The first hit with E refunds a substantial part of its cooldown. When a minion wave is present, land E to use it for both entry and escape in quick succession.
notes.gwen-skill-e-range: E's empowered auto attacks gain attack speed and range. Even when a ranged opponent starts backing away, try to land another attack with E's extended range.
notes.gwen-skill-passive: Gwen's passive deals magic damage based on the target's maximum health. Her passive heals her only when it hits a champion. Gwen's sustain depends on how long she can auto attack champions. Clearing minions alone cannot heal Gwen through her passive.
notes.gwen-skill-r: R can be cast up to three times, with more needles on each cast. Hit a fleeing enemy with the first R cast to slow them and catch up. Before casting R again, check whether you can keep the enemy in range through the third cast.
notes.gwen-skill-r-passive: R applies Gwen's passive when it hits an enemy champion. Slow the enemy with the first R cast before closing in with E.
notes.gwen-phase: Trading is weak at levels 1–2 because Q stacks are hard to build. Once you learn W, you can avoid poke from ranged opponents. Gwen grows stronger in duels from midgame as she builds ability power items. Late game, use maximum health damage to cut down the enemy frontline directly.
notes.gwen-laning: In lane, build Q stacks with auto attacks and use W to avoid the enemy's counterattack. Her damage per minute at 14 minutes ranks high, but her kill numbers tend to be low, so securing farm is important. Early on, avoid forcing an engage and focus on CS and levels.
notes.gwen-laning-w-gank: Activate W when a gank starts to avoid targeted crowd control from enemies outside the mist. Keep W available while pushing the wave so you can respond to a gank.
notes.gwen-teamfight: In teamfights, attack the enemy frontline directly. Engage with E, use W to avoid focused attacks, then land the center of Q on the frontline. Engage when the enemy's key crowd control is down or W is ready.
notes.gwen-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing can turn a duel, buy Morellonomicon for healing reduction. Gwen can stay close and keep landing auto attacks and Q to maintain healing reduction.
notes.vs-gwen-w: Gwen cannot be targeted from outside the mist while she is inside it. When Gwen's W is active, move inside the mist or wait for it to expire before using targeted abilities or Ignite. Turrets ignore the mist, so push Gwen under the turret.
notes.vs-gwen-q: The center of Gwen's Q cone deals heavy true damage. Move sideways to get out of the center of Q's cone. Armor and magic resistance cannot reduce Q's true damage.
notes.vs-gwen-e: Gwen gets a large cooldown refund when she hits something with E. To catch Gwen, draw her into an area without minions or have immobilizing crowd control ready.
notes.vs-gwen-passive: Gwen needs to auto attack champions for sustain. Stay out of auto attack range to stop Gwen from healing. Trade at early levels before Gwen builds Q stacks. Do not get close to Gwen when her Q is fully stacked.
notes.vs-gwen-mr: Gwen's maximum health magic damage means stacking health alone makes her hit you harder. Build magic resistance items such as Spectre's Cowl against Gwen's magic damage. Keep your distance to avoid the true damage from the center of Q, which magic resistance cannot reduce.
notes.hecarim-combo-gank: For ganks, activate E early and run in from outside vision, then use W, Q, and the empowered E basic attack as you approach. The empowered E basic attack deals more damage based on the distance traveled after activation. The empowered E basic attack knocks the target back farther based on the distance traveled after activation. Do not attack right after activating E; loop around once to build up travel distance.
notes.hecarim-combo-e-r: E’s remaining duration stops decreasing during R. E retains its accumulated travel distance after R ends. For maximum damage, activate E and run in, then chain R’s landing fear, the empowered E basic attack, and Q.
notes.hecarim-combo-q-stack: Q gains a stack each time it hits. Q stacks increase Q’s damage. Q stacks shorten Q’s cooldown. Hit a jungle monster with Q just before a gank or objective fight to build stacks. When you reach the fight, use your prepared, fully stacked Q twice in quick succession.
notes.hecarim-skill-passive: P converts bonus movement speed into attack damage. Start the fight when bonus movement speed takes effect. When Hecarim loses bonus movement speed, his damage drops sharply even with the same items.
notes.hecarim-skill-q: Q deals area damage around Hecarim. As a rule, use Q whenever its cooldown ends. Q deals reduced damage to minions. During fights, keep hitting monsters or minions with Q to maintain stacks.
notes.hecarim-skill-w: W heals Hecarim based on damage nearby enemies take. W’s healing also counts damage allies deal to nearby enemies. Use W in the middle of a fight where allies and enemies are clustered together. W provides almost no healing when you are fleeing alone. Healing from jungle monsters during W is capped.
notes.hecarim-skill-e: You can pass through minions and monsters during E. Enter the lane through the minion wave with E. Adjust your position to knock the enemy in the intended direction with the empowered E basic attack.
notes.hecarim-skill-r: When using R, Hecarim travels only to the targeted location. R’s spectral riders always advance to the end of its range. Stop beside a nearby target with R to fear them while the spectral riders also damage enemies behind them. R’s fear duration increases with the distance charged. To extend R’s fear duration, start the charge from as far away as possible.
notes.hecarim-phase: After learning W, Hecarim clears the jungle faster without losing health. Hecarim reaches his first power spike at level 6 when he learns R. Hecarim’s strength peaks in the mid game once he has attack damage and ability haste. In the late game, engage from the side because it is hard to survive a frontal entry.
notes.hecarim-jungle-path: Use Hecarim’s fast jungle clear to keep cycling through camps. Before level 6, E’s knockback is his only hard crowd control. Before level 6, focus on clearing camps and reaching level 6 instead of forcing ganks. As soon as you reach level 6, approach a lane and look for an opening to use R.
notes.hecarim-gank-angle: Before level 6, look for ganks where you can get behind the enemy. Activate E outside vision and circle toward the enemy’s escape route. Use the empowered E basic attack from behind the enemy to knock them toward your allies. Avoid frontal ganks that leave little distance to travel with E.
notes.hecarim-teamfight: In teamfights, use R from the side or behind to split the enemy damage dealers’ formation. Use the moment R’s fear disrupts the enemy formation as the cue for your allies to enter. After entering, stay in the middle of the fight with W active to keep healing.
notes.hecarim-situational-cc: Hecarim relies on movement speed for damage, making him vulnerable to crowd control that stops his movement. If the enemy has a root, buy Quicksilver Sash after your first core item so you can remove it right after engaging.
notes.hecarim-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing makes it hard to finish a dive, buy Executioner’s Calling to reduce healing. Buy Executioner’s Calling after completing your first core item. Sell Executioner’s Calling last if you no longer need it.
notes.vs-hecarim-w: Hecarim’s W heals him based on damage nearby enemies take. Hecarim’s W healing also counts damage dealt by his allies. Avoid prolonged fights where several players stay close to Hecarim while his W is active. Kill Hecarim with a short burst of focused damage. Back out of Hecarim’s W range, then approach again.
notes.vs-hecarim-e: Hecarim’s E deals more damage based on the distance he runs after activation. Hecarim’s E knocks targets back farther based on the distance he runs after activation. If Hecarim suddenly turns and runs the other way, treat it as an attempt to build up E travel distance. Block vision while Hecarim builds up E travel distance. Move toward your allies so E’s knockback does not leave you isolated.
notes.vs-hecarim-r: Hecarim’s R can fear several clustered enemies at once. Keep your teamfight formation spread out so fewer players are hit by R together. R’s fear takes away the target’s control over their movement. Be ready to use a cleanse or mobility ability before R’s fear hits you.
notes.vs-hecarim-ms: Slows and roots also reduce Hecarim’s damage. When the fight starts, apply movement impairments to Hecarim first.
notes.vs-hecarim-early: Hecarim’s lack of reliable hard crowd control before level 6 is a weakness in his ganks. Hecarim reaches level 6 early thanks to his fast camp clear. Manage the lane early so you do not push it too far.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-q-placement: There is a limit to how many turrets you can place. Turrets far from Heimerdinger stop working after a short time. Place turrets where you plan to stand. As support, place turrets at brush entrances or river approaches for vision and poke. You can store multiple turret placement charges. Keep at least one placement charge so you can put down a turret immediately during a fight.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-q-priority: Turrets prioritize enemies Heimerdinger has recently damaged. Turrets prioritize enemies attacking Heimerdinger. First damage the target you want your turrets to focus with an auto attack or ability. As support, if you want to target the enemy ADC, attack them first even if a tank is in front.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-q-charge: Turrets charge over time. A fully charged turret fires much more powerfully than a newly placed one. Check your turrets' charge before starting a fight. Each rocket that hits a champion charges nearby turrets a little. Hitting an enemy champion with a grenade instantly fully charges nearby turrets.
notes.heimerdinger-combo-basic: Set up turrets where you plan to fight, hit the center of your grenade, then fire rockets while the charged turrets shoot. Auto attack the enemy you want to take down to direct your turrets' fire. Using your grenade first in a fight can instantly fully charge your turrets. Rockets converge at your cursor, and only the first hit deals full damage. Aim your cursor a little behind the enemy so they overlap the point where the rockets converge. When firing rockets, choose an angle that minions will not block.
notes.heimerdinger-combo-r-e: The empowered grenade bounces several times and has larger stun and slow areas. Throw the empowered grenade along the enemy's retreat path. Empower your grenade with your ultimate to stun the enemy, then attack with turrets and rockets. If you activate your ultimate by mistake, use it again to cancel it.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-r-choice: A turret empowered by your ultimate does not count toward the regular turret placement limit. The empowered turret applies an area slow and is immune to crowd control. Use the empowered turret in narrow passages near objectives or when defending an allied turret. Empowered rockets deal burst damage through successive volleys. Use empowered rockets to finish off a fleeing enemy or clear an incoming wave. Abilities empowered by your ultimate cost no resources. When low on mana, you can use an empowered ability in a pinch.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-e: The grenade damages and slows enemies in its area. Only enemies hit by the center of the grenade are stunned. Throw your grenade after the enemy has used their mobility ability. Layer your grenade on an ally's crowd control. If you cannot land a direct hit, predict the enemy's retreat through a narrow passage and throw your grenade there. Do not spend your grenade carelessly on wave clear; keep it available to fully charge your turrets.
notes.heimerdinger-skill-passive: Heimerdinger gains movement speed near allied turrets and his own turrets. Heimerdinger has no mobility ability, so he relies on the movement speed near turrets to escape. When holding a risky lane position, set up a turret on your retreat path beforehand. When defending under an allied turret, use the movement speed boost to dodge enemy engage abilities.
notes.heimerdinger-laning-support: Support Heimerdinger's turrets can push the wave. If you do not want to push, place turrets in brush outside minion range or behind the lane. To push the enemy ADC out of lane, place turrets in the lane and secure vision alongside them. Look for a direct grenade hit when the enemy steps forward to destroy a turret.
notes.heimerdinger-laning-mid: In mid, turrets help absorb the wave, making it easier to hold the lane and farm. Cluster turrets behind the lane, then counter an enemy jungle engage with turret fire and a grenade. Heimerdinger has no mobility ability, making it hard for him to roam on his own. In mid, push the lane decisively to keep your opponent there and let your jungler gain an advantage elsewhere.
notes.heimerdinger-phase: Levels 1–2, when Heimerdinger has only one turret, are his most dangerous period. From level 3, multiple turrets and a grenade give him control of the lane. Learning your ultimate at level 6 greatly improves your ability to start fights. Late in the game, Heimerdinger loses strength in moving skirmishes because his turrets cannot keep up. Late in the game, draw fights to a position you have chosen in advance.
notes.heimerdinger-teamfight: Before a teamfight, place and charge turrets in a narrow passage near an objective or beside an allied turret. Lure enemies into your prepared turret position. Avoid moving fights in open areas where turrets struggle to contribute. When an enemy engages, stop them with a grenade stun and retreat behind your turrets. While your allies hold the position, use an empowered turret to block the route.
notes.heimerdinger-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who dives in all at once, include Zhonya's Hourglass in your core item order. Turrets you have already placed keep firing while Zhonya's Hourglass protects you.
notes.heimerdinger-situational-antiheal: If the enemy sustains through turret damage with healing, consider Morellonomicon for Grievous Wounds. If you are short on gold as support, delay Morellonomicon until after completing one core item.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-turret: Turrets far from Heimerdinger stop working after a short time. Push Heimerdinger away instead of destroying his turrets one by one. Turrets prioritize targets Heimerdinger has recently damaged or targets attacking him. When diving, have a durable ally attack Heimerdinger first and draw turret fire before your damage dealers go in.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-e: The grenade stuns enemies hit by its center; hits outside the center only slow. When the grenade's landing marker appears, move sideways out of its center. A direct grenade hit is Heimerdinger's only guaranteed crowd control and instantly fully charges his turrets.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-r: After level 6, Heimerdinger's ultimate empowers his next ability. The empowered grenade bounces several times and has a much larger stun area. Empowered rockets can finish off a low-health ally with burst damage. When Heimerdinger has his ultimate available, do not group up in narrow passages. When Heimerdinger has his ultimate available, do not group at one spot in front of an objective for a standoff.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-body: Heimerdinger has no mobility ability. Go around his turret position, or withstand it before attacking Heimerdinger himself. Do not repeatedly trade damage head-on in front of his turrets. Change your approach angle from the side or from brush.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-timing: Turrets charge over time and fire more powerfully when fully charged. Engage when a turret has just been placed or immediately after it fires a powerful shot. When Heimerdinger hits an enemy champion with his grenade, nearby turrets instantly become fully charged. Move out of turret range immediately after the grenade hits you.
notes.vs-heimerdinger-melee: Melee champions can get hit by both turrets and rockets while last-hitting inside turret range. As a melee champion, do not force yourself to take the wave; wait outside turret range. Step forward when Heimerdinger uses his grenade or spends all his turret placement charges. If you are not confident you can get close and take him down, give up the lane and put pressure on a side lane.
notes.hwei-skill-subject-system: Press Q, W, or E to open that subject’s three spells, then press Q, W, or E again to cast one. The three spells in the same subject share a cooldown. Selecting a subject without casting a spell uses no resources. Select the subject you plan to use in advance to react faster.
notes.hwei-skill-passive: Hit an enemy champion with a spell, then hit them with a different spell to detonate the Signature. The Signature mark lasts only briefly, so follow the first hit immediately with a second spell. Land the second hit on grouped enemies to deal area damage with the Signature explosion.
notes.hwei-skill-q: Subject: Disaster is Hwei’s main source of damage. Use Devastating Fire (QQ) to poke a single target or fight a bulky enemy. Severing Bolt (QW) can be aimed from far away, but takes time to land. Use Molten Fissure’s (QE) damage over time and slow to deny an area. The three Subject: Disaster spells share a cooldown, so choose the one you need first.
notes.hwei-skill-q-lightning: Severing Bolt (QW) deals more damage based on missing health to isolated or immobilized targets. Use Severing Bolt (QW) as a finisher right after you or an ally applies crowd control. Predict where a fleeing enemy is headed and land Severing Bolt (QW) ahead of them.
notes.hwei-skill-w: Subject: Serenity is Hwei’s only way to support allies. Place Fleeting Current (WQ) along the path of allies engaging or retreating. Shield allies inside Pool of Reflection’s (WW) area. If you run low on mana midway through the laning phase, use Stirring Lights (WE) for bonus damage and mana restoration. Subject: Serenity has the longest cooldown and highest mana cost, so don’t use it out of habit.
notes.hwei-skill-e: Use Grim Visage (EQ) to fear the first enemy hit and stop an engage. Gaze of the Abyss (EW) leaves an eye at the target location, granting vision and rooting enemies who enter its area. Crushing Maw (EE) pulls enemies toward the target point and slows them. Place Gaze of the Abyss (EW) at river entrances or bush openings in advance for vision and protection against ganks. Under heavy jungle pressure, use Subject: Torment’s eye to guard against ganks instead of poking.
notes.hwei-skill-r: R attaches to the first enemy champion hit, grows while stacking slows, then explodes. Land R when enemies have trouble spreading out. Attach R to the front line of grouped enemies, then follow up with Subject: Disaster.
notes.hwei-combo-pull: Pull enemies together with Crushing Maw (EE), then land Severing Bolt (QW) there for increased damage and a Signature explosion.
notes.hwei-combo-poke: Hit with Devastating Fire (QQ), then complete the Signature with Grim Visage (EQ). Hit with Devastating Fire (QQ), then complete the Signature with Molten Fissure (QE). You cannot attack twice in a row with spells from Subject: Disaster because they share a cooldown.
notes.hwei-combo-ult: In teamfights, hit grouped enemies with R, pull them together again with Crushing Maw (EE), then finish with Molten Fissure (QE). In teamfights, hit grouped enemies with R, pull them together again with Crushing Maw (EE), then finish with Devastating Fire (QQ). While R’s slow stacks, enemies struggle to walk out of Molten Fissure’s (QE) pool.
notes.hwei-phase: At levels 1–2, only one subject is available and mana is tight, so Signature poke is very weak. Signature poke becomes possible once two subjects are available. Hwei gets a major power spike at level 6 when he learns R and when he completes his first core item. At every stage, deal damage safely from behind instead of stepping forward.
notes.hwei-laning: Clear waves with Molten Fissure (QE), then use Devastating Fire (QQ) to poke with the time left over. Prioritize farming over risky poke. Use a Signature combo when an enemy lines up behind minions. Mana costs are high enough that you could miss the next wave, so don’t use a subject every time its cooldown ends.
notes.hwei-teamfight: At the edge of your range, place Molten Fissure (QE) on the enemy’s approach to block their path. When the enemy starts an engage, use Grim Visage (EQ) to turn back the leader. Wait for an ally to catch an enemy first, then unleash Subject: Disaster. Don’t spend all of Subject: Torment on poke; keep it available to deal with enemies who reach you.
notes.hwei-situational-zhonya: Buy Zhonya’s Hourglass earlier against melee enemies who get close to deal damage. Hwei has virtually no mobility, making it hard to survive once caught. Using Zhonya’s Hourglass to wait out an enemy engage lets your remaining subjects come off cooldown.
notes.vs-hwei-signature: Hwei’s Signature damage triggers when two different spells hit in quick succession. Move immediately after the first spell hits to dodge the second.
notes.vs-hwei-lightning: Severing Bolt (QW) deals much more damage if it hits you while you’re immobilized or isolated. Stay close to allies to avoid meeting Severing Bolt’s (QW) isolation condition.
notes.vs-hwei-eye: The eye left by Gaze of the Abyss (EW) grants vision and roots the first enemy to enter it. Before ganking, check whether Gaze of the Abyss (EW) has placed an eye. If there’s an eye, take another route or let a minion or something else trigger it first.
notes.vs-hwei-dive: Hwei has no mobility, and Subject: Torment is his only way to counterattack when an enemy gets close. Engage right after Hwei uses Subject: Torment to poke or clear a wave. If Subject: Torment is ready, the first champion to engage may be feared or rooted.
notes.vs-hwei-zone: Hwei uses ground effects and his eye to limit where enemies can move.
notes.illaoi-combo-basic: For trades, pull out the spirit with E, cast Q toward the tentacle, then use W to close in on the target. Cast Q first so the two slams overlap when W lands.
notes.illaoi-combo-teamfight: In teamfights, pull out the nearest enemy’s spirit with E, use R immediately, then attack the spirit. If you use R while a spirit pulled out by E is present, the spirit also counts toward the tentacle count if hit.
notes.illaoi-combo-aoe: The spirit and its host can both be hit by the same area damage. Damage dealt to the spirit transfers to its host. Pull out the spirit where your allies’ area abilities can hit it.
notes.illaoi-skill-tentacle-terrain: Tentacles spawn near impassable terrain, a set distance apart. Illaoi’s damage drops sharply in open areas without tentacles. Draw fights toward walls and areas with tentacles.
notes.illaoi-skill-tentacle-queue: Give an attacking tentacle another attack command, and it will strike again right after its first attack. Use Q and W in quick succession to keep the tentacle slams going.
notes.illaoi-skill-e-vessel: A spirit pulled out by E inherits the target’s current health. To make an enemy a Vessel, lower their health before landing E.
notes.illaoi-skill-e-finish: Damage dealt to the spirit transfers to its host, but damage dealt to the host does not transfer to the spirit. If a fleeing enemy has less health than their spirit, finish them by attacking the spirit. Land E before a fight so you can finish a fleeing enemy through their spirit.
notes.illaoi-skill-e-position: Cast E from the side with your allied turret and tentacles. If the enemy moves in to defend the spirit, they have to fight among the tentacles. If the enemy does not move in to defend the spirit, they become a Vessel and carry tentacles with them.
notes.illaoi-skill-r: Use R when your allies engage or the enemy moves in. R spawns one tentacle for each enemy champion it damages. Avoid going in alone first and using R.
notes.illaoi-skill-r-window: After R, tentacles briefly cannot be targeted and slam faster. The brief window after R is when Illaoi deals the most damage. Have a way to keep enemies in place during R’s peak damage window.
notes.illaoi-skill-passive-heal: When a tentacle hits an enemy champion, Illaoi heals based on her missing health. Where tentacles can reach, choose to fight back even at half health. Where tentacles cannot reach, Illaoi has virtually no way to heal.
notes.illaoi-phase: At level 1, Illaoi has only one tentacle, so her trades are weak. Her laning gets stronger once she starts leveling E. Getting R at level 6 is her biggest turning point. Her damage per minute at 14 minutes ranks among the highest. Late in the game, Illaoi lacks guaranteed crowd control, so going in alone has less value and she takes a frontline role.
notes.illaoi-laning: In lane, draw the wave toward an area where you have placed tentacles. Keep the wave near a wall and cast E when the enemy steps up to last-hit. Her CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute both rank among the highest. Maintain lane pressure instead of forcing a dive.
notes.illaoi-laning-tp: Both active and inactive tentacles can be targeted by Teleport. Before recalling, leave a tentacle near the lane or objective you plan to return to.
notes.vs-illaoi-tentacle: Illaoi is stronger in fights near tentacles. Destroy tentacles when you can. If you cannot spare the time to destroy tentacles, draw Illaoi into open ground away from walls. Do not take a fight with Illaoi in an area covered by tentacles.
notes.vs-illaoi-e-fight: If she has pulled out your spirit and you can fight, counterattack Illaoi. Each time you damage Illaoi, the spirit’s duration decreases. If you only run away after your spirit is pulled out, the spirit survives and you become a Vessel.
notes.vs-illaoi-vessel: If you are not fighting, break the spirit tether and dodge the first tentacle after becoming a Vessel. After dodging the first tentacle, wait beside it until the mark expires. If you stay beside that tentacle without destroying it, you will not be hit by another slam, and Illaoi will not gain more tentacles.
notes.vs-illaoi-heal: Illaoi’s healing gets stronger as her health gets lower. If you dive Illaoi after bringing her to half health, a few tentacle hits can restore her health. Apply Grievous Wounds with Executioner’s Calling before committing to a dive.
notes.vs-illaoi-r: R is Illaoi’s peak damage window, but it is short. When Illaoi uses R, spread out so she has no targets to attack. R spawns one tentacle for each enemy champion it damages. Do not group up in front of Illaoi.
notes.vs-illaoi-laning: In lane, Illaoi draws the wave near a wall and sets up tentacles. Keep the wave away from walls and last-hit from outside E range. Illaoi has no guaranteed crowd control, so if you dodge E, she cannot keep you in place.
notes.irelia-combo-engage: Place the first E behind the opponent, stun them with the second E, then follow up with a Q dash, a basic attack, and W. The mark left on a champion hit by E resets Q's cooldown. You can use Q twice before E's stun wears off.
notes.irelia-combo-farm: Killing a low-health minion with Q resets Q's cooldown. Repeatedly resetting Q by killing minions lets you dash through them in a chain. Check the wave's position before using chained Q dashes to engage or escape.
notes.irelia-skill-e-placement: E's two blades fly toward each other, stunning enemies between them. Place the first E behind the opponent or along their escape route to account for their movement. If you do not recast E, it fires automatically from Irelia's position after a short delay. Adjust Irelia's position so the automatic E cast does not go to waste.
notes.irelia-skill-w: You cannot move while charging W. You take reduced damage while charging W. Save W instead of using it early for damage. Use W as an enemy assassin engages or a gank arrives. From mid game onward, bait out the opponent's abilities before using W.
notes.irelia-skill-passive: Attack speed increases as passive stacks build. At maximum passive stacks, basic attacks deal bonus damage. Attacking a champion, structure, or large monster refreshes the passive's duration. Hit minions with abilities just before a fight to build passive stacks.
notes.irelia-skill-r: R traps the first champion it hits inside a blade wall. An opponent who crosses R's blade wall takes damage and is heavily slowed. An opponent can Flash out of R's blade wall. Aim R to block the opponent's escape route. Place R so its blade wall opens toward your allies, letting them catch the trapped target.
notes.irelia-skill-mark-vision: Champions and large monsters marked by E or R remain visible through brush and fog. You can follow an opponent marked by E or R with Q even after losing vision of them.
notes.irelia-phase: Irelia is weak in level 1 trades. Once Irelia has her abilities at level 3, she starts winning short trades. Irelia reaches her first major power spike at level 6, when she gets R. After level 6, Irelia grows stronger as she gets items. Avoid repeated risky engages so you do not fall behind.
notes.irelia-laning-ranged: Irelia has trouble finding chances to trade against ranged opponents. Against ranged opponents, use chained Q dashes to secure CS safely and keep up in growth. After you waste E trying to force an approach against a ranged opponent, you become vulnerable to ganks.
notes.irelia-laning-melee: Build passive stacks before trading with a melee opponent. Against melee opponents, repeat short trades where you engage and back off. Save E to interrupt a melee opponent's counterattack or escape.
notes.irelia-laning-q-reserve: Using Q carelessly on minions leaves you without an escape when the opponent approaches. Use Q only on minions you can kill to keep resetting its cooldown. Do not engage by using Q first on an unmarked opponent.
notes.irelia-teamfight: In teamfights, use R to split the enemy formation. Stun a target trapped by R with E, then chain Q dashes into the backline. To survive teamfights, engage after your allies land crowd control.
notes.irelia-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps negating short trades, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.irelia-situational-cc: Against a team that locks you down and kills you immediately after you engage, before you can use W, get Quicksilver Sash. Irelia relies on continuing to basic attack after she closes the gap. Irelia is vulnerable to roots that stop her from continuing her basic attacks.
notes.vs-irelia-r: If you are trapped in Irelia's R blade wall, wait until the blades disappear. Crossing Irelia's R blade wall deals additional damage and heavily slows you.
notes.vs-irelia-teamfight: When a teamfight starts, focus Irelia first. Irelia's R splits formations in teamfights. Irelia's E can stun multiple targets at once.
notes.vs-irelia-w: Abilities that deal true damage ignore the damage reduction from Irelia's W. If Irelia uses W to withstand damage, use Ignite's true damage. Use Ignite's healing reduction to limit Irelia's Q healing.
