notes.vs-irelia-q-minion: Irelia approaches by chaining Q dashes through low-health minions. Do not leave a half-health minion between you and Irelia that she can use to approach with Q. Step back and keep your distance from Irelia when minions are about to die.
notes.vs-irelia-early: Irelia is weak in level 1–2 trades. Gain control before Irelia has all her abilities. Use that early control to disrupt Irelia's farming and slow her growth.
notes.ivern-combo-gank: After landing Q, use E on an ally as they close in, then recast Q to engage if needed. An ally who attacks an enemy rooted by Q automatically dashes into attack range. Use Q once your ally is ready to close in.
notes.ivern-combo-e-timing: E explodes after a short delay, not immediately when applied. Use E a little early so it explodes as Q's root ends. If E's slow takes hold as the root ends, the enemy has no opening to escape.
notes.ivern-combo-daisy: Summon Daisy!, command her to attack, then use E on her. You can cast E on Daisy! as well as allies. Use E on Daisy! in the middle of the enemy team to slow multiple enemies. Keep Daisy! attacking the same target so her third attack knocks them up.
notes.ivern-skill-passive-jungle: Ivern does not fight monsters other than epic monsters. Plant a grove at a camp, then harvest it when fully grown for gold and experience. Planting a grove at a camp costs health and mana. Plant groves at several camps in advance, then make a circuit to harvest them. Groves grow faster as Ivern levels up.
notes.ivern-skill-passive-smite: Using Smite on a growing grove frees the camp immediately. If it is nearly time to take Dragon or Rift Herald, save Smite instead of using it on a camp. Ivern can attack epic monsters directly. In objective fights, deal damage with basic attacks and Daisy!.
notes.ivern-skill-q: Q has long range, but it is a skillshot that can hit only one target. Hitting a monster with Q halves its cooldown. While moving or escaping, hit a nearby camp monster with Q to prepare for the next gank. Do not waste Q on a monster right before a fight.
notes.ivern-skill-w: Brush created by W blocks vision and creates ambush spots. Brush created by W adds damage to the basic attacks of Ivern inside it and nearby allies. If your team loses vision inside the brush, it disappears. Keep vision inside ambush brush with a ward or an ally's position. Just before a teamfight, create brush under your allies for stronger basic attacks and a vision advantage.
notes.ivern-skill-e: If E does not hit an enemy, the shield refreshes. Put E on your allied carry before the fight starts.
notes.ivern-skill-r: Daisy! can take non-targeted abilities for allies. Position Daisy! between your allied carry and an incoming enemy engage. Daisy!'s third consecutive hit on the same target knocks them up. When aiming for Daisy!'s knockup, do not keep switching her target.
notes.ivern-jungle-route: Plant a seed at a camp, try to gank a lane, then return to harvest it. Spend more time showing up in lanes.
notes.ivern-jungle-vision: Ivern is very weak in a 1v1. Avoid routes where you might meet the enemy jungler. Secure vision first and path toward your allies. Help all three allied lanes in turn instead of counterjungling.
notes.ivern-phase: Ivern can gank with Q from level 2 or 3, giving him early gank pressure. Getting Daisy! at level 6 greatly increases Ivern's control over fights. In the mid and late game, keep your allied carry alive and stop enemy engages. Ivern relies on his allies' damage, so he has less to do if they fall behind.
notes.ivern-teamfight: Start teamfights from the back. Catch an enemy with Q so your allies can attack them. Use E the moment an enemy engage reaches your allied carry. Use Daisy! as a wall in front of your allied carry. If the enemy formation has already broken, place Daisy! in their escape path to look for a knockup. If Ivern stands in front and dies, his shield and Daisy! disappear together.
notes.ivern-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has a lot of crowd control that locks down your allied carry, buy Mikael's Blessing between core items to remove effects E cannot cleanse.
notes.vs-ivern-q: When you are hit by Ivern's Q, his allies automatically dash into attack range. Take a favorable position before Ivern fires Q, rather than after it hits you. Stand with minions or terrain between you and Ivern to limit his Q angles.
notes.vs-ivern-brush: Brush Ivern creates appears where there was none and lasts a long time. If Ivern's team loses vision inside the brush, it disappears. Deny vision inside Ivern's brush to remove the ambush spot. Do not walk carelessly past brush that suddenly appears.
notes.vs-ivern-daisy: While Daisy! is alive, Ivern's team has one more frontline unit. Daisy! can absorb skillshots. Do not fire non-targeted abilities at an enemy behind Daisy!. Daisy!'s third consecutive hit on the same target knocks them up. If Daisy! starts attacking you, move to break the chain of consecutive attacks.
notes.vs-ivern-solo: Ivern himself deals almost no damage. Instead of spending time trying to kill Ivern, stop the ally receiving his shield first. If only Ivern is left, you have already won the fight. Ivern escapes well with his mobility and brush, so do not chase him too far.
notes.vs-ivern-jungle: Ivern plants seeds at camps and waits for them to grow, so you can predict his harvest route. Place vision in Ivern's jungle early to track when he will harvest camps. As the enemy jungler, ambush Ivern when he comes to a camp; he is weak in a 1v1.
notes.vs-ivern-e: Ivern's E explodes shortly after being applied and leaves a slow. If you engage on a shielded target, the slow that follows makes it hard to back away. Engage on a shielded target after E explodes.
notes.janna-skill-q-charge: Q charges where it is cast and launches when recast. The longer Q charges, the greater its range, damage, and knockup duration. Launch Q immediately to stop an enemy engage. Only charge Q when the enemy is out of vision.
notes.janna-combo-q-brush: When aiming for a fully charged Q, hide the tornado behind a wall or in a bush as it charges. Launch Q the moment an enemy enters the tornado's path. Follow up an ally's immobilizing crowd control with Q. Enemies can hear Q charging and back away.
notes.janna-skill-w: W's passive grants movement speed and ghosting. W's ghosting lets you pass through minions. Using W while you have bonus movement speed increases its poke damage.
notes.janna-skill-e: E grants its target a shield and attack damage. Cast E as damage is about to land. Disrupting an enemy champion's movement with Q or W reduces E's cooldown.
notes.janna-skill-e-turret: You can cast E on an allied turret. When enemies attack or dive an allied turret, cast E on it to help it survive longer.
notes.janna-skill-r: R heals nearby allies throughout its duration. R ends immediately if Janna moves or uses an ability. If you need R's healing, stand still after casting it. If you need to escape after the knockback, give up R's healing and move immediately. R's knockback cannot push enemies over walls.
notes.janna-combo-r-timing: Use R to interrupt an enemy's engage the moment it reaches an ally. Use R to interrupt an enemy's channeled ultimate as soon as it starts. Use R just before an ally is caught and killed. You can Flash into the middle of the enemy formation, then use R to split their front and back lines. If you Flash in and use R, Janna remains in the enemy formation.
notes.janna-skill-passive: P increases an ally's movement speed when they move toward Janna. When retreating, stay ahead of your allies in the direction of retreat. When chasing, move ahead so your allies can follow you.
notes.janna-laning: If the enemy support walks in, knock them up immediately with Q, then slow them with W. To conserve mana, avoid using Q and W to clear minions or for pointless poke. Save Q for a tower dive, then launch it immediately when the enemy goes in.
notes.janna-roaming: W's passive and ghosting let Janna roam quickly without getting blocked by minions. Roam away from lane only when the wave has been pushed safely or your ADC has recalled. Place vision around mid or jungle entrances to spot enemy ganks early.
notes.janna-vision: After identifying the enemy's approach, decide whether to launch Q immediately or charge it. Get vision in bushes to create chances to charge Q from inside them. Do not walk alone through areas without vision.
notes.janna-teamfight: Stay beside your allied carry instead of standing in front of an enemy looking for an engage. As the enemy engages, push them back with Q or R. Against a dive-focused enemy composition, save R to stop their engage. If the enemy composition struggles to engage, use E and W to give your allied carry more time to attack.
notes.janna-phase: Janna has very little kill pressure in the early laning phase. Janna is very good at surviving the laning phase. At level 6, learning R makes Janna stronger because she can stop enemy engages. From the mid game, as support items build up, her shields and healing become more valuable. In the late game, she can change the outcome of a teamfight by keeping her allied carry alive longer.
notes.janna-situational-cleanse: If the enemy's plan is to lock down and kill your allied carry, buy Mikael's Blessing early. E's shield cannot remove crowd control that has already landed.
notes.vs-janna-r: Janna's R pushes nearby enemies away and stops their engage. If you have an interrupt, save it for when Janna uses R. Engage with your back to a wall to shorten the distance R pushes you.
notes.vs-janna-q: Q's tornado makes a sound while charging. If you hear Q charging from a bush or outside your vision, avoid the tornado's path. A fully charged Q has much greater range and knockup duration. When Janna has just disappeared from vision, watch for a fully charged Q as you engage.
notes.vs-janna-e: A target with E absorbs damage and gains attack damage. Engage after E's shield is gone, or target someone else. Each time Janna disrupts an enemy with an ability, E comes back sooner.
notes.vs-janna-target: Establish vision and look for a moment when Janna is isolated. If Janna keeps stopping engages from behind her allied carry, look to pick off Janna first.
notes.vs-janna-lane: Keep poking the ally Janna protects to make her use E. Make Janna waste Q and W to drain her mana.
notes.vs-janna-w: W's ghosting lets Janna pass through minions. To catch Janna, use immobilizing crowd control or an engage ability that closes the distance at once.
notes.jarvan-combo-eq: Place your flag with E, then immediately use Q to dash toward it and knock up enemies along the path. Press E and Q almost simultaneously so the enemy cannot leave the flag's range. Place the flag beyond the enemy to dash past them and block their path. Place the flag between the enemy and your allies to drive the enemy toward your team.
notes.jarvan-combo-full: After knocking them up with EQ, land an auto attack as soon as you land, trap them with R, then use W. Weave an auto attack between abilities so you do not miss the bonus damage from Martial Cadence.
notes.jarvan-combo-eq-flash: Flash after the EQ dash begins to change where you land and knock up an enemy beyond its normal range. Save EQ Flash for a target you absolutely need to interrupt.
notes.jarvan-skill-q-unstoppable: The Q dash toward your flag still works while slowed or rooted. Before entering a dangerous area, leave a flag in your escape direction.
notes.jarvan-skill-q-wall: Throw a flag over a thin wall and dash to it with Q to cross the wall. Before a fight, identify walls you can cross with EQ. In the jungle, use EQ to cross walls between camps and shorten travel time.
notes.jarvan-skill-w: Golden Aegis absorbs more damage for each enemy champion it hits. Use W after entering a group of enemies instead of activating it early when you are alone. Use W's slow to limit an enemy's escape route or delay their approach.
notes.jarvan-skill-e-aura: E grants attack speed through its passive effect even when you do not use it. Placing a flag also increases nearby allied champions' attack speed. When attacking an objective, place a flag beside it. When no fight is underway, place your flag outside enemy vision so you do not reveal your angle of approach.
notes.jarvan-skill-r-cage: The wall created by Cataclysm also blocks your allies' movement. Check where you will land before using R so you do not trap your allied damage dealers. If needed, recast R to bring down the wall immediately. Use R's wall to cut off an enemy chasing an ally.
notes.jarvan-skill-passive: Martial Cadence deals bonus damage based on current health to the same target once every set period. An auto attack with Martial Cadence hits hardest against a full-health enemy. Land your first auto attack of the trade on the enemy champion. Time your auto attacks around when Martial Cadence can trigger again.
notes.jarvan-phase: You can gank from level 2, once you have EQ. Early jungle clear speed and damage per minute are average. Early on, gain an advantage through early ganks and objective pressure. At level 6, R lets you catch out one enemy. Jarvan IV is strongest through the mid game, as his items come together. In the late game, contribute through engages and trapping enemies more than damage.
notes.jarvan-laning-gank: When ganking, get close enough to put the enemy within EQ range. Gank after your ally's lane has been pushed in. Before ganking, check whether the enemy has used their mobility ability. Place your flag in advance, then use only Q when the enemy approaches.
notes.jarvan-teamfight: In teamfights, trap one enemy backline damage dealer with R. Use R where your allies can follow up immediately. If an ally is engaged on first, use R to stop the enemy engager.
notes.jarvan-teamfight-object: In objective fights, place your flag in advance to increase your allies' attack speed. In objective fights, save EQ for the enemy's approach route.
notes.jarvan-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Trapping an enemy with R lets you stay close and fight, making it easier to maintain Grievous Wounds.
notes.vs-jarvan-eq: When you see the flag, immediately move away from it to dodge the Q dash that may follow. Q without a flag is a short poke.
notes.vs-jarvan-flag-wall: Jarvan IV can dash to a flag thrown over a thin wall to cross it. When Jarvan IV disappears from vision, position with possible approaches over walls in mind.
notes.vs-jarvan-r: Jarvan IV can recast R to remove the wall himself. If trapped by R, escape with a movement ability that crosses walls. If trapped by R, do not circle indecisively along the wall.
notes.vs-jarvan-w: Jarvan IV's W shield grows stronger with more enemy champions nearby. If Jarvan IV uses W among several enemies, wait until the shield is gone before dealing finishing damage.
notes.vs-jarvan-passive: Jarvan IV's first auto attack deals bonus damage based on current health. Martial Cadence's bonus damage can trigger on the same target only once every set period. Right after taking Jarvan IV's first auto attack is a window to trade back.
notes.vs-jarvan-early: Jarvan IV can gank from level 2, once he has EQ. Early on, establish vision first in bushes that give Jarvan IV an EQ angle. Do not push the lane too far early on. Jarvan IV is most dangerous through the mid game, as his items come together. In the late game, Jarvan IV's ability to trap a target with R is more threatening than his damage.
notes.jax-combo-engage: Engage with E → Q → recast E mid-leap → auto attack → W → auto attack. Activate E before Q to stun almost as soon as you land, before the opponent can disengage. If you need to guarantee the stun, use Flash and recast E together as soon as E can be recast.
notes.jax-skill-e-core: E dodges all basic attacks except turret attacks for its duration. E's recast damage increases in proportion to the number of attacks dodged. Activate E just as the opponent starts their auto attack animation. E also dodges bonus damage and crowd control carried by basic attacks. You can choose when to recast E. Approach with E active, feint a retreat, then immediately jump in with Q or Flash to reduce the opponent's reaction time. During a gank, activate E immediately when two enemies attack you at once.
notes.jax-skill-e-vs-melee: Jax has the advantage in level 1 trades against melee opponents. E dodges enemy and minion basic attacks, the main sources of damage in level 1 trades. Use the health advantage gained from a level 1 trade against a melee opponent to get through the rest of the laning phase.
notes.jax-skill-e-vs-ranged: Against ranged opponents, save E for an all-in you can reliably win or for responding to a gank instead of spending it on a single poke. After using E against a ranged opponent, stay outside their range until its cooldown ends, even if you have to give up CS. Against ranged opponents, look for opportunities to engage with Q. When engaging a ranged opponent, activate E just before Q so the stun follows your landing.
notes.jax-skill-e-limit: E's dodge only applies to basic attacks. Of ability damage, E only partially reduces area-of-effect ability damage. Against opponents who mainly deal magic damage with abilities, do not assume E will let you withstand their damage. Against opponents who mainly deal magic damage with abilities, activate R as you enter combat to gain armor and magic resistance. Use E to negate the opponent's key basic attacks or crowd control carried by basic attacks.
notes.jax-skill-q: Use Q primarily to engage and disengage rather than to deal damage. Q targets units and can also be used on minions and wards. Use a pre-placed ward as an escape route with Q. Against melee opponents, start trades by moving into range and save Q to chase or disengage. When the opponent advances away from their turret, use Q to land on their retreat path.
notes.jax-skill-r: R's passive deals bonus magic damage on every third consecutive attack. Keep attacking without breaking your auto attack rhythm to make use of R's bonus damage. R's active grants more armor and magic resistance based on the number of champions hit. Use R from a position where it can hit multiple enemy champions. Both W and R have AP ratios. W and R's AP ratios let Jax make efficient use of items that grant both attack damage and ability power.
notes.jax-phase: Jax is strong in level 1 melee slugfests. Jax is weakest at levels 2–5 because he lacks poke, farming abilities, and sustain. Jax gets a sharp power spike at level 6 when he learns R. Jax gets a sharp power spike when he completes his first core item. Late game, with passive stacks and items built up, Jax excels in head-on fights against champions who rely on basic attacks. As the game goes on, Jax lacks damage against tanks who build both health and armor.
notes.jax-situational-item: Choose situational items based on how you are dying. If an enemy auto attack carry is doing well, use Frozen Heart to reduce their attack speed and help you trade blows after E ends. If magic burst kills you before you can act, use Banshee's Veil to block the opening ability. Against a team composition that kills you as soon as you are crowd controlled, use Sterak's Gage to survive.
notes.jax-laning: Aim to get through the laning phase without falling behind. Start trades with passive stacks already built up. When E is on cooldown, farm from outside the opponent's range. Position yourself between the opponent and their turret first to make E and Q easier to land. If you need a safe recall window, use E's recast area damage to push the wave into the enemy turret.
notes.jax-teamfight: Use Q to jump into grouped enemies and stun several of them with E. When entering a teamfight, activate E before leaping with Q. To survive, go in second, following an ally's crowd control or engage. If there is no reason to start a teamfight, push side-lane turrets to draw enemy defenders.
notes.vs-jax-e: Do not use basic attacks while Jax's E is active. Jax's E also dodges bonus damage and crowd control carried by basic attacks. Jax's E deals more recast damage for each attack it dodges. When Jax activates E, back out of its stun range and wait for its duration to end. Save your mobility ability to get out of Jax's E range. Since Jax's E does not block ability damage itself, plan your trades around abilities.
notes.vs-jax-bait: Jax can activate E, feint an approach, then retreat to bait out the opponent's mobility ability or ultimate. Do not spend your escape or defensive ability just because Jax activates E. After Jax's E ends, use its cooldown window to trade. Pressure Jax with your jungler while his E is unavailable.
notes.vs-jax-early: Jax has a weak laning phase because he lacks poke, farming abilities, and healing. Avoid forcing melee trades at level 1, when Jax has the advantage. From level 2 onward, build a CS and level lead over Jax. Secure an advantage before Jax gets stronger by learning R at level 6 and completing his first core item.
notes.vs-jax-ranged: When playing a ranged champion against Jax, whittle down his health with auto attack poke. Even when poking with a ranged champion, stop auto attacking while Jax's E is active. Jax gains attack speed with successive basic attacks, increasing his damage. Repeat short trades instead of prolonged fights to disrupt Jax's basic attack rhythm. Jax can use minions or wards as stepping stones to engage with Q. Avoid standing next to minion groups so Jax cannot use Q to close in. Watch how many allied minions remain in front of Jax while staying outside his Q range.
notes.vs-jax-teamfight: When Jax engages, avoid grouping up nearby so his E's area stun does not hit you together. If Jax engages with E active, use your abilities after E's duration ends. Immediately after Jax's E stun ends, focus crowd control on him to kill him. If Jax pushes a side-lane turret, split your team to pressure his team's territory and trade objectives instead of forcing a duel.
notes.jax-combo-trade: For short trades, use basic attack → W → basic attack. W resets your basic attack timer. Press W before the basic attack animation finishes to cancel it. Hit minions before trading to stack your passive. After activating R, time W with the bonus damage from consecutive attacks to concentrate your burst damage.
notes.jayce-combo-gate-poke: In cannon form, place E Acceleration Gate and fire Q Shock Blast through it. Q gains range, movement speed, and damage when it passes through the gate. Minimize the delay between E and Q so it hits before the opponent sees the gate and dodges.
notes.jayce-combo-allin: After landing cannon Q, use R to switch to hammer, then attack with Q leap, a basic attack, W Lightning Field, and E knockback, in that order. Your first basic attack right after switching to hammer deals bonus magic damage. Basic attack immediately after switching to hammer.
notes.jayce-combo-shred: Your first basic attack after switching from hammer to cannon lowers the opponent’s armor and magic resistance. After your melee combo, switch to cannon and land one basic attack as you disengage. Lowering their resistances with a cannon swap basic attack strengthens your follow-up Q poke and your allies’ damage.
notes.jayce-combo-e-knockback: Hammer E knocks the opponent back. To keep chasing, knock the opponent toward your allies or a wall. Angle E so you don’t knock the opponent out of your range and interrupt your combo. Use hammer E to push out an opponent who dives under your turret or to peel off an enemy engaging on you.
notes.jayce-skill-passive: Each weapon swap briefly increases your movement speed. Keep swapping weapons while moving to dodge the opponent’s poke or close the distance. Keep the swap cooldown running to reduce the time needed to prepare your combo.
notes.jayce-skill-r-defense: Hammer form increases your armor and magic resistance. Switch to hammer form when you’re likely to take heavy damage or get caught.
notes.jayce-skill-q-cannon: Cannon Q explodes on hitting an enemy or reaching the end of its range, dealing area damage. Fire cannon Q so its explosion overlaps where the opponent is moving. Cannon Q passes through minions and can hit an opponent behind them.
notes.jayce-skill-e-gate: Allies also gain movement speed when they pass through Acceleration Gate. Place Acceleration Gate along your allies’ path when following up on a gank or retreating.
notes.jayce-skill-w: Hammer W’s passive restores mana with every hammer basic attack. When mana is tight, clear minions in hammer form. Cannon W speeds up your next few attacks. Save cannon W for attacking objectives or pressuring turrets.
notes.jayce-phase: Jayce can use both forms from level 1, so he is strongest early. Build a lead in the early to mid game by securing lane advantage and objectives.
notes.jayce-laning: Farm in cannon form while poking with Q from outside the opponent’s range. Keep the wave near the middle and disrupt the opponent’s last hits. If the opponent closes in, switch to hammer to raise your armor, then counter with a Q leap and E knockback.
notes.jayce-teamfight: Open teamfights by poking with cannon Q from the back. Go in briefly only when the enemy formation breaks up. Switch to hammer, combo the backline, then immediately switch to cannon and disengage.
notes.jayce-situational-antiheal: Buy Executioner’s Calling if the opponent sustains through your damage with healing. Jayce’s poke comes in separate hits, so without stopping the opponent’s healing, the health you chipped away comes back.
notes.jayce-situational-mercurial: If the opponent opens with crowd control that locks you down, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. Jayce can easily die when caught by crowd control that locks him down.
notes.vs-jayce-stance: Adjust your response based on Jayce’s weapon form. If Jayce holds his cannon, he’s preparing ranged poke; if he holds his hammer, he’s preparing to leap in and knock you back.
notes.vs-jayce-gate: When Jayce places Acceleration Gate, he may soon fire Shock Blast. As soon as you see Acceleration Gate, sidestep out of the line to dodge the empowered Q.
notes.vs-jayce-early: Jayce is strongest early. If you fall behind early, farm defensively and stall until your power spike.
notes.vs-jayce-squishy: Use the moment after Jayce leaps with To the Skies! (hammer Q) and has no mobility as an opening to engage. Bait out Jayce’s hammer Q leap, then close in.
notes.vs-jayce-poke: Jayce’s cannon Q passes through minions, so it can hit you even behind them. Move side to side while farming to avoid cannon Q’s path. If your health gets low, clear the wave and recall instead of staying in lane.
notes.jhin-skill-passive: Jhin has a fixed attack speed. His final shot always critically strikes. His final shot deals more damage based on the target's missing health. Landing his final shot increases his movement speed.
notes.jhin-skill-reload: Jhin can use abilities while reloading. Jhin is most vulnerable while reloading after using all his shots. Use Q, W, and E to fill the gap between attacks while reloading. Last-hitting with an ability refreshes the empowered state's duration, delaying the reload. In a dangerous position, use abilities instead of basic attacks to secure CS.
notes.jhin-skill-q-bounce: Q bounces to the nearest target it has not yet hit. Q does not prioritize low-health targets or champions. Plan Q's bounce path around target positions and the number of targets. Each target Q kills during a bounce increases the damage of its next hit. Set up Q so its final bounce hits a champion.
notes.jhin-skill-q-timing: Q's travel time between bounces depends on the distance between targets. If Q's targets are far enough apart, there is time to add a basic attack between bounces. While Q is bouncing, lower a target's health with a basic attack to strengthen a later bounce.
notes.jhin-skill-w: W has very long range. When aiming W, account for its cast time rather than travel time after firing. W is very narrow, making it easy to dodge. Use W after an ally's immobilizing effect or your trap has hit. Before approaching a fight, look for a target you can hit with W from afar.
notes.jhin-skill-w-root: W roots only targets recently hit by Jhin's basic attack, his trap, or an ally's attack. Targets outside W's range do not receive a mark. Targets do not receive a mark before W is learned. To root a target with W, first mark them with a basic attack or trap.
notes.jhin-skill-e: E stops recharging when both charges are available. Keep one E charge for escaping or following up. Place spare E traps in bushes and along the river to block gank routes in advance. E traps slow enemies who step on them. Place E in areas without vision to reveal them.
notes.jhin-skill-e-stack: When an enemy steps on overlapping traps, the rear trap usually deals reduced damage. If two traps are placed in exactly the same spot, they explode together and deal full damage. Stack traps only in front of objectives where you know exactly where enemies will enter.
notes.jhin-skill-r: R grows stronger as the target's missing health increases. Do not waste R's high-damage final shot on a target with almost no health left. Roots, slows, and blinds cannot interrupt R. Use R from a safe position where you can avoid stuns or knockbacks that interrupt it.
notes.jhin-skill-r-lane: From far enough away, R's firing cone covers the entire lane. Against an enemy fleeing down a narrow lane, keep your distance and open R.
notes.jhin-combo-lane: Use basic attacks to lower caster minions' health so Q can kill them in succession. Hit a champion with the final bounce of a Q empowered by minion kills, then land the empowered final shot.
notes.jhin-combo-root: Root an enemy caught in an E trap with W, use basic attacks through the final shot, then finish with R if needed. Using W first on an unmarked target deals damage without rooting them.
notes.jhin-phase-early: Jhin is easily pressured by enemies who can close the gap quickly. Early on, threaten your opponent while holding your final shot and securing CS. Jhin is better suited to playing safely early than building up damage on opponents.
notes.jhin-phase-power: Jhin excels at burst damage rather than sustained damage. Once Jhin learns R at level 6, he can join fights outside his lane. As Jhin gets more items, Q and his final shot make it easier to kill fragile targets. Jhin is weak against enemies who build a lot of health. Prioritize less durable enemies as attack targets.
notes.jhin-laning: After using the final shot, retreat out of the enemy's range. Use abilities to secure CS while reloading. Before recalling or leaving to place traps, clear the caster minions with Q to push the wave.
notes.jhin-teamfight: Jhin relies heavily on durable frontline allies who provide immobilizing effects. In teamfights, stay at the back and make full use of your range. In teamfights, use W and R right after an ally's crowd control lands. Jhin has no mobility ability, making it hard to escape when caught. Place traps in advance along routes enemies may use to engage.
notes.jhin-teamfight-scout: If deep vision spots an enemy alone in the jungle, target them from afar with W or R. While waiting for a teamfight, use vision and traps to limit enemy routes.
notes.jhin-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents you from finishing kills, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Upgrade Executioner's Calling to Mortal Reminder against enemies whose healing needs to be reduced. When enemies heal, it becomes harder for Jhin to calculate finishing damage with his final shot and R.
notes.vs-jhin-reload: After firing his set number of shots, Jhin cannot basic attack while reloading. Engage when Jhin is reloading or has fired his first one or two shots. Back off if Jhin still has his final shot. Count Jhin's remaining shots when facing him.
notes.vs-jhin-w-root: W roots only targets recently hit by Jhin's basic attack, his trap, or an attack from one of his allies. Right after Jhin's basic attack hits you or you step on a trap, move out of W's straight path. When the enemy's crowd control lands, check Jhin's position for a follow-up W.
notes.vs-jhin-traps: Jhin places traps that are invisible on the map. E traps explode after a delay, not immediately when stepped on. With enough movement speed, you can pass through a trap before it explodes. Before deliberately stepping on a trap to remove it, check whether Jhin is using it as bait. While on a trap, dodge W to avoid being rooted in its explosion area.
notes.vs-jhin-r: R deals more damage the less health its target has. R's final shot deals more damage than its other shots. When low on health, prioritize dodging R shots. If an ally must block an R shot, the ally with the highest current health percentage should take it.
notes.vs-jhin-q-bounce: Each target Q kills while bouncing strengthens its next hit. Stay away from low-health allies and minions so an empowered Q cannot bounce to you.
notes.vs-jhin-tank-lead: Jhin struggles to kill enemies who build a lot of health. When advancing on Jhin, have your frontline go first and block W and R shots. The frontline should step on traps first so the damage dealers behind them can approach safely.
notes.jinx-combo-rocket-poke: Switch Q to rockets, then basic attack a minion next to the enemy champion. Rocket basic attacks deal full damage to every enemy in the blast radius. To poke a champion without drawing minion aggro, hit an adjacent minion with a rocket basic attack.
notes.jinx-combo-fight: Slow the enemy with W, attack from a distance with rockets, then switch to the minigun if they close in. If an enemy champion gets too close, prioritize attack speed over range.
notes.jinx-combo-escape: When chased, place E behind you along your escape route, then slow the pursuer with W. E's traps root targets as soon as they step on them. Place E traps together in a narrow passage so the pursuer has to pass through them.
notes.jinx-skill-q-rocket: Q rockets increase basic attack range. Q rocket basic attacks deal area damage. Q rocket basic attacks cost mana. Attack speed is slower while using Q rockets. Use rockets only to poke, clear waves, siege turrets, or attack grouped enemies; use the minigun otherwise.
notes.jinx-skill-q-minigun: The minigun builds attack speed stacks with consecutive basic attacks. The minigun is strongest at full attack speed stacks. When a fight looks likely, build minigun stacks in advance, even if you have to attack minions.
notes.jinx-skill-w: W attacks from very long range. W reveals the location of the first enemy it hits. Use W to check vision in brush or ahead of an objective. Slow the enemy with W before moving in. Once minigun stacks increase your attack speed, W's cast time gets shorter, making it easier to land.
notes.jinx-skill-e: E has a long cooldown. Jinx relies on E to protect herself. Save E for an enemy engage instead of spending it on poke. To deter an enemy engage, place E in a narrow passage near an objective or at a brush entrance in advance.
notes.jinx-skill-r: R deals more damage the farther it travels. R deals bonus damage based on the target's missing health. Use R to finish off fleeing enemies or enemies in other lanes from afar, rather than enemies right in front of you.
notes.jinx-skill-passive: Get Excited! triggers on champion takedowns, epic monster kills, and structure destruction. Right after destroying a turret, Get Excited! greatly increases movement speed. Right after destroying a turret, Get Excited! greatly increases attack speed. Use the moment after taking down a turret to move to the next objective or chase an enemy.
notes.jinx-phase-early: Jinx is not strong at gaining an early lane advantage. Early on, focus on rocket poke and safe CS to reach your item timing sooner instead of forcing trades.
notes.jinx-phase-late: Jinx uses Get Excited! to turn a fight win into an advantage in the next fight. After winning a late game teamfight, use Get Excited! to keep control of the game.
notes.jinx-laning-mana: Rocket basic attacks consume mana with every attack. To conserve mana, use rockets only for poke and take routine CS with the minigun. When Jinx runs out of mana, she struggles to clear waves and protect herself. Find a chance to recall before running out of mana.
notes.jinx-teamfight: When a teamfight starts, poke with rockets and W from the edge of the fight. Move in with the minigun only once you're sure it's safe. Jinx has no dash and struggles to survive once caught. Jinx relies on positioning to deal enough damage in teamfights.
notes.jinx-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Executioner's Calling is effective because rocket basic attacks can apply Grievous Wounds to multiple enemies at once.
notes.vs-jinx-minigun: Jinx's minigun needs time to build attack speed stacks. Use the moment Jinx pokes with rockets as an opening to engage while she has no minigun stacks. When Jinx pokes with rockets, close in and kill her with burst damage.
notes.vs-jinx-r: Jinx's R deals less damage the closer you are to her. If Jinx tries to finish you with R, move out of its attack area or close in on her.
notes.vs-jinx-e: Jinx's E has a long cooldown. Jinx relies almost entirely on E to protect herself. Engage after Jinx misses or uses E.
notes.vs-jinx-mobility: Jinx has no dash. Save your engage ability until Jinx has used her defensive tools. Engage as soon as Jinx misses her W slow. Bait out Jinx's E, then engage.
notes.vs-jinx-passive: Jinx gains a large movement speed boost right after a takedown or destroying a structure. Jinx gains a large attack speed boost right after a takedown or destroying a structure. Avoid fighting right after an ally dies or a turret is destroyed and triggers Jinx's Get Excited!.
notes.vs-jinx-rocket-splash: Jinx's rocket basic attacks also deal full damage to enemies near the target. When Jinx uses rockets to take CS, keep your distance from the minions.
notes.ksante-combo-q-shockwave: Each Q hit builds a stack. At full stacks, the next Q becomes a shockwave that pulls in and stuns enemies. Hitting minions also builds Q stacks. Hit the wave with Q just before a fight to build stacks in advance.
notes.ksante-combo-w-timing: K'Sante is unstoppable while charging W. K'Sante takes reduced damage while charging W. Start charging W as the enemy's combo lands to reduce the damage. Charging W longer increases the stun duration. Only charge W for a long time after the enemy has used their mobility ability or been caught by the Q shockwave, so they cannot simply walk away.
notes.ksante-combo-allin: Build Q stacks, pull the enemy in with the shockwave, then chain a W stun, R toward a wall, E to close the gap again, an auto attack, and Q. Each ability leaves a passive mark. Weave an auto attack between abilities to get the full passive damage.
notes.ksante-skill-r-transform: Using R transforms K'Sante into his All Out form. If R pushes an enemy into a wall, they fly through it and take an additional hit. Use R on enemies with terrain behind them to get the additional hit. In All Out, K'Sante loses a large amount of maximum health and bonus armor and magic resistance. Only use R when the enemy's main crowd control is down and your team can follow up immediately.
notes.ksante-skill-r-upgrades: In All Out, Q and E have shorter cooldowns. In All Out, E dashes faster. Entering All Out resets W's cooldown. In All Out, W gains true damage. In All Out, W does not knock back or stun enemies. Use all your crowd control for holding enemies in place before activating R. After entering All Out, focus on staying close to the enemy and attacking.
notes.ksante-skill-q-scaling: Q deals more damage as armor and magic resistance increase. Q's cooldown decreases as armor and magic resistance increase. Prioritize defensive items over attack items to improve both Q's damage and cooldown.
notes.ksante-skill-e-ally: Using E on an allied champion greatly increases its dash range. Using E on an allied champion also shields that ally. Save E to reach and shield an ally who gets caught.
notes.ksante-skill-passive: Proc the passive marks left by your abilities with auto attacks. Finish trades with an auto attack after an ability. In All Out, both auto attacks and abilities gain damage based on maximum health. In All Out, keep using abilities and stay on the enemy to attack.
notes.ksante-phase: Levels 1–2 are K'Sante's weakest point because he has only Q to rely on. Start trading at level 3, once you have W and E. At level 6, look for a solo kill when you can drive the enemy into terrain with R. K'Sante is strong in the mid game as defensive items improve Q's damage and cooldown. In the late game, focus on engaging and crowd control over damage.
notes.ksante-laning-farm: Keep the wave in the middle of the lane instead of forcing a push. Last-hit minions with Q. Build Q stacks and catch the enemy with the shockwave only when they move among the minions. Focus on surviving and preventing the enemy jungler from intervening instead of repeatedly taking short trades.
notes.ksante-laning-trade: After slowing the enemy with Q, proc the mark with an auto attack, then retreat with E if they fight back. Keep E available for disengaging so you have a way out after going in. Only use E to dive in right after the enemy uses a mobility ability or key ability.
notes.ksante-teamfight-r: In teamfights, prioritize using R to push one enemy backline damage dealer toward your team and isolate them. Using R in a teamfight also leaves K'Sante in the middle of the enemy team. K'Sante becomes less durable the moment he uses R. Only use R when your team is close enough to follow up immediately. If your team is not ready, save R and hold the front line with the Q shockwave and W stun.
notes.ksante-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between defensive items. Because K'Sante spends a long time fighting up close in All Out, it is easy to keep applying a healing reduction item's effect.
notes.ksante-situational-mr: If the enemy's main damage is magic, buy Spectre's Cowl or Spirit Visage earlier. Magic resistance items provide defense while improving Q's damage and cooldown.
notes.vs-ksante-r-window: When K'Sante activates All Out, his maximum health and bonus armor and magic resistance drop significantly. Focus your damage on K'Sante the moment he activates All Out. K'Sante deals more damage in All Out. K'Sante gains more lifesteal in All Out. Do not face K'Sante alone in All Out.
notes.vs-ksante-r-wall: If K'Sante's R drives you into a wall, you are pushed through the terrain toward K'Sante's team's side. If K'Sante's R drives you into a wall, you take an additional hit. When facing K'Sante, position without terrain behind you to reduce R's impact.
notes.vs-ksante-q: Once K'Sante has enough Q hit stacks, his next Q becomes a shockwave that pulls in and stuns enemies. If you have been hit by consecutive Qs, move out of range of the next Q or save a mobility ability to dodge it. K'Sante can also build Q stacks by hitting minions. Watch the Q stack indicator on K'Sante.
notes.vs-ksante-w: K'Sante is unstoppable while charging W. K'Sante takes reduced damage while charging W. When you see K'Sante charging W, hold off on using crowd control and focusing your damage. Watch the direction of W's dash and sidestep it. The longer K'Sante charges W, the longer the knockback and stun last.
notes.vs-ksante-early: K'Sante is weakest at levels 1–2, when he only has Q. Chip away at K'Sante's health during his weak levels 1–2. K'Sante's Q deals more damage as he builds defensive items. K'Sante's Q cooldown decreases as he builds defensive items.
notes.vs-ksante-omnivamp: In All Out, K'Sante heals from all damage he deals. If you expect a long close-range fight with K'Sante, make sure at least one teammate has a way to reduce healing. Do not let K'Sante keep attacking while surrounded by multiple allies in All Out.
notes.kaisa-skill-passive: Stack Plasma with basic attacks and W. At maximum stacks, Plasma detonates, dealing magic damage based on the target's missing health. Detonating Plasma after the target has lost more health is more effective. Plasma also gains a stack when an ally immobilizes the target. With a support who has hard CC, count your Plasma stacks one step ahead.
notes.kaisa-skill-w: W has very long range. W costs a lot of mana, so missing it hurts your laning. Hitting a champion with W refunds most of its cooldown. Use W only when you are confident it will hit. W grants true sight of the target it hits, revealing their position even after they hide in brush or stealth.
notes.kaisa-skill-q-wave: Q deals much more damage to low-health minions. Before recalling or roaming, use basic attacks to lower minions' health evenly, then clear the wave with Q. When you need to let the wave push toward you, avoid using Q to farm.
notes.kaisa-skill-q-target: Q missiles automatically split among and track nearby enemies. Repeated Q missile hits on the same target deal much less damage. Q is most effective when only one enemy champion is in range. If minions and champions are together, Q missiles split between them, weakening your trade. Use Q to trade when the enemy steps away from the wave.
notes.kaisa-skill-e: E's charge time decreases as attack speed increases. Early on, when attack speed is low, E charges slowly and is hard to rely on for escape. Activating E lets you pass through units. After activating E, move through the minions. Each basic attack reduces E's cooldown.
notes.kaisa-skill-r: R can dash only to enemies with a Plasma mark. Apply a Plasma mark with W or a basic attack before using R to engage. Save R for finishing enemies and adjusting your angle.
notes.kaisa-combo-poke: For a poke combo, use W, follow with a basic attack, and finish with Q. W applies multiple Plasma stacks, setting up a detonation with one or two basic attacks. Time Q to hit as Plasma detonates. If W misses, save Q and retreat.
notes.kaisa-combo-allin: For an all-in, approach with E, stack Plasma with basic attacks, then use Q last. Use E's unit passing and movement speed boost during its charge to close the gap. Time the final Q's damage to overlap with the Plasma detonation. Using Q before you approach lets the enemy back away, causing the missiles to split among minions.
notes.kaisa-combo-r-entry: For a long-range engage, apply a mark with W, wait for the enemy to use their response ability, then follow with R and finish with basic attacks and Q. Use R after the enemy has reacted to your ally's engage by using their immobilizing and counterattack abilities. If the enemy still has a way to counterattack, avoid using R immediately after W hits.
notes.kaisa-phase-early: Kai'Sa is weakest at levels 1–2. At levels 1–2, prioritize safe farming over trading. At levels 1–2, chip away at the enemy's health with W poke. Learning R at level 6 does not give Kai'Sa an immediate power spike.
notes.kaisa-phase-evolution: Kai'Sa's power spikes depend more on completed items than on levels. Abilities evolve when their stat thresholds are met. Kai'Sa grows stronger with each completed core item. Until your first core item, focus on avoiding losses. After completing your second core item, start fights proactively.
notes.kaisa-laning: In lane, let the wave push toward you and poke with W. When the enemy marksman pushes the lane, farm CS from behind. When you need to push, clear the damaged wave at once with Q. Recall or secure vision right after clearing the wave with Q.
notes.kaisa-teamfight: Start teamfights from the back by applying marks with W. After the enemy frontline has used all its immobilizing abilities and engage tools on your frontline, use E and R to find an angle to enter. After entering a teamfight, detonate Plasma with basic attacks. Before entering with R, check whether E is available for your escape.
notes.kaisa-teamfight-vs-stealth: Against stealth champions, land W just before a fight to keep track of their position. Landing W on a stealth champion gives you a chance to chase them with R.
notes.kaisa-situational-antiheal: If the enemy's healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling after your first core item. Upgrade Executioner's Calling to Mortal Reminder for healing reduction. Healing reduction items work well because repeated basic attacks keep the effect active.
notes.kaisa-situational-mercurial: If the enemy team can lock Kai'Sa down with immobilizing effects, buy Quicksilver Sash earlier. Kai'Sa relies on E and R to find an engage angle, so immobilizing her can stop her engage.
notes.vs-kaisa-r-mark: Kai'Sa's R can dash only to targets with a Plasma mark. Right after Kai'Sa's W hits is the most dangerous time for her to engage with R. If W hits you, retreat toward your allies until the Plasma mark disappears to deny Kai'Sa an R angle.
notes.vs-kaisa-q-minions: Kai'Sa's Q missiles split among nearby enemies. Kai'Sa's Q missiles deal less damage with each additional hit on the same target. If Kai'Sa looks ready to use Q, stay near allied minions to split the missiles.
notes.vs-kaisa-early: Kai'Sa is weakest at levels 1–2. At levels 1–2, push the lane to make it harder for Kai'Sa to farm CS. At levels 1–2, lower Kai'Sa's health to delay her item progression.
notes.vs-kaisa-plasma: Plasma's detonation damage increases as the target's health decreases. If you have Plasma stacks and about half your health remains, the next one or two basic attacks could deal heavy damage. When you have Plasma stacks, stay out of range until they disappear.
notes.vs-kaisa-e-vision: Evolved E gives Kai'Sa brief stealth. Before a fight, place Control Wards in side brush and along approach routes to prepare for a flank from Kai'Sa. Draw Kai'Sa near a turret to reveal her while she is stealthed.
notes.vs-kaisa-burst: Immediately after Kai'Sa enters with R, immobilize and kill her before her shield wears off. If you fail to stop Kai'Sa's R engage, she deals sustained damage with basic attacks.
notes.kalista-skill-passive-hop: Issue a move command during an auto attack or Q windup to hop in that direction. Keep moving by hopping as you auto attack. The more attack speed you have, the more often you hop in the same amount of time. Kalista's mobility depends on how often she auto attacks.
notes.kalista-skill-passive-limit: A single move command to hop keeps your original auto attack target. You cannot hop if there is no target within attack range. Attack speed slows also reduce the distance you travel by hopping.
notes.kalista-skill-e-lasthit: Killing a target with E resets its cooldown and refunds mana. Kill multiple speared minions with E to clear the wave and reset its cooldown.
notes.kalista-skill-e-stacks: E's damage depends on how many spears are in the target. Stack spears during a trade, then use E when the enemy retreats. Use E before the spears disappear or the enemy gets completely out of range.
notes.kalista-skill-q: If Q kills the first target it hits, it passes through and leaves spear stacks on the next target. Check the front minion's health, then use Q to clear the wave and stack spears on a target behind it. You can hop with Martial Poise during Q's cast animation. Choose your hop direction as you fire Q to retreat or close in.
notes.kalista-skill-w: W's passive triggers only when you and your Oathsworn attack the same target. During trades, attack the same target as your support. Use W's active to scout around objectives or enemy jungle entrances.
notes.kalista-skill-r: Coordinate your R plan with your Oathsworn support before using it. Use R to pull in and rescue an allied support in danger of being caught. Your Oathsworn cannot act while in stasis, so use R when your team is ready.
notes.kalista-combo-trade: Stack spears with Q, maintain distance with auto attacks and hops, then use E when the enemy retreats. If the enemy closes in, keep auto attacking while hopping backward. If the enemy retreats, hop forward to stay within attack range.
notes.kalista-combo-wave-finish: Kill a speared minion with E to reset its cooldown, then use E again on the enemy champion.
notes.kalista-phase: Kalista is strong at early lane pressure and harass when she levels E first. Kalista dies easily early on. Kalista is strongest in the mid game as she builds attack speed items. Kalista remains vulnerable to immobilization and heavy slows late in the game.
notes.kalista-laning: During laning, harass while hopping near minions.
notes.kalista-teamfight: In teamfights, hop just behind the front line and deal sustained damage. Hop backward as soon as an enemy with an engage ability closes in. Stack spears on one target, then use E when that target retreats. Look for chances to use R to rescue an ally in teamfights.
notes.kalista-situational-qss: When Kalista is rooted, her auto attacks and hops are interrupted. If the enemy has a root, consider Quicksilver Sash before defensive items to preserve your ability to hop.
notes.kalista-situational-antiheal: Choose Executioner's Calling if the enemy team has a champion with healing. Kalista relies on sustained auto attack damage, so she can keep Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.vs-kalista-poise: Push Kalista out of attack range to stop her from hopping. Lower Kalista's attack speed to reduce the distance she travels by hopping.
notes.vs-kalista-windup: Kalista cannot cancel her auto attack windup. Predict when Kalista will start an auto attack to hop, then use a skillshot.
notes.vs-kalista-vision: If Kalista loses vision of you, even an auto attack already in flight will miss. Move into brush or behind a wall to reduce the damage from Kalista's auto attacks.
notes.vs-kalista-rend: If spears are embedded in you, Kalista's E can hit you even outside its range. If spear stacks have built up on you, leave the lane until they disappear.
notes.vs-kalista-r: If Kalista's Oathsworn support stays close beside her, prepare for them to be thrown with R. Prepare crowd control where Kalista's thrown Oathsworn is expected to land. Spread out in advance to prepare for Kalista's R.
notes.vs-kalista-catch: Kalista relies on hopping for mobility, so she has trouble escaping once caught. When you have an opening to engage, catch Kalista immediately with forced movement or immobilization.
notes.karma-skill-passive: Damaging an enemy champion with an ability reduces Mantra's cooldown. When you can poke, land abilities to keep Mantra cycling.
notes.karma-skill-r-early: Mantra is available from level 1 without a skill point. If a level 1–2 fight breaks out, use your advantage from having an empowered ability.
notes.karma-skill-q: Q damages and slows the first target hit and nearby enemies. Minions block Q. Look for Q when the enemy champion steps out from behind the minion wave. Hitting an enemy champion with Q reduces Mantra's cooldown. Place Mantra Q's burning zone where the enemy has to stay.
notes.karma-skill-w: W only roots if the tether stays connected. Use W when you've slowed the enemy with Q or can keep up with E. Mantra W restores missing health and extends the root duration. When you're caught, use Mantra W to survive.
notes.karma-skill-e: E grants both a shield and movement speed. Cast E on an ally just before they go in or pull back. Mantra E also shields nearby allies.
notes.karma-combo-engage: Slow with Q, root with W, then use E to help your ally move in while they attack. If you can't get close, cast E on yourself for movement speed, then move into W range.
notes.karma-combo-mantra-q: Mantra Q's burning zone detonates shortly after the first explosion. Use Mantra Q on an enemy rooted by W. Use Mantra Q while an ally's crowd control holds the enemy in place. If you poke with Mantra Q without any crowd control, the enemy can walk out of the zone.
notes.karma-phase: Karma can use Mantra from level 1, making her relatively strongest in early 2v2 fights. Single-target burst has less impact later in the game. Later in the game, keep allies alive with area shields and movement speed.
notes.karma-laning-mana: Using Q and E carelessly will leave you short on mana by the middle of the laning phase. Use Q only when you have a chance to hit an enemy champion. Don't waste Q just to clear minions.
notes.karma-laning-disengage: As support Karma, focus on peeling against engages in lane. When the enemy support engages, use W to catch the engaging champion and E to get your allied marksman out.
notes.karma-roaming: E's movement speed makes roaming with an ally faster. When preparing for a mid gank or to join an objective fight, save Mantra so you can move together with Mantra E.
notes.karma-teamfight: In teamfights, Gathering Fire can recharge Mantra multiple times. Don't hold back your first Mantra in a teamfight. Use Mantra W when you need to stop an enemy engage. Use Mantra E against teams with area burst damage. Use Mantra Q when you need to secure an already favorable position. After using Mantra, keep landing basic abilities to bring the next Mantra up sooner.
notes.karma-situational-cc: If the enemy team can lock down your carry with immobilizing crowd control, get Mikael's Blessing early. E's shield blocks damage but does not remove crowd control.
notes.karma-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, reduce it with Morellonomicon.
notes.vs-karma-passive: Karma reduces Mantra's cooldown each time she lands an ability. Move behind minions or out of range to avoid Karma's abilities.
notes.vs-karma-mantra-q: The burning zone left by Mantra Q detonates in place after a short delay. If Mantra Q hits you, immediately walk out of the zone.
notes.vs-karma-w-disengage: Karma's W can catch an engaging champion and stop their advance. Keep your distance to draw out Karma's W, then engage.
notes.vs-karma-mantra-w: Mantra W roots only after the tether has been connected for a while. Karma restores missing health while Mantra W is connected. If Mantra W catches you, burst Karma down before the root takes hold. If Mantra W catches you, create distance to break the tether before the root takes hold.
notes.vs-karma-mantra-e: Mantra E shields all nearby allies. Engage after Mantra E's shield expires.
notes.karthus-skill-passive-death: After dying, Karthus can use all his abilities without mana for a short time. If you have little health left, die among the enemies and use E and Q in spirit form. Die near enemies so you can make use of your time in spirit form.
notes.karthus-skill-passive-r: Karthus can use R in spirit form. If you can use R when you die and the enemy is low on health, finish them with R. Do not let your time in spirit form pass without using abilities.
notes.karthus-skill-q: Q deals much more damage when it hits only one enemy. When trading, hit an opponent who is not overlapping with minions with Q. When farming, use Q where multiple targets overlap.
notes.karthus-skill-e: E can be toggled on and off, and it drains mana quickly while active. Keep E on only while close to an opponent, and turn it off as soon as they leave its range. E's passive restores mana whenever Karthus kills an enemy unit. To restore mana, Karthus must last-hit the enemy unit himself. The mana restored by E from killing enemy units is Karthus's only source of mana.
notes.karthus-skill-w: Enemies can pass through W, so it cannot block their path. Enemies who pass through W are heavily slowed and lose magic resistance. Place W where the opponent must pass through it. The magic resistance reduction from W increases the damage of the Q and R that follow.
notes.karthus-skill-r: R damages all enemy champions regardless of distance. R has no effect if its channel is interrupted. Use R from a safe position or when an ally can protect its channel. At the start of a teamfight, use R to lower every enemy's health and help your allies engage. Pressure scattered opponents at the same time with R to go for an objective. Ask your allies how other lanes are doing to time your R.
notes.karthus-combo-basic: For a basic trade, place W along the opponent's escape path, then land Q beyond the wall. Enemies who pass through W lose magic resistance and take more damage from the Q that follows. Enemies slowed by W have a harder time dodging Q's warning indicator.
notes.karthus-combo-melee: In close combat, turn on E, stay close to the opponent, and land Q at their feet. E deals continuous damage while active, so staying close to the opponent increases its damage. In close combat, land Q when the opponent is not overlapping with minions. Turn off E as soon as the fight ends to save mana for the next fight.
notes.karthus-laning-clear: At camps, turn on E and land Q where the monsters overlap. If your mana falls below half, do not force another camp. Karthus's CS at 14 minutes and damage per minute are among the highest of jungle champions. Clear camps and waves instead of repeatedly trying to gank.
notes.karthus-laning-gank: Karthus has no mobility ability or instant immobilizing effect, making it hard for him to pull off a gank alone. Gank when an ally has already immobilized the opponent or the opponent has pushed far up the lane. In other ganks, use W to limit the opponent's escape path and help your allies engage.
notes.karthus-phase: Before level 6, Karthus has no way to escape and is easy for the enemy jungler to catch. From mid game, once Karthus has R and core ability power items, he can affect the entire map. Karthus keeps dealing damage after dying in late-game teamfights.
notes.karthus-teamfight: In teamfights, keep landing Q from the back. In teamfights, position yourself to die as late as possible. If the entire enemy frontline has engaged your allies, turn on E and move in to deal area damage. If you are going to die, die among the enemies to make use of E and Q in spirit form.
notes.karthus-situational-zhonya: If the opponent has a way to jump onto Karthus, buy Zhonya's Hourglass early. Karthus has no mobility ability, so he is easy to catch when an opponent gets close. If an opponent's engage interrupts R's channel, the ultimate has no effect.
notes.karthus-situational-banshee: If the opponent deals heavy magic damage and can interrupt R with a targeted immobilizing effect, buy Banshee's Veil. Blocking the first ability often lets you finish channeling R.
notes.vs-karthus-passive: Karthus can use all his abilities without mana for a short time after dying. Immediately after killing Karthus, move away from his body to avoid Q and E in spirit form. Do not start healing or attacking an objective where you killed Karthus.
notes.vs-karthus-r: Karthus's R damages all enemy champions regardless of distance. After a fight or when returning to lane, keep enough health to survive R. If you are unsure whether you can survive R, recall again.
notes.vs-karthus-q: Karthus's Q deals much more damage when it hits only one enemy. Stand with minions or allies to avoid Q's single-target damage. Walk out of Q's warning area when it appears. When Karthus misses Q while farming, he loses that mana.
notes.vs-karthus-w: Passing through Karthus's W reduces your magic resistance and heavily slows you. After passing through W, you take more damage from Karthus's Q and R. When W is placed, change your escape route to go around it.
notes.vs-karthus-early: Before level 6, Karthus has no mobility ability or immobilizing effect. Disrupt Karthus's growth with jungle invades or early ganks. Karthus clears camps among the fastest, so he grows quickly if left undisturbed early.
notes.vs-karthus-teamfight: Karthus keeps dealing damage in teamfights after dying. If you kill Karthus, reposition immediately. Clear the frontline before Karthus gets within E range.
notes.kassadin-skill-passive: The passive reduces magic damage taken. The passive lets Kassadin ignore unit collision. When chasing, cut through minion waves to take the shortest path.
notes.kassadin-skill-q: Q interrupts enemy channels. Q grants a shield that absorbs magic damage. Time Q to absorb an enemy mage's poke.
notes.kassadin-skill-w: W's passive adds magic damage to basic attacks. Using W greatly empowers the next basic attack. The W-empowered basic attack restores missing mana. W restores much more mana when it hits a champion. In late-game teamfights, use a W-empowered basic attack to get the mana needed for the next R.
notes.kassadin-skill-e: Each nearby spell cast reduces E's cooldown. Position with both a safe distance from poke and E's cooldown reduction in mind.
notes.kassadin-skill-r: Using R repeatedly in a short time doubles its mana cost. Using R repeatedly in a short time increases its damage. Kassadin's sustained damage depends on his remaining mana. Secure the blue Smite buff to ease R's mana cost.
notes.kassadin-combo-burst: For a basic burst combo, enter with R, then use E, a W-empowered basic attack, and Q in that order. After entering, keep the enemy close with E's slow. Use a W-empowered basic attack to restore some mana for the next R. Save Q for the end of the combo to interrupt the enemy's channel.
notes.kassadin-combo-chase: Use R repeatedly when a chase is sure to secure the kill. Before chasing, calculate how many more times you can use R with your remaining mana. When Kassadin runs out of mana, he cannot move with R and is vulnerable to counterattacks.
notes.kassadin-laning-early: Kassadin is vulnerable to one-sided poke at levels 1–5. Early on, focus on securing CS while using Q's shield to absorb magic poke. Keep the early wave near your turret without pushing it. Early on, focus on staying alive and buying time to scale.
notes.kassadin-laning-wave: Nearby spell casts reduce E's cooldown, speeding up waveclear. After pushing the wave, retreat to a warded area to prepare for an attack from the enemy jungler.
notes.kassadin-phase-six: At level 6, Kassadin can turn the lane in his favor once he gets R. R's cooldown drops sharply as its rank increases. Kassadin comes into his own after maxing R. Do not overextend by treating the moment you hit level 6 as your strongest point.
notes.kassadin-phase-late: Kassadin has strong carry potential late in the game. Even if you fall behind early, play to extend the game. In unfavorable matchups, give up some CS if needed to keep leveling safely.
notes.kassadin-teamfight: Do not start teamfights from the front. Once the enemy has used immobilizing abilities on your frontline and their formation breaks, use R to enter their backline. After bursting down the backline, use R to get out. Before entering, set aside R casts for both entry and escape.
notes.kassadin-teamfight-side: Kassadin is suited to side-lane play because R lets him join fights and leave quickly. While no teamfight is happening, collect waves in a side lane. If a fight starts while you are in a side lane, join it.
notes.kassadin-situational-banshee: Against a composition that blocks your entry with magic damage and targeted immobilization, choose Banshee's Veil to create an opening. Banshee's Veil improves survivability alongside the passive's magic damage reduction.
notes.vs-kassadin-early: Before level 6, Kassadin has few ways to reach an enemy. Build a level and CS lead before Kassadin reaches level 6. Push the wave to keep Kassadin under his turret. Pressure Kassadin with your jungler early.
notes.vs-kassadin-r: Kassadin's mana cost doubles as he uses R repeatedly. While chasing, watch Kassadin's mana to calculate how many R casts he has left. Counterattack when Kassadin runs out of mana and cannot use R.
notes.vs-kassadin-q: Kassadin's Q interrupts channels. Kassadin's Q shield absorbs magic damage. Poke with magic damage while Kassadin's Q is on cooldown. Start channeling spells after confirming Kassadin has used Q.
notes.vs-kassadin-e: Each spell cast near Kassadin reduces E's cooldown. Avoid unnecessary spell casts near Kassadin so E does not come back sooner. Clear waves from outside Kassadin's range when possible.
notes.vs-kassadin-passive: Kassadin ignores unit collision, so a wall of minions cannot stop his chase. In a magic-damage-heavy composition, have an ally with immobilization and physical damage lock down Kassadin first.
notes.vs-kassadin-late: Late-game Kassadin attacks the backline with R, then uses R again to escape. Backline champions should build magic resistance against Kassadin. Backline champions should have instant immobilization to respond to Kassadin. Choose Banshee's Veil or Quicksilver Sash to neutralize the first step of Kassadin's entry combo. Do not stand alone within Kassadin's R range.
notes.kata-combo-qe: For the basic combo, wait for the Q dagger to land behind the enemy, then E to it. Picking up a dagger deals passive damage to all nearby enemies. Picking up a dagger almost resets E's cooldown. After Q, check where the dagger will land before using E directly on the enemy.
notes.kata-combo-we: W throws a dagger above Katarina that lands on the ground shortly afterward. Pick up the W dagger while overlapping the enemy to guarantee damage. From a distance, use W, then E to your dagger to recover E's cooldown. Use W as a way to make E available again.
notes.kata-combo-allin: For the full combo, place daggers with W and Q, E to the Q dagger to engage, then pick up the remaining W dagger while using R. Place the two daggers in different spots so you can reposition during R to pick one up.
notes.kata-combo-w-during-r: Use W just before R to deal extra damage without interrupting R. While channeling R, walk to a nearby dagger and pick it up for extra passive damage.
notes.kata-skill-passive: When a champion Katarina recently damaged dies, her passive greatly reduces all her skill cooldowns. As soon as a kill reduces your cooldowns, continue the combo on the next target. In teamfights, kill the lowest-health target first to chain passive resets.
notes.kata-skill-passive-radius: The damage area from picking up a dagger is much larger than the area where you can pick it up. Dagger pickup damage is centered on Katarina, not the dagger's location. Pick up a dagger as you move into the middle of a group of enemies.
notes.kata-skill-q: Q hits its targeted enemy, then bounces to nearby targets. The Q dagger lands behind the first target hit. Q a front minion to poke safely from a distance with the bounce. Account for where the Q dagger will land behind the minion, and decide in advance whether to engage or stop at poke.
notes.kata-skill-e: E can target an enemy, ally, or dagger and move Katarina to a chosen spot near that target. Using E on a dagger brings its cooldown back almost immediately; using it on another target applies the full cooldown. Practice until you have a feel for E's maximum range. Before engaging with E, check for a dagger or ally you can use to escape. E can also leap to jungle plants and interactive objects.
notes.kata-skill-r: R channels rapid attacks against the three nearest enemy champions. R applies healing reduction to enemies it hits. R partially applies on-hit effects, triggering item effects too. Before casting R, check that the enemy's immobilizing skills are on cooldown so crowd control does not interrupt it. If you need to escape, cancel R before it finishes.
notes.kata-phase: Katarina is weak at levels 1–2, when Q has a long cooldown and it is hard to cycle daggers. Start looking for short trades at level 3, once you have both Q and E. Use the increased kill opportunities at level 6, when you learn R, and when you finish your first core item. Katarina spends no separate resource, so she can use her skills continuously. Katarina relies on E leaps for defense, so she can struggle to engage even late in the game against teams with crowd control.
notes.kata-laning: In lane, focus on poking with Q bounces through minions and last-hitting. Avoid forcing the wave to push during lane. Focus on spotting the enemy's mistakes more than on farming. Right after the enemy uses a skill on the wave, try to engage with E using the Q dagger.
notes.kata-laning-reset: Katarina excels at building on a lead by refreshing her skills through takedowns. After clearing the wave, use dagger rotations to join a side lane or objective fight quickly. Each kill makes your next move faster. To make use of her strengths, avoid staying in lane just to farm.
notes.kata-teamfight: Avoid engaging first in teamfights. Engage after the enemy uses its immobilizing skills on your frontline. E to a dagger placed in advance to reach the backline, then use R. Before engaging, secure one escape dagger or an ally you can E to.
notes.kata-teamfight-antiheal: R applies healing reduction to targets it hits. Against an enemy with strong healing, position to include them in R as their healing begins.
notes.vs-kata-dagger: Katarina relies on daggers on the ground to link her damage and movement. Stay away from daggers on the ground to limit Katarina's attack angles. In teamfights, have your whole team stay clear of dagger locations to discourage Katarina from engaging.
notes.vs-kata-q: If Q hits you, its dagger lands behind you. After Q hits you, move toward Katarina to put distance between yourself and the dagger. After Q hits you, avoid retreating in a direction that puts you on the dagger.
notes.vs-kata-r: Keep an immobilizing crowd control skill available to interrupt R's rapid burst of damage. When Katarina starts casting R, interrupt it with crowd control to block most of its damage. When judging whether you can survive R with healing, account for its healing reduction.
notes.vs-kata-e-cd: E has its full cooldown when used on a target other than a dagger. Punish Katarina during E's cooldown after she uses it on a target other than a dagger. Picking up a dagger after using E still reduces E's cooldown. Occupy or block the remaining dagger locations to prevent Katarina from reducing E's cooldown.
notes.vs-kata-mr: Katarina deals most of her damage as magic damage. Even if Katarina builds attack damage items, prioritize magic resistance because most of her damage is magic. R also includes physical damage, so magic resistance alone cannot negate all of its damage.
notes.vs-kata-reset: When Katarina gets a kill, her skill cooldowns decrease and she can immediately engage again. Pull back or protect low-health allies to deny Katarina her first kill.
notes.kayle-phase-early: Kayle is very weak at levels 1–5. At levels 1–5, prioritize survival while securing experience and CS.
notes.kayle-phase-6: At level 6, P increases her basic attack range to ranged. From level 6, use the extra range to harass melee opponents with basic attacks. Manage the wave from late level 5 to reach level 6 before your opponent. Use the moment after reaching level 6 to try trades that were difficult before.
notes.kayle-phase-11: From level 11, basic attacks at maximum P stacks launch fire waves. From level 11, E explodes around the target on hit. At level 11, Kayle gains area damage, making her stronger at wave clear and teamfights. After level 11, push the lane quickly and join objective fights.
notes.kayle-phase-16: At level 16, P's Exalted state remains active permanently. At level 16, P brings her basic attack range to its maximum. At level 16, she gains P's maximum attack speed bonus without stacking it first. Kayle aims to scale into the late game, reaching her full fighting strength at level 16. Before level 16, avoid rushing into decisive fights.
notes.kayle-phase-tradeoff: Kayle's fighting strength depends heavily on her level. Avoid dying and leaving the lane so you do not delay your level milestones. Avoid joining fights if it means losing wave experience. Early on, avoid joining counterjungling attempts to prevent experience loss. If your team can buy time, farm CS in a side lane to scale.
notes.kayle-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use Q, then an E empowered basic attack, and follow with regular basic attacks. Q's armor and magic resistance reduction helps increase the damage of follow-up basic attacks and E. E empowers the next basic attack. E increases the range of the next basic attack. Right after a basic attack hits, use E before its recovery animation ends to bring forward the next basic attack.
notes.kayle-combo-stack: Before level 16, attack minions or jungle monsters to reach maximum P stacks before starting a fight. Prestacking P gives you its maximum attack speed bonus from the start of a fight. At levels 11–15, prestacking P lets you use fire waves from the start of a fight.
notes.kayle-skill-q: Q stops at the first enemy hit but also damages enemies behind them. Use Q's slow and resistance reduction to follow up on allied ganks. When escaping, use Q to slow pursuing enemies. Before level 6, avoid using Q for unnecessary minion clearing or poke so you can respond to ganks.
notes.kayle-skill-w: Prioritize W's movement speed boost over its heal. Use W's movement speed boost to escape ganks or enemy engages. If you do not select a target, W targets the most injured ally. When you need to survive, target yourself directly with W.
notes.kayle-skill-e: E adds magic damage to basic attacks even when you do not activate it. Activating E makes the next basic attack deal bonus damage based on the target's missing health. Use E on a damaged opponent rather than one at full health. E applies on-hit effects and magic item effects. From level 11, use E's explosion to clear waves.
notes.kayle-skill-r: R grants damage immunity to one ally, including Kayle herself. R deals area damage around its target. Crowd control can still affect a target during R's damage immunity. Use R on an ally as their engage reaches the enemy team.
notes.kayle-laning: Before level 6, avoid trades. Before level 6, stay behind the wave and only last-hit. Before level 6, save Q for escaping. If your opponent engages, retreat using Q and W. If your health falls below half, prioritize staying inside your turret's range over CS.
notes.kayle-laning-wave: Before level 6, keep the wave near your turret. Avoid farming in front of the enemy turret, where you are exposed to ganks. After level 11, push the lane quickly before joining your team. After level 11, you can also keep the opposing laner occupied in a side lane.
notes.kayle-teamfight: In teamfights, use your increased range to keep attacking from the back. While your frontline blocks enemy engages, hit multiple enemies with fire waves. Before an enemy assassin reaches you, decide whether to use R on yourself or an ally who has engaged.
notes.kayle-situational-antiheal: Kayle's sustained basic attacks are well suited to maintaining Grievous Wounds. Against opponents who sustain through healing, buy the inexpensive Oblivion Orb first to suit Kayle's magic damage. When you need healing reduction and can spare a core item slot, upgrade to Morellonomicon. Avoid Executioner's Calling because its attack damage does not suit Kayle's scaling.
notes.vs-kayle-early: Kayle is very weak at levels 1–5, when she fights at melee range. Take lane control while Kayle is level 1–5. Keep denying Kayle CS and experience early. Kayle gains the advantage over time, so use the early game to build a lead.
notes.vs-kayle-level6: Carry out plans to gain a laning advantage against Kayle before she reaches level 6. Once Kayle reaches level 6, reassess the melee trades you took before. After Kayle reaches level 6, engage with your jungler.
notes.vs-kayle-r: Kayle's R blocks damage but still allows crowd control to affect its target. When Kayle uses R, use crowd control to hold the target in place and run out its duration instead of focusing damage. Resume attacking after Kayle's R damage immunity ends.
