Start a full fight after Kayle has already used R.
notes.vs-kayle-dive: Kayle is vulnerable to surprise attacks. Call your jungler repeatedly to attempt ganks and dives from outside Kayle's vision. Kayle uses W's movement speed boost to escape. Apply immobilizing crowd control before dealing damage so Kayle cannot escape with W.
notes.vs-kayle-late: Avoid a direct teamfight against Kayle after level 16. Secure objectives and turrets and try to end the game before Kayle reaches level 16. Force fights with a numbers advantage on the side of the map away from Kayle.
notes.vs-kayle-teamfight: Kayle stands at the back in teamfights and deals damage with basic attacks. Find a route to reach Kayle directly from the flank or outside her vision. Coordinate when allied crowd control will land before engaging to account for Kayle's R.
notes.kayn-combo-gank: For a standard gank, use E to pass through a wall, slow the target with W, land Q and a basic attack, then finish with R. R can only be cast on a target Kayn has recently damaged. Land W or Q before using R to meet its cast condition.
notes.kayn-combo-r: Kayn remains untargetable while inside the target with R. Use R to dodge a key enemy ability as it comes in. Keep attacking after exiting R. You can choose where to exit R during the cast. Choose an exit position from R toward your escape route.
notes.kayn-combo-shadow-assassin: Shadow Assassin's bonus damage only applies for a short window after entering combat with an enemy champion. Shadow Assassin gets right next to the enemy and lands Q, a basic attack, and W during the bonus damage window. If Shadow Assassin lacks damage, use R to pull back, then re-enter when the bonus damage window returns.
notes.kayn-skill-passive-form: Gain the orbs needed to transform by fighting enemy champions. Fighting melee champions grants Darkin orbs. Fighting ranged champions grants Shadow Assassin orbs. Plan your route around ganking the champion type that grants orbs for your desired form.
notes.kayn-skill-passive-pick: Choose your form based on both team compositions. Choose Shadow Assassin if the enemy has many squishy damage dealers and your team has a frontline. Choose Darkin if the enemy team is mostly melee or durable and fights will last longer; Darkin heals from ability damage. Darkin heals more when his abilities hit multiple enemies. Healing from hitting multiple enemies makes Darkin valuable in teamfight compositions.
notes.kayn-skill-e: E lets Kayn pass through terrain. Nearby enemies see an indicator showing which wall Kayn entered with E. Don't wait inside the wall for long; exit as soon as you have an opening to engage. E's duration is greatly reduced while fighting enemy champions. Don't rely on E to escape during a fight.
notes.kayn-skill-q: Both the dash and strike of Q deal damage. Q deals bonus damage to minions and jungle monsters. Start camps with Q to clear them faster. Save Q just before a gank so you can close the gap. Don't enter the enemy jungle when both Q and E are on cooldown.
notes.kayn-skill-w: W is a linear ability with a cast animation. Predict the enemy's movement to land W. In a gank, land W first so its slow gives you room to chase even without Q. Before transforming, use W in ganks after an ally lands crowd control or the enemy uses their mobility ability.
notes.kayn-skill-w-form: Shadow Assassin can move while casting W. Rhaast's W knocks up enemies it hits. Shadow Assassin follows the enemy to narrow their dodge angle and land W. Rhaast looks to knock enemies up with W just before an ally engages.
notes.kayn-skill-e-form: E ends immediately if Kayn is immobilized. E ends immediately if Kayn stays outside terrain for too long. Don't stay in a wall for long with E while the enemy still has a root or stun available. E grants increased movement speed in Shadow Assassin form. Shadow Assassin is immune to slows while using E.
notes.kayn-phase-early: Kayn is weak in fights before transforming. Early on, prioritize clearing camps and collecting orbs over fighting. Avoid risky early jungle invades.
notes.kayn-phase-form: Kayn starts to show his full strength once he transforms. Shadow Assassin's assassination power is strongest from just after transforming through the mid game. Shadow Assassin dies easily in late teamfights. Darkin has underwhelming power immediately after transforming. Darkin gains strong teamfight sustain as he builds items.
notes.kayn-laning-clear: Plan a route that uses E to cross walls between camps and cut travel time. Prioritize a full jungle clear over risky early ganks.
notes.kayn-laning-gank: In a gank, approach through a wall behind the lane with E to cut off the enemy's escape route. Enter a wall with E as your ally starts trading damage, then come out immediately. Even without a kill, consider the value of a gank that earns orbs by fighting an enemy champion.
notes.kayn-teamfight: Shadow Assassin should not start teamfights. After the enemy uses its crowd control, Shadow Assassin approaches from the flank or rear with E. Shadow Assassin focuses on one damage dealer in teamfights. After killing a damage dealer, Shadow Assassin uses R's untargetable window to disengage.
notes.kayn-teamfight-rhaast: Darkin stays up front, hitting multiple enemies with his abilities and sustaining through healing. Darkin looks for angles to hit as many enemies as possible with W and R. Darkin enters after the enemy uses its key crowd control on his team's frontline. Darkin relies on healing to survive. Darkin should be more cautious about engaging if the enemy has healing reduction.
notes.vs-kayn-r-condition: Kayn's R can only be cast on a target he has damaged first. Dodge W's straight-line hitbox to stop Kayn from enabling R at range.
notes.vs-kayn-e: Damaging Kayn while he uses E reduces its duration. Immobilizing Kayn while he uses E ends it immediately. Interrupt Kayn's E while he is inside the wall instead of waiting for him to come out.
notes.vs-kayn-wall-warning: If Kayn is inside nearby terrain, a warning indicator appears along its edge. When you see the warning indicator along a wall, stop trading damage and retreat toward your turret.
notes.vs-kayn-early: Kayn is noticeably weak in fights before transforming. Pressure Kayn's jungle route early to delay his transformation. Force early objective fights to delay Kayn's transformation. Don't give Kayn early kills that could speed up his transformation.
notes.vs-kayn-r-exit: When Kayn uses R on an ally, prepare crowd control around the target. Apply crowd control the moment Kayn exits R.
notes.kennen-combo-stun: For the basic stun combo, land Q, use a basic attack with W's passive ready, then cast W. Use your abilities in the right order to complete the stun with three marks.
notes.kennen-combo-teamfight: For a teamfight combo, enter with E, then use R, W, and Q in that order. Use R immediately after entering to give the marks time to build up for an area stun. Hitting at least one enemy with E restores energy. When entering with E, choose a path that passes through at least one enemy.
notes.kennen-skill-passive: Three stacks of Mark of the Storm stun the target. Mark of the Storm stacks expire over time. When applying the second mark, check that you still have a way to apply the third. If you have no way to apply the third mark, delay applying the first.
notes.kennen-skill-q: Q hits only the first enemy it strikes. Use Q as your main poke tool in lane. When using Q to apply a mark, prioritize landing it over dealing damage. Q's cooldown drops significantly as you level it up.
notes.kennen-skill-w: W's passive adds damage to a basic attack after a set number of attacks. A basic attack empowered by W's passive applies a mark to the target. Casting W attacks nearby marked enemies all at once. Use the basic attack empowered by W's passive before casting W.
notes.kennen-skill-e: You can pass through units during E. E applies a mark to enemies you pass through. Your attack speed increases when E ends. Hitting at least one enemy with E restores energy. Decide in advance whether to use E, your only escape, to enter or to leave.
notes.kennen-skill-r: R repeatedly damages nearby enemies throughout its duration. R repeatedly applies marks to nearby enemies, causing an area stun. Kennen gains armor during R. Kennen gains magic resistance during R. Save R if your angle would only catch one enemy.
notes.kennen-laning-poke: Against melee opponents, use your range to poke only with Q. Keep the opponent at no more than two marks until they step up for a last hit. When the opponent steps forward for a last hit, complete the stun with a basic attack and W.
notes.kennen-laning-wave: W's passive lets you clear waves with basic attacks alone, without casting abilities. Kennen relies on E to escape, so pushing the lane without vision leaves him vulnerable to ganks. After pushing the lane, secure river vision first. After pushing the lane, save E to respond to a gank.
notes.kennen-phase: Kennen is strong against melee opponents early by focusing his ability points on Q for poke. Look for your first solo kill at level 6, when you learn R. Kennen peaks in the mid game when he has both an engage item and ability power. Late game Kennen depends heavily on making a single engage work.
notes.kennen-teamfight-entry: Before activating R, find an angle to enter where the opponents are grouped. Enter only when an ally has caught an enemy or you can flank from outside their vision. Avoid walking in from the front, where you could be caught before activating R.
notes.kennen-teamfight-exit: Save E to escape after landing an area stun with R. If you use E to enter, check that your allies can follow immediately.
notes.kennen-situational-banshee: If the enemy's damage is mostly magic, add Banshee's Veil between core items. Choose Banshee's Veil to block the first targeted ability that hits you as you enter.
notes.vs-kennen-marks: Three stacks of Kennen's marks cause a stun. When you have two marks, move out of Kennen's range to prevent the third. Back off briefly and wait for the mark stacks to expire.
notes.vs-kennen-q: Kennen's Q hits only the first target it strikes. Stand behind minions to block Kennen's Q poke. Move so you are exposed to Q only briefly when stepping up for a last hit.
notes.vs-kennen-e: Kennen relies on E as his only escape. Counterattack when Kennen uses E to enter recklessly. Even if you take some poke, bait out Kennen's E before approaching.
notes.vs-kennen-r: Kennen gains resistances during R. Anticipate Kennen's entry angle and spread out so you do not get caught together in R's area stun. Keep vision on Kennen's likely entry points to stop him from starting a teamfight with R.
notes.vs-kennen-cleanse: Use a cleanse to remove the stun so you can avoid Kennen's follow-up damage. Physical damage dealers should consider Mercurial Scimitar to remove Kennen's stun. Ability power champions should consider Quicksilver Sash to remove Kennen's stun. If you cannot remove the stun, avoid standing together with allies in Kennen's entry path.
notes.khazix-combo-assassination: Start an isolated-target assassination by breaking vision with a brush or R to activate Unseen Threat. As soon as E lands, attack with Q, an empowered basic attack, then W. Use Q immediately after E so Leap’s landing damage and Q hit together.
notes.khazix-combo-r-reload: Disappearing from sight with R during a fight refreshes Unseen Threat. After disappearing with R, move to the side, then follow up with an empowered basic attack and Q. Use R to repeat your combo, not just to escape.
notes.khazix-combo-gank: When ganking, it is usually better to save E instead of using it to engage. For a gank, walk in, slow the target with W, then attack with Q. Save E to follow the target’s Flash or to escape. If you use E first, it is hard to chase when the target Flashes.
notes.khazix-skill-isolation: Kha'Zix’s decision to fight depends heavily on whether the target is isolated. An isolation marker appears when no allied units are near the target. Q deals nearly double damage to an isolated target. Check for the isolation marker on screen before engaging. Do not expect an isolated Q against a target near a wave, allied units, or jungle monsters.
notes.khazix-skill-evolve-q: Each time you rank up R, evolve one ability for an added effect. Evolving Q increases the range of Q and basic attacks. Using evolved Q on an isolated target reduces its cooldown. Choose Q as your default first evolution to attack from outside counterattack range and clear camps faster.
notes.khazix-skill-evolve-e: Evolving E increases Leap’s range. Evolved E resets its cooldown when you participate in a champion takedown. Use evolved E’s reset to escape after an assassination or move to the next target. Prioritize evolving E more when the enemy formation is tight and escaping after engaging will be difficult.
notes.khazix-skill-evolve-w: Evolving W fires spikes in three directions. Evolving W adds a slow and reveals targets. Evolved W slows isolated targets more strongly. Choose W evolution when you need to poke because you cannot get close. Choose W evolution when you need to catch a fleeing target. Choose W evolution when enemies group up and isolation is hard to create.
notes.khazix-skill-evolve-r: Evolving R increases its stealth duration. Evolving R increases its number of uses. Consider evolving R if you need to engage twice in a teamfight. Consider evolving R if dense enemy vision makes approaching difficult. Lower the priority of R evolution when you only need to assassinate one target.
notes.khazix-skill-w-sustain: Kha'Zix heals if he is within W’s explosion radius. When clearing the jungle, fire W close to the monster to reduce health loss.
notes.khazix-phase: Level 6, when Kha'Zix gains his first evolution, is his first power spike. Before level 6, spend time on camps and vision instead of forcing fights. Kha'Zix reaches his peak strength in the mid game when he has two or more evolutions. If enemies keep grouping in the late game, isolated targets disappear and Kha'Zix’s impact drops sharply. As the game goes late, create chances to catch enemies who split off.
notes.khazix-jungle-path: Path through the jungle to create isolated targets. An enemy ahead of the wave in a side lane is isolated. An enemy jungler clearing a camp alone is also isolated. If you can read the enemy jungler’s path, take a camp on the opposite side and leave.
notes.khazix-gank-angle: When ganking, avoid the river entrance, wait behind a wall, then cross it with E. E’s Leap can cross terrain. Look for a moment when the wave is pushing toward the enemy turret and the target is separated from allied minions.
notes.khazix-teamfight: Do not engage a teamfight from the front. Wait on the flank or behind the enemy, then engage when an enemy backline damage dealer separates from the formation. Engage after the enemy has used their targeted crowd control. After engaging, break vision with R, pull back, then go in again. Do not stay in a fight hitting a tank with unevolved abilities.
notes.khazix-situational-antiheal: An assassination target is hard to kill if their healing offsets your burst damage. Against an assassination target with healing, buy Executioner’s Calling between core items.
notes.vs-khazix-isolation: Stay near allied champions or minions to reduce isolated Q damage. Spend less time moving alone through side lanes. Keep Kha'Zix from reading where you clear jungle camps alone.
notes.vs-khazix-e: E’s Leap is Kha'Zix’s only mobility ability. Right after Kha'Zix engages with E is your chance to counterattack. Save crowd control and Flash for the moment Kha'Zix engages with E.
notes.vs-khazix-passive-vision: When Kha'Zix is out of sight, his next basic attack deals bonus magic damage and slows. Keep vision in brushes to prevent Kha'Zix’s empowered basic attack and slow. Prioritize vision in brushes by the river and jungle entrances.
notes.vs-khazix-r: Control Wards do not reveal Kha'Zix during R’s invisibility. When Kha'Zix disappears, use area-of-effect abilities ahead of time on his expected approach path. When Kha'Zix disappears, stay close to allies and apply crowd control as soon as he appears. The brief moment when Kha'Zix becomes visible after stealth ends is a chance to counterattack.
notes.vs-khazix-teamfight: Group up and start teamfights in narrow areas where you have vision. Keep backline damage dealers beside tanks to prevent isolation. When contesting an objective, do not go out of vision one at a time.
notes.vs-khazix-phase: Pressure Kha'Zix before level 6, when he gets his first evolution. Pressure Kha'Zix’s jungle early or take objectives first to delay his evolution timing. Avoid acting alone from the mid game onward once Kha'Zix has two or more evolutions.
notes.kindred-combo-basic: Apply E, weave in Q, then keep basic attacking the same target to trigger Wolf's pounce. Q's attack speed boost helps you meet the conditions for Wolf's pounce faster. Don't switch targets while building stacks for E's pounce.
notes.kindred-combo-w-zone: In a fight, place W first, then use Q repeatedly inside its zone to reposition. Q's cooldown is much shorter inside W's zone. Wolf only fights inside W's zone. Place W where the enemy will stand.
notes.kindred-skill-passive: You gain a mark for participating in a takedown, and each mark is permanent. Marks strengthen your basic abilities. Collecting enough marks increases your basic attack range. In the first few minutes, focus on securing marks over kills.
notes.kindred-skill-passive-choice: Kindred can choose which champion to mark. When an enemy jungle monster is marked, work counterjungling into your route. When you mark a champion, work a gank on that lane into your route. The enemy can also see that they have been marked. Only go for a mark deep in unseen enemy territory when your team has lane priority.
notes.kindred-skill-q: Q is a short leap that fires arrows, useful for both dodging and attacking. Outside W's zone, save Q for escaping because its cooldown is long. Inside W's zone, use Q often because its cooldown is short. While clearing the jungle, use Q between monster attacks to reposition and take fewer hits.
notes.kindred-skill-w: W's Wolf deals bonus damage to jungle monsters. When clearing a camp, place W in the middle so Wolf can attack. Once movement and attacks fully stack your passive, your next basic attack heals you based on your missing health. When low on health, use the healing from your passive stacks to keep clearing camps.
notes.kindred-skill-e: E slows the enemy. E's Wolf's pounce deals more damage the more health the enemy is missing. Apply E as you engage, then use basic attacks to meet the conditions for the pounce. If the enemy looks likely to escape with a mobility ability, use E first for the slow.
notes.kindred-skill-r-basic: R creates a zone at the chosen location where allies, enemies, and monsters cannot die. A target whose health falls near zero inside R's zone takes no damage or healing until the zone ends. Everyone inside the zone is healed when R ends. Use R to make the enemy waste a finishing ability and Ignite.
notes.kindred-skill-r-timing: R also saves enemies. Activate R right after an enemy engages on your team's main damage dealer. At an objective, activate R as the enemy comes in to use Smite. Lower the enemy's health while R is active. Finish the enemy as R's zone ends.
notes.kindred-jungle-pathing: Low movement speed makes wasted trips costly. Plan a route that clears camps toward the mark. If a gank is uncertain, use W's bonus monster damage to farm and counterjungle for marks.
notes.kindred-ganking: With only E's slow for crowd control, it's hard to make a gank work alone. Gank when an ally has reliable crowd control or the enemy has pushed too far up the lane. If gank conditions are poor, clear vision and apply pressure by counterjungling. Dying from an overaggressive early engage severely disrupts your mark progress.
notes.kindred-teamfight: Don't engage first in a teamfight. After your team starts the fight, place W behind your allies, then reposition with Q inside its zone while basic attacking. Don't stand at the front while the enemy still has an engage ability available.
notes.kindred-phase: Early on, Kindred is fragile and slow, making encounters with the enemy jungler easy to lose. In the mid game, Kindred can duel once marks have stacked up and attack speed items are ready. Once marks start increasing Kindred's range, Kindred can fight melee champions without taking hits back. If you don't collect marks on time, it's hard to make use of Kindred's mid-game power spike. Early on, prioritize marks and farming over fights.
notes.kindred-situational-antiheal: Build Grievous Wounds against enemies with strong healing. Kindred deals sustained damage with basic attacks, so Mortal Reminder provides armor penetration and Grievous Wounds together with less disruption to the core item build.
notes.vs-kindred-mark: Kindred's growth depends heavily on marks. When a jungle monster is marked, clear that camp first. Delaying Kindred's marks several times reduces their mid-to-late-game damage and range.
notes.vs-kindred-early: Kindred is fragile and slow, making them vulnerable to early pressure. Ward Kindred's jungle and disrupt their route to slow their mark progress. When you encounter Kindred, close in before they place W.
notes.vs-kindred-r-inside: When Kindred activates R, enter its zone. Inside R's zone, allies at near-zero health survive too. Allies inside R's zone are also healed when it ends.
notes.vs-kindred-r-displace: If you have a displacement ability, push or pull Kindred out of R's zone. If you have a displacement ability, push or pull the ally Kindred is trying to save out of R's zone. R's zone stays in place, so moving a target outside it removes the effect that prevents death.
notes.vs-kindred-e: Much of Kindred's damage comes from Wolf's pounce, which triggers after consecutive hits on a target marked by E. If E marks you, create distance or break line of sight to avoid triggering the pounce. The lower your health, the more dangerous E's Wolf's pounce is.
notes.vs-kindred-w: Inside W's zone, Kindred has a shorter Q cooldown and can keep repositioning. Pushing Kindred out of W's zone removes Wolf's damage. Use a knockback or movement impairment to keep Kindred out of W's zone.
notes.kled-combo-basic: Engage with E, land Q, hit four W-enhanced basic attacks, then recast E to disengage. E's recast only goes toward the target hit by the first cast. To use E's recast to disengage, hit your opponent with the first E.
notes.kled-combo-q-hold: After landing Q, stay close for a short time to trigger the pull and heavy damage. As soon as Q lands, use E or W to stay close to your opponent. If your opponent uses a mobility ability to get out of Q's range, the follow-up effect is lost.
notes.kled-skill-dismount: When Skaarl runs out of health, Kled dismounts. Dismounted Kled has very low health and deals less damage to champions. Dismounted Kled gains movement speed when moving toward enemy champions. Dismounted Kled gains armor and magic resistance based on the number of nearby enemy champions. When you dismount, stay close to enemies to build Courage.
notes.kled-skill-courage: Attacking champions builds Courage fastest. You can also build Courage by attacking epic monsters or structures, or by killing minions. When Courage fills, Skaarl returns with restored health and Kled remounts. If you have nowhere to run while dismounted, attack a turret or minion wave to fill your Courage bar. If you can stay close to your opponent while dismounted, attack them to build Courage quickly.
notes.kled-skill-pistol: While dismounted, Q becomes Pocket Pistol, a ranged attack that knocks Kled backward when cast. Pocket Pistol's recoil pushes you opposite the direction you aim. Right after dismounting, aim Pocket Pistol so its recoil pushes you toward your escape route. You can build Courage with Pocket Pistol while escaping.
notes.kled-skill-w: W's fourth attack deals damage based on the target's maximum health. Activate W when you can land all four basic attacks. Each basic attack reduces W's cooldown, and hitting a champion reduces it further. Stay close to your opponent during a fight and keep using basic attacks to get W back.
notes.kled-skill-e: As Kled dashes, E pulls minions and small monsters in front of him. Use E to pull a minion wave or group a jungle camp. Hitting a champion or large monster with E grants movement speed. If E hits a champion or large monster, you can recast it shortly afterward to return to that target. Use E to dash out and dodge an opponent's ability, then recast it to return.
notes.kled-skill-r: Because R starts from far away, cast it based on where the enemy team will be when you arrive. R's shield forms during the charge and lasts briefly after it ends. Use R's shield to survive the burst combo that hits right after you engage. R charges only the first enemy champion along its path.
notes.kled-laning: Kled is strong at trading from level 1. If Skaarl is nearly out of health, back off instead of trading and build Courage. Encountering the enemy jungler while dismounted can easily get Kled killed.
notes.kled-laning-wave: Step forward in lane when Q is available. Without Q, you cannot hold your opponent in place, making trades difficult. While Q is unavailable, use E to pull the wave and keep the lane on your side. While Q is unavailable, use basic attacks to reduce W's cooldown. If you win a trade, pressure the turret to turn it into an advantage.
notes.kled-phase: Kled is strongest during laning and mid-game skirmishes. In late-game teamfights, Skaarl can be lost easily after an R engage, and Kled's reduced champion damage while dismounted weakens his sustained damage. Build on an early lead and decide the game through turrets and objectives in the mid game.
notes.kled-teamfight: Start teamfights with R. Use R along a path your allies can follow with its movement speed boost. Even if you lose Skaarl after engaging, stay in the skirmish to build Courage instead of retreating immediately. After engaging with R, survive the skirmish and remount to start a second fight.
notes.kled-situational-mr: Against magic damage, Skaarl can be lost in an instant. If the enemy's main damage is magic, buy Maw of Malmortius between core items for its shield and magic resistance to help you survive after dismounting.
notes.kled-situational-antiheal: If your opponent's healing lets them withstand W's maximum-health damage, buy Executioner's Calling earlier. Kled stays close and keeps attacking, so he can apply Grievous Wounds consistently.
notes.vs-kled-courage: Check Kled's Courage bar when facing him dismounted. When Courage fills, Skaarl returns with restored health and Kled remounts. If you can reliably kill dismounted Kled, do it before he remounts. If you struggle to kill dismounted Kled, keep your distance so he can't build Courage.
notes.vs-kled-courage-source: Kled also builds Courage by killing minions and attacking structures or epic monsters. After forcing Kled off Skaarl, push him out of lane to deny him farm.
notes.vs-kled-w: Kled is more dangerous when W is ready. W's fourth basic attack deals maximum-health damage, so it deals more damage the more health you have. When Kled activates W, back off before he lands all four basic attacks, then move in again.
notes.vs-kled-q: Even if Q catches you, Kled must stay close for a short time to trigger the pull. Right after Q catches you is your chance to escape before the pull. Save your mobility ability and Flash for right after Q catches you. If Q catches you and you have no way to escape, move toward your minion wave or allies.
notes.vs-kled-r: Kled can engage with R from far away and out of vision. Keep vision on the flanks to spot Kled's R engage early. R charges only the first enemy champion along its path.
notes.vs-kled-late: After laning and the mid game, Kled becomes weaker because he deals less damage to champions while dismounted. Avoid giving Kled an early lead and extend the game.
notes.kogmaw-combo-basic: For a basic trade, activate W, auto-attack, land Q, then keep auto-attacking. Activating W first lets you start auto-attacking from outside the enemy's response range. Use Q after closing in so its resistance reduction overlaps with W's on-hit damage. If you throw Q first, W's duration runs down while the enemy backs away.
notes.kogmaw-combo-kite: Walk backward, place E along your retreat path, then auto-attack again when the enemy is slowed. E leaves a trail where its projectile passes. Throw E ahead of where the enemy will move rather than aiming to hit them directly.
notes.kogmaw-combo-finish: Cut off the escape route with E, then fire R repeatedly to finish them off. R is most efficient when fired in a burst after the enemy's health drops below a certain point. Firing R repeatedly at a high-health enemy wastes mana.
notes.kogmaw-skill-w: W increases your range for its duration and adds magic damage based on maximum health to your auto-attacks. W has a limited duration and a long cooldown. Using W to clear waves makes it hard to use its range advantage in a fight. W's damage against monsters has a cap. Most of your damage to objectives comes from auto-attacks and items.
notes.kogmaw-skill-q: Putting a point in Q grants attack speed through its passive. Landing Q reduces the target's armor and magic resistance. Q's resistance reduction also increases the damage your allies deal. Land Q on the enemy frontline just before a dragon or Rift Herald fight.
notes.kogmaw-skill-r-mana: Using R repeatedly in a short time increases its mana cost in steps. Spamming R for poke in lane leaves you short on mana for fights. Fire only one or two R shots for poke. Fire R repeatedly only when you can secure the finish. R reveals targets that are not stealthed, so you can use it to check brush.
notes.kogmaw-skill-passive: After dying, Kog'Maw briefly moves through units, then explodes to deal true damage. Armor and magic resistance cannot reduce his passive's explosion damage. If the enemy backs away, walk toward your allies or an objective in passive form to deny the area.
notes.kogmaw-laning: Low movement speed and no mobility ability make him vulnerable to ganks. When W is down, position yourself behind the middle of the lane. Move forward only while W is active. Before moving forward, check both W's cooldown and the enemy jungler's position.
notes.kogmaw-laning-wave: Do not force the wave forward. E hits every enemy in a line and can clear waves, but you also need it to escape ganks. Let the lane push toward you and farm near your turret. Push forward only where your support has established vision.
notes.kogmaw-phase: Kog'Maw is weakest at levels 1–2. His range advantage grows as W gains levels. He is strong in the mid to late game once he has at least two attack speed and damage items. As a hypercarry who fights with range and attack speed, he benefits from longer games. Even if you fall behind early, you can recover by keeping up your farm.
notes.kogmaw-teamfight: Attack enemies from behind your frontline using W's range. You have no way to escape enemies who dive onto you by yourself. Stay within range of your allies' protective abilities. If your frontline collapses, stop attacking and retreat.
notes.kogmaw-teamfight-target: W's damage based on maximum health makes attacking a high-health enemy frontline worthwhile. Attack the nearest enemy in range instead of moving forward to target the backline.
notes.kogmaw-situational-antiheal: If the enemy's healing is enough to turn a fight, reduce it with Executioner's Calling. You can keep the healing reduction active with sustained auto-attacks.
notes.kogmaw-situational-qss: Getting caught once by reliable immobilizing crowd control can easily get you killed. If the enemy has reliable immobilizing crowd control, buy Mercurial Scimitar between core items.
notes.vs-kogmaw-w: Kog'Maw's range increases only while W is active. Wait for W to expire, then close in on Kog'Maw. When Kog'Maw approaches with W active, wait out its duration.
notes.vs-kogmaw-mobility: Kog'Maw has no mobility ability and low movement speed, making him vulnerable to immobilizing crowd control. Prioritize Kog'Maw in jungle ganks and roams. If your team has an engage composition, target Kog'Maw first in teamfights.
notes.vs-kogmaw-passive: Immediately after killing Kog'Maw, walk backward away from his body. Even after dying, Kog'Maw can follow you through units and deal damage that defensive stats cannot reduce.
notes.vs-kogmaw-r: R can come from off-screen and deals heavy damage to low-health targets. If your health is low, leave Kog'Maw's vision to heal. Getting hit by R reveals your position and exposes you to a follow-up gank.
notes.vs-kogmaw-q: Getting hit by Q increases the damage from Kog'Maw's subsequent auto-attacks and his allies. Block Q's projectile with a minion or dodge it sideways. If Q hits you, stay away from Kog'Maw during the brief resistance reduction.
notes.vs-kogmaw-late: Kog'Maw is a hypercarry who grows stronger over time. Secure objectives and turrets in the early to mid game to end the game quickly. Keep pressuring Kog'Maw in lane to disrupt his farming.
notes.leblanc-combo-basic: The basic combo is to mark the target with Q, dash in with W to detonate the mark, then recast W to return. The Q mark detonates when you hit the target with another ability.
notes.leblanc-combo-full: The full combo is to dash in with W, use Q and R, then return with W. R mimics your most recently used ability. Use the ability you want to mimic immediately before R.
notes.leblanc-combo-e-lock: As the E root activates, use Q, then W. E roots the target after the chain remains attached for a while. Stay within chain range until the E root activates.
notes.leblanc-combo-w-return: You can return with W only for a short time after the dash. Check that your W return point is safe before going in. Choose whether to go in again or return with W based on the enemy's remaining counterattack abilities. If you miss the W return window, you cannot use it to escape.
notes.leblanc-skill-q: If the Q hit or mark detonation kills the target, all mana spent is refunded. If the Q hit or mark detonation kills the target, Q's remaining cooldown is reduced. Use the refund on kills to clear the wave or secure last hits with Q.
notes.leblanc-skill-passive-clone: P briefly makes you invisible when your health falls below a certain threshold. P creates a clone when your health falls below a certain threshold. You can control the clone created by P separately. When escaping, send the clone in the opposite direction to confuse pursuers.
notes.leblanc-skill-e-aim: E's slow projectile makes it hard to land head-on. Use E from a bush or behind minions while out of sight. Use W to get beside the enemy and narrow the angle before using E. E grants true sight of the target it hits. Use E's true sight to track a fleeing enemy.
notes.leblanc-skill-r-choice: When a kill is certain, use R to mimic Q. If you need another engage or an escape, use R to mimic W. If you need guaranteed crowd control, use R to mimic E. Decide which ability R will mimic before starting your combo.
notes.leblanc-phase: LeBlanc is strongest from just after she learns R at level 6 through the mid game. Kill opportunities are most frequent from just after level 6 through the mid game. In the late game, once enemies have magic resistance and vision, LeBlanc is vulnerable to counterattacks if an assassination fails. If LeBlanc cannot build a lead earlier, her late-game impact drops sharply.
notes.leblanc-laning-push: Clear the wave quickly with Q, then join fights in a side lane or the jungle. Stay in lane if you have not pushed the wave.
notes.leblanc-laning-trade: Trade damage only right after the enemy uses a key ability. Repeat short trades by going in with W and returning. Go in only while your W return is available.
notes.leblanc-teamfight: Avoid going in first in a head-on teamfight. After the fight starts and the enemy focuses on your allied tank, go in from the side. Before going in, pick one enemy backliner to eliminate. After eliminating your target, disengage with W.
notes.leblanc-teamfight-pick: LeBlanc gets more value from picks than from teamfights. Use E to root and eliminate enemies moving alone through areas without vision. Look first for picks that can prevent a teamfight instead of starting one.
notes.leblanc-situational-banshee: If the enemy mid laner is a mage with targeted burst damage, choose Banshee's Veil to block the first ability in their combo. LeBlanc cannot counterattack once she is locked down.
notes.vs-leblanc-clone: The clone created by P cannot deal damage. If a low-health LeBlanc splits into two, hold your abilities until you can tell which is real. When the clone appears, track the one that actually attacks.
notes.vs-leblanc-mark: If the Q mark remains, the next ability hit deals double damage. If Q marks you, back away to give the mark time to disappear.
notes.vs-leblanc-e: The E root activates after the chain remains attached, rather than on impact. If E hits you, move out of chain range before the root activates. Use Flash or a movement ability right after E hits you to avoid the root.
notes.vs-leblanc-w: After LeBlanc dashes in with W, she can return to her original position only for a short time. Approach and fight after LeBlanc's W return expires or is used.
notes.vs-leblanc-roam: LeBlanc tries to roam after pushing the lane. If LeBlanc disappears from mid vision, alert your team immediately. In a side lane, secure vision of the river before moving forward.
notes.leesin-skill-passive-weave: Flurry increases the attack speed of the next two basic attacks after using an ability and restores energy. When clearing the jungle or fighting, weave two basic attacks between abilities to maintain damage and energy.
notes.leesin-skill-q: Q's first cast is a skillshot projectile blocked by minions and jungle monsters. Approach from the side when ganking so the wave does not block Q. Avoid firing Q into empty space to check vision if you want to preserve your engage tool. Q's first cast grants true sight of the target hit, keeping them visible even if they flee into brush.
notes.leesin-skill-q2-timing: Q's second cast deals more damage the more health the target is missing. Use allied CC and basic attacks to lower the target's health first, then finish with Q's second cast. When delaying Q's second cast, use it before its short recast window expires.
notes.leesin-skill-w: W dashes to allies and your own wards. Place a ward over a wall to create a W path for an engage from an unseen angle. Before placing a ward, decide whether to use it for a W engage or escape.
notes.leesin-skill-w-recast: W's second cast increases omnivamp. Use W's second cast to sustain your health while clearing jungle camps and heal during skirmishes. Use W's second cast as you start basic attacking immediately after engaging.
notes.leesin-skill-e: E's first cast deals area damage around you and provides stealth detection. Use E's first cast to check unwarded brush or reveal a hidden opponent. E's second cast slows opponents. Use E's second cast after the opponent uses their escape ability to chase them.
notes.leesin-skill-r: R holds the target in place during its cast. The target knocked back by R knocks up other enemies they collide with. Use R to kick the opponent toward your allies. To knock up multiple enemies, kick R's target through a group of enemies.
notes.leesin-combo-basic: The basic gank combo is Q's first cast, basic attack, E's first cast, basic attack, then Q's second cast, adding E's second cast if needed. Weave Flurry-empowered basic attacks between abilities in your gank combo. Use Q's second cast in your gank combo after lowering the opponent's health.
notes.leesin-combo-ward-jump: To ward jump, place the ward first, then use W before the ward lands. To approach from outside Q range, place a ward over a wall or behind the opponent and use W to dash to it. When escaping with a ward hop, place a ward over a wall toward your team's side.
notes.leesin-combo-insec: To perform an Insec, land Q's first cast, approach with Q's second cast, get behind the opponent, then use R to kick them toward your allies. To perform a ward Insec, land Q's first cast, use a ward and W to get behind the opponent, then use R to kick them toward your allies. To change R's direction with Flash, start casting R, then Flash during the cast. Before starting an Insec, make sure your allies are close enough to follow up with attacks.
notes.leesin-combo-r-q2: If your allies are far away, land Q's first cast, use R to kick the opponent toward them, then follow with Q's second cast. Hold Q's second cast until after R so you can close the gap created by the kick.
notes.leesin-phase-early: Lee Sin is strongest in early jungle duels and counter-jungling. Look for a chance to disrupt the enemy jungler's route immediately after clearing your first two or three camps. From level 6, when R becomes available, look for opportunities to break open a lane with an Insec.
notes.leesin-phase-late: Lee Sin's damage contribution drops as the game goes on, making solo kills harder. In the late game, use R to separate one enemy so your strong allied carry can fight more easily. In the late game, use R to knock away opponents who dive your backline.
notes.leesin-laning: Plan your jungle route to turn your early strength into an advantage. Steal camps or influence a lane when the enemy jungler is tied up on the opposite side. Keep in mind that you have no escape tools immediately after using both Q and W. Save W to escape when going deep into the enemy jungle.
notes.leesin-teamfight: Only engage when your allies can follow up immediately. If your allies have not engaged yet, save R to knock away an enemy engager. Lee Sin has limits to how long he can hold the frontline in teamfights. Before entering a teamfight, plan an escape route using W or Q's second cast.
notes.leesin-situational-antiheal: Against opponents who sustain through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items to capitalize on your early dueling advantage. Upgrade Executioner's Calling to Mortal Reminder to reduce the healing of opponents who rely on it to survive.
notes.vs-leesin-q-block: Most of Lee Sin's engages depend on landing Q's first cast. Lee Sin's first Q cast is a projectile blocked by minions and jungle monsters. If you expect a Lee Sin gank, keep the wave between you and him to block Q's straight path.
notes.vs-leesin-ward-jump: Lee Sin can cross walls by using W on his own wards. Watch for Lee Sin engaging with a ward and W from beyond walls where you lack vision. Use Control Wards to clear wards beyond walls and prevent Lee Sin from engaging with a ward and W. Position one space away from the wall to prepare for Lee Sin's ward-W engage.
notes.vs-leesin-q2: Lee Sin's second Q cast deals more damage the more health the target is missing. If Q's first cast hits you while you are below half health, move toward an allied turret or your team during the short window for Q's second cast.
notes.vs-leesin-r-position: If Lee Sin has room to get behind you, watch for the risk of being kicked by R. Position with your back to a wall or your team's frontline so that even if R kicks you, you move toward your allies. If an ally knocked back by Lee Sin's R collides with you, you will also be knocked up. Spread out from your allies just before a teamfight so R cannot knock up multiple teammates together.
notes.vs-leesin-early-duel: Lee Sin is strong in early duels and falls off in the late game. If you encounter Lee Sin in the jungle early, avoid dueling him and retreat. Use objective and lane advantages to buy time until the late game, when Lee Sin falls off.
notes.vs-leesin-w-sustain: Lee Sin heals during skirmishes through the omnivamp from W's second cast. Apply healing reduction if Lee Sin survives longer than expected in extended fights through W's omnivamp. Focus your damage on Lee Sin immediately after he uses W to engage.
notes.leona-combo-engage: For a basic engage, land E, activate Q, stun with an auto attack, then use W. Prepare E and Q together before engaging to chain their crowd control.
notes.leona-combo-flash: Q is not consumed on cast; it makes the next auto attack stun. Activate Q first, then Flash in and auto attack to give the enemy less time to react. An activated Q expires if you do not auto attack within a certain time.
notes.leona-skill-passive: Leona cannot trigger a Sunlight mark herself; an ally must attack the target. Get in first to apply a Sunlight mark, then have an ally attack that target. Avoid wasting a Sunlight mark on a target your allied damage dealer cannot see.
notes.leona-skill-w: W provides damage reduction and increased armor and magic resistance. W explodes when its duration ends. W's bonus defensive stats can only be extended if the explosion hits at least one enemy. Use W just after reaching an enemy, rather than right before going in, so the enemy is nearby when it explodes.
notes.leona-skill-e: E travels in a straight line and dashes to the last enemy champion it hits. If another enemy champion is behind your E target, you may dash farther in and become isolated. Before casting E, check how many enemy champions are in its straight path.
notes.leona-skill-r: Remember that R stuns only enemies hit by its center. R only slows enemies hit by its outer area. Use R on a target already caught to land its center. An enemy who can move freely can easily dodge the center of R when you use it on its own. Once you have vision, use R's long range to join an engage from outside the lane.
notes.leona-phase: In early trades, your role is to absorb the enemy's attacks. Look for a kill at levels 2–3, when both Q and E are available. Look for a kill at level 6, when you learn R. After that, your damage falls short, so shift your focus to engaging and crowd control.
notes.leona-laning-timing: Engage as the enemy marksman steps forward to last-hit. Use E during your auto-attack animation to give the enemy less time to react. Before engaging, check that your allied marksman is close enough to follow up. Before engaging, check that your allied marksman's damage abilities are ready. Leona lacks the damage to go in alone and needs her allies' damage.
notes.leona-laning-cooldown: If an engage fails, you risk remaining in enemy range with both E and Q unavailable. E functions as an engage ability more than an escape. When looking for a risky engage, at least keep Flash available. Once your engage abilities are down, pull the wave toward your turret to deny a counterattack.
notes.leona-roaming: You can make your strongest engage before the enemy spots Leona. Look for an E engage from a brush or an area without enemy vision. If the lane stalls, establish vision in the river, then try to roam mid. Leona's long crowd control helps secure kills, making her strong at roaming.
notes.leona-teamfight-engage: When entering a teamfight first, use E and R to attack the enemy formation. When protecting your carry, stop enemies who jump on them with Q and E. If your team has less damage than the enemy, protect your carry instead of engaging first. After engaging, absorb focused attacks while W lasts and draw out enemy abilities.
notes.leona-teamfight-target: Choose an engage target your allies can reach and attack. An ally must attack to trigger a Sunlight mark. Do not go so far in that your allies cannot attack targets marked with Sunlight.
notes.leona-situational-cc: If the enemy team uses crowd control to shut down your carry, prioritize Mikael's Blessing to save them.
notes.leona-situational-thorn: If an enemy physical damage dealer sustains through auto attacks, buy Thornmail to apply reflected damage and Grievous Wounds in close combat.
notes.vs-leona-w: Use the time between Leona activating W and its explosion to create distance. Move out of W's area before it explodes to avoid its damage. If W's explosion hits no enemies, Leona's bonus defensive stats will not be extended.
notes.vs-leona-r: Remember that Leona's R stuns only enemies in its center. Leona's R only slows enemies in its outer area. Move sideways as soon as R's indicator appears to dodge the stun at its center.
notes.vs-leona-e: Leona's E passes through targets in a straight line and dashes to the last champion hit. The marksman and support should avoid lining up along E's path so Leona cannot reach the target behind them.
notes.vs-leona-q: Leona can approach with Q already activated. Even if you do not see the Q animation, do not let Leona get close enough to reach you.
notes.vs-leona-armor: Avoid taking early trades against Leona with physical damage. Wear down Leona's health beforehand with magic damage or ranged poke. Counterattack after Leona's engage abilities are down.
notes.vs-leona-passive: An ally of Leona must attack to trigger a Sunlight mark. If you see a Sunlight mark on you, retreat immediately to prepare for the enemy's follow-up attack.
notes.lillia-combo-gank: For ganks, slow the target with E, hit the center of W, then finish with Q. Without E's slow, landing the center of W is difficult.
notes.lillia-combo-r: R puts only enemies marked with dream dust to sleep. Before using R, land at least one ability to apply dream dust. Use R when your allies can wait for drowsiness to become sleep. Don't place a persistent damage area on a sleeping enemy.
notes.lillia-combo-r-setup: It's best to use R before a teamfight breaks out. Apply dream dust to several enemies from afar with Q and E, then use R from outside their vision. If you use R during a head-on fight, sleeping enemies take damage and wake up right away.
notes.lillia-skill-q: Q has a short cooldown. Each Q hit stacks movement speed. Lillia's chases and escapes depend on Q's movement speed stacks. During fights, keep using Q and hit anything you can. The true damage at Q's edge is effective even against enemies with high defenses.
notes.lillia-skill-w: W's windup gives away the cast. W deals much more damage when its center hits. Aim W's center at slowed or sleeping enemies. Aim W's center at stationary jungle monsters. W cannot cross terrain.
notes.lillia-skill-e: E rolls until it hits an enemy or terrain. Roll E down long, straight corridors or along walls to hit enemies outside your vision. Roll E ahead of a fleeing enemy's expected path. E reveals enemies it hits. Use E to check jungle entrances without vision.
notes.lillia-skill-passive: Applying dream dust to a champion or large jungle monster restores health. When low on health, clear a large camp to heal instead of recalling. Passive healing lets Lillia keep clearing the jungle.
notes.lillia-phase: Lillia clears the jungle and scales well early. Lillia is weak at solo ganks early. After learning R at level 6, Lillia can gank in coordination with allies. Lillia peaks in the mid to late game when items strengthen her damage over time and movement speed. Early on, clear camps quickly instead of looking for kills.
notes.lillia-laning-clear: Catch the monster pack with Q's edge, then hit the large monster with W's center. Early on, use passive healing to clear camps back to back without interrupting your route.
notes.lillia-laning-gank: Wait for the enemy to move farther into the lane before lining up an E gank. When ganking, roll E along a wall. Just before a gank, hit a camp or minion with Q to build movement speed stacks. Without Q movement speed stacks, chasing during a gank is difficult.
notes.lillia-teamfight: In teamfights, use Q from the side to apply passive damage over time to several enemies. Slow enemy divers with E to keep them away from your damage dealers. Avoid getting caught while trying to land W's center from the front.
notes.lillia-teamfight-r: If you start a teamfight with R, decide the order in which your team should wake the sleeping enemies. Enemies put to sleep by R take extra damage when awakened. Focus sleeping enemies one at a time, waking and finishing each one.
notes.lillia-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin, get Zhonya's Hourglass early to prepare for being caught while using Q up close.
notes.lillia-situational-rylai: Against mostly ranged compositions that keep their distance, choose Rylai's Crystal Scepter to slow enemies with Q hits and stay close longer.
notes.vs-lillia-r-condition: Lillia's R puts only enemies marked with dream dust to sleep. Even at high health, dodge Q and E so Lillia cannot meet R's condition.
notes.vs-lillia-r-drowsy: R does not put you to sleep immediately. You can still move while drowsy. While drowsy, move to safety or use a way to remove movement impairing effects. If you miss the drowsy window, you are stuck until an ally wakes you.
notes.vs-lillia-w: Lillia's W has a visible windup. W deals much more damage when its center hits. When you see W's windup, move slightly sideways to avoid the center. Keep a wall between you and Lillia so W cannot reach you.
notes.vs-lillia-speed: Lillia becomes hard to catch when ability hits build her movement speed stacks. You have a chance to chase Lillia when she has no movement speed stacks. Keep dodging Lillia's abilities, then close in.
notes.vs-lillia-squishy: Lillia needs to deal sustained damage at close range. In teamfights, save crowd control that prevents movement for Lillia when she comes in from the side.
notes.vs-lillia-e: Lillia's E rolls until it hits an enemy or a wall. If you don't know where Lillia is, don't walk straight through jungle entrances or river passages.
notes.lissandra-combo-engage: Cast E, recast it to engage, then use W, Q, and R in that order. Press W as soon as you arrive with E to stop the enemy from escaping.
notes.lissandra-combo-self-r: To use R on yourself, press your self-cast key and R key together for an instant cast. Check your self-cast key setting beforehand.
notes.lissandra-skill-q: Q shatters on the first target it hits and pierces enemies behind it. Q does not shatter if it hits nothing. Against an enemy using minions as a shield, aim Q at a minion first so it reaches the champion behind it.
notes.lissandra-skill-w: W instantly roots enemies around you, but its range is short. Missing W at low levels leaves you vulnerable during its long cooldown. Do not use W carelessly to clear waves; use it when an engage or jungle follow-up is certain.
notes.lissandra-skill-e: E can be used both to engage and to escape. If you delay recasting E after throwing it, the claw stays in place. Throw E, then run in the opposite direction to make your movement harder to predict. If you are immobilized before recasting E, the teleport fails. If the enemy still has crowd control available, do not delay recasting E.
notes.lissandra-skill-r-offense: R cast on an enemy stuns the target and leaves an area slow around them. Use R to stop an enemy engager as they come in. If enemies are grouped up, cast R in the middle of them.
notes.lissandra-skill-r-defense: R cast on yourself prevents damage during stasis and restores health. R cast on yourself heals more the more health you are missing. Cast R on yourself late enough to block an enemy finishing ability or delayed damage. You cannot do anything during the stasis from casting R on yourself.
notes.lissandra-skill-passive: When an enemy champion dies nearby, your passive creates a Frozen Thrall. Frozen Thralls slow nearby enemies and explode after a short delay. After the first kill, account for the Frozen Thrall's slow and area damage when looking for more kills.
notes.lissandra-phase: From level 6, when both W and R are available, look for a guaranteed engage. Lissandra is strongest in the mid game, once she has one core item. In the late game, her raw damage falls short of other mages. In the late game, focus on stopping engages and applying crowd control.
notes.lissandra-laning: Her short ability ranges make her weak in ranged poke fights. Use Q to last-hit and clear waves while keeping up in levels. Trade only when you can use E and W together. You are most vulnerable to a jungle gank right after using E to poke.
notes.lissandra-laning-roam: Push the wave with Q, then use E to cross terrain and roam to a side lane. Do not roam if you have used W and R in lane.
notes.lissandra-teamfight: Before a teamfight, decide whether to engage with E and W or counter an enemy engage with R. If you are unsure about engaging, save R for an enemy engager. If you decide to engage in a teamfight, lock enemies down with E and W, then follow up with R.
notes.lissandra-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who dives in, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier for its ability power and defense.
notes.lissandra-situational-banshee: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, build Banshee's Veil between core items to block one targeted ability before engaging.
notes.vs-lissandra-e: Lissandra throws E, then recasts it to teleport to the claw's position. Immobilize Lissandra while the claw is traveling to stop her E teleport.
notes.vs-lissandra-w: Lissandra's W has a long cooldown at low levels. Move in and trade right after Lissandra uses W on the wave or misses it.
notes.vs-lissandra-r: Lissandra's R stuns when cast on an enemy and prevents damage during stasis when cast on herself. If Lissandra still has R, spread out your attacks so you can deal damage after her stasis ends.
notes.vs-lissandra-mobility: Lissandra has no escape besides E. Check whether Lissandra has used E before deciding to engage.
notes.vs-lissandra-q: Lissandra's Q must hit the first target to shatter and pierce through behind it. Farm from an angle that keeps you out of Q's path through your allied minions.
notes.locke-combo-basic: For a basic trade, land Q, then use basic attacks to consume the nails. Nails only detonate from basic attacks. Before throwing Q, work out how many follow-up basic attacks you can land.
notes.locke-combo-allin: To engage, use Q, E's teleport, the dashing basic attack, then follow-up basic attacks. E's teleport and the next basic attack's dash work as separate steps. Use the dashing basic attack on a target with nails in them to focus your damage.
notes.locke-skill-q: The more nails embedded, the more damage each basic attack deals. Each nail you fail to consume refunds some of Q's cooldown. If you can't reach a target with nails in them, don't force the chase.
notes.locke-skill-w: W increases your attack speed and movement speed while draining your health. When W ends, you recover health based on the damage you took and the health you lost during it. Activate W just before a fight where you need to consume nails quickly. Recasting W to end it early reduces the healing. If you don't need health urgently, let W run its full duration.
notes.locke-skill-w-cc: You can use W even while under crowd control. Activate W when crowd control keeps you from moving. Activating W during crowd control still gives you healing and increased attack speed afterward.
notes.locke-skill-e: E teleports to a target location and damages nearby enemies. After E, your next basic attack dashes to the target and also hits enemies along the path. Use E's teleport to cross terrain. Use the dashing basic attack after E to close in on a target. A takedown resets E's cooldown. Don't save E when a kill is certain.
notes.locke-skill-passive: The more health an enemy has lost, the more bonus damage your passive's basic attacks deal. Keep using basic attacks against enemies who have lost health. When finishing a target, don't wait for your abilities to come off cooldown.
notes.locke-skill-r: R heavily slows enemies in its area and marks them. An enemy with an R mark is sealed if their health falls below the threshold. Sealing an enemy with R drops a relic on the ground. Picking up a relic permanently raises R's execution threshold. Collect dropped relics after a fight.
notes.locke-phase: Locke's melee range and high early mana costs make it hard to use combos back to back at levels 1–2. Locke ranks among the top mid champions for takedowns during the laning phase. Locke builds a lead through kills more than farming. After learning R at level 6, look for executions. As you collect relics, your ability to finish enemies keeps improving into the late game.
notes.locke-laning: As a melee champion, you have to accept losing some CS against ranged opponents. Use Q to put nails in your opponent rather than clear minions. After landing nails, win trades with basic attacks. If your opponent won't trade, use E's teleport to find an angle to engage.
notes.locke-laning-e-save: E is Locke's only escape tool in lane. Don't use E to engage first when you don't know where the enemy jungler is. A takedown resets E's cooldown. If you can secure the kill, use E to engage, then use it again to escape.
notes.locke-teamfight: Don't engage first in teamfights. Engage with E after your allies have damaged the enemy. After engaging, focus your passive and nail damage on enemies who have lost health. Use R where several enemies are grouped to spread its marks.
notes.locke-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has healing, buy Morellonomicon between core items. Locke deals damage over time by consuming nails with basic attacks. If the enemy heals while you're dealing damage, it's hard to bring them below the execution threshold.
notes.vs-locke-q: Locke's basic attacks deal rapidly increasing damage if you keep taking them while nails are stuck in you. If you're hit by nails, get out of Locke's basic attack range first.
notes.vs-locke-e: After Locke teleports with E, his next basic attack dashes to the target. Locke's dashing basic attack after E also hits enemies along its path. After Locke teleports with E, stand so your allies aren't lined up along his dash path.
notes.vs-locke-e-reset: A takedown resets Locke's E cooldown, letting him dive in repeatedly. The moment just after an ally is picked off is the most dangerous time for Locke's repeated engages. As soon as the first ally dies, retreat and regroup.
notes.vs-locke-w: With W active, Locke gains a large attack speed and movement speed boost while draining his own health. When W ends, Locke recovers a substantial portion of the health he lost. If you can't finish Locke while W is active, retreat before his healing triggers.
notes.vs-locke-r: If your health falls below the threshold while marked by R, you are sealed. When you see an R mark, retreat with more health remaining than usual. The more relics Locke collects, the higher R's sealing threshold rises.
notes.lucian-combo-weave: After Lucian uses an ability, his next basic attack fires twice. To deal full damage, alternate abilities with double-shot basic attacks. Using abilities back to back triggers the double shot only once.
notes.lucian-combo-lane: For lane trades, use Q, a double-shot basic attack, E, a double-shot basic attack, then W. Use E mid-combo to reposition and make up for his short range. Using E mid-combo lets you land one more double-shot basic attack.
notes.lucian-combo-q-minion: Q extends beyond its displayed range. Q cast on a front minion pierces through and hits a champion behind it. Target a front minion with Q to poke a champion behind it.
notes.lucian-combo-r: You can use E while casting R. While firing R, use E to keep your firing angle or move to safety. You cannot change R's aim during the cast. Line up with your target before starting R.
notes.lucian-skill-vigilance: When an ally heals or shields Lucian, his next two shots gain bonus damage. When a nearby enemy is immobilized, Lucian's next two shots gain bonus damage. Time your basic attacks with your support's shields or crowd control.
notes.lucian-skill-w: Hitting an enemy marked by W increases Lucian's movement speed. An ally hitting an enemy marked by W also triggers the movement speed boost. Mark enemies with W just before engaging or chasing.
notes.lucian-skill-e: Each double-shot basic attack reduces E's cooldown. Save E for when you need to dash.
notes.lucian-skill-r-usage: While escaping, fire R down a narrow passage to block the enemy's path. When enemies siege an allied turret, use R to clear the minion wave quickly.
notes.lucian-skill-r-cancel: You can recast R to stop it. Casting R triggers the passive double shot. If attacked from another angle, stop R and retaliate with a double-shot basic attack.
notes.lucian-skill-tower: Against turrets, regular basic attacks are faster than using abilities to trigger double shots. Save your abilities when attacking structures.
notes.lucian-phase-early: Lucian has short range for a marksman. Lucian is strong in early trades thanks to his double shot and E. Build a lead in lane.
notes.lucian-phase-late: Lucian excels at short bursts of damage over sustained damage. Other marksmen outperform him in prolonged teamfights. Take repeated short trades: move in, deal damage, then retreat with E.
notes.lucian-laning: Push the wave, since his short range makes him easy to poke. Use E to dodge the enemy support's engage. Trade when both Q and your double shot are ready. After trading, retreat behind your minions immediately.
notes.lucian-teamfight: In teamfights, come in from the side or follow up to finish targets already under crowd control. Mark your target with W before closing in to gain movement speed. Save E to disengage in teamfights.
notes.vs-lucian-extended: Weather Lucian's first combo, then extend the fight. Counterattack after Lucian has used all his abilities.
notes.vs-lucian-r: Lucian cannot change R's aim during the cast. When Lucian uses R, sidestep out of its firing path.
notes.vs-lucian-q: Lucian's Q extends beyond its displayed range and pierces through targets. When Lucian farms with Q, move out of the line behind his target minion.
notes.vs-lucian-vigilance: When the enemy support shields or heals Lucian, his next two shots are empowered. When an ally is immobilized, Lucian's next two shots are empowered. Avoid trading and back off while Lucian's next two shots are empowered.
notes.vs-lucian-e: Lucian reduces E's cooldown with each double-shot basic attack. To catch Lucian, engage during the brief window right after he uses E.
notes.lulu-combo-peel: When an ally is caught, protect them with W polymorph, E shield, then Q slow. Use W first as the enemy tries to follow up with another ability right after engaging. Use E for the damage that comes after W to make use of the shield's duration.
notes.lulu-combo-ult: R instantly increases the target ally's maximum health. Use R just before an ally dies to help them survive a burst of damage. R knocks up enemies around the target ally. Use R on an allied tank to help them engage.
notes.lulu-combo-q-angle: Q fires bolts from Lulu's and Pix's positions at different angles. Q's two bolts overlap more narrowly when the cursor is close and spread wider when it is far away. Keep the cursor close when using Q to reliably hit a single target. Keep the cursor far away when using Q to clip multiple targets.
notes.lulu-skill-w-ally: W increases an ally's movement speed when cast on them. W increases an ally's attack speed when cast on them. Use W on an ally when they chase or flee. Use W on an ally when focusing damage on the enemy carry. When you need to stop a reliable enemy engage, save W for the enemy.
notes.lulu-skill-w-enemy: W silences an enemy when cast on them. W prevents an enemy from attacking when cast on them. W does not stop an enemy from moving. Casting W during a dash does not stop the dash in progress. Use W when an enemy's dash ends and they try to use a follow-up ability to interrupt their combo.
notes.lulu-skill-e: E shields an ally when cast on them. E moves Pix to an ally when cast on them. Use E on a ranged ally who attacks frequently to add damage with Pix's bolts. E grants true sight of an enemy when cast on them. Use E to reveal an enemy's position in a brush or while stealthed.
notes.lulu-skill-e-timing: E's shield is short-lived, so using it too early lets it expire before the damage arrives. Watch the enemy's cast animation and time E for when the damage arrives.
notes.lulu-skill-passive: Other units in the path can take Pix's bolts instead and absorb the damage. Harass with a basic attack when the enemy steps beside the minions so they do not block Pix's bolts.
notes.lulu-phase-early: Lulu is strong early with Q poke and its slow. Maintain your poke advantage in lane. Avoid stepping forward to create the first opening to attack in lane.
notes.lulu-phase-scaling: Once Lulu gets R at level 6, she can save allies and punish enemies who overcommit to an engage. Lulu scales into the late game as her allied carry grows stronger. Prioritize protecting your allied carry's growth over your own.
notes.lulu-laning-bait: Lulu is strongest at responding when enemies commit heavily to an engage. Look to draw out an enemy engage, then counter with W and E. Lulu is vulnerable when she overcommits first because she lacks the damage to finish the fight.
notes.lulu-laning-mana: Q and E cost a lot of mana. Avoid pointless Q and E poke so you have mana to protect allies. Save E for its shield rather than poke. When you run out of mana, avoid overcommitting and look for a chance to recall.
notes.lulu-teamfight: In teamfights, stay close to your most fed ally. In teamfights, focus W, E, and R on your most fed ally. In teamfights, position to respond to whoever the enemy engages on instead of engaging yourself.
notes.lulu-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has a lot of lasting crowd control, buy Mikael's Blessing early to cleanse it from allies. W and E cannot cleanse crowd control already affecting an ally.
notes.vs-lulu-passive: Other units in the path can take Pix's bolts instead and absorb the damage. Stand behind minions to reduce damage from Pix's bolts that accompany Lulu's basic attacks.
notes.vs-lulu-commit: Lulu responds well when enemies commit heavily all at once. Use steady poke instead of a single committed engage to push Lulu and her lane partner out of lane.
notes.vs-lulu-w: An enemy affected by Lulu's W is silenced. An enemy affected by Lulu's W cannot attack. Before engaging with a dash, bait Lulu into using W on another ally.
notes.vs-lulu-r: Lulu's R instantly increases the target's health. Lulu's R knocks up enemies around the target. When Lulu's R is available, target Lulu herself or someone else instead of the ally she would protect.
notes.vs-lulu-squishy: Lulu has no dash to escape. Target Lulu herself while her shield and Pix are on her allied carry.
notes.lux-combo-full: Use the kill combo in this order: Q → place E → R → auto attack → detonate E → auto attack. Weave auto-attacks between abilities to keep consuming Illumination marks. Delay detonating E so you can land both auto-attacks.
notes.lux-combo-poke: In lane, poke by placing and detonating E, then auto-attacking to consume the Illumination mark. Use Q for kill opportunities or to stop enemy engages rather than for poke. Lux loses her means of fighting back when Q is down.
notes.lux-skill-passive: Illumination marks enemies hit by Lux's damaging abilities. Lux's auto-attacks consume Illumination marks to deal bonus magic damage. R consumes Illumination marks on hit, then reapplies them. After using R, auto-attack to consume the Illumination mark for extra damage. Use auto attacks after landing abilities to deal enough damage.
notes.lux-skill-q: Q fully roots the first two enemies it hits. Angle Q to root both the tank and the carry standing behind them. Lux relies on landing Q to land follow-up abilities and defend herself. Use Q carefully so a miss does not leave you defenseless.
notes.lux-skill-w: W grants a shield on both its outward and return paths. The two shields granted by W stack. Cast W toward grouped allies. While fleeing, cast W in the direction you are running to receive the returning shield sooner.
notes.lux-skill-e-zone: To control an area, place E and delay its detonation. Place E ahead of time on entry or escape routes to hinder enemy movement. Throw E into a brush to check for an ambush. E is Lux's most reliable ability to land. Avoid spamming the mana-heavy E so you do not run out of mana midway through laning.
notes.lux-phase: Look for kill opportunities as early as level 1 if Q's root lands. Treat level 6 as the first power spike, when R lets you finish enemies beyond your range. Lux deals her strongest damage during her mid-to-late-game burst window, after building up ability power. In the late game, prioritize positioning over damage to prepare for enemy assassins closing in.
notes.lux-laning-safety: Lux has no mobility ability. Lux has almost no way to respond when caught in an ambush. Play at maximum range to prepare for ambushes. Check unwarded brush with E before entering.
notes.lux-laning-wave: When support Lux hits minions with E, it pushes the lane and increases the risk of exposure to enemy jungle ganks. When you need to let the wave push toward you, use E so it only hits enemy champions. Use E on the wave only when you need to push.
notes.lux-teamfight: Position behind your team's frontline in teamfights. Use Q to stop enemy engages. Use E to block enemy movement routes. Use W to protect allies from burst damage. To get value for the mana spent, avoid angles that hit only one enemy and use abilities on multiple enemies.
notes.lux-situational-assassin: Buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier to prepare for enemy assassins closing in. With no mobility ability, Lux relies on W's shield for her own survival when caught.
notes.lux-situational-antiheal: Choose Morellonomicon to reduce healing when enemy healing becomes a problem. E and R apply Morellonomicon's healing reduction to multiple enemies at once.
notes.vs-lux-q: Lux relies on Q's root to guarantee that her remaining abilities land. Treat the moment after Lux misses Q as an opportunity to engage while she is defenseless. Bait out Lux's Q, dodge it, then engage.
notes.vs-lux-q-line: Q roots the first two enemies it hits. Avoid lining up with allies and leave space to the side so Q does not root you together.
notes.vs-lux-e: E hinders access to a specific area. Spread out and approach from different directions so E does not block you all.
notes.vs-lux-r: R displays a red targeting line before firing its main beam. When retreating at low health, avoid fleeing in a straight line to prepare for R. Prepare to dodge sideways as soon as R's red targeting line appears.
notes.vs-lux-passive: Getting hit by Lux's abilities applies an Illumination mark. Lux's auto-attacks consume Illumination marks to deal bonus damage. Move out of Lux's auto-attack range immediately after an ability hits you to avoid Illumination's bonus damage.
notes.vs-lux-squishy: Lux has no mobility ability. Lux struggles to survive when an enemy manages to get close. Find an approach angle from a brush or the flank to get close to Lux.
notes.lux-skill-r: R has a cast time. A red targeting line appears before R fires. R has a relatively short cooldown. As you level up, you can use R once per teamfight.
notes.lux-teamfight-ult: R passes through enemies in a straight line. Prioritize angles that let R pass through multiple grouped enemies in a line. Use R immediately when you can secure a kill or hit multiple enemies in a line.
notes.malphite-combo-trade: For short trades against melee opponents, activate W and attack in this order: basic attack → E → basic attack. W empowers your next basic attack and makes each basic attack leave an aftershock for the next few seconds. Use E after the opponent starts a basic attack to reduce their retaliation.
notes.malphite-combo-ult: Use R → W → basic attack → Q → E for your ultimate burst combo. Q and E are guaranteed to hit while R's knockup lasts. Activate W immediately after R to empower the basic attack you weave between abilities. Aim to kill squishy targets with one full ultimate combo.
notes.malphite-skill-armor-scaling: Both W and E deal damage that scales with armor. W's passive increases Malphite's armor. W's armor bonus increases greatly while Granite Shield is active. Armor items improve both survivability and W and E damage, so avoid leaving them out of your build entirely.
notes.malphite-skill-passive: Granite Shield regenerates only after you take no damage for a certain time. Start trades with Granite Shield charged. Back off and recharge Granite Shield when it breaks. Higher armor reduces the amount of Granite Shield depleted by physical attacks. Approach melee opponents while using Granite Shield to absorb their first basic attack. If ranged poke keeps interrupting your shield’s regeneration, find another way to sustain in lane.
notes.malphite-skill-e: E deals area damage to enemies within its range. E reduces the attack speed of enemies it hits. Use E immediately after a basic attack-focused opponent starts attacking. Save E until you have a target to fight instead of using it on cooldown to farm.
notes.malphite-skill-r-utility: R makes you unstoppable during the cast, ignoring most crowd control as you dash to the target location. Use R as an escape tool when fleeing a gank. Use R to dodge incoming skillshots by passing through them. Given R's long cooldown, decide in advance whether to use it to escape or save it to engage. Build ability haste to poke with Q and use R more often.
notes.malphite-phase: Malphite is weakest before level 6, when he has no R. Malphite's limited mana restricts how often he can poke early on. Take advantage of the power spike immediately after learning R. Take advantage of your peak strength in the mid game, when you have two or three armor items. Your damage contribution drops late in the game, so focus on starting teamfights with R.
notes.malphite-situational-armor: If the enemy's main damage is physical, focus on armor items that improve both survivability and W and E damage. Against physical damage, buy Glacial Buckler early, then build into Plated Steelcaps, Thornmail, Frozen Heart, and Randuin's Omen. If the enemy has plenty of healing, finish Thornmail first to apply Grievous Wounds.
notes.malphite-situational-mr: If the enemy's main damage is magic, choose Hollow Radiance for magic resistance and farming power. Choose Spirit Visage as your magic resistance item if you have allies who provide healing or shields. Choose Force of Nature when taking magic damage from multiple enemies. Keep one armor item for W and E damage even in a magic resistance-focused build.
notes.malphite-situational-ap: Choose an ability power build to secure kills with R when your team has another frontline tank and the enemy backline is squishy. Choose Rylai's Crystal Scepter to keep enemies from getting away after R. Choose Rabadon's Deathcap and Void Staff to increase R's damage. Choose Zhonya's Hourglass to buy time for your allies to join you after you engage with R. Choose Liandry's Torment to apply damage over time to multiple enemies with R.
notes.malphite-laning: During the laning phase, repeatedly poke with Q, then back off to recharge Granite Shield. Q steals the opponent's movement speed, making it harder for them to chase you after you poke. At low Q ranks, time your poke around when you can use a source of mana restoration. Malphite struggles to gain a lead through kills in lane. Extend your lead by pushing the wave and chipping away at turret health.
notes.malphite-teamfight: Only engage when R is available. When enemies group up, find an angle to knock up at least two with R.
