Look for a chance to kill a key damage dealer with R when they step out alone. Coordinate R's timing with your allies so they can follow up with area-of-effect ultimates at the knockup location.
notes.vs-malphite-r: Malphite's R is an unstoppable dash that cannot be interrupted by crowd control. If you don’t know where Malphite is, avoid standing close to allies near lanes or objectives.
notes.vs-malphite-early: Gain lane control before Malphite reaches level 6, while he has no R and is short on mana. Arrange a jungle gank before Malphite reaches level 6 to delay his scaling. Keep in mind that Malphite becomes harder to beat one-on-one once he has R and armor items.
notes.vs-malphite-passive: Break Malphite's Granite Shield before starting your combo. Prevent Granite Shield from regenerating with damage over time or frequent poke. Avoid starting a trade immediately after Q hits you, since it steals your movement speed.
notes.vs-malphite-e: E's attack speed reduction lowers the damage output of basic attack-focused champions. As a basic attack-focused champion, stay behind your allies and maintain your range while keeping outside E's range. Move in and attack after Malphite uses E.
notes.vs-malphite-grouping: Malphite’s R knocks up multiple enemies around where his dash ends. Before a teamfight, spread out so Malphite’s R can hit only one person. The opposing team is weakest right after Malphite uses his R. Counterattack hard right after Malphite uses his R.
notes.malzahar-combo-basic: For a basic trade, apply E, summon Voidlings with W, then silence with Q. Hitting a target affected by E with Q resets E's duration. Hitting a target affected by E with R resets E's duration. Using Q before E prevents you from refreshing E, greatly reducing your damage.
notes.malzahar-combo-ult: To secure a kill, apply E, summon Voidlings with W, then suppress with R. R refreshes E, so E keeps dealing damage after the suppression ends. While R suppresses the target, Voidlings attack them. R's zone remains around the target. Use R from a position where you can force the enemy toward your team.
notes.malzahar-skill-w: Each time you use another ability, W gains a stack. More W stacks summon more Voidlings. Use W after preparing for the fight. Build stacks with Q and E, then use W when the enemy enters range. Using W early when there are no nearby enemies to attack only wastes the Voidlings' duration.
notes.malzahar-skill-passive: Void Shift returns after you go without taking damage for a while. Void Shift greatly reduces incoming damage while active. Void Shift makes you immune to immobilizing effects and interruptions while active. Check often whether Void Shift is active in lane. Even minor damage from minions or jungle monsters can remove Void Shift.
notes.malzahar-skill-q: Q's hit area is the line segment between the two portals. Place Q across the enemy's path. Q's silence can interrupt an enemy as they begin to cast an ability. Save Q to stop enemies with engage abilities.
notes.malzahar-skill-e: When a target affected by E dies, E spreads to the nearest enemy. When a target affected by E dies, Malzahar restores mana. Early on, apply E to a minion to clear the wave as it spreads. As E spreads between minions, the wave pushes toward the enemy. Without vision, don't push the wave blindly with E.
notes.malzahar-skill-w-wave: Voidlings deal much more damage to lane minions affected by E. To clear a wave quickly, apply E, then use W. Using E and W together helps secure minion last hits. Push the lane quickly with E and W to make time for roams or objectives.
notes.malzahar-skill-r: A target suppressed by R cannot move, cast abilities, or use basic attacks. Most escape abilities cannot break R's suppression. Immobilizing crowd control on Malzahar interrupts R's suppression. Use R where your teammates can protect Malzahar. Use R after the enemy's follow-up engage ends.
notes.malzahar-laning: In lane, avoid losing while keeping your opponent tied to the lane. Continually pushing the wave with E and W forces the enemy mid laner to return to farm. After pushing the wave, spend time on objectives or securing vision. Don't step forward to harass with your short range.
notes.malzahar-laning-defense: Malzahar has no mobility ability and has short range. Against ranged poke champions, keep Void Shift active even if it means giving up a few CS. Against melee engage champions, save Q until they engage. Avoid using your abilities first in lane.
notes.malzahar-phase: Malzahar is weak at levels 1–2. Leveling E makes farming more reliable. At level 6, gaining R sharply increases Malzahar's ability to kill an enemy alone. Malzahar's impact in fights depends heavily on R's cooldown. After using R, don't force a fight.
notes.malzahar-teamfight: If you can't target the enemy carry, use R on an engaging champion to stop their engage. Summon Voidlings before a fight. Save Q until the enemy uses an engage ability. You can defend a side lane alone when R is available and you have vision.
notes.malzahar-situational-zhonya: Buy Zhonya's Hourglass early against an assassin who can engage instantly. Once Void Shift is broken, Malzahar has no way to escape. After Void Shift breaks, Zhonya's Hourglass lets you avoid an engage while waiting for your team.
notes.malzahar-situational-antiheal: Against champions with strong healing, buy Morellonomicon between core items. The sustained damage from E and Voidlings can keep Grievous Wounds applied continuously.
notes.vs-malzahar-e: Don't stand near a minion affected by E. When Malzahar applies E to the wave, back off and wait for the minions to be cleared.
notes.vs-malzahar-passive: Once Void Shift is removed, crowd control and burst damage become effective.
notes.vs-malzahar-r: Mobility abilities and shields cannot break R's suppression. Use Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar to remove R's suppression. Without a cleanse item, an ally must immobilize Malzahar to interrupt R's cast. When Malzahar has R available, don't walk alone through areas without vision.
notes.vs-malzahar-w: Close in on Malzahar when the Voidlings have disappeared or have not been summoned yet. If Voidlings have already been summoned, clear them first with an area ability.
notes.vs-malzahar-q: To dodge Q, move outside the line between the two portals. If you see Q being cast, delay your engage ability.
notes.vs-malzahar-gank: Call for a gank while Malzahar is pushing the lane. Before going in for a gank, remove Void Shift. In lane, look to kill Malzahar with your jungler.
notes.maokai-combo-engage: For a basic engage, use W to close in, land a Sap Magic basic attack, then use Q. While W roots the target, you can restore health with a Sap Magic basic attack. If you use Q first, it knocks the enemy away and throws off where your W lands.
notes.maokai-combo-q-direction: Q knocks nearby enemies away from Maokai. To knock an enemy toward your team, use W to pass through them, land on the other side, then use Q. To peel an enemy off your carry, stand between them and use Q.
notes.maokai-combo-ult: R's root lasts longer the farther the wall travels. For a longer root, cast R from as far away as possible. When R's wall hits an enemy champion, Maokai gains movement speed. After casting R, follow in with W.
notes.maokai-skill-passive: Using an ability or being hit by an enemy champion's ability reduces the cooldown of Sap Magic's heal. The more intense the fight, the more often you can use Sap Magic's heal. In a teamfight, keep using basic attacks whenever you have a target. In lane, use your Sap Magic empowered basic attack even on a minion to restore health.
notes.maokai-skill-w: Maokai cannot be targeted while casting W. Using W just as an enemy's targeted finishing ability comes in can negate it. Use W to close in while dodging an enemy's key ability.
notes.maokai-skill-e-brush: Saplings thrown into brush last longer and explode over a larger area. Place saplings at separate paths, one per path, instead of stacking them in one spot. Place saplings where enemies pass, such as river brush or the tri-brush, to gain vision and block their approach.
notes.maokai-skill-e-cooldown: When a sapling hits an enemy champion or epic monster, Sap Magic's heal cooldown is reduced further. Just before an objective fight, place saplings along the enemy's approach to create more chances to heal.
notes.maokai-laning: In bot lane, place saplings in both brushes to make them harder for the enemy to use. Root an enemy with W as they step forward to last-hit. Engage with W only when your ADC is close enough to land basic attacks. Maokai lacks the damage to engage alone in lane. Q costs a lot of mana, so don't waste it clearing minions.
notes.maokai-laning-wave: Don't force the wave to push. The closer the wave is to your side, the easier it is to get out after engaging with W. If you've pushed the wave near the enemy turret, don't engage with W.
notes.maokai-phase: Level 2, when both Q and W are available, is your first chance to trade. At level 6, R lets you look for forced engages during roams and objective fights. Later, health items increase sapling explosion damage and durability, letting Maokai keep engaging.
notes.maokai-teamfight-ult: If you cast R head-on, the enemy can see it and back away. Cast R from the side or behind. Cast R when the enemy enters a narrow passage with nowhere to dodge.
notes.maokai-teamfight-peel: When engaging is unfavorable, stay beside your carry and protect them. If an enemy gets onto your carry, knock them away with Q, then root them with W. Maokai deals little damage. Protect the space your carry needs instead of chasing one enemy.
notes.maokai-situational-mikael: If the enemy can immobilize and kill your carry, buy Mikael's Blessing before Locket of the Iron Solari. Maokai has no way to remove crowd control already affecting an ally.
notes.maokai-situational-armor: If the enemy's damage is mostly physical, choose Dead Man's Plate or Thornmail to survive longer and get more use from Sap Magic's heal.
notes.vs-maokai-sapling: A sapling chases the first enemy that comes close and explodes after some time or when it hits another enemy. A sapling placed in brush explodes over a larger area. If a sapling is chasing you, lead it toward minions or monsters to make it explode, away from your team.
notes.vs-maokai-passive: The more abilities you hit Maokai with, the faster Sap Magic's heal cooldown decreases. Use poke abilities on the enemy carry instead of Maokai. Ignore Maokai or deal with him using basic attacks.
notes.vs-maokai-w: Maokai cannot be targeted while dashing with W. Use targeted abilities after Maokai finishes his W dash and lands. Trade after Maokai has used W.
notes.vs-maokai-ult: The farther R's wall travels, the longer its root lasts. When you see R's wall, dodge perpendicular to its path. If you must cross R's wall, do it while it has traveled only a short distance. Fight Maokai's team in open areas with room to dodge.
notes.vs-maokai-cooldown: Maokai's threat in fights comes from W and R. Right after making Maokai use W without effect, step forward and trade. If Maokai's W is ready, stay out of its range near brush.
notes.masteryi-combo-basic: Activate E as you engage, use R if needed, then go in with Q and keep basic attacking. E and R durations do not tick down during Q and W.
notes.masteryi-combo-q-dodge: Master Yi cannot be targeted during Q. Dodge targeted crowd control or a finishing blow with Q as it comes in. If the enemy has guaranteed crowd control, walk in and save Q to dodge it.
notes.masteryi-combo-q-cd: Each basic attack reduces Q's cooldown. Just before a fight or objective, hit a camp to reduce Q's cooldown. With no other targets nearby, Q hits the same enemy repeatedly for maximum single-target damage. In a 1v1, lure the enemy away from minions and monsters.
notes.masteryi-combo-w: W Meditate restores health and reduces damage taken. Activate W as the enemy's burst damage lands. Double Strike stacks build during W's channel. R and E durations pause during W's channel. Immobilizing crowd control interrupts W, so use it after the enemy has spent their crowd control.
notes.masteryi-skill-passive: The passive makes a basic attack strike twice after a set number of attacks. Passive stacks remain when you switch targets. Build passive stacks on jungle monsters or minions before attacking a champion. Passive stacks build during W's channel, strengthening the first basic attack after Meditate.
notes.masteryi-skill-e: E adds true damage to basic attacks. E's true damage is not reduced by armor, so it matters more against enemies who build defensive stats. E's duration does not tick down during Q and W. E has a short duration, so wait until you have a target before activating it.
notes.masteryi-skill-r: R increases movement speed and attack speed and grants immunity to slows. Use R to close the gap against enemies who use slows to keep their distance. A takedown during R extends its duration and greatly reduces basic ability cooldowns. Activate R when you can secure a takedown.
notes.masteryi-jungle-clear: Q deals bonus damage to monsters, and basic attacks reduce Q's cooldown. Master Yi's high movement speed cuts travel time between camps. Early on, turn fast jungle clears into a lead in growth.
notes.masteryi-jungle-gank: Master Yi has no crowd control. Look for a gank when an ally has applied crowd control or the enemy has used their mobility and escape abilities. If the conditions for a gank are not there, steal enemy jungle camps or prepare an objective. In games with frequent fights, plan your path around the time you cannot spend helping lanes.
notes.masteryi-jungle-counter: Early on, basic attacks are his only fighting tool, so junglers with crowd control can catch him easily. Get vision and confirm the enemy jungler is at camps on the opposite side before counterjungling.
notes.masteryi-phase: From level 1 until you learn R, focus on farming; fights are usually unfavorable. After learning R, takedowns reduce ability cooldowns and accelerate your growth. The mid to late game, when you have at least two items with attack speed and penetration, is your strong period. You become weaker again if the enemy has both crowd control and defensive items.
notes.masteryi-teamfight: Do not engage first in teamfights. Wait out of vision until the enemy has used their immobilizing crowd control, then use Q to reach the backline. Take down the first target, use R's takedown effect to get Q back, and move to the next target. If you cannot take down the first target in a teamfight, you can die easily. Pressure a side lane and wait for the enemy to split up instead of facing them head-on at an objective.
notes.masteryi-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has a champion with strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Master Yi keeps Grievous Wounds applied through repeated basic attacks.
notes.masteryi-situational-qss: If the enemy has several sources of guaranteed crowd control, consider Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar before damage items. Master Yi struggles to act when locked down by crowd control. Q's untargetability does not remove crowd control already applied.
notes.vs-masteryi-q: Master Yi cannot be targeted while casting Q. Use targeted crowd control or a finishing blow right after Q ends and Master Yi lands.
notes.vs-masteryi-w: Immobilizing crowd control can interrupt W Meditate. When Master Yi activates W, interrupt it with a stun, root, or knockup. Save one of your team's crowd control abilities to interrupt Master Yi's W.
notes.vs-masteryi-r: Slows do not work on Master Yi while R is active. If Master Yi gets no takedown, R's duration is not extended and it ends.
notes.vs-masteryi-reset: A takedown greatly reduces Master Yi's basic ability cooldowns, letting him reach the next target. Do not let Master Yi catch an ally alone in a teamfight. Stay grouped and layer crowd control to catch Master Yi on his first engage.
notes.vs-masteryi-truedamage: Master Yi's basic attacks deal some true damage while E is active. To counter E's true damage, build health and bring crowd control and ways to keep him from closing in.
notes.vs-masteryi-early: Early on, Master Yi is weak in the jungle and has very little gank potential. Early on, you can meet Master Yi in his jungle and fight him. Secure early objectives quickly to slow Master Yi's growth. Master Yi grows stronger the longer the game lasts.
notes.mel-combo-basic: After landing E's root, follow up with Q and an auto, then finish with R if you have enough Overwhelm. Q keeps exploding after the first blast, so the target must stay in place to take every hit. Use Q on the rooted target after E's root lands.
notes.mel-combo-passive: Each ability you use adds extra projectiles to your next auto. Using several abilities in a row lets you load the maximum number of extra projectiles onto one auto. Weave one auto into the end of your combo to fire your stored extra projectiles.
notes.mel-combo-execute: Overwhelm stacks from both ability and auto damage, with no stack limit. When its stored damage exceeds the target's remaining health plus shields, your next attack becomes an execute. Attack right after the target's shield breaks or expires.
notes.mel-skill-q: Use Q when the target has a reason to stay in its blast area. Look for Q when the target is rooted, steps among minions for a last hit, or is trapped in a narrow passage. In lane, use Q to clear the wave and harass at the same time.
notes.mel-skill-w: W reflects projectiles for a short time. Time W for the moment an enemy skillshot projectile comes toward you. W's reflected damage is calculated using the original caster's stats. W cannot reflect dashes, targeted abilities, or area effects that have already been cast. With W's long cooldown in mind, pick a catch ability to reflect and watch for it.
notes.mel-skill-w-mana: Leveling W reduces both its cooldown and mana cost. W is maxed last in the statistically preferred skill order, so its mana cost and cooldown remain a burden during lane. In the early and mid game, save W to reflect projectiles. Later, when mana is no longer a concern, use it defensively.
notes.mel-skill-e: E roots targets hit by the center of its orb and deals slow and damage over time around it. Even if the root misses, use E's lingering area to cut off the target's path. E deals reduced damage to minions, so do not use it to farm.
notes.mel-skill-r: R hits every enemy with Overwhelm, regardless of distance. Use R to join fights in other lanes or around objectives when you have vision. Use R before the remaining Overwhelm stacks on enemy champions expire. If you can add another Overwhelm stack, do so before using R for more damage. Learning R increases Overwhelm's damage, letting you reach the execute threshold sooner.
notes.mel-laning: Mel's long range and Q waveclear make it easy for her to gain lane priority. Stand behind your minion wave so melee opponents have farther to travel to reach you.
notes.mel-laning-trade: In trades, stack Overwhelm with Q and push the opponent back, then land E as they approach. Save E from early harass so you can stop the opponent's engage.
notes.mel-phase: Mel is weakest at levels 1–2 because her mana costs are high and W has a long cooldown. At level 6, learning R increases Overwhelm's damage and lets you finish fights from afar. Mel has a low win rate with only one core item, but it rises sharply as she completes her core build. Play safely early and wait for your core items.
notes.mel-teamfight: In teamfights, stay at the back and use Q on grouped enemies to apply Overwhelm to several of them. Use W as an enemy engage ability comes toward you. If you miss the chance to use W in a teamfight, do not step forward. Use R after the enemies have lost health and several have Overwhelm stacks.
notes.mel-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier in your core build. W only reflects projectiles, so it cannot stop dashes or targeted engages.
notes.mel-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps raising the execute threshold, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Overwhelm's execute checks the target's remaining health plus shields.
notes.vs-mel-w-reflect: Mel's W reflects projectiles for a brief moment. If Mel looks ready to use W, bait it out with a low-value ability or auto before using your main skillshot. If you have a dash, targeted ability, or an area effect already on the ground, use it against Mel's W first.
notes.vs-mel-passive: Each hit from Mel adds Overwhelm stacks. If the stored damage exceeds your remaining health plus shields, her next attack executes you. If you have taken several hits from Mel's harass, back off based on how many times she has hit you, rather than your current health.
notes.vs-mel-e: Mel's E roots at the center of its orb and only slows at the edges. When Mel's E comes toward you, sidestep its center. Save a movement ability or cleanse for the Q barrage after Mel's E root.
notes.vs-mel-r: Mel's R has no range limit and can hit enemies with Overwhelm from far away. Even after leaving a fight, wait somewhere safe until your Overwhelm stacks expire.
notes.vs-mel-early: Mel has no movement ability. If you are melee or have a dash, close the distance to Mel during lane. Pressure Mel before she completes her core items to delay her build.
notes.milio-skill-q-aim: Q knocks back the first enemy it hits, then bounces up and explodes. Aim Q differently to peel an enemy away or slow a group. Hitting a champion with Q refunds some mana.
notes.milio-skill-q-peel: Q is Milio's only displacement tool. Save Q to peel enemies off your allied marksman. Don't spend Q on lane poke.
notes.milio-skill-w-follow: W follows the ally closest to where it was cast. Place W on the ground near the ally you want it to follow. If W follows the wrong ally, recast it to switch targets. In a teamfight, recast W immediately if the ally it follows retreats or falls.
notes.milio-skill-w-timing: W's main value is increasing allies' attack range. Use W when your allied marksman starts attacking the enemy frontline. Don't use W before a fight just for the healing.
notes.milio-skill-e-charges: E has two charges, and its shields stack on the same target. If an ally needs a large shield, use E on them twice. If a fight is coming, keep one E charge ready.
notes.milio-skill-e-speed: E's movement speed boost is used more often than its shield. Use E on an ally before roaming or moving to an objective. Use E on an ally before an enemy skillshot hits them.
notes.milio-skill-passive: Allies touched by Milio's abilities deal bonus damage on their next attack. Use E on an ally just before a trade to add passive damage. While W lasts, it reapplies the passive at regular intervals. Start lane trades by using an ability on an ally.
notes.milio-skill-r: R provides area healing, cleanses immobilizing effects, and grants tenacity. R cannot cleanse airborne effects. Use R when multiple allies are immobilized.
notes.milio-combo-trade: In lane, use E on an ally and proc the passive with a basic attack, then use Q to knock the enemy back if they close in. Starting a trade with Q knocks the enemy out of your ally's attack range.
notes.milio-laning: Against a hard engage opponent, move forward only after securing vision of the brush.
notes.milio-laning-early: From the early levels when E can hold two charges, your allies can better withstand poke. When the enemy support pokes, absorb it with E and maintain the wave. Take a head-on fight only when W has increased your allies' range.
notes.milio-phase: Milio has low kill participation and damage early on. Early on, keep your allies alive instead of starting fights. Milio's shields and healing grow as he gets more items. Milio is strongest in late teamfights where his allied marksman can keep attacking. Don't overextend and die early.
notes.milio-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your team's main damage dealer and use W to increase their range. In teamfights, spread E among your allies. Use R right after the enemy's area crowd control lands. Save Q for champions who engage on your allies.
notes.milio-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has a lot of sustained crowd control, fit Mikael's Blessing between core items for a cleanse besides R.
notes.vs-milio-focus: Use an engage ability to catch Milio first and cut off the enemy team's sustain.
notes.vs-milio-q: Q knocks back the first enemy it hits and is Milio's only escape tool. Check whether Milio's Q is down before deciding to engage.
notes.vs-milio-w: W increases the attack range of Milio's allies. When the enemy marksman's range increases, delay the frontline fight until W ends.
notes.vs-milio-r: Milio's R cleanses immobilizing effects but cannot cleanse knockups. When engaging with a knockup, you can still look for an opening even if Milio has R available.
notes.vs-milio-early: Milio's team composition gets stronger over time. During the early laning phase, wear down Milio's mana through poke and take control of the wave. When Milio's healing starts to become a problem, get healing reduction earlier.
notes.missfortune-combo-lovetap: Love Tap triggers only when you basic attack a different target from the previous one. In lane, alternate basic attacks between minions and the enemy champion to harass. Basic attacking the same enemy repeatedly greatly reduces your harass damage.
notes.missfortune-combo-q-bounce: Use Q on a front minion to harass the enemy champion behind it with the bounce. If Q kills the first target, it always critically strikes the second target. To increase Q bounce harass damage, choose a low-health minion as the first target.
notes.missfortune-combo-teamfight: At the start of a fight, slow the enemy formation with E, then use R. If an ally's area crowd control lands first, skip E and use R immediately.
notes.missfortune-skill-passive: Each Love Tap trigger reduces W's cooldown. If W is on cooldown, switch basic attack targets to trigger Love Tap.
notes.missfortune-skill-q: Q is targeted, so it cannot miss. Q costs a lot of mana, so using it too often will leave you out of mana by mid-laning phase. Using Q only on minions without an angle to bounce it onto a champion pushes the lane without gaining any harass advantage. Look to harass with Q when the enemy champion stands behind a minion.
notes.missfortune-skill-w: W's movement speed bonus reaches its maximum only after you spend time without taking damage. Miss Fortune uses W's movement speed bonus to survive and roam. Activate W for trades that need attack speed or when taking down a turret, rather than to escape.
notes.missfortune-skill-e: E's main value is its slow and the vision it provides, more than its damage. Use E to stop the enemy from engaging. Use E to gain vision inside a brush. Use E to block the enemy's escape route. Just before a teamfight, place E on the enemy's approach to discourage an engage.
notes.missfortune-skill-r: If R's channel is interrupted, all remaining waves are lost. Use R when you have at least one of these conditions: you are at the edge of its range, you have a wall or brush behind you, or an ally has just landed crowd control. R's cone direction is fixed when you cast it. Before enemies spread out, aim R where it will hit the most of them.
notes.missfortune-phase: Miss Fortune is an early-game marksman who can gain a harass advantage from level 1 with her passive and Q. Once you learn R at level 6, use your support's landed crowd control as a kill opportunity. Miss Fortune has no dash and average range, making it hard for her to position alone in the late game. Play to end the game with the lead you build in the early and mid game.
notes.missfortune-laning-wave: Harassing with Q inevitably pushes the lane toward the enemy. Continuously pushing the lane without knowing the enemy jungler's path leaves you open to ganks. Without vision, save Q and harass only with passive basic attacks. If you plan to push the lane, use Q to clear minions quickly. After pushing the lane, use W's movement speed to get river vision or recall.
notes.missfortune-laning-roam: W's movement speed bonus lets Miss Fortune return from base and rejoin the lane faster than other marksmen. Moving without taking damage lets W's movement speed bonus reach its maximum. After pushing the enemy out of lane, actively look for chances to join your team at mid or an objective.
notes.missfortune-teamfight: In teamfights, deal area damage from the back line. After your team absorbs the enemy engage, use R when the enemies group up in one direction. If you use R before the enemy formation overlaps and they spread out, its damage drops sharply. When R is unavailable, use E to discourage enemy engages. When R is unavailable, rely on basic attacks to get through teamfights.
notes.missfortune-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has a champion with healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items for Grievous Wounds. With Executioner's Calling, each hit of R reapplies Grievous Wounds.
notes.missfortune-situational-qss: If enemy stuns keep interrupting R, buy Quicksilver Sash before other defensive items. Miss Fortune's teamfight impact depends heavily on completing R's channel.
notes.vs-missfortune-q: Q hits the front target, then bounces to a target behind it. Standing directly behind a lane minion exposes you to Q's bounce. To avoid Q harass, stand to the side so you are not in line with a minion.
notes.vs-missfortune-r: R is a channeled ability, so if crowd control interrupts it, all remaining waves are lost. If you have no crowd control, use a wall or brush to block vision. R's cone direction is fixed when you cast it. To dodge R, move out through the side of the cone rather than retreating straight back.
notes.vs-missfortune-w: When Miss Fortune takes damage, W's movement speed bonus resets. Damage a fleeing Miss Fortune to remove W's movement speed bonus. Save damage-over-time or long-range abilities to use when chasing Miss Fortune.
notes.vs-missfortune-mobility: Miss Fortune has no mobility ability. If your champion has an engage ability, get onto Miss Fortune after level 6 and try to kill her. If you cannot get onto her, use vision to deny Miss Fortune an angle to attack instead of fighting over range.
notes.vs-missfortune-e: Avoid starting a fight where E has been placed. E's slow delays both engaging and disengaging. If R overlaps E, you risk taking heavy damage. When E is placed, delay your engage. Lure the enemy out of E's area.
notes.wukong-combo-eq: Buffer Q while dashing in with E. Q empowers your next basic attack. Activate Q during the dash to land the empowered attack faster than if you activate it after arriving.
notes.wukong-combo-rw: Use W immediately after starting R. A W clone created immediately after R mimics Cyclone. Use W's invisibility to retreat and avoid the enemy's counterattack.
notes.wukong-combo-r-flash: You can move while casting R. To compensate for R's short range, Flash into the middle of the enemy team while casting it. To knock up multiple enemies with R, reach them before they spread out.
notes.wukong-skill-r: Your movement speed increases during R. Walk into grouped enemies while spinning with R. Use the first R as a signal for your team to engage. Use the second R to finish enemies off or hinder their escape. Stuns and roots interrupt R, so use it after the enemy's main crowd control has been used.
notes.wukong-skill-w: W is a dash that briefly makes you invisible. W leaves a stationary clone where you cast it. Use your W clone to draw targeted enemy abilities away from you. Do not use W immediately after engaging, so you can disappear from enemy vision and disguise your movement direction. W's invisibility is revealed by turrets and true sight.
notes.wukong-skill-q: Q is an empowered basic attack with increased range. Q's armor reduction also increases your allies' physical damage. Q's cooldown decreases whenever Wukong or his clone attacks an enemy. Save Q for champion fights instead of wasting it on a wave or camp beforehand.
notes.wukong-skill-passive: Gain P stacks whenever you attack champions or jungle monsters. P stacks increase your armor. P stacks increase your healing. Attack nearby jungle monsters just before a fight to build up P stacks. Clone attacks also build P stacks.
notes.wukong-skill-e: E is a targeted dash that enemies cannot dodge. E has short range, so first find an opening to get close to the enemy. Do not use E first while the enemy still has their mobility ability available. Follow up with basic attacks immediately after E lands to use the increased attack speed.
notes.wukong-phase: Wukong's early clear speed and damage per minute are average. Wukong is especially vulnerable to magic damage. Build an advantage through early ganks. Wukong is strongest when he gets R at level 6 and in the mid game when he completes his first core item.
notes.wukong-jungle-path: To clear faster, move between camps without letting your P stacks expire. R deals heavy damage to jungle camps. R has a long cooldown, so save it for fights instead of using it to clear camps.
notes.wukong-objective: Decide whether to start an objective fight based on whether R is available. Without R, engaging and disengaging are difficult, so secure vision and retreat. Force an objective fight as soon as R becomes available again.
notes.wukong-teamfight: In teamfights, wait for an opening to land R. When two or more enemies overlap, close in with E and use R. Time your engage so you do not go in late alone and get picked off. Coordinate the timing of your R casts with your team's crowd control.
notes.wukong-teamfight-clone: Enemies have a hard time distinguishing the W clone from the real Wukong. While enemies attack your W clone, circle around the side and enter their backline. When close to death, use W as a last resort to escape and deceive enemies.
notes.vs-wukong-clone: The real Wukong uses W to turn invisible and retreat in another direction. Avoid mistaking the W clone for the real Wukong and unloading your abilities on it. When a W clone appears, first check the directions the real Wukong is likely to move. Identify the W clone by the fact that it stays in place.
notes.vs-wukong-r: R knocks up multiple enemies at once. R deals damage based on maximum health. Spread out when Wukong's R is available. Account for R's second cast when deciding how far to retreat. Account for the clone copying R when deciding how far to retreat.
notes.vs-wukong-e: E is a targeted dash, so it cannot be dodged. Stay outside E range to prevent Wukong from engaging. If Wukong closes in and reduces your armor with Q, subsequent trades become unfavorable.
notes.vs-wukong-passive: Wukong gains more armor through P as he attacks champions or jungle monsters. Wukong gains more healing through P as he attacks champions or jungle monsters. P stacks give Wukong a greater advantage the longer he stays in close combat. Against Wukong, repeatedly go in for short trades and disengage instead of taking extended duels.
notes.vs-wukong-mr: Champions focused on magic damage can come out far ahead in early trades against Wukong. If your champion focuses on magic damage, fight back aggressively when Wukong closes in during the early game.
notes.vs-wukong-r-window: Wukong has a harder time engaging and disengaging without R. Force an objective or a fight immediately after Wukong uses R. If Wukong disappears from vision with R available, first break up your grouped formation.
notes.mordekaiser-combo-basic: Start a basic trade by pulling the enemy in with E, then landing Q. Follow up Q with basic attacks. Use Q from an angle where the enemy does not overlap with minions. Without using E first, the enemy can walk out of Q range.
notes.mordekaiser-combo-passive: The passive aura activates after landing three abilities or basic attacks on enemy champions or jungle monsters. Weave a basic attack between E and Q to activate the passive aura in time. When the passive aura activates, your movement speed increases, making it easier to chase.
notes.mordekaiser-combo-w: On activation, W converts stored damage dealt and taken into a shield. Use W's shield after exchanging damage. W's stored amount decays over time. Recasting W heals you for a percentage of the remaining shield. If you will not take more damage, recast W to heal while the shield is still large.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-duel: R takes one target into another realm, forcing a one-on-one duel for its duration. Neither side's allies can intervene inside R. R steals a portion of the target's key stats. R's stat steal gives you a chance to win duels against enemies who are hard to beat outside it.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-target: Mordekaiser relies heavily on his choice of R target. Taking an enemy frontliner with R leaves your allies to face the remaining enemy damage dealers. Taking an enemy damage dealer with R leaves your allies to face the remaining frontline. Among targets you can kill within R's duration, choose the most important champion in the enemy composition. Exclude high-health frontliners and enemies with instant-cast invulnerability from your R targets.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-defense: Protect your allies by taking an enemy diver into R as soon as they reach an allied damage dealer. Killing the target inside R lets you keep the stolen stats until they respawn.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-cast: R is a short-range targeted ability. Use R immediately after pulling the enemy in with E. Use Flash to close the distance and cast R. Use R on a clear target rather than holding it until you miss the chance to cast it.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-e: E passively provides magic penetration even without being cast. Do not delay putting skill points into E to increase your overall damage. E pulls all enemies within its area. In teamfights, use E to pull multiple enemies into Q and passive aura range.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-q: Q deals greatly increased damage when it hits a single target. When trading in lane, avoid minions and hit only the enemy champion with Q. When using Q to clear waves, account for giving up its single-target damage bonus. Do not try to trade and farm with the same Q.
notes.mordekaiser-phase: Start looking for trades from level 3 onward, when you have both E and Q. Look for kills in lane once you learn R at level 6. Use R for clear kill opportunities rather than forcing early dives. Late in the game, R can isolate only one enemy, so its impact varies greatly with the enemy composition.
notes.mordekaiser-laning-melee: Start a trade by pulling a melee opponent with E as they step forward to last-hit. Stay close to melee opponents, weaving in basic attacks until the passive aura activates. Keep pressuring melee opponents once the passive aura activates.
notes.mordekaiser-laning-ranged: Do not push the wave against ranged opponents. Farm safely with Q against ranged opponents. Mordekaiser has no mobility ability, so forcing an approach against ranged opponents can easily cost him health. Against ranged opponents, fight back with R after level 6 in coordination with your jungler's gank.
notes.mordekaiser-teamfight: Use E to group multiple enemies in teamfights. In teamfights, hold your ground among enemies with the passive aura active. Cast R on a key enemy champion after they use their main abilities. Choose your initial entry position carefully, as having no mobility ability makes it hard to retreat and re-engage.
notes.mordekaiser-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, choose Morellonomicon for healing reduction. The passive aura's continuous damage makes it easy to maintain Morellonomicon's healing reduction. Morellonomicon's healing reduction is especially effective when forcing a duel inside R.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-r: If you are caught in R, your allies cannot help you for its duration. R steals some of your stats, so you can lose a duel you would win outside it. Do not enter Mordekaiser's ultimate range alone while his R is available.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-passive: Mordekaiser's passive aura activates after landing three abilities or basic attacks. Keep trades short, exchanging only one or two hits before backing off to prevent the passive aura from activating. Once the passive aura activates, limit the time you spend fighting up close.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-w: The more damage Mordekaiser deals and takes, the larger the shield he gains from W. Mordekaiser can convert his remaining W shield into healing. Focus your damage after his W shield wears down or is converted into healing.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-e: E pulls all enemies within its area at once. In narrow passages or tight formations, multiple players can be pulled by E and hit by both Q and the passive aura. Spread out from your allies when standing in front of Mordekaiser.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-mobility: Mordekaiser has low mobility because he has no mobility ability. Use slows and maintain distance to fight outside Mordekaiser's E range. Once Mordekaiser backs off, he struggles to close the distance again. Prioritize a position where Mordekaiser cannot catch you over dealing more damage.
notes.morgana-combo-basic: When you have a kill opportunity, root the target with Q, place W under them, then use R. Time R so its stun follows as the Q root ends. If Q misses, don't use R first; the target can walk away.
notes.morgana-combo-r-flash: Flash into the enemy team right after casting R, keeping the chains connected to bind more enemies. Morgana gains movement speed while casting R.
notes.morgana-combo-r-survive: If Morgana dies before R's stun triggers, the chains break. Use Zhonya's Hourglass to survive until R's stun triggers. If you have no way to survive after using R, use it only after an ally holds the enemy in place.
notes.morgana-skill-q: Q roots only the first target it hits. Minions block Q. Cast Q along a clear line, such as beside the wave or through a jungle entrance. Morgana relies on landing Q to make her other abilities more effective.
notes.morgana-skill-w: W deals more damage the more health its target has lost. Use W to force a wounded enemy out of an area. Each time Morgana heals through her passive, W's cooldown decreases. Use W freely during fights.
notes.morgana-skill-e-timing: E blocks crowd control and immobilizing effects while the shield remains. Use E as soon as you see the enemy begin casting, rather than applying it early. Use E to block the crowd control an enemy uses to engage.
notes.morgana-skill-e-self: You can cast E on yourself. If an enemy engages on you, cast E on yourself to buy time to use R. Using E on yourself leaves your allied damage dealer unprotected from the next engage, so choose the shield target carefully.
notes.morgana-skill-e-vs-engage: Against enemies who start combos with a pull or knockback, save E to block that engage. Don't use E for anything else until the enemy's key engage ability is spent.
notes.morgana-skill-r: R is an area ability centered on Morgana. Move among enemies to hit them with R. Use R only when allies can follow up immediately, since you need to survive until its stun triggers. Gain vision of every enemy affected by R.
notes.morgana-phase: Morgana's laning strength depends heavily on landing Q. At level 6, learning R gives Morgana her first reliable kill opportunity. From mid game, once she has items, use E and R to start and stop teamfights. Statistically, Morgana has low early kill participation. Don't force kills early.
notes.morgana-laning-wave: In bot lane, avoid pushing the wave unnecessarily with W. Place W under an enemy champion to poke and deny space. Only push the wave with W when leaving bot lane to ward or roam. If you're holding a lane alone, use W to farm.
notes.morgana-laning-mana: Missing Q repeatedly can leave you out of mana and unable to respond. Don't cast Q if the angle is uncertain. If landing Q is unlikely, poke only with W and conserve mana. When the enemy can engage, prioritize keeping enough mana for E.
notes.morgana-teamfight: In teamfights, prioritize using E to block the enemy engage champion's crowd control. In teamfights, block the engage with E, then prioritize using R. Q is hard to land once a teamfight starts, so line up a shot beforehand.
notes.morgana-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, choose Morellonomicon to reduce it. Dealing continuous damage with W and R makes it easier to maintain healing reduction.
notes.vs-morgana-q: Morgana's Q roots only the first target it hits. Keep a minion between you and Morgana to block Q.
notes.vs-morgana-w: Morgana's W deals more damage to targets with more missing health. When retreating on low health, don't cross Morgana's W.
notes.vs-morgana-e: Don't waste crowd control on a target while E is active. Track E's cooldown and engage while it's unavailable.
notes.vs-morgana-r: R's stun triggers after a delay, not as soon as the chains connect. When you see R's chains, use a movement ability to leave its range before the stun triggers. If you can't leave R's range, kill Morgana before the stun triggers.
notes.vs-morgana-phase: Morgana relies on landing Q to threaten opponents in lane. Getting hit by Q leaves you exposed to W and a follow-up combo. In lane, prioritize positioning to dodge Q over calculating damage.
notes.naafiri-combo-q: You can use Q's two casts separately. The second Q deals extra damage based on missing health if it hits a bleeding target. Apply bleed with the first Q, then line up the second Q while the bleed lasts. When the first Q hits, the pack leaps at the target and helps close the gap.
notes.naafiri-combo-allin: For an all-in, activate W, land the first Q, close in with E, then land the second Q and an auto attack. Activate W before going in: it boosts attack damage and movement speed and adds two packmates. Save E so you can follow if the enemy backs away.
notes.naafiri-combo-r: R is a targeted dash to a champion. A takedown reveals nearby enemies and lets you cast R again. The second R cast grants a shield. Use R to engage when you can secure the first takedown, then use the second R to escape or move on to the next target.
notes.naafiri-skill-pack: The pack accounts for a significant share of Naafiri's damage. Packmates replenish slowly, one at a time. Hitting a champion or large monster with an ability speeds up packmate regeneration. Just before a fight, land an ability to replenish your pack. If every packmate dies, Naafiri loses a lot of damage.
notes.naafiri-skill-pack-target: The pack follows and attacks Naafiri's designated target. If you hit a minion just before trading, the pack goes after it, delaying your damage against the champion. Just before closing in, target the enemy champion or mark them with Q to send the pack ahead.
notes.naafiri-skill-e: E recalls the pack and fully restores its health. If area damage has hurt the pack, use E during the fight to heal it. When the pack is at full health, you can use E to engage.
notes.naafiri-skill-w: W briefly makes Naafiri untargetable and recalls the pack. W does not heal the recalled pack. Use E to restore the pack's health. Use W's untargetability when targeted crowd control or a finishing ability is coming.
notes.naafiri-skill-w-aoe: Recall the pack with W or E before enemy area damage hits. Recalled packmates cannot be targeted, so they avoid area damage.
notes.naafiri-skill-r-vision: You need a takedown to cast R a second time. A takedown reveals nearby enemies, letting you choose your next target. If you engage with R without a secure takedown, you have no way back.
notes.naafiri-laning: As a melee mid laner, Naafiri struggles to farm against ranged opponents. The pack helps attack minions, and Q's bleed can secure last hits from range. Clear waves the enemy has pushed in with the pack and Q to keep up in levels. Go in when the enemy's skillshot is on cooldown.
notes.naafiri-laning-roam: Naafiri has high movement speed, and W makes her faster, so she can roam quickly. Push the lane, then move to a side lane or the enemy jungle to create a numbers advantage. Roam to get ahead instead of only farming mid.
notes.naafiri-phase: Even early on, the pack lets Naafiri clear waves and harass. At level 6, learning R gives Naafiri many more kill opportunities with its targeted dash. Naafiri is strongest at roaming and flanking in the mid game. In late-game front-to-back teamfights, area damage can wipe out the pack and reduce her damage. Build on your lead before the game goes long.
notes.naafiri-teamfight: Do not enter teamfights from the front. From the side or behind, use the first R to take out a backline target, then use the second R gained from the takedown to reach another target or escape. Check your pack count and whether the enemy has area damage before going in. If the pack has taken damage, heal it with E before going in.
notes.naafiri-situational-antiheal: If the enemy is surviving through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Naafiri chips away at health with bleed and her pack, so enemy healing makes assassinations harder.
notes.vs-naafiri-pack: Removing the pack greatly reduces Naafiri's damage. Clear the pack first with area damage. Naafiri can fully restore the pack's health with E. Counterattack right after Naafiri uses E. Save area damage while the pack is recalled.
notes.vs-naafiri-w: Naafiri is untargetable for a short time while W is active. Use targeted crowd control or finishing abilities after W ends.
notes.vs-naafiri-q: If the second Q hits while the first Q's bleed is active, the damage rises sharply. If the first Q hits you, keep your distance until the bleed ends. If you get close to Naafiri while bleeding, you will take the second Q and the pack's attacks together.
notes.vs-naafiri-r: R is a targeted dash to a champion, so you cannot dodge it. Do not go alone when Naafiri has R available. Immediately back away after an ally dies so Naafiri cannot take you out next with her second R.
notes.vs-naafiri-range: As a melee champion, Naafiri is outranged by ranged champions. Harass Naafiri and farm from behind minions. Do not give Naafiri an opening to close in with E. The pack clears waves, making it hard to fully freeze the lane against Naafiri.
notes.vs-naafiri-late: In late-game front-to-back teamfights, area damage hurts the pack and reduces Naafiri's damage. In the late game, fight together to deny Naafiri an opening to reach the backline. Keep broad vision during Naafiri's mid-game roaming phase.
notes.nami-combo-engage: To engage, use R to knock enemies up, then place Q where they will land. R travels slowly, so confirm it hits before throwing Q. Chain Q's stun as R's knockup ends to leave the enemy no time to react.
notes.nami-combo-trade: For lane trades, cast E on your ADC, throw Q when the enemy steps up, then use W while they are stunned. E empowers a fixed number of attacks. Use E after checking that your ally is in position to land basic attacks.
notes.nami-combo-w-bounce: W bounces between allies and enemies. W hits each target only once. W is most effective when allies and enemies are close together. Choose W's first target based on whether healing or damage takes priority. W only bounces to visible enemies.
notes.nami-skill-q: Q takes time to land, so enemies can dodge it by walking away. Throw Q when an enemy starts a last-hit animation. Throw Q at enemies already under crowd control. Time Q with an ally's dash. Q has a long cooldown, leaving a long gap in your ability to intervene if it misses.
notes.nami-skill-q-terrain: Q lands at a targeted location, so you can cast it over walls. Predict the path of an enemy fleeing into a bush or behind a wall and catch them with Q, even without vision. Enemies may anticipate Q over a wall, so do not use the same angle repeatedly.
notes.nami-skill-w-mana: W costs a lot of mana. Nami's lane sustain depends on W's healing. Avoid using W only to poke enemies so you have enough mana left to heal allies. Early on, save W until an ally's health is actually at risk. During trades, use W only when it can bounce between an ally and an enemy.
notes.nami-skill-e: E has a short duration. E empowers a limited number of attacks. Use E after a fight starts instead of casting it in advance. During a chase, use E's slow to keep the enemy from getting away. When escaping, cast E on an ally to slow pursuers.
notes.nami-skill-passive: When Nami's abilities touch an ally, P increases that ally's movement speed. Trigger P with W and E to help allies engage and disengage. Allies hit by R receive double the movement speed bonus from P. Even if R will not hit an enemy, send it through allies to help them engage.
notes.nami-phase: Nami is weak at level 1 because she has only one way to intervene. Once Nami learns W, she gains an advantage through lane sustain. Learning R at level 6 gives Nami her first engage tool. As Nami gains ability power, her healing and buffs grow stronger. Nami can still be caught easily late in the game, so do not stand in front.
notes.nami-laning: In lane, sustain through W's healing. Look for Q when the enemy steps forward. Do not push the lane while Q is unavailable. Keep your distance while Q is unavailable. Prioritize staying alive and holding the lane.
notes.nami-roaming: When roaming, chain Q and R with your mid laner's crowd control. Nami has no mobility ability, so roaming and returning takes a long time. Roam only after pushing the wave in to keep the enemy bot lane occupied. Do not go into the river without a purpose.
notes.nami-vision: Do not venture blindly into areas without vision. Use a Control Ward to clear enemy vision. Check the enemy's position before entering a bush.
notes.nami-teamfight: In teamfights, stand behind your ADC. In teamfights, keep E on your ADC. In teamfights, use W to heal allies. For safer teamfights, prioritize using R to stop enemy engages over starting fights. Use R to cut off a fleeing enemy's escape route.
notes.nami-situational-cleanse: If the enemy has a lot of crowd control that locks down allies, choose Mikael's Blessing to cleanse it. Nami cannot cleanse crowd control from allies on her own.
notes.vs-nami-q: Q falls slowly. Q has a long cooldown. When you see Q's warning indicator, walk sideways to dodge it. Target Nami and the enemy ADC right after she misses Q.
notes.vs-nami-r: R has very long range. R travels slowly. When you see R, move sideways to dodge it. Save your mobility ability to dodge the Q that follows R. If R hits you, you are at high risk of being hit by the follow-up combo.
notes.vs-nami-e: Do not fight an enemy affected by E head-on. Back off until E's short duration ends, then fight again. If an attack empowered by E slows you, you may be caught while escaping.
notes.vs-nami-squishy: Nami has no mobility ability. Secure vision to find an angle to target Nami. In lane, prioritize targeting Nami over the enemy ADC.
notes.vs-nami-heal: Nami relies on W's healing for lane sustain, making her vulnerable to healing reduction. Apply healing reduction with Executioner's Calling or Morellonomicon to weaken her W sustain.
notes.nasus-combo-basic: Use W → E → Q in fights. Lowering armor with E before landing Q deals more damage than using Q first.
notes.nasus-skill-q-stack: Nasus's damage depends heavily on Q stacks. Prioritize last-hitting with Q throughout the laning phase. Killing champions, large minions, or large jungle monsters with Q grants more stacks. Do not miss opportunities to last-hit champions, large minions, or large jungle monsters with Q.
notes.nasus-skill-q-tower: Dealing damage with Q triggers on-hit effects. Q's bonus damage also applies to turrets. Once you have built up Q stacks, consider split-pushing to pressure turrets with your fast demolition.
notes.nasus-skill-w: W's slow grows stronger over time. W also reduces the target's attack speed. Prioritize enemy carries who rely on basic attacks when choosing a target for W. W is a targeted ability with a cooldown that is not short. Nasus has no dash, so he relies on W to stop enemies from kiting him.
notes.nasus-skill-e-mana: E lowers enemy armor, increasing Q's damage. E has a high mana cost. Using E during the laning phase pushes the wave. Limit E poke to save mana for W → E → Q when following up on ganks or fighting.
notes.nasus-skill-e-wave: Using E near your turret pushes the wave and causes you to miss Q last hits. While holding out under your turret, avoid using E and focus on Q last hits.
notes.nasus-skill-r: R increases maximum health, armor, and magic resistance. R deals continuous damage to nearby enemies based on their maximum health. R greatly reduces Q's cooldown. Activate R at the start of a teamfight to use its continuous damage and repeated Q attacks. In skirmishes, wait until the enemy commits, then activate R at the last moment to use the health increase.
notes.nasus-skill-r-objective: Combining R's health and defense increases with P's life steal lets you tank an objective's attacks alone. A team with Nasus can attempt Baron relatively early. Suggest attempting an objective when R comes off cooldown.
notes.nasus-phase: Nasus is weakest at levels 2–3. At levels 2–3, Nasus loses head-on fights against most bruisers. At levels 2–3, Nasus relies on W to fight back. Nasus becomes much stronger from the mid to late game, once he has built up Q stacks and has R available. Late in the game, Nasus is difficult to face head-on while R is active.
notes.nasus-laning-freeze: Stack safely when the enemy pushes the wave and lets you last-hit with Q under your turret. Avoid forcing a push and take Q last hits from incoming waves. Conserve mana while collecting incoming waves.
notes.nasus-laning-zoned: If enemy pressure makes Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap. Without building Q stacks, Nasus struggles to grow stronger as the game progresses.
notes.nasus-teamfight: Nasus has no dash or guaranteed crowd control, making him very vulnerable to kiting. Avoid leading the charge alone; enter after your teammates start the fight. Use W on the enemy carry to hinder their movement. Use Q on enemies standing in E's area. If an enemy ignores Nasus and goes for your backline, use W on that enemy.
notes.nasus-situational-defense: Without enough defensive stats, Nasus falls quickly to focused attacks even while R is active. Even with a damage-focused build, buy at least one survival item, such as Dead Man's Plate, to withstand focused attacks.
notes.nasus-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner's Calling to reduce it. With Executioner's Calling, even a single Q can apply healing reduction.
notes.vs-nasus-r: Nasus gains health and defensive stats while R is active. Nasus is stronger than most champions while R is active. Unless you have a clear advantage in numbers or damage, delay the fight until Nasus's R ends.
notes.vs-nasus-w: With more ranks, W cripples champions who rely on basic attacks by reducing their movement speed and attack speed. Avoid moving alone within Nasus's range so you do not get caught by W on your own.
notes.vs-nasus-kite: Nasus is vulnerable to kiting. Even at full health, keep your distance and attack instead of fighting Nasus head-on. Nasus relies on W to close in on enemies who keep their distance.
notes.vs-nasus-early-allin: Attempt an all-in at levels 2–3, when Nasus is weaker than most bruisers. Go beyond poking and bring Nasus down to half health with your first all-in. Once your cooldowns are back after the first all-in, go all-in again and aim for the kill. Take Ignite for the level 2–3 all-in strategy. Avoid picking champions with weak early games that struggle to exploit Nasus's early weakness.
notes.vs-nasus-wave: Do not push the wave toward Nasus. Nasus can easily build stacks by last-hitting with Q under his own turret. Let the wave push toward your side and ask for a jungle gank. Nasus relies on Flash to escape. Even one successful gank against Nasus can turn the entire laning phase around.
notes.nautilus-combo-engage: For a standard engage, land Q, then use a passive auto attack → E → W. As the Q stun ends, follow up with a passive auto attack to keep the target under crowd control. To chain crowd control after Q, do not skip the passive auto attack.
notes.nautilus-combo-flash-q: To catch an enemy outside Q range, Flash and use Q before they can react. If Q lands after Flash, follow up with a passive auto attack → E. Taking too long to line up Q without Flash makes it easier for the enemy to escape.
notes.nautilus-combo-gank: During a gank or when entering a narrow passage, aim Q at terrain beside the enemy to close the gap more reliably. Use E immediately after closing the gap with Q on terrain. When Q hits terrain, you recover a substantial portion of its cooldown and mana cost.
notes.nautilus-combo-ult-chain: Auto attack an enemy knocked up by R to follow up with your passive root. Save Q until the enemy tries to escape. To lock down one enemy for as long as possible, use R → passive auto attack → Q.
notes.nautilus-skill-q: Q only affects the first target it hits. Minions block Q. In lane, use Q when a gap opens between minions. In lane, line up Q from a brush or the side.
notes.nautilus-skill-q-terrain: If Q hits terrain, you get a cooldown and mana refund. When returning to lane, roaming, or joining an objective fight, hit terrain with Q to travel.
notes.nautilus-skill-w: W grants a shield. While W lasts, your auto attacks deal area damage around the target. While W is active, weave in auto attacks to make use of its area damage. Use W just before the enemy's burst damage hits.
notes.nautilus-skill-e: E explodes in multiple waves. E's first explosion has a delay. Use E while fleeing to slow the enemy's pursuit. Use E ahead of time along the enemy's approach to deter their engage.
notes.nautilus-skill-r: R follows its targeted enemy. R also knocks up other enemies along its path. When targeting a backline carry, aim R's path to knock up enemies in front and open a path for your team to engage.
notes.nautilus-phase: Nautilus gains kill pressure at level 2, when both Q and E are available. Nautilus is strongest at level 6, when R gives him a reliable engage. Nautilus deals very little damage of his own in the late game. In the late game, focus on engaging and shutting down the enemy carry.
notes.nautilus-laning-mana: Using Q without hitting anything costs a lot of mana.
notes.nautilus-laning-level2: Reaching level 2 first opens your strongest trading window, letting you lock down the enemy for a long time. After reaching level 2 first, trade with Q → passive auto attack → E. Push the first wave quickly to reach level 2 first. Before starting a trade, check whether your ADC can follow up.
notes.nautilus-teamfight: Prioritize the enemy's main damage dealer as your teamfight engage target. If there is no opening to engage, do not force Q. If there is no opening to engage, hold the front line with W and E and draw out the enemy's engage. After the enemy uses their engage ability, use R as the signal for your team to go in.
notes.vs-nautilus-e: If Nautilus uses E right next to you, stay in place until its waves end. If you run away before E's waves end, you will enter later explosions and take extra damage and a slow.
notes.vs-nautilus-w: With W active, Nautilus deals area damage around his auto attack target. If you have time, stay close to Nautilus and break his W shield before continuing the fight.
notes.vs-nautilus-q: Nautilus relies on Q for direct engages and most kill opportunities. Keep minions between you and Nautilus to block Q. If Nautilus misses Q, trade safely while it is on its long cooldown.
notes.vs-nautilus-passive: Nautilus's first auto attack roots its target. After a trade, immediately leave Nautilus's auto attack range so you do not get rooted and hit by follow-up abilities.
notes.vs-nautilus-r: R follows its targeted enemy, so it cannot be dodged. R also knocks up allies standing along its path. While Nautilus has R available, avoid standing in line with allies along his engage path.
notes.vs-nautilus-mobility: Apart from using Q on terrain, Nautilus has no way to move quickly. Save your own engage ability to create distance after Nautilus uses Q.
notes.neeko-combo-basic: Root with E, then place Q and follow up with an auto attack. E's root can hold the target in Q's area until it bursts again. Don't throw Q before E; the target can walk out of it.
notes.neeko-combo-e-minion: If E hits something first, it grows larger and faster, and its root lasts longer. In lane, throw E at an angle that lets it pass through minions and hit your opponent. Don't walk around the minion wave to cast E.
notes.neeko-combo-r: Approach in disguise, start preparing R, then use E or allied crowd control to hold the target for R's landing. While Neeko is disguised, opponents cannot see R's preparation animation. The disguise wears off shortly after you cast R, revealing where you started preparing it.
notes.neeko-skill-passive: P lets Neeko disguise herself as an allied champion or a nearby unit. Immobilizing crowd control breaks the disguise. Using a damaging ability breaks the disguise. Taking damage equal to the disguised unit's health breaks the disguise. Assume your first offensive ability will reveal you, and use the disguise to approach until then.
notes.neeko-skill-passive-credibility: The disguise changes only Neeko's appearance. Disguise yourself as an ally who is out of enemy vision. Walk a route the ally you're disguised as would plausibly take. Move with a group of allies while disguised.
notes.neeko-skill-q: Q bursts again in the same spot if it kills a unit or damages a champion or large monster. Place Q over both the minion wave and your opponent to clear the wave and harass them. If Q hits nothing, it ends after the first burst. In objective fights, hit the large monster with Q to trigger another burst.
notes.neeko-skill-w-passive: W's passive grants bonus damage and a brief movement speed boost on every third auto attack. Track W's empowered auto attack and use it on the enemy champion. Auto attack minions twice, then hit your opponent with the third, empowered auto attack.
notes.neeko-skill-w-active: Casting W makes Neeko briefly invisible and sends a clone running in the chosen direction. Use W's brief invisibility to interrupt enemy targeted abilities and throw off their aim. When escaping, send the clone in the opposite direction to mislead pursuers. W's clone copies Neeko's ability and recall animations.
notes.neeko-skill-r: R leaps only after its preparation animation ends, and its area stun applies on landing. If opponents scatter while R is preparing, you may miss them when you land. If the enemy frontline is sturdy and strong crowd control is still available, wait for an ally's engage or your E root to hold enemies before using R.
notes.neeko-laning: Neeko's laning depends heavily on landing E; without it, Q and R are also hard to land reliably. If you don't have an angle for E, don't force it. Harass with W's empowered auto attack and wait. Watch for an enemy engage while E is on cooldown.
notes.neeko-laning-roam: Support Neeko gets especially high value from roaming. After pushing the lane, disguise yourself as an ally while crossing the river to establish vision and find angles for E and R. Crossing the river disguised as an ally can delay the enemy's reaction even if they spot you.
notes.neeko-teamfight: In teamfights, start with E from the backline, then finish with R after your allies' engage holds the enemy in place. If you cast R first and dive in alone, you may be taken down during its preparation animation. Once caught in a teamfight, W's invisibility is Neeko's only way out.
notes.neeko-phase: At levels 1–5, Neeko struggles to withstand trades from melee champions who dive in. Once Neeko learns R at level 6, combining it with her disguise gives her the power to turn a fight around. Neeko's power peaks in the mid game as she builds ability power. In the late game, Neeko has few options left after using both E and R.
notes.neeko-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing can undo your burst damage, buy Morellonomicon between core items to apply Grievous Wounds during a single engage.
notes.vs-neeko-disguise: If you encounter an enemy champion somewhere unexpected, check whether they were already seen elsewhere. Check whether a suspicious enemy champion has a reason to be there. If Neeko disappears from vision and a lone enemy champion approaches, watch for a disguised engage.
notes.vs-neeko-clone: W's clone runs in only one direction and does not attack.
notes.vs-neeko-e: If E hits something first, it grows larger and faster, making it easier to hit someone standing behind it. Spread out from your allies so E cannot root several of you together.
notes.vs-neeko-r: R only goes off after Neeko enters herself and finishes its preparation animation. Use a sturdy frontline and reliable crowd control held in reserve to stop Neeko's engage. If you see R's preparation animation, move out of the area. A disguised Neeko's R preparation animation is hidden, so spread out as soon as a suspicious opponent gets close.
notes.vs-neeko-early: Before level 6, Neeko has no way to turn a fight around. If you play a melee champion who dives in, close the gap and force a trade right after Neeko uses E.
notes.nidalee-combo-gank: When ganking, land Javelin Toss from a distance, transform into cougar form, then use Pounce, Takedown, and Swipe in that order. Landing Javelin Toss in human form applies the Hunted mark and resets the transformation cooldown. If Javelin Toss misses, don't force an engage hoping for the empowered effect.
notes.nidalee-combo-cougar: In cougar form, close the gap with Pounce, then use Takedown and Swipe. In cougar form, Takedown is applied to your next basic attack. Use Takedown once you are in basic attack range.
notes.nidalee-skill-q: Javelin Toss deals more damage the farther it travels. Look for an angle to land Javelin Toss at maximum range. Landing Javelin Toss grants true sight of an enemy even if they are hiding in a bush.
notes.nidalee-skill-w-trap: Bushwhack in human form lasts a long time and reveals enemies who step on it. Place Bushwhack traps at river entrances and jungle junctions ahead of time to track the enemy jungler's path. An enemy who steps on Bushwhack gets the Hunted mark.
notes.nidalee-skill-e-heal: Primal Surge in human form heals more when more health is missing. Use Primal Surge after your health has dropped somewhat. Using Primal Surge on an ally increases their attack speed. Use Primal Surge on an allied damage dealer just before an objective fight.
notes.nidalee-skill-cougar-q: Takedown in cougar form deals more damage the lower the target's health is. Takedown is stronger against a target with the Hunted mark. Use Takedown to finish an enemy when their health is low.
notes.nidalee-skill-pounce: Pounce in cougar form can cross terrain to escape. Don't spend every Pounce on engaging; save one for escape. Pounce travels farther when used toward an enemy with the Hunted mark.
notes.nidalee-skill-r-form: Aspect Of The Cougar switches forms and has a short cooldown. Applying Hunted in human form immediately resets Aspect Of The Cougar's cooldown. Switch to cougar form when closing in on an enemy. Switch to human form when healing or creating distance. Switching back to human form makes your basic attacks ranged.
notes.nidalee-skill-passive-brush: Prowl increases movement speed when passing through bushes. Prowl increases movement speed when there is a Hunted target. Plan your jungle routes through bushes. Move in and out of bushes to position yourself during fights, too.
notes.nidalee-phase: Nidalee clears the jungle quickly early on thanks to cougar form. Pressure objectives with Javelin Toss poke even before level 6. Avoid fighting the enemy jungler head-on. Nidalee is strongest in the mid game as she builds ability power. Nidalee has less impact late in the game if she cannot land Javelin Toss.
notes.nidalee-jungle-path: Nidalee has no crowd control, so her gank success depends on help from allied laners. Gank lanes with allies who can lock down enemies first. If no ally can lock down the enemy, gain an advantage by farming the jungle or invading the enemy jungle.
notes.nidalee-teamfight: Don't engage head-on in teamfights. In teamfights, throw Javelin Toss from the side or behind in human form to apply the mark. Engage in cougar form only after the enemy's main damage dealer has lost enough health. After finishing an enemy in a teamfight, escape with Pounce. Nidalee is fragile and is easily caught if hit by crowd control.
notes.nidalee-situational-antiheal: If the enemy has healing, choose Morellonomicon to stop them from healing between fights. If the enemy heals between fights, you have fewer chances to finish them with Takedown.
notes.vs-nidalee-spear: Javelin Toss deals more damage when thrown from farther away. Dodge spears Nidalee throws from a distance. Keep minions or your allied frontline between you and Nidalee to block Javelin Toss.
notes.vs-nidalee-hunt: Only Javelin Toss and Bushwhack apply the Hunted mark. Dodge Javelin Toss and Bushwhack to prevent her cougar abilities from being empowered. If you dodge both Javelin Toss and Bushwhack, you won't be marked for true sight by Hunted.
notes.vs-nidalee-pounce: If Nidalee uses Pounce to engage after marking you, Takedown follows. Use crowd control or defensive abilities the moment Nidalee closes in with Pounce. Right after a spear hits you, have a defensive ability ready for Nidalee's engage.
notes.vs-nidalee-nocc: Nidalee has no crowd control. When Nidalee is caught, Pounce is her only escape tool. Catch Nidalee by applying an immobilizing effect. Remember where Nidalee came out to throw a spear and look for an angle to attack her.
notes.vs-nidalee-trap: Move through jungle entrances and the river assuming Nidalee has placed Bushwhack traps there. Before entering, clear Bushwhack traps with a Control Ward or an area-of-effect ability.
notes.nilah-combo-eq: Cast Q while dashing through a target with E to hit enemies along the path too. Q used during E has a different hit check from Q used after E passes through. When several enemies overlap, use Q during E.
notes.nilah-combo-trade: For a short trade, land Q to activate its buff, then basic attack. Q's buff activates only when Q hits a target, such as a minion or champion. Before closing in on an opponent, hit a minion with Q to activate the buff.
notes.nilah-combo-allin: When going all in, enter with E, use Q during the dash, basic attack, then finish with W and R. Activate W after the opponent's basic attacks and sustained damage start hitting.
notes.nilah-skill-passive: When Nilah last-hits a minion, the nearest ally regains half the experience lost from sharing it. During lane, keep your support close to Nilah. If the support leaves lane, Nilah loses her experience advantage.
notes.nilah-skill-passive-heal: Nilah amplifies healing and shields she receives from allies. The ally who provided the healing or shield also receives the amplified effect. Nilah benefits greatly from pairing with a support who provides shields or healing. During fights, stay within range of your support's healing and shields.
notes.nilah-skill-q: Q's passive grants armor penetration and basic attack lifesteal based on critical strike chance. As Nilah's critical strike chance rises, both her damage and sustain improve. Excess healing becomes a shield. Even at full health, attack minions to turn excess healing into a shield.
notes.nilah-skill-w: While W is active, Nilah dodges all basic attacks. Use W when the opposing marksman or a basic attack focused champion attacks. While W is active, Nilah can pass through units. Use W to escape when minions block your path. Allies Nilah touches while W is active also dodge basic attacks. When entering with W, take a path that touches your allied marksman or support.
notes.nilah-skill-e: E dashes through a targeted unit, so you can target minions too. Nilah uses E both to enter and escape, so spending all its uses to enter makes escaping difficult. Before entering, identify a unit you can target with E to get out.
notes.nilah-skill-r: Use R to pull together and finish opponents who are already grouped. R heals Nilah and nearby allies based on the damage it deals to champions. The more champions R hits, the more it heals allies. Use R to group enemies where your allies' area abilities will hit.
notes.nilah-laning: As a melee marksman, Nilah struggles to last-hit against ranged opponents. During lane, avoid forcing an approach and use Q to last-hit from range. Enter with E when an opponent steps forward to attack a minion. During lane, focus on keeping up in levels without falling far behind.
notes.nilah-laning-trade: Because her support's shields and healing are amplified, Nilah can fight back in 2v2s. Nilah must fight at melee range, leaving her vulnerable to immobilizing crowd control. Enter after the opponent uses their key skillshot crowd control.
notes.nilah-phase: Nilah is very weak at levels 1–2 because of her range and health disadvantages. Nilah grows stronger from mid game as critical strike items increase Q's penetration and lifesteal. In late game teamfights, Nilah can save allies with W and R.
notes.nilah-teamfight: In teamfights, avoid entering first; go in second. After the opponent engages on an ally, move in with W. When enemies group up, pull them together with R to heal your allies. If Nilah takes the front line first, she is likely to die from focused crowd control.
notes.nilah-situational-antiheal: If the opponent sustains through healing, buy Executioner's Calling while building your core items. Nilah needs to stay close and attack for a long time, so an opponent's healing makes fights hard to finish.
notes.vs-nilah-range: As a melee marksman, Nilah struggles to last-hit when harassed from outside her range. During lane, deny Nilah chances to close in and harass her from outside her range.
notes.vs-nilah-w: When Nilah activates W, all basic attacks miss her. When Nilah activates W, respond with ability damage instead of basic attacks. Resume basic attacks after Nilah's W ends. Allies who touch Nilah while her W is active also gain its basic attack dodge effect.
notes.vs-nilah-r: If Nilah's R catches several champions, her team gains both damage and healing. Spread out from your allies when Nilah has R available. If R has already pulled you in, attack Nilah immediately to stop her from maintaining the cast.
notes.vs-nilah-heal: Nilah amplifies healing and shields provided by allies and shares those effects with them. If Nilah's support provides healing, buy a Grievous Wounds item early. Choose Executioner's Calling or Morellonomicon based on your own scaling.
notes.vs-nilah-q: Right after Q hits, Nilah briefly gains attack range and attacks in a cone. While Nilah's Q buff is active, back away farther than usual.
notes.vs-nilah-cc: Nilah has low health and is highly vulnerable to immobilizing crowd control. Nilah is vulnerable when both E and W are down. Use targeted crowd control after Nilah enters and uses W.
notes.noct-combo-gank: When ganking, land Q, follow the trail to close in, apply E, and trigger your passive with a basic attack. Enemies hit by Q also leave a trail. After landing Q, chase along the trail the enemy leaves.
notes.noct-combo-ult: Use R to cut off vision, recast it to dash in, activate W just before landing, then attack with E and basic attacks. W remains active while Nocturne flies in with R.
