notes.noct-combo-e-hold: E only triggers fear if the tether to the target holds. Apply E after closing in on the target. If you close in along the Q trail before applying E, the target has a harder time leaving tether range. If you apply E from far away, the enemy can walk back to break the tether.
notes.noct-skill-passive: Periodically, your passive adds area damage and healing to your next basic attack. Each basic attack reduces your passive's cooldown. Hitting a champion or jungle monster reduces your passive's cooldown by more. Keep using basic attacks while clearing camps to benefit from your passive's healing.
notes.noct-skill-q: Q damages enemies and leaves a trail. On the Q trail, Nocturne can move through units and gains movement speed and attack damage. Q leaves a trail even if it misses enemies. Outside combat, use the Q trail to close the gap or escape. When ganking, lay the Q trail along your approach in advance.
notes.noct-skill-w: W's shield blocks one enemy ability for a short time. Blocking an ability with W doubles your attack speed. Activate W to block the enemy's key immobilizing ability.
notes.noct-skill-w-monster: W can also block monster abilities. Block a dragon attack with W to gain attack speed and hit the objective faster. Save W if the enemy jungler can reach the objective.
notes.noct-skill-e: E triggers fear only if the tether to the target holds for a set time. Nocturne gains a large movement speed boost when moving toward a feared enemy. Chase the target as soon as fear triggers. Draw out the enemy's mobility ability or force them toward a wall before applying E.
notes.noct-skill-r: R reduces every enemy's vision radius. R prevents enemies from sharing vision with each other. You can use R without dashing to conceal an ally's engage or the start of an objective.
notes.noct-skill-r-target: To dash with R, you must be able to see a target in range. If enemies scatter in R's darkness, pick an isolated target and dash in. Do not use R to dive into the middle of an enemy group if one shield will not be enough to survive.
notes.noct-phase: Nocturne's jungle clear speed at levels 1–2 is average. Using the Q trail and W's attack speed helps clear camps faster. Level 6, when Nocturne learns R, is his first power spike. Nocturne is strongest in the mid game after completing his first core item. In the late game, Nocturne is easily killed if he engages poorly.
notes.noct-laning: Before level 6, prioritize ganking lanes where an ally can hold the enemy in place. During a gank, apply E after closing in on the enemy. If there is no gank opportunity, clear camps to reach level 6 sooner.
notes.noct-laning-r-timing: After level 6, look at the lane state and use R proactively. If the enemy laner has pushed the wave and stepped forward, and your ally can follow up, engage with R. In R's darkness, enemies cannot see their allies, increasing the chance of a successful dive.
notes.noct-teamfight: In teamfights, target one backline enemy in the darkness instead of the frontline. After activating R, wait for the enemies to scatter before dashing in. Activate W as you engage to block the enemy support's crowd control. Engage after your allies start the fight.
notes.vs-noct-r-group: Nocturne uses R to target isolated enemies. While R cuts off shared vision, do not scatter and flee separately.
notes.vs-noct-e: Nocturne's E does not trigger fear if the tether breaks. Save a mobility ability or Flash for when Nocturne applies E.
notes.vs-noct-w: Nocturne's W blocks one ability. If Nocturne blocks an ability with W, his attack speed doubles.
notes.vs-noct-q: Targets hit by Nocturne's Q also leave a trail. Nocturne quickly chases along the trail left by a target hit by Q. If Nocturne's Q hits you, angle toward your allies or a turret until the trail disappears.
notes.vs-noct-vision: Nocturne is strong in areas without vision. Maintain vision around the river and jungle entrances.
notes.nunu-combo-gank: Roll W long enough from outside vision to knock the enemy up, then throw E and finish with R. Start rolling W far from the enemy and outside vision so it can gain size and speed. W started near an enemy has little size or speed and is easy to dodge.
notes.nunu-combo-wer: While E's root is delayed, use R's slow to keep the enemy from walking out of range. Against enemies without a dash, combining E and R makes the root nearly guaranteed.
notes.nunu-combo-r-setup: If you cast R on its own, the enemy can walk out and take almost no explosion damage. Cast R alongside W's knockup, E's root, or an ally's immobilizing crowd control. If the enemy tries to escape with a cleanse, recast R immediately to detonate it.
notes.nunu-skill-w-timing: W's cooldown starts when you begin rolling the snowball. Once the snowball is fully grown, collide with the enemy right away if you're confident you'll hit. In open areas, roll W in a circle to keep enemies from entering.
notes.nunu-skill-w-cleanse: Casting W immediately removes slows on Nunu. When escaping near a wall, use W to clear the slow, then hit the wall immediately to end the snowball. While rolling W, you turn sideways more slowly than you move forward.
notes.nunu-skill-w-momentum: The snowball's size and speed increase with movement speed bonuses on Nunu. Roll W while benefiting from terrain effects or ally buffs that increase movement speed. Take a wide route around the river to give the snowball room to roll and find a hidden approach angle.
notes.nunu-skill-q-heal: Q heals far more when used on a minion or monster than on a champion. If you need healing, click a minion precisely and use Q instead of targeting a champion. Q heals more when your health falls below half. At low health, you can use Q on a jungle monster to heal instead of running away.
notes.nunu-skill-e: An enemy hit by all three E snowballs is slowed, then rooted after a delay. If you have no way to hold the enemy in place after throwing E, the root will rarely trigger. If the enemy's escape path is clear, land all three E hits and chase. E can reveal a stealthed enemy.
notes.nunu-skill-passive: The passive increases attack speed and movement speed for Nunu & Willump and one nearby ally. The passive's duration starts when you damage a large monster. When attacking an objective, stand beside your allied marksman to give them the passive buff. Passive-empowered basic attacks also damage enemies around the target. At jungle camps, position so the empowered basic attack hits multiple monsters.
notes.nunu-skill-r-peel: R's slow lasts for twice its channel time. When you need to stop an enemy engage, cast R at your allied carry's feet. Nunu gains a shield while channeling R.
notes.nunu-laning-jungle: Try your first gank after learning W at level 3. After a lane gank, grow your snowball while rolling around the Rift Scuttler, then gank again. Q deals true damage to monsters, helping clear jungle camps quickly. Statistically, both CS and damage per minute rank near the bottom. Focus on securing objectives and ganking over competing in farm.
notes.nunu-phase: Ganks become stronger from level 3, when you learn W. Objective fights are strongest after you learn R at level 6. Statistically, early damage is among the lowest overall, making solo kills difficult. As health and ability power build up in the mid and late game, Q's sustain and R's burst both improve. Keep engaging fights and protecting allies in the late game.
notes.nunu-teamfight: Start the teamfight when the snowball reaches the enemy backline. Engage with W only when allies are close enough to follow. If you engage alone, your low damage makes you easy to take down. If you have no engage angle, cast R in front of your allied carry to stop the enemy engage.
notes.nunu-situational-slowresist: Rolling W also slows Nunu himself. Slow resistance helps the snowball reach maximum speed sooner. Slow resistance makes it easier to land E's root on a fleeing enemy. If the enemy has many slows, take Mercury's Treads and Unflinching together.
notes.vs-nunu-w-dodge: The W snowball moves forward much faster than it turns sideways. When the snowball comes toward you, walk toward it and escape through the spot Nunu just left. The snowball has very long range, making it hard to outrun.
notes.vs-nunu-gank: Nunu & Willump can gank with the snowball from level 3. Early on, secure river vision before positioning in lane. Nunu can roll around the Rift Scuttler and come back immediately after a gank.
notes.vs-nunu-r: Interrupt R's channel with immobilizing crowd control to prevent its explosion damage. If you cannot interrupt R, accept the slow and walk out of range. R's slow lasts for twice its channel time. If a Nunu who has built only health is channeling R, leave the area instead of forcing an attack.
notes.vs-nunu-heal: Nunu can keep healing by using Q on minions and monsters. Nunu's Q heals more when his health is below half. Get Executioner's Calling or Morellonomicon early to reduce Nunu's Q healing.
notes.vs-nunu-magic: Virtually all of Nunu & Willump's damage is magic damage. Nunu & Willump's main threat comes from the snowball's crowd control more than its damage. Against Nunu, options that increase both magic resistance and tenacity are effective.
notes.vs-nunu-e: If an E snowball hits and slows you, the root triggers after a delay. If E hits you, leave the area immediately. If you have a mobility ability, use it after E hits you and before the root triggers.
notes.olaf-combo-basic: For a basic trade, throw Q in the direction your opponent is moving, pick up the axe as you close in, then use a basic attack followed by E. Picking up the axe reduces Q's cooldown. If you fail to pick up the axe, the long gap before your next Q can leave you open to a counterattack. Throw Q where the path to retrieve the axe also lets you close in.
notes.olaf-combo-allin: When going all in, land Q, close in for a basic attack, activate W, then finish with E. E's true damage goes through even if the opponent builds armor or magic resistance. Save E for the final hit of an all in.
notes.olaf-combo-ult: Use R just before or just after the opponent's crowd control hits you. Each basic attack or E hit on a champion extends R's duration. After activating R, stay on the opponent and keep attacking.
notes.olaf-skill-q-axe: The Q axe stays on the ground, and picking it up greatly reduces its cooldown. The route to retrieve the axe determines Olaf's movement path. When chasing, throw Q ahead of the opponent and pick it up as you follow. When retreating, throw Q along your escape route behind you and pick it up as you leave. Before throwing an axe over a wall, check whether the terrain lets you retrieve it.
notes.olaf-skill-q-armor: Champions hit by Q briefly lose armor. In a teamfight, time Q with the engage of allies who mainly deal physical damage. The armor reduction from a Q timed with your allies' physical damage engage increases the team's total damage.
notes.olaf-skill-w: W provides both attack speed and a shield. W's shield grows stronger the more health you have lost. Activating W early at full health makes its shield less effective. After taking the opponent's combo, activate W and use its attack speed and shield to counterattack.
notes.olaf-skill-e: E costs Olaf health to deal true damage. If E kills the target, Olaf gets back the health it cost. Each basic attack reduces E's cooldown. Keep using E while you stay close to the opponent. If you're low on health and a kill isn't certain, hold E so its health cost doesn't kill you first.
notes.olaf-skill-r: R prevents movement impairing effects but does not prevent damage. If the opponent has already used their crowd control, there's no reason to activate R. If you activate R before the opponent uses their crowd control, they can hold the ability and wait out R's duration. Use R a beat after the opponent's crowd control comes out.
notes.olaf-phase-early: Olaf is strong in level 1 trades against melee opponents. Olaf is strongest between levels 3 and 6, when he can use Q and E together. Late in the game, Olaf struggles against long range compositions that keep him from closing in.
notes.olaf-phase-lowhp: Berserker Rage gives Olaf more attack speed and lifesteal the more health he has lost. Even below half health, Olaf can fight hard if he stays close to a target he can lifesteal from.
notes.olaf-laning: Against melee opponents, close in early to win trades. Drop Q between you and the opponent, rather than beyond the wave, so you can pick it up as you close in. Olaf has limited mana, so failing to retrieve a Q costs him.
notes.olaf-laning-vs-ranged: Against ranged opponents, avoid forcing your way in; use Q to last hit and scale. Activate R and engage when a ranged opponent has used their poke ability or your jungler can follow up. Poking with Q from a position where you cannot retrieve the axe costs you.
notes.olaf-teamfight: In teamfights, use R to ignore crowd control and run straight at the backline damage dealers. In a narrow approach, throw Q behind the opponent first to slow them, then engage and retrieve the axe.
notes.olaf-situational-antiheal: If the opponent's healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Olaf stays close and attacks for a long time, so he can keep Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.vs-olaf-lowhp: Olaf gains attack speed and lifesteal as his health gets lower. Closing in on a half health Olaf can get you killed instead. Save crowd control that can reliably stop Olaf for the finishing stage.
notes.vs-olaf-axe: During lane, move to prevent Olaf from picking up his Q axe. Move away from where the axe lands to hinder Olaf's poke and approach.
notes.vs-olaf-ult: Movement impairing effects like stuns and roots do not work on Olaf while his R is active. When Olaf activates R, create distance behind a wall or your allies and wait out its duration. Apply crowd control right after Olaf's R ends. Getting hit by Olaf's basic attacks or E during R extends its duration.
notes.vs-olaf-e: Armor and magic resistance cannot reduce Olaf's E true damage. When low on health, counter Olaf's E with shields, healing, or distance.
notes.vs-olaf-scaling: Olaf is strongest early and becomes relatively weaker as the game goes on. Avoid giving Olaf early kills and stall until the matchup turns in your favor. If you have a range advantage, fight Olaf without getting close.
notes.orianna-skill-ball-position: All of Orianna's abilities work around the ball's position. Q sends the ball to a target location, where it stays. W and R activate at the ball's location. E attaches the ball to an ally. Decide where to place the ball before choosing which ability to use.
notes.orianna-skill-ball-return: The ball returns automatically if it gets too far from Orianna. While the ball is away from Orianna, she loses the armor and magic resistance from E's passive. Orianna is most vulnerable right after casting Q, when she loses E's passive. Move through dangerous areas with the ball returned to Orianna.
notes.orianna-combo-poke: For basic poke, use Q then W. Press W right after Q to make W activate when the ball arrives. If the ball is near Orianna, pressing W before Q makes W activate out of the enemy's reach.
notes.orianna-combo-e-delivery: E is the only way to move the ball beyond Q's range. Use E on an engaging ally to make the ball move with them. Before a teamfight, first consider the path E will take to send the ball to an engaging ally.
notes.orianna-combo-ult: Before starting an R combo, place the ball beyond or beside the enemy group. After placing the ball, use R, then Q, then W. R pulls enemies toward the ball. Place the ball where R can pull enemies toward your team. Poor ball placement can make R pull enemies away from your team.
notes.orianna-combo-flash-ult: If you cannot get the ball where you want it, use Flash to move Orianna there, then cast R. Save Flash if the ball is near the enemy or on an ally and gives you the same R angle.
notes.orianna-skill-w: W deals area damage around the ball. W slows enemies around the ball. W increases the movement speed of allies at that location. When allies engage or you retreat together, keep the ball near them and use W to help them move.
notes.orianna-skill-e: E shields its target. E sends the ball to an ally. An ally carrying the ball gains armor and magic resistance from E's passive. Before a teamfight, use E to attach the ball to the ally who will engage. If you expect to be targeted, use E on yourself to retrieve the ball and gain a shield.
notes.orianna-skill-passive: P adds magic damage to basic attacks. P's bonus damage increases with consecutive attacks on the same target. Early in lane, trade back if the opposing mage starts a basic attack trade.
notes.orianna-phase: Orianna can be taken down in a single catch early on. Orianna gets stronger once Q's cooldown becomes shorter. Orianna gets stronger at level 6, when she gains R. Orianna peaks in the mid to late game, when she has enough items to turn a teamfight with one R.
notes.orianna-laning: In lane, use Q for both last hits and poke. Manage your mana in lane. Keep the ball near the enemy while staying farther back yourself. Send Q to a spot where the enemy and the backline minions overlap to clear the wave and poke at the same time.
notes.orianna-laning-wave: Orianna is vulnerable to jungle ganks when she pushes the wave all the way in. Without vision, keep the wave in the middle instead of pushing it all the way in. Without vision, poke with Q while keeping the wave in the middle.
notes.orianna-teamfight: In teamfights, use R to pull multiple enemies toward your team. Send the ball to an engaging ally with E, then use R. Cast R the moment the ally you gave the ball to with E reaches the enemy. Going up to the enemy team with the ball on Orianna and using R is a last resort.
notes.orianna-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who can engage, buy Zhonya's Hourglass sooner to survive after using R. Orianna is most likely to be focused right after using R.
notes.vs-orianna-ball: Judge Orianna's threat by the ball's position. If the ball is not nearby, R cannot pull you from your current position. When you stand near the ball, R can pull you at any time. Position yourself based on the ball's location.
notes.vs-orianna-no-ball: When the ball is away from Orianna, she loses the armor and magic resistance from E's passive. Try to trade damage right after Orianna casts Q.
notes.vs-orianna-peel: Orianna has several ways to defend herself: W's slow, E's shield, and R's pull. Trying to make Orianna use her defensive tools one by one delays the fight.
notes.vs-orianna-auto: Orianna's P adds magic damage to basic attacks. Orianna's P bonus damage increases with consecutive attacks on the same target. If you play an ability power champion, avoid basic attack trades early. If you play an ability power champion, trade damage only with abilities early on.
notes.ornn-combo-pillar: Place a pillar with Q, then use E to hit it and knock up nearby enemies. A magma pillar rises at the end of Q's path. Q's pillar lets you knock up enemies with E even in open terrain. Before casting Q, choose where to place the pillar you'll hit with E.
notes.ornn-combo-brittle: Land W's final flame, then auto attack for bonus damage and a knockback. Only enemies hit by W's final flame become Brittle. Move forward until W's final flame can reach the target.
notes.ornn-combo-order: Brittle extends the duration of immobilizing crowd control. If you're already close to the target, apply Brittle with W, then knock them up with E. If you're already close to the target, apply Brittle with W, then knock them up with R. If the target has a mobility ability, lock them down with E first, then land W. If the target has a mobility ability, lock them down with R first, then land W.
notes.ornn-combo-ult: The first spirit summoned by R slows enemies it passes through and makes them Brittle. Recast R to headbutt the spirit, changing its direction and knocking up enemies. Summon the spirit behind the target, let it pass through the enemy team, then headbutt it back toward your allies from the other side.
notes.ornn-skill-forge: Living Forge lets you spend gold to craft items anywhere. Stay in lane and craft items while continuing to farm CS and pressure the turret. Crafting takes time, so don't try it when an enemy is close. Don't try to craft items when the jungler's location is unclear.
notes.ornn-skill-masterwork: Masterwork upgrades strengthen allies' completed items without costing gold. Prioritize Masterwork upgrades for your main damage dealer with plenty of items. Prioritize allies whose item upgrade can directly change the outcome of a teamfight. As Ornn levels up, the number of upgrades he can grant increases. If there's no reason to save a Masterwork upgrade, use it as soon as it becomes available.
notes.ornn-skill-q: If Q hits an enemy champion, the fissure stops there and the pillar rises near them. If Q misses enemy champions, the pillar rises at maximum range. When using Q to farm and poke, hit your opponent with it. To position the pillar for E's shockwave, cast Q past your opponent. Place Q's pillar where your opponent would approach to farm CS or along the jungler's entry path to block the way.
notes.ornn-skill-w: Ornn is Unstoppable while moving forward with W. Use W to push through opponents who stop your engage with slows or knockbacks. W's direction is fixed and its movement speed is low, so its final flame is hard to land on opponents who escape with mobility abilities. Use W right after your opponent uses a mobility ability or when they're cornered against a wall.
notes.ornn-skill-e: E must hit terrain to knock up enemies. If E doesn't hit terrain, it only deals damage as Ornn passes through. If an enemy created wall blocks your allies' escape route, break it with E. If your allies aren't nearby, save E to disengage.
notes.ornn-laning: Ornn's early damage is among the lowest of top lane champions. In lane, farm safely with Q and keep up in CS and levels. If your opponent pushes the lane, farm under your turret. When your opponent recalls, use Living Forge to finish an item and reverse the item gap.
notes.ornn-phase: Ornn is weakest at levels 1 and 2, when his cooldowns are long and his damage is low. Once you get R at level 6, you can force a fight with your allies. Ornn's real power spike comes in mid game, after he builds two or three defensive items. Late game, the Masterwork upgrades you've given your allies increase your value to the team.
notes.ornn-teamfight: Start teamfights near terrain you can use to knock enemies up with E. In a narrow passage with walls, hit a wall with E to knock enemies up, then apply Brittle with W. In open terrain, let the R spirit sweep through opponents, then use E. Counter the enemy engage and protect your damage dealers.
notes.ornn-situational-thornmail: If the enemy's main damage is physical and they attack Ornn with auto attacks, buy Thornmail early. Ornn can use Thornmail's reflected damage and healing reduction while taking hits on the front line.
notes.ornn-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing makes them hard to finish with sustained damage, build healing reduction. Ornn deals magic damage, so buy Oblivion Orb on the way to Morellonomicon. Morellonomicon's health also helps Ornn serve as a frontliner. Executioner's Calling only provides attack damage, so it doesn't suit Ornn. Ornn's fights last a long time, making it easy for him to maintain healing reduction.
notes.vs-ornn-wall: To avoid Ornn's E shockwave, stand away from walls. If Ornn's E doesn't hit terrain, it only deals damage as he passes through. When Ornn prepares E, retreat toward the open area away from the wall.
notes.vs-ornn-pillar: Ornn's Q pillar acts like a wall, letting him knock enemies up with E even in open terrain. When a Q pillar appears, move away from it.
notes.vs-ornn-forge: Move close and attack when Ornn tries to craft an item in lane. Interrupting his crafting denies Ornn the laning advantage of finishing an item without recalling.
notes.vs-ornn-brittle: If Ornn's final W flame hits you, you become Brittle. While you're Brittle, immobilizing crowd control from Ornn's team lasts longer and deals bonus damage. Keep your distance and don't move forward until Brittle wears off. If Ornn auto attacks you while you're Brittle, the knockback can separate you from your allies.
notes.vs-ornn-ult: The first R spirit approaches slowly, so sidestep it. Ornn can headbutt the R spirit back, so don't stand on a straight line between him and the spirit. After the spirit passes, account for where Ornn could headbutt it back from the other side.
notes.vs-ornn-early: Ornn's early damage is very low. Pressure Ornn as much as possible in early laning to get ahead. Keep up the pressure to end the game before Ornn's items and his allies' Masterwork upgrades stack up.
notes.pantheon-combo-allin: The basic engage is W leap, empowered basic attack, E, then tap Q. W targets an enemy, so it cannot miss. If the passive is fully stacked right after W lands, the empowered basic attack hits multiple times.
notes.pantheon-combo-poke: Tap Q to thrust or hold it to throw the spear. Tapping Q greatly reduces its cooldown. Use tap Q to farm and stack the passive. When you cannot get close enough, poke with held Q.
notes.pantheon-skill-passive: After enough abilities and basic attacks, the passive empowers the next basic ability. Stack the passive with tap Q and basic attacks before a fight. Decide whether to empower W or E, then use that ability last. Hitting minions also stacks the passive.
notes.pantheon-skill-e: E only blocks damage coming from the direction Pantheon faces. E does not block turret damage. While using E, keep facing the enemy. E is almost useless when you are surrounded from multiple directions. Recast E to end it early and trigger the finishing strike sooner. If there is no more damage to block, end E immediately and move to your next action.
notes.pantheon-skill-w: W is Pantheon's only engage ability. W only closes the gap toward an enemy, so it cannot be used to escape. Before using W, check the enemy's mobility abilities and where your allies are positioned to help.
notes.pantheon-skill-q-finish: Thrown Q deals much more damage to low-health enemies. Throw Q to finish fleeing enemies when they are in range. Do not use Q early during a chase.
notes.pantheon-skill-r: R is an area ability that makes Pantheon leap and land at a chosen location. You need vision of the area to aim R's landing spot accurately. Land with R toward an allied ward. Enemies have time to move away while Pantheon is descending with R. Time R's landing to coincide with allied crowd control.
notes.pantheon-phase: Pantheon is strongest early. Tap Q has a short cooldown, letting you poke throughout the laning phase. Once you learn R at level 6, you can influence other lanes. As items build up in the late game, Pantheon's damage and durability both fall behind. Use the lead you built early to end the game.
notes.pantheon-laning: Chip away at the enemy's health with held Q, then use W to close in when they focus on last-hitting. Use brush to set up an angle to approach with W. Engage with W only right after the enemy uses their counterattack ability.
notes.pantheon-laning-support: As support, prioritize building up poke damage. Pantheon support has very high kill participation but also dies often. If your engage fails, the enemy marksman gets ahead. Use W only when your allies are close enough to follow up.
notes.pantheon-laning-top: In top lane, use tap Q to secure CS while stacking the passive. Go in with W right after the enemy uses their poke ability. Against ranged enemies, use E like a shield to close the gap. If you cannot close the gap, poke with held Q.
notes.pantheon-teamfight: In teamfights, push through the frontline and lock down the enemy carries. Use E to block damage from the front as you move in, then use W to reach a priority target. If you engage alone first, you have no way out after W. Engage with W after an ally lands crowd control. When engaging with R, land alongside your allies.
notes.pantheon-situational-antiheal: Buy Executioner's Calling early if the enemy has a way to heal. Pantheon deals his damage in a short burst, so enemy healing during the fight can take away your chance to secure a kill.
notes.vs-pantheon-e: Pantheon's E only blocks damage coming from the direction he faces. Pantheon's E does not block turret damage. When Pantheon uses E, move to his side or behind him to attack. If you must attack from the front, wait until E ends.
notes.vs-pantheon-w: Pantheon's W is a targeted stun, so it cannot be dodged. Stay out of Pantheon's W range. Stand farther back if Pantheon has an ally with crowd control beside him.
notes.vs-pantheon-q: Pantheon's held Q deals reduced damage to enemies behind the first target hit. Keep minions between you and Pantheon when he pokes with held Q.
notes.vs-pantheon-r: Pantheon needs vision of an area to aim R's landing spot accurately. Step into brush to make it harder for Pantheon to aim R's landing spot. When R's landing warning appears, walk out of the landing area.
notes.vs-pantheon-phase: Pantheon is very strong in early trades. Pantheon's impact falls sharply as the game goes late. Buy time without giving Pantheon kills early.
notes.poppy-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use E to stun the enemy against a wall, then follow with Q and a basic attack. During the E stun, Q's zone detonates beneath the enemy, dealing damage both times. If you can catch the enemy, use E before Q so they cannot dodge the zone's detonation.
notes.poppy-combo-e-angle: To stun with E, Poppy, the enemy, and the wall must line up. If there is no wall behind the enemy, move around them to create an angle that pushes them into a wall, then use E. In lane, look for a short angle that pushes the enemy into a side wall rather than straight ahead.
notes.poppy-combo-passive: The passive shield tends to land near a wall, making it easy to collect after pushing an enemy into the wall with E. After stunning with E, walk forward to collect the shield and continue trading while shielded. If you kill the target, the shield returns immediately, so you do not need to collect it when finishing them off.
notes.poppy-skill-passive: When the passive is ready, your next basic attack gains a large amount of range. Do not use the passive shield on a minion when you need it to harass a ranged opponent. A shield that lands near the enemy disappears if they step on it, so do not overextend to collect it.
notes.poppy-skill-q: Q deals immediate damage, then its lingering zone detonates once more. Q's maximum health damage deals more damage to enemies with more health. Q has a damage cap against minions and monsters, so its farming efficiency is average. When finishing an enemy off, you can use Q first to slow them.
notes.poppy-skill-w: Activate W when you see the enemy dash. Enemies stopped by W briefly cannot use movement abilities. W's passive Armor and Magic Resist increase as Poppy's health gets lower.
notes.poppy-skill-e: E is both an engage tool and a reliable stun, so do not use it just to move around. If E does not knock the target into terrain, it only pushes them and deals no stun or bonus damage. Even without a wall stun, you can angle E to push the enemy toward your team.
notes.poppy-skill-r: In a 1v1, cast R without charging it to interrupt the enemy's counterattack. Fully charging R lengthens the fissure and knocks all enemies hit far away. When charging R for a long time, start behind a wall or out of vision so the enemy has trouble seeing Poppy slow down. When using R to peel an enemy off your damage dealer, calculate the direction that will knock them toward the Nexus.
notes.poppy-laning-melee: When a melee opponent steps forward to last hit, use E from an angle with a wall behind them. A wall stun with E guarantees a follow-up Q and basic attack. If there is no wall stun angle, save E and harass with the passive shield. Save W while the enemy still has an engage ability available.
notes.poppy-laning-ranged: Against ranged opponents, avoid forcing an engage with E; harass with the passive shield and secure CS. Collecting the shield lets you stay in lane longer.
notes.poppy-jungle-gank: When ganking, approach from behind the lane and find an E angle that pushes the enemy into a side wall. If you charge in with E from the front, you may only push the enemy away. Draw the enemy toward places with nearby walls, such as a river entrance or beside a turret.
notes.poppy-teamfight: In teamfights, position yourself to protect your backline. Stop the enemy engager's dash with W, then stun them against a wall with E. When your damage dealer is targeted, save E to intercept the enemy instead of using it to engage.
notes.poppy-phase: At levels 1–2, Poppy has a long Q cooldown and no E, so she has little ability to force a fight. Once you learn E and Q's cooldown gets shorter, you can pressure melee opponents. At level 6, learning R lets you intervene in dives and teamfights. As items build up in the mid to late game, Poppy becomes especially valuable. In the late game, your raw damage falls behind, so focus on stopping enemy damage dealers.
notes.poppy-situational-antiheal: Against an enemy with strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling to reduce it. If you are building defensive items, upgrade Executioner's Calling into a completed item. Poppy stays close to enemies for a long time, making it easy to maintain Grievous Wounds.
notes.vs-poppy-w: When Poppy activates W, it stops movement abilities that dash into the area around her. If W stops a dash, you briefly cannot use movement abilities. If you need to engage with a dash, wait for W to end or walk up to her.
notes.vs-poppy-r: When Poppy starts spinning her hammer, she is charging R. The longer Poppy charges R, the longer the fissure becomes and the farther it knocks enemies away. When you see Poppy charging R, move sideways out of the line directly in front of her. Poppy also slows down while charging R, making it easier to create distance.
notes.vs-poppy-e: Poppy's E must knock you into terrain to stun you and deal bonus damage. Avoid standing with your back to a wall or narrow passage; stay in open space to avoid the E stun.
notes.vs-poppy-passive: Poppy's thrown shield lands on the ground and is destroyed if an enemy steps on it. Step on the fallen shield first to stop Poppy from gaining a shield.
notes.vs-poppy-q: Poppy's Q leaves a zone where it hits that detonates again shortly afterward. Q deals damage based on maximum health, so it hurts champions who build health more. If Q's first hit lands, immediately walk out of the lingering zone.
notes.vs-poppy-lowhp: As Poppy's health gets lower, W's passive Armor and Magic Resist increase. When finishing off a low-health Poppy, check that you have enough guaranteed damage.
notes.pyke-combo-qe: The basic kill combo is to pull with Q, then immediately use E, a basic attack, and R in that order. Using E right after Q lands makes the phantom's stun hit as the target can move again. If you leave a gap between Q and E, the target can escape with Flash.
notes.pyke-combo-w-approach: From outside vision, close in with W, tap Q when in range, then use E. Tapping Q casts faster and deals more damage than holding it. At close range, tap Q.
notes.pyke-combo-r-engage: When engaging with R, hold Q to pull the target immediately after arriving. When engaging with R, you can use E immediately after arriving. Targets with plenty of health are less likely to expect an R engage, giving them less time to react.
notes.pyke-skill-passive: P stores some damage taken from enemy champions and heals Pyke when he leaves enemy vision. After a fight, break vision with W or a brush, heal, then engage again. If P's healing has not started, the enemy can still see you.
notes.pyke-skill-passive-ad: Pyke converts all bonus maximum health into attack damage, regardless of its source. Items with health increase both durability and damage. Items with only armor or magic resistance do not convert into damage.
notes.pyke-skill-q: Tap Q to stab forward. Hold Q to throw the harpoon and pull the target. Even a half charged Q pulls the same distance at close range. Cancel Q before its channel ends or hit an enemy champion to recover most of the mana spent.
notes.pyke-skill-w: W camouflages Pyke, hiding him until he enters an enemy champion's detection range. Use W to approach from an unexpected angle. In a one on one trade, it is often better to save W for P's healing.
notes.pyke-skill-e: E stuns when the phantom left at the starting point returns, not during the dash itself. To stun with E, keep the target on the line between your starting and ending points. E works for both engaging and escaping. Before engaging, decide whether E or allied crowd control will give you a way out.
notes.pyke-skill-r: R teleports Pyke to enemies below its health threshold in the X shaped area and executes them. R deals only half damage to enemies above its execution threshold. R's execution threshold rises with bonus attack damage and lethality. Use Q and E to lower the health of enemies you cannot execute yet.
notes.pyke-skill-r-gold: When Pyke gets a kill with R, the kill gold goes to the last ally who assisted, and Pyke receives a separate reward. Use R without hesitation on a target an ally has damaged. If an enemy champion dies within R's X shaped area, you can use R again for a short time. In teamfights, execute the lowest health enemy first with R to keep the recasts going.
notes.pyke-phase: Kill opportunities start at level 2, when you have both Q and E. Pyke's power rises sharply at level 6, when he learns R. Pyke reaches his peak when he completes his first core lethality item. After completing your first core lethality item, roam to pressure other lanes. Late in the game, it is hard to bring enemies with increased health below the execution threshold. In late game teamfights, Pyke is fragile and can easily die first.
notes.pyke-laning: Pyke is a support who takes almost no CS and grows through kills. In lane, move between brushes and blind spots to keep opponents under pressure within Q range. Look for an opening to engage together after your ADC pushes the wave. Taking one heavy hit removes your chance to engage, so do not force the first attack.
notes.pyke-laning-w-pressure: Simply activating W can pressure opponents into backing away. While W pushes opponents back, secure river vision or roam mid. Roam only when the wave is pushing toward the enemy and your ADC can hold the lane alone.
notes.pyke-teamfight: In teamfights, target the single most dangerous enemy in the backline. Once allied crowd control lands and draws the enemy's attention, use W to enter from the flank. Leave yourself an escape route when entering a teamfight. If other enemies are grouped around a low health target, use R to aim for both the execution and area damage.
notes.vs-pyke-w-vision: When Pyke uses W nearby, a shark shadow circles beneath your feet. If you see the shark shadow, Pyke is already in range. If you see the shark shadow, retreat toward your allies or under your turret. Use control wards to cover brush entrances and limit Pyke's W approach angles.
notes.vs-pyke-e: Against Pyke, prioritize dodging E. E's stun occurs along the line between Pyke's starting and ending points. Move sideways from Pyke's path to dodge the E phantom. If you dodge E, Pyke is left in a position where engaging or escaping is difficult.
notes.vs-pyke-r: Do not stand next to a low health ally. If Pyke executes an ally with R, others in the X shaped area also take damage. If Pyke executes someone with R, he can use R again immediately. In teamfights, wounded allies should spread out to stop a chain of R executions.
notes.vs-pyke-passive: Pyke must leave vision to heal his stored health. After a trade, place a ward toward Pyke as he retreats to prevent his healing. Keep retreating Pyke in sight as you follow him to prevent his healing.
notes.vs-pyke-antiheal: Pyke's sustain depends on P's healing. With Grievous Wounds applied, Pyke has a harder time repeatedly engaging and disengaging. If you deal physical damage, buy Executioner's Calling earlier than usual to reduce Pyke's healing.
notes.vs-pyke-late: Pyke struggles to bring high health targets below his execution threshold. Late game champions with health items will not die to a single Pyke R. Late in the game, keep squishy allies Pyke might target behind the frontline and move together.
notes.qiyana-skill-element: Qiyana chooses how to fight based on the element she takes with W. An element taken from the river gives Q a root. An element taken from a wall or rock deals extra damage when finishing off an enemy below half health. Using Q with a brush element makes Qiyana invisible and increases her movement speed inside the area it creates. Choose the element you need before a fight and move to that terrain first.
notes.qiyana-skill-w-reset: W is a movement ability that resets Q's cooldown. After using Q, take a different element with W and use Q again. Taking a new element with W also resets the passive's cooldown on each target. Use W's reset to deal the passive's bonus damage twice to the same enemy.
notes.qiyana-skill-q-range: Without an element, Q is a short melee attack; with an element, its range increases. Avoid using Q without an element out of habit in case you need to get close. Before farming with Q, check whether there is nearby terrain you can target with W. Do not use E to farm; it costs a lot of mana. To save mana, clear waves with the attack speed and bonus basic attack damage you gain while holding an element.
notes.qiyana-skill-e-autotarget: E is a dash that passes through its target and moves you behind them. If you use Q while dashing to a champion with E, Q automatically targets that champion. To land Q, use it immediately after using E on a champion. Do not use E carelessly on minions; it is your only targeted way in.
notes.qiyana-skill-r-terrain: R's shockwave knocks enemies back. If it hits a wall, river, or brush, the entire edge of that terrain explodes. Aim R along the line between the enemy and the terrain. If R hits a long stretch of river, the explosion covers a long area too. R's stun duration is proportional to the distance its shockwave travels. Fight in narrow passages or by the river to use R's terrain explosion.
notes.qiyana-combo-basic: After taking an element, use E and Q during the dash, land a basic attack, then reset with W and use Q again. Use E first and save W so you can reset and have a way out. While holding an element, weave basic attacks between abilities.
notes.qiyana-combo-ult: To finish an enemy, push them into a wall with R to stun them, then switch elements with W and land Q and a basic attack. Use R first, then land your remaining attacks during the stun. When using Flash in the combo, reposition with Flash before casting R toward the terrain.
notes.qiyana-combo-bush: You become invisible inside the area created by brush element Q. While brush element Q blocks the enemy's vision, use E and W to set up an ambush angle. When chased, use brush element Q to break pursuit. You are revealed as soon as you leave brush element Q's area. While inside brush element Q's area, plan your W path to the next terrain.
notes.qiyana-laning-trade: Approach with the brush element, land E and Q, then immediately use W on different terrain to escape. After using all your abilities, avoid staying in the middle of the lane where you can be hit back. Look for the moment an enemy steps forward to last-hit a minion.
notes.qiyana-laning-wave: Qiyana gains an advantage by moving to other lanes and the jungle rather than staying in lane to build up CS. Push the wave toward the enemy turret, then move along the river. Do not leave lane when the wave is pushing toward your side.
notes.qiyana-phase: Qiyana becomes much stronger when she learns R at level 6. Qiyana is at her strongest in the mid game with one or two core items. In the late game, enemy defensive items make it harder to kill in one burst, and engaging becomes riskier. Use your mid-game lead to take objectives and push towers, bringing the game to a close sooner.
notes.qiyana-teamfight: If enemies group in a narrow passage or near a river or brush, start the teamfight with R. If you have no angle to engage with R, wait for an ally to engage and draw out enemy abilities, then use W and E to reach the backline. Engage after the enemy uses targeted crowd control and defensive abilities on your ally who engages. Before engaging, check which terrain you can target with W when retreating.
notes.qiyana-situational-antiheal: If enemies sustain through healing, that healing can stop your assassination damage, so buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.qiyana-situational-mercurial: If the enemy team has a lot of crowd control that can lock down Qiyana when she engages, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item.
notes.vs-qiyana-terrain: Qiyana depends on terrain to take elements and trigger R's terrain explosion. Against Qiyana, stand in open ground away from walls, brush, and the river. Move to a wide area to avoid facing Qiyana by the river or in a narrow passage.
notes.vs-qiyana-r: Qiyana's R shockwave explodes when it hits terrain, and its stun duration is proportional to the distance it travels. When facing Qiyana, do not stand with your back to a wall. If Qiyana's R hits you, use a movement ability away from the terrain because the explosion spreads along its edge.
notes.vs-qiyana-element: If Qiyana approaches with the river element, back out of Q's root range first. If Qiyana disappears while holding the brush element, move into your allies' vision. If you are below half health and Qiyana has the rock element, create distance before she gets close.
notes.vs-qiyana-cooldown: Try to fight back right after Qiyana uses W and E to engage. In lane, trade with Qiyana if she stays forward after using all her abilities.
notes.vs-qiyana-lategame: Qiyana is strongest in the mid game and becomes relatively weaker as the game goes late. Avoid giving up a lead in the early and mid game, then build defensive stats and move together. When moving together, stand away from terrain so Qiyana has no angle for R.
notes.quinn-combo-harrier: After a marked auto, land one or two more autos with W's passive, then use E to knock the target back and retreat. The faster you consume a Harrier mark, the sooner the next one appears. Take short trades in sync with Harrier's mark cycle.
notes.quinn-combo-allin: When going all in, dash with E, land an empowered auto as soon as you land, then follow with Q and autos. E marks the target with Harrier, so your next auto is empowered. The empowered auto triggers W's passive, increasing the attack speed of your follow-up autos. When going all in, do not save E until the end.
notes.quinn-combo-e-direction: E reaches the target, then vaults back to land, so the direction you use it determines where you land. Use E from the far side of the enemy to knock them toward your team while backing away. Using E with your back to a wall can let you land across the terrain.
notes.quinn-skill-q: If Q first hits a non-champion, only that target is disabled; champions receive neither the mark nor reduced vision. Aim Q straight at the opponent when they step outside the minion line. Q deals greatly increased damage to jungle monsters. Use Q to clear camps or contest objective steals.
notes.quinn-skill-w: Attacking a target marked by Harrier increases both your attack speed and movement speed through W's passive. Save W's active for information on the jungler's position and to check around objectives and in bushes.
notes.quinn-skill-e: E follows its target even if they Flash or use a mobility ability deeper into enemy territory. Before engaging with E, check whether the opponent's mobility ability is down. Before engaging with E, check whether your team can follow up. Quinn is easily killed when caught by crowd control.
notes.quinn-skill-r: R is a travel tool that activates after its channel completes. R's movement speed bonus ends when Quinn takes damage from anything other than minions. When traveling with R, take a route outside enemy vision. Push the lane, then use R to move to another side lane. Right after a teamfight ends, use R to push the lane on the opposite side.
notes.quinn-skill-passive: Harrier periodically marks nearby enemies. Consuming a Harrier mark on a minion also restarts the mark cycle. If the opponent is in trading range, save the mark for the champion instead of consuming it on a minion. Quinn's trades depend heavily on whether a Harrier mark is available.
notes.quinn-laning: When a melee opponent steps up for a last hit, land a marked auto and retreat immediately. If the opponent closes in to retaliate, use E to knock them back and escape. Repeat short trades with marked autos to chip away at the opponent's health and build a lane advantage.
notes.quinn-laning-wave: Push the wave into the enemy turret, then use R to move to another lane or the enemy jungle and create a numbers advantage. Even if you lose ground in top lane while roaming, push it back out from the side lane. To make use of Quinn's strengths, avoid holding the lane near your turret and playing defensively.
notes.quinn-phase: Quinn has a strong early lane phase, pressuring melee opponents with marked autos from level 1 or 2. At level 6, Quinn gains R's mobility and can move across the map. Quinn is strongest in the mid game after her first core item. Quinn lacks sustained damage in late-game front-to-back teamfights, greatly reducing her role. End the game in the mid game or maintain your impact through side-lane pressure.
notes.quinn-teamfight: Avoid entering teamfights from the front. Come in from the side or behind and only finish off targets already under attack. Save E to knock back an enemy who closes in and escape.
notes.quinn-teamfight-split: Consider pushing the opposite side lane instead of taking a front-to-back teamfight. If a teamfight looks likely, R's mobility lets you delay the decision to join. If your team can hold out, keep pushing the side lane. If your team is likely to collapse, join them early.
notes.quinn-situational-antiheal: If the opponent sustains through your poke with healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Quinn's short trades lose their poke value if the opponent heals the damage.
notes.vs-quinn-harrier: Quinn's poke is strong when a Harrier mark is on the target. When you are marked, move outside Quinn's auto range and let the mark expire. Farm or start a trade while Harrier's mark is unavailable.
notes.vs-quinn-q: If Quinn's Q hits a minion first, it does not affect the champion. Stand behind the minion line to block Quinn's Q angle. While Q has reduced your vision, hold your skillshots and decide only whether to approach or retreat.
notes.vs-quinn-e: Quinn backs away as soon as she reaches you with E, making it hard to retaliate. Quinn has no escape when E is down. Engage Quinn right after she uses E; do not force an engage before then.
notes.vs-quinn-r: Damaging Quinn while she travels with R ends her movement speed bonus. If you lose track of Quinn, establish vision in the side lanes or along jungle routes. Warn your team early when you spot Quinn roaming. After level 6, Quinn excels at creating numbers advantages in other lanes.
notes.vs-quinn-teamfight: Quinn lacks staying power in front-to-back teamfights. Force teamfights instead of fighting Quinn one-on-one in a side lane. If Quinn enters a teamfight from the flank, catch her with crowd control.
notes.vs-quinn-melee: Quinn has a range advantage in lane against melee champions. When playing a melee champion against her, collect CS and preserve your health early. When playing a melee champion against her, do not try to engage alone without jungle help. Melee champions should start a trade only when Quinn's E is down or their jungler arrives.
notes.rakan-combo-engage: Start a basic engage with W to knock them up, then follow with Q and an auto attack. W moves in two stages: a dash, then a leap to land. During W's cast, the enemy has time to move away from the landing spot. Use W from a brush or out of vision, keeping the travel distance short.
notes.rakan-combo-r-w: After level 6, charm an enemy with R, then immediately knock them up with W. R gives another large movement speed boost the moment it touches the first champion. Rakan's dash speed scales with his movement speed. Using W when R's speed boost triggers on the first champion gives you the longest, fastest dash.
notes.rakan-combo-e-w-e: To go in and out, use E to reach an ally, knock the enemy up with W, then recast E to return. E can only be recast for a short time after its first use. Recasting E costs nothing. Check that you can recast E before using W.
notes.rakan-combo-q-heal: If Q hits a champion or epic monster, Rakan and nearby allies heal shortly afterward. If Rakan touches an ally after Q hits, the heal triggers immediately. During a trade, land Q, then use E to reach an ally and trigger the heal sooner.
notes.rakan-skill-passive: Rakan's passive periodically grants a shield. Each auto attack or ability that hits an enemy champion reduces the passive's cooldown. Poke with Q before engaging to bring the passive shield back. Engaging with the shield up greatly improves your chances of surviving.
notes.rakan-skill-q: Q damages only the first enemy it hits. Q is used up if it hits a minion in front. Throw Q from an angle clear of the minion line. Q heals only when it hits a champion or epic monster. Hit an enemy champion with Q to get both poke and lane sustain.
notes.rakan-skill-w: W is Rakan's only forced engage tool and effectively his only escape tool. If you use W to poke first, it is hard to respond to a gank or counterattack afterward. Decide whether to engage with W based on whether an ally is available for E.
notes.rakan-skill-e: E requires an allied champion to cast. E cannot target minions. When moving away from allies, Rakan becomes a melee champion with no mobility ability. Do not cross the jungle or areas without vision alone.
notes.rakan-skill-r: Activating R gives a large movement speed boost. Enemies Rakan touches while rushing with R are charmed. To charm multiple enemies, move in from an angle where they are lined up. When escaping, use R's movement speed even if you cannot hit an enemy.
notes.rakan-phase: Rakan has weak poke at level 1, so play quietly through it. From level 2, with both W and E, you can go all in and get back out. Getting R at level 6 gives Rakan his second power spike. Rakan is strongest in the mid game, when his mobility can shape the game. In the late game, getting caught once right after engaging can easily kill him.
notes.rakan-laning: In lane, use Q to chip away at the enemy's health and reduce the passive shield's cooldown. Only start an all in when W is available and an allied E target is close. Do not force the wave to push. Catch the enemy marksman with W the moment they step in front of the minion line.
notes.rakan-laning-roam: Rakan's two mobility abilities make his roams very effective. Roam mid right after pushing the wave into the enemy turret. When returning from a roam, use E on your allied mid laner to shorten your travel time.
notes.rakan-teamfight: Before a teamfight, decide whether your role is to engage or protect. When you need to catch the enemy carries, charm multiple enemies with R, then knock them up with W. When you need to protect your carries, save W to knock up an enemy champion diving in. When protecting your carries, hold out with E's shield and Q's heal. If you split your role between engaging and protecting in a teamfight, it is hard to do both well.
notes.rakan-situational-cc: If Rakan is crowd controlled right after engaging, he cannot act despite having mobility abilities. If the enemy has a root, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item to remove a root that hits right after you engage.
notes.vs-rakan-w: Rakan's W dashes, then leaps to land, and its landing spot is visible beforehand. When Rakan starts moving with W, step sideways to dodge the knockup. The farther away Rakan starts W, the easier it is to dodge.
notes.vs-rakan-e: Rakan can only use E on allied champions. Away from allies, Rakan is effectively a melee champion with no mobility ability. Look for moments when Rakan is alone while roaming or setting up vision.
notes.vs-rakan-cc: Rakan is very vulnerable to crowd control that applies immediately. Right after W lands, use a stun or root that does not require aiming to stop Rakan's mobility. It is hard to catch Rakan with skillshots alone.
notes.vs-rakan-r: With R active, Rakan charms enemies he touches as he passes. It is hard to escape an R active Rakan on foot. Put terrain between you and Rakan when dodging his R. Crowd control Rakan before he touches you with R active. If you stand in a line, Rakan's R can charm several of you at once.
notes.vs-rakan-passive: Rakan's passive shield returns periodically. Each time Rakan lands poke, his passive shield returns sooner. Trading while Rakan's shield is up puts you at a disadvantage. Rakan is most vulnerable right after his shield breaks.
notes.rammus-combo-basic: Collide with Q to knock back and slow the target, then taunt a priority enemy with E, activate W, and auto-attack. Do not activate W before engaging. Activate it right after the enemy starts hitting Rammus.
notes.rammus-combo-qr: Using R while rolling with Q knocks enemies at the center of the area airborne. If you use R after Q collides with an enemy and stops, it does not knock them airborne. Use R while Q is still rolling, just before reaching the enemy.
notes.rammus-combo-taunt-tower: Taunting an enemy with E near an allied turret makes them auto-attack Rammus, causing the turret to attack them. Taunt enemies diving under your turret with E instead of knocking them back with Q.
notes.rammus-skill-q: Q gains movement speed the longer it rolls. When ganking, start Q out of vision so you arrive at maximum speed. Q stops when it hits an enemy, minion, or neutral monster, so roll along a path that avoids them. Recast Q to end it early if you want to change direction. When escaping with Q, choose a direction clear of enemies and minions so you do not stop midway.
notes.rammus-skill-w: Activating W greatly increases armor and magic resistance for a set duration. Enemies who hit Rammus while W is active take reflected damage. Activate W after the enemy actually starts hitting Rammus. When you no longer need W, recast it to end it early and start its cooldown sooner.
notes.rammus-skill-e-taunt: E is a targeted taunt, so it cannot miss. Enemies affected by E walk toward Rammus and only auto-attack. E interrupts enemy ability casts and channels. Use E on one of the enemy team's main damage dealers. Using E just as an enemy tries to escape with a mobility ability makes that ability useless.
notes.rammus-skill-passive: Rammus's passive converts armor and magic resistance into attack damage. Increasing your defensive stats with defensive items also increases auto-attack damage and turret destruction speed. The armor and magic resistance gained from W also count toward the passive.
notes.rammus-skill-r-tower: R deals double damage to turrets. Later in the game, combine auto-attacks boosted by W with R to destroy turrets quickly, even alone. If a teamfight stalls, disengage and attack structures.
notes.rammus-skill-r-zone: After landing, R causes repeated aftershocks in the same spot, stacking slows. Use R in narrow paths enemies must cross or in objective pits. Do not use R where an enemy has already escaped from.
notes.rammus-laning-jungle: Statistically, Rammus ranks among the lowest overall in early CS and damage per minute. Clear camps quickly, then use Q's long engage range to spend time on ganks and objectives. Statistically, Rammus ranks among the highest in deaths.
notes.rammus-phase: At levels 1–2, Rammus clears camps slowly and deals almost no damage on his own. Ganks become viable once you have both Q and E. Once you learn R at level 6, you can force fights over objectives. As defensive items stack up, the passive also increases Rammus's damage, so he peaks in the mid to late game. Later in the game, destroying turrets becomes a separate source of pressure.
notes.rammus-teamfight: In teamfights, taunt a main damage dealer in the enemy backline with E. Engage with Q, taunt with E, and use R to lock down that area. If you cannot reach a target to taunt, stand in front of your carry and counter the enemy engage with Q's knockback and E's taunt.
notes.rammus-teamfight-vs-marksman: Rammus's W reflected damage and E taunt pressure ranged damage dealers who rely on auto-attacks. Against a ranged damage dealer who relies on auto-attacks, keep positioning within their vision to disrupt their attacks.
notes.rammus-situational-mr: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, do not build only armor. The passive converts magic resistance into attack damage, and W also increases magic resistance. If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buying Spirit Visage or Banshee's Veil early does not reduce your damage.
notes.vs-rammus-w-window: Rammus's defensive stats are extremely high while W is active. With W down, Rammus is slightly less durable than a typical tank. When W activates, back off briefly, then focus your damage as soon as it ends.
notes.vs-rammus-armor: Rammus stacks armor to extreme levels, and that armor converts into attack damage. Have allies with magic damage, true damage, or damage based on maximum health deal with Rammus.
notes.vs-rammus-autoattack: Auto-attacking Rammus while W is active deals reflected damage to the attacker. The faster a champion attacks, the more they suffer from Rammus's W reflected damage. While W is active, attack another target instead of auto-attacking Rammus. Unless you must kill Rammus, wait for W to end.
notes.vs-rammus-taunt: E is a targeted taunt that cannot be dodged; while affected, you cannot issue movement commands or use abilities. Fight outside Rammus's E range. Time Flash or a mobility ability so you can use it as soon as the taunt ends. Do not start channeling an ability while Rammus is close.
notes.vs-rammus-q-block: Q needs time to build speed and stops where it hits something. To block Rammus's approach, stand behind a minion wave or inside a narrow passage.
notes.vs-rammus-r-range: R's area grows with Rammus's movement speed, so using it from Q at maximum speed covers more area than expected. If you see Rammus rolling toward you, allow plenty of room for R's expected area and back away. After R lands, aftershocks continue in the same spot, stacking slows. Leave the spot where R lands immediately.
notes.reksai-skill-q: Unburrowed Q empowers the next three basic attacks to hit nearby enemies too. Each basic attack refreshes the duration of unburrowed Q. After using unburrowed Q, keep your basic attacks going without interruption. Burrowed Q fires soil at range and reveals the location of enemies it hits. Dealing damage with burrowed Q can meet R's targeting requirement.
notes.reksai-skill-w-knockup: Using W to emerge while burrowed knocks up nearby enemies. Burrowed W is Rek'Sai's only guaranteed crowd control. Track the moving enemy's direction, move beneath them, and emerge with W.
notes.reksai-skill-e-fury: Unburrowed E deals true damage at maximum Fury. Build Fury with basic attacks and abilities, then finish with E. E's true damage at maximum Fury ignores the enemy's armor.
notes.reksai-skill-e-tunnel: Tunnels made with burrowed E last a long time and can be used again. Tunnel entrances are visible to enemies and break when they step on them. Dig a tunnel for escape before the fight starts.
notes.reksai-skill-r: R leaps to an enemy Rek'Sai has recently damaged. Rek'Sai cannot be targeted while underground during R. R's leap cannot be stopped midway. R deals damage based on maximum health. Landing with R resets W's cooldown.
notes.reksai-combo-gank: Approach while burrowed, knock the enemy up with W, build Fury with Q-empowered basic attacks, then finish with E. Press Q right after the W knockup to land all three empowered basic attacks on the enemy. Use E after building Fury. If the enemy is already caught, walk up while unburrowed and start with a basic attack.
notes.reksai-combo-ult: Hit a fleeing enemy with burrowed Q, leap to them with R, then knock them up with W after landing. Right after damaging an enemy, use R to dodge a targeted ability, then escape through a tunnel you dug earlier. Before pressing R, check whether the landing spot is in the middle of the enemy team.
notes.reksai-laning-tunnelmap: Rek'Sai is not a jungler who gets ahead through farming alone. Early on, dig tunnels leading to lanes to create routes into multiple lanes. Dig tunnels in the enemy jungle to use for invasions and escapes.
notes.reksai-phase: Rek'Sai can make an impact through ganks from level 3, when she has W, until level 6, when she learns R. Rek'Sai's power peaks in the mid game when she gets her core items. Late in the game, Rek'Sai's relative damage falls, making it hard to kill backline enemies alone. Gain an advantage through ganks and objectives in the early and mid game to end the game sooner. Late in the game, engage with R and knock up an enemy.
notes.reksai-teamfight: In teamfights, land behind the enemy team with R, then open the fight with a W knockup. Go in when your allies can follow up immediately and the enemy has used their crowd control to respond. Do not overcommit to chasing backline enemies; catch tanky enemies too.
notes.reksai-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Rek'Sai stays close and keeps basic attacking, so she can maintain Grievous Wounds throughout a fight.
notes.reksai-situational-mercurial: If the enemy has a lot of crowd control that locks down Rek'Sai when she goes in, buy Quicksilver Sash after one core item. Rek'Sai can be killed easily if she is crowd controlled right after going in with R.
notes.vs-reksai-knockup: Rek'Sai's guaranteed crowd control is the knockup from W while burrowed. Use a mobility ability as Rek'Sai emerges to dodge the knockup. If you dodge Rek'Sai's W knockup, she loses her way to catch you.
notes.vs-reksai-tunnel: Rek'Sai's tunnel entrances are visible and break when enemies step on them. If you find a Rek'Sai tunnel near a lane or in your jungle, step on it to destroy it. Destroying a Rek'Sai tunnel removes her gank route and escape route through it.
notes.vs-reksai-r: Rek'Sai's R only leaps to enemies she has recently damaged. If burrowed Q hits you, stay near your allies for the next few seconds. Do not use targeted abilities while Rek'Sai is leaping with R. Place untargeted crowd control at Rek'Sai's R landing spot in advance.
notes.vs-reksai-phase: Rek'Sai tries to build an advantage through early and mid-game ganks and end the game early. Avoid giving Rek'Sai kills early and stall the game to make her easier to deal with. Do not push your lane too far against Rek'Sai early on. Do not travel alone through areas without vision early on.
notes.rell-combo-engage: Use E to approach with an ally, knock enemies up with W, stun them with Q, then pull them together with R. E's explosion triggers on whichever hits first: your next basic attack or Q. Landing Q right after W's knockup applies crowd control and E's explosion together.
notes.rell-combo-remount: You can use two knockups by switching between W's two forms. Using W to remount after Crash Down grants movement speed. Your next basic attack after remounting knocks an enemy up. The shield gained from Crash Down disappears when you remount. Remount when your shield is already depleted or you need to catch a fleeing enemy.
notes.rell-combo-flash: W's Crash Down immediately hits around Rell. Flash to close the gap, then knock enemies up with W and stun them with Q. If you press W before Flash, the knockup hitbox stays at your original position.
notes.rell-skill-q: Q thrusts in a straight line and briefly stuns enemies. Q destroys all shields on targets it hits. If the enemy support grants a shield, use Q as soon as it appears. Q cannot destroy monster shields.
notes.rell-skill-w: W switches between mounted and dismounted forms. While mounted, the movement speed makes it easier to approach. Dismounting into armored form increases armor, magic resistance, attack speed, and basic attack range. Movement speed drops sharply in armored form. Stay in armored form to withstand a fight that has already started. Remount when moving to find the next fight.
notes.rell-skill-e: E increases movement speed for Rell and one ally. E's movement speed increase doubles when moving toward an enemy or each other. Activate E just before engaging to close the gap. When retreating after a fight, E's double-speed condition no longer applies, halving its effectiveness. Rell's base movement speed is among the lowest of all champions. Do not look for an engage while E is unavailable.
notes.rell-skill-passive: Each basic attack and ability hit steals the target's armor and magic resistance, stacking the passive. After using crowd control, keep weaving in basic attacks in armored form to maintain passive stacks. Maintaining passive stacks also increases your allied damage dealer's damage.
notes.rell-skill-r: R pulls nearby enemies toward Rell, then keeps pulling them briefly. R has short range, so walking in to use it alone leaves Rell exposed. Use R immediately after W's knockup to keep enemies grouped together. Use R after an ally has already engaged.
notes.rell-phase: Starting with W at level 1 and gaining Q at level 2 is Rell's first strong window. Following W's knockup with Q's stun can force the enemy marksman to use an escape tool. Getting R at level 6 gives Rell a second power spike. Rell peaks in the mid game as she builds defensive items. Late in the game, her short range and lack of an escape after engaging make solo engages easy to punish.
notes.rell-laning: Rell struggles to reach enemies on foot, so she relies on vision and brush in lane. Keep the wave pulled toward your allied turret. Look for the moment an enemy enters W's Crash Down range from the brush. Basic attack range and attack speed increase in armored form. Once you close the gap, keep trading with basic attacks.
notes.rell-laning-roam: Activate E when setting out to roam. Activate E and move with your marksman toward the river or mid; both of you move faster. Roam right after pushing the wave into the enemy turret. Account for your slow movement speed when timing your return so you do not lose the bot turret.
notes.rell-teamfight: Group enemies together so your allies' area abilities hit them. Engage when your allies are ready to go in with you. Engage when at least two enemies are within R range. If the enemy team is spread out, stay in armored form in front of your allied damage dealer and absorb the dive.
notes.rell-situational-mr: If the enemy team deals mostly magic damage, build magic resistance first. Build Spirit Visage earlier against a team that deals mostly magic damage. If a single burst of damage is the problem rather than sustained damage, use Banshee's Veil to block one engage ability.
notes.rell-situational-armor: If the enemy's physical damage is strong, buy Plated Steelcaps and build armor first. Against a team centered on basic attacks, prioritize Frozen Heart over Thornmail to protect your allied damage dealer too.
notes.vs-rell-w: Rell's forced engage depends on W's Crash Down, which has very short range. When Rell is mounted, she is looking to engage. When Rell dismounts into armored form, her movement speed becomes one of the slowest in the game. Stay outside W's Crash Down range, then create distance right after Rell uses W.
notes.vs-rell-q: If Rell's Q hits you, it destroys all your shields. Apply shields after Rell uses Q. Sidestep Q's straight-line thrust.
notes.vs-rell-e: If Rell and one ally suddenly speed up together, E is active and an engage is coming. If Rell runs toward you, E's movement speed increase doubles. If Rell activates E and runs toward you, stop trading and retreat beyond W's Crash Down range.
notes.vs-rell-r: Rell's R is effective when it pulls several nearby enemies together. Spread out from your allies before a teamfight engage so R cannot pull several of you together. If R has already pulled you in, use a movement ability or cleanse while it keeps pulling.
notes.vs-rell-early: Rell has no way to heal in lane. If you can poke with magic damage, keep lowering Rell's health from outside her engage range.
notes.renata-combo-q: Q roots the first enemy it hits. Enemies hit by a champion thrown with Q are stunned. When enemies are grouped, throw the champion caught by Q into them to stun multiple enemies. When an ally needs to close the gap, pull the enemy caught by Q toward that ally.
notes.renata-combo-q-direction: If you don't recast Q, only the root remains. Throw a fleeing enemy toward your allies with Q. Use Q to push an enemy who jumps on an ally away from them. When Q roots an enemy, move your cursor toward the throw direction, then recast Q.
notes.renata-combo-order: Slow with E, root with Q, then recast Q to throw the target where you want. E's slow helps you land Q's slow projectile. To save an ally, use W first and E's shield afterward. You can't use W after an ally has already died.
notes.renata-skill-passive: Your basic attack mark can only be on one target at a time. When an ally hits a marked target, the mark is consumed and deals bonus damage. The basic attack mark's damage based on maximum health is effective against the enemy frontline too. In lane, mark the enemy marksman with a basic attack to help your ally trade damage.
notes.renata-skill-w-nature: An ally with W briefly revives at full health when they die. An ally revived by W gradually loses health. An ally revived by W survives if they get a takedown during that time. Use W on an ally dealing damage now, rather than one certain to die.
notes.renata-skill-w-timing: W has a long cooldown. Use W on your main damage dealer just before a fight to increase their attack speed and movement speed. W's duration refreshes when its target gets a takedown.
notes.renata-skill-e: E's missiles damage and slow enemies while shielding allies. If an ally and an enemy are in the same line, fire E at the enemy beyond your allied damage dealer. Use E, with its short cooldown, as your main tool for trading damage in lane. Use E's slow to start a fight.
notes.renata-skill-r-frenzy: Enemies hit by R are forced to attack nearby units, prioritizing their own allies. Use R when the enemies it hits are close enough to attack one another. Don't use R on an isolated enemy.
notes.renata-skill-r-timing: Land R right after the enemy engage composition jumps in together. Enemies hit by R gain a large amount of attack speed. Move an isolated ally near an enemy hit by R out of the berserk range.
notes.renata-laning: Don't stand in front of the enemy in lane. Support your ally's trades with E's shield. In lane, just apply the auto-attack mark briefly. Use Q when the enemy support steps forward or a gap opens between minions.
notes.renata-laning-trade: Hit the enemy with E as they step forward to last-hit. E damages and slows the enemy while shielding your allied marksman. Don't step forward in lane while E is on cooldown.
notes.renata-phase: Renata Glasc is weak at level 1, when she has only one ability. Kill opportunities open up once you learn Q. At level 6, Renata Glasc becomes much stronger because R lets her counter enemy engage compositions. Late in the game, Renata Glasc deals almost no damage herself. Her ability to save allies and disrupt the enemy formation remains useful until the end of the game.
notes.renata-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your allied frontline instead of engaging. Use Q to interrupt the enemy's engage. Use Q to throw an enemy damage dealer toward your allies. Use W and E to help allies survive fights.
notes.renata-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps undoing your allies' damage, buy Blighting Jewel first to apply healing reduction. The basic attack mark and E let you deal steady damage, making healing reduction easy to maintain.
notes.vs-renata-r: If Renata Glasc's R hits you, you briefly lose control and attack nearby allies. If you have a way to cleanse crowd control, remove Renata Glasc's R immediately. If you have no way to cleanse it, move away from your allies immediately after Renata Glasc's R hits you. If you have Cleanse or Quicksilver Sash, save it while within range of Renata Glasc's R.
notes.vs-renata-r-spacing: Enemies affected by Renata Glasc's R prioritize attacking their own allies, so grouping up makes the damage worse. While Renata Glasc's R is available, space yourselves out as you engage. When Renata Glasc's R is available, don't engage with all five players lined up together.
notes.vs-renata-q: Renata Glasc's Q roots only the first target it hits. Stand behind minions or your frontline so they take Renata Glasc's Q instead. If Renata Glasc's Q roots you, decide immediately whether to escape with Flash or a mobility ability. After you're thrown by Renata Glasc's Q, your allies can be stunned too.
notes.vs-renata-w: An enemy with Renata Glasc's W briefly revives and keeps fighting after dying. An enemy revived by W stays alive if they get a takedown during that time. Right after killing an enemy affected by W, back away so your allies don't die.
notes.vs-renata-e: Renata Glasc's E shields allies and damages and slows enemies. Dodge Renata Glasc's straight-line E by moving sideways. Rather than focusing only on dodging Renata Glasc's E, target Renata Glasc herself, who deals little damage.
notes.vs-renata-body: Renata Glasc has no mobility ability of her own. If your composition can reach Renata Glasc, kill her first. In lane, pressure Renata Glasc herself to give her less room to use her engage abilities.
notes.renekton-combo-basic: Use the basic combo in this order: E in → basic attack → W → basic attack → Q → E out. W replaces your next basic attack, so use it between basic attacks. E can only be cast again if the first dash hits a unit. If you expect to lose the trade, take a short trade with E → W → basic attack → Q → E.
notes.renekton-combo-allin: When you have kill pressure, build Fury, then use E → empowered W → Q → basic attack → E. You can land both Q and a basic attack during empowered W's stun. Empowered abilities do not generate Fury. After level 6, use R just before engaging. R grants bonus maximum health for its duration and removes it when it ends. R continuously generates Fury for its duration. Use the Fury gained from R to attempt a second combo or a dive.
notes.renekton-skill-fury: Gain Fury by hitting enemies with basic attacks and Q, W, or E. Fury steadily decreases out of combat. Just before trading, build Fury with minion last hits and basic attacks. If you lack Fury, engage with E, hit both your opponent and minions with Q, then use empowered W. For a simple trade or sustain, choose empowered Q for its increased healing. When you have kill pressure, choose empowered W for its longer stun. Renekton uses ability haste efficiently because it speeds up both Fury generation and spending.
