If E cannot hit a wall, recast it to end the charge early.
notes.skarner-skill-r-mechanic: Most mobility abilities and Cleanse cannot break R's suppression. R is not a channel, so stuns and silences cannot interrupt it. Quicksilver Sash and Mercurial Scimitar remove R's suppression. Before using R, check whether the target has Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar. Use R to pull enemies standing at the edge of the Dragon or Baron pit into the pit.
notes.skarner-skill-r-target: R suppresses multiple targets hit in front of Skarner at once. To stop an enemy engage, suppress the champion coming in with R. Use R to pull an enemy away from your carry. Before a fight, decide whether to use R to stop an engage or protect your carry.
notes.skarner-laning-path: Skarner's early jungle path is not focused on getting kills. Early on, clear camps safely to gain levels and items, then take control of objectives. When counterjungling out of enemy vision, use E routes that cross walls.
notes.skarner-laning-gank: When ganking, choose the wall first, then approach from the opposite side with E to push the target into it. E cannot stun in an open area without a wall. When ganking in an open area, use Q's slow and your allies' crowd control. Delay ganks in lanes where you cannot line up a wall hit until after level 6.
notes.skarner-phase: Before level 6, Skarner's ganks work when E can slam the target into a wall. From level 6, R's suppression lets you gank regardless of terrain. Skarner grows stronger as he gets items because Q and E scale with health and W's shield scales with maximum health.
notes.skarner-teamfight: In teamfights, engage from the front and use R to pull one key target toward your team. Engage when your carry is positioned to damage the R target immediately. If your carry cannot damage the R target immediately, hold R and buy time with Q's slow and W.
notes.skarner-situational-mr: If the enemy team deals mostly magic damage, include Spirit Visage in your core item build to strengthen W's shield and your defenses.
notes.skarner-situational-attackspeed: If the enemy team has a champion with a large attack speed boost, consider Frozen Heart to reduce the basic attacks you take while dragging them with R.
notes.vs-skarner-e: Skarner's E passes through terrain, but it only stuns a caught target if he slams them into a wall. To avoid Skarner's E stun, do not stand with your back to a wall. If Skarner catches you with E in an open area, you are pushed but not stunned. If Skarner slams you into a wall with E, back away in anticipation of his next charge.
notes.vs-skarner-r-cleanse: Skarner's R is not a channel, so stuns and silences cannot interrupt it. Carries facing Skarner should decide in advance whether to buy Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar to remove R.
notes.vs-skarner-r-position: Skarner's R has short range. Skarner can drag a target across terrain with R. When trying to steal an objective, watch out for Skarner's R at the edge of the Dragon or Baron pit.
notes.vs-skarner-range: Skarner deals most of his damage when he stays close and stacks Quaking with Q empowered basic attacks. Stay outside melee range to avoid Skarner's Q empowered basic attacks.
notes.vs-skarner-scaling: Because Skarner has abilities that use health and defensive stats, tank items increase both his damage and survivability. Take early jungle control and objectives to delay Skarner's item completions.
notes.smolder-skill-passive: Hitting a champion with an ability grants a Dragon Practice stack. Killing an enemy with Q grants a Dragon Practice stack. Dragon Practice stacks never expire. Even if you fall behind in lane, don't miss Q last hits.
notes.smolder-skill-q-evolve: Q evolves whenever Dragon Practice reaches certain stack thresholds. Before its first evolution, Q damages only one target. After its first evolution, Q's damage spreads around the target. After its next evolution, Q's explosions travel beyond the target. After its final evolution, Q burns the target, dealing damage based on their maximum health over time. Each Q evolution greatly improves waveclear and teamfight impact.
notes.smolder-skill-q-mana: Killing a target with Q refunds mana. Using Q repeatedly only on champions drains mana quickly. Harass with Q between minion last hits to recover mana.
notes.smolder-skill-w: W explodes only when it hits a champion. W grants one stack per champion hit. Using W on minions does not trigger explosion damage. Using W on minions does not grant stacks. When W hits multiple champions, each later explosion deals less damage. In teamfights, position W so it hits your intended target first. Use W's slow to keep enemies who get close away.
notes.smolder-skill-e: E lets you fly over terrain. E automatically attacks the enemy with the lowest health. You cannot choose E's target directly. E is Smolder's only escape tool and way to cross walls. Save E for potential ganks instead of using it to attack first.
notes.smolder-skill-r: R damages a wide area and slows enemies at its center. Smolder heals when R's flames reach him. In teamfights, aim R at the center of grouped enemies.
notes.smolder-combo-trade: Look for a W hit before trading damage. If W misses, give up the trade and back off.
notes.smolder-combo-escape: When escaping, slow the enemy with W, cross a wall with E, and heal with R if needed. Choose where to go before crossing a wall with E. If E stops ignoring terrain halfway through a wall, you can get stuck.
notes.smolder-laning: In lane, farm safely and build stacks with Q last hits.
notes.smolder-laning-wave: Before Q's first evolution, you have virtually no way to push the wave. Before Q's first evolution, let the wave come toward your tower and last hit there. Once Q starts damaging enemies around its target, faster waveclear gives you lane priority. When you gain lane priority, secure vision and objectives.
notes.smolder-phase: Smolder is weakest at levels 1–2 and early on when he has few stacks. Smolder gets noticeably stronger each time Q evolves. Smolder becomes powerful late in the game as he gains both stacks and items. The further behind you are, the more you should favor farming for stacks over fighting.
notes.smolder-teamfight: Smolder is a backline damage dealer with no way to engage. In teamfights, stay behind your frontline and use Q whenever it is ready. Save E to survive teamfights.
notes.smolder-teamfight-target: Q targets an enemy directly, so it can damage your intended target even in a chaotic fight. In teamfights, attack the closest enemy in range first. Attacking a frontline enemy with evolved Q also spreads damage to nearby enemies.
notes.smolder-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps undoing Q's damage over time, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.vs-smolder-stacks: Smolder grows permanently stronger each time he hits a champion with an ability or kills an enemy with Q. In lane, avoid Smolder's poke and deny him CS.
notes.vs-smolder-early: E is Smolder's only escape tool. Keep pressuring Smolder in the early and mid game so he cannot stay in lane. Make Smolder a priority target for jungle ganks.
notes.vs-smolder-e: E is Smolder's only escape that lets him cross terrain. Right after Smolder uses E is your chance to catch him. Save immobilizing crowd control and Flash until Smolder uses E. Smolder's E attacks focus on the enemy with the lowest health.
notes.vs-smolder-w: Smolder's W explodes only when it hits a champion. Smolder gains the W stack only when he hits a champion with it. Stand behind minions or move sideways to dodge Smolder's W. If Smolder's W hits you, its slow leaves you open to a follow-up Q and basic attacks.
notes.vs-smolder-r: Smolder's R deals much more damage at its center. Smolder heals when R's flames reach him. Move out of the R area beneath Smolder, then approach again.
notes.vs-smolder-late: The longer the game goes, the more it favors Smolder. Secure objectives and towers quickly to end the game in the mid game. If the game looks likely to go late, have a way to engage and kill Smolder as soon as a teamfight starts.
notes.sona-skill-aura-switch: Sona's basic abilities have an immediate effect and a briefly lingering aura. Only the aura from her most recently used basic ability remains active. Keep the aura your team needs active. Right after casting, move toward allies so the aura reaches them.
notes.sona-skill-powerchord: After using basic abilities a set number of times, her next basic attack is empowered. If Q was used last, Power Chord deals more bonus damage. If E was used last, Power Chord slows the target. When a kill is within reach, finish stacking Power Chord with Q. When escaping or helping allies chase, finish stacking Power Chord with E.
notes.sona-skill-accelerando: Effective basic ability casts permanently stack Accelerando's ability haste. Once Accelerando reaches its cap, subsequent stacks reduce her ultimate's cooldown. Q must hit a champion to stack Accelerando. W must actually heal an ally or block damage with its shield to stack Accelerando.
notes.sona-skill-q: Q automatically attacks two nearby enemies, prioritizing champions. Q's aura empowers allies' next basic attacks. Use Q when your AD carry can land a basic attack. During laning, Q is the main way to stack Accelerando.
notes.sona-skill-w: W heals immediately and provides a brief aura shield. Time W's shield for the moment an enemy ability is about to hit. W costs the most mana of her basic abilities. During laning, don't spam W just to restore a little health.
notes.sona-skill-e: E increases Sona's movement speed and also speeds up allies through its aura. If Sona takes no damage, E's self movement speed boost lasts longer. In a fight, use E when engaging or disengaging.
notes.sona-combo-lane: Hit the enemy with Q, let your AD carry land a basic attack empowered by Q's aura, then use W to absorb the counterattack. Use Q, W, then Q so the last cast gives you the bonus damage Power Chord.
notes.sona-combo-r: R is an area stun that travels in a straight line. If R is out of range, Flash and immediately cast R through the enemy formation, then use E to help your allies engage. If the enemy engages first, cast R across the incoming enemies to stun them. The aura after R depends on the last basic ability used before R.
notes.sona-laning: Sona relies heavily on mana management during laning. Early on, poke mainly with Q. Use W when guaranteed enemy damage is coming in. Against melee engage supports, secure vision in the brush first.
notes.sona-roaming: E lets Sona join fights and roam quickly. Roam when you've pushed the wave or your AD carry has recalled. Keep vision around the mid entrances and river to help your jungler move in. After level 6, head mid with R ready and look for a gank.
notes.sona-vision: Don't walk alone through areas without vision. Place wards from outside the brush, close enough to cover it without entering.
notes.sona-teamfight: In teamfights, stay back while keeping allies within aura range. Before a fight starts, use E to speed up your allies' engage. Once the fight starts, alternate W and Q to give your allies their auras. If enemies group up, hit multiple targets with R.
notes.sona-phase: Sona is weakest early on. At level 6, learning R lets her start or stop fights. From mid game, Accelerando stacks and support items build up, letting her cycle abilities faster. Late game, sustained aura use improves her team's staying power in teamfights.
notes.sona-situational-cleanse: If the enemy team uses crowd control to lock down and kill an allied carry, buy Mikael's Blessing between core items. W's shield lasts only briefly, making it hard to absorb damage while an ally is already under crowd control.
notes.vs-sona-r: Sona's R stuns every enemy in its line. When Sona is visible, spread out sideways instead of lining up with allies. Treat Sona stepping forward as a warning that she's about to cast R.
notes.vs-sona-aura: Sona's healing, shielding, and movement speed effects reach nearby allies through her auras. Separate Sona from her allies or push her back so her auras cannot reach them.
notes.vs-sona-lane: During laning, keep forcing trades so Sona has to spend mana on W. Look for the moment Sona steps forward to deliver an aura.
notes.vs-sona-e: If Sona takes no damage, E's movement speed boost lasts longer. When targeting Sona, apply immobilizing crowd control first. Decide whether to chase the enemy team before Sona activates E.
notes.vs-sona-powerchord: After Sona uses basic abilities several times, her next basic attack is empowered. If Sona suddenly moves into basic attack range, watch for an empowered attack.
notes.vs-sona-heal: Late game, Sona's auras keep healing her team, making them strong in long teamfights. Against Sona, make sure your team has at least one anti-heal item. Physical damage dealers can choose Executioner's Calling for anti-heal. Magic damage dealers can choose Morellonomicon for anti-heal.
notes.soraka-combo-qw: Land Q on an enemy champion, then use W. Landing Q on an enemy champion nearly removes the health cost of the following W. W used after landing Q also passes the Rejuvenation effect to an ally. Using W before Q costs Soraka much more health for the same healing.
notes.soraka-combo-eq: Using E alone rarely lands the root. Slow the enemy with Q, then place E over them to try to root them. Place E over an enemy caught in an ally's crowd control.
notes.soraka-skill-q-lead: The farther you cast Q, the longer it takes to land. At long range, cast Q ahead of time where the enemy will retreat after last-hitting. When you must land Q, cast it from as close to the enemy as possible.
notes.soraka-skill-q-vision: Q briefly reveals the area where it lands. When checking a brush yourself is risky, cast Q into it.
notes.soraka-skill-w-cost: Soraka spends her own health when she uses W. Using W repeatedly without Rejuvenation quickly drains Soraka's health. Soraka cannot use W when her health falls below a certain level.
notes.soraka-skill-e-interrupt: E casts instantly and can interrupt channeled abilities. Enemies inside E are silenced. Place E ahead of time in the path an enemy will take when engaging. Place E ahead of time at an enemy's Teleport landing spot.
notes.soraka-skill-e-nowave: E does not damage minions or jungle monsters. Save E for fights instead of using it to manage the wave.
notes.soraka-skill-passive: P only grants movement speed when moving toward a heavily wounded ally. An ally marked by P receives increased healing from R. Use the P marker on an ally to help decide when to cast R. An enemy can notice a nearby low-health ally from Soraka's sudden speed boost.
notes.soraka-skill-r: R heals all allies regardless of distance. R heals heavily wounded allies more. Save R if it is certain that only one ally will die and R cannot save them.
notes.soraka-laning: Soraka's laning relies on a cycle of restoring her health with Q and transferring it to an ally with W. During laning, keep landing Q poke to restore Soraka's health. If Q keeps missing, stop poking and save mana.
notes.soraka-laning-position: Soraka has no mobility ability. Against enemies that engage, save E to stop their entry. Right after Soraka uses E to poke is a good time to engage.
notes.soraka-teamfight: In teamfights, stay out of enemy vision when possible.
notes.soraka-phase: Learn Q at level 1 if you want to reach level 2 first or take early poke control. Learn W at level 1 if you plan to help leash your jungler or play defensively. After that, the usual approach is to prioritize healing. Soraka's map-wide impact grows in the mid to late game as R's cooldown gets shorter.
notes.soraka-teamfight-antiheal: Engage as soon as the enemy's healing reduction wears off.
notes.vs-soraka-e: Soraka's E has a long cooldown. Engage when you see Soraka use E first. Use your engage ability before stepping into Soraka's E.
notes.vs-soraka-w: During laning, pressure Soraka's marksman to force her to use W. Keep Soraka from landing Q to maintain pressure on her health.
notes.vs-soraka-r: Account for Soraka's R cooldown even when trying to get a kill in another lane. Damage dealt over time can be healed by a single cast of Soraka's R. Against a team with Soraka, deal your damage in a short burst.
notes.swain-combo-lane: In lane trades, place W in the enemy's path, root them with E, pull them in, then use Q at close range. Place W first to make E harder for the enemy to dodge.
notes.swain-combo-q-close: Q hits with more overlapping bolts up close, but only one bolt at maximum range. Use Q to finish an enemy after catching them, rather than to poke at range. Pull the enemy in with E before using Q so its damage does not drop to half or less.
notes.swain-combo-ult: After activating R, E's cooldown becomes shorter. After activating R, root and pull the enemy with E, then recast R. Delay the R recast until you have drained and healed as much as possible.
notes.swain-skill-e-range: E sends out a wave that travels forward and then returns. Land E at maximum range, where the enemy has less time to react. If you use E up close, the enemy can see the wave's path and walk out of it. Rooting an enemy with E from far away also helps secure a Soul Fragment.
notes.swain-skill-e-pull: When waiting for an ally to engage, leave E's root in place without recasting it. Recast E immediately when you need to move the enemy toward your allies or out of turret range. Pulling an enemy with E grants a Soul Fragment. If you are unsure whether to pull, choose the option that grants a Soul Fragment.
notes.swain-skill-w: W takes time to land, but covers a wide area and reveals it. Use W to check brushes or track the enemy jungler's path. Use W to interrupt an enemy's recall. Overlap W with E to force the enemy's Flash. It is best not to use W to clear minions.
notes.swain-skill-passive: Hitting a champion with W, pulling one with E, or an enemy champion dying grants a Soul Fragment. Soul Fragments permanently increase maximum health. To build health for the late game, use W and E on champions during the laning phase.
notes.swain-skill-r: R stays active only while it keeps draining enemy champions. If the enemy leaves R's range, R ends. Activate R when you can hold the enemy in place with E or allied crowd control.
notes.swain-phase: At level 1, you lack the mana for repeated fights. Wave clear and poke become stronger as you level Q. After learning R at level 6, you become stronger in 2v2 fights. As Soul Fragments stack, your health rises and you become tougher over time. As long as you do not fall too far behind early, you retain your late-game value.
notes.swain-laning-poke: Manage the lane by hitting both the wave and the enemy with Q. Use Q when the enemy ADC steps forward to last-hit.
notes.swain-laning-zone: Landing E makes it hard for the enemy bot duo to approach the wave for a while. Do not save E only for kill opportunities; use it whenever it is off cooldown to pressure the lane. Do not push the lane while E is on cooldown and you have no way to catch the enemy.
notes.swain-roaming: Swain has low movement speed and no dash or escape ability. Roaming takes too much time, so stay in lane and keep up the pressure. Limit trips out of lane to managing river vision. If the enemy jungler catches you while roaming, escaping is difficult.
notes.swain-teamfight: In teamfights, stand just behind your frontline and pull in one enemy with E. Activate R when enemies engage as a group and it can reach several of them. Without a dash, Swain has trouble walking in first to start a teamfight.
notes.swain-situational-zhonya: Get Zhonya's Hourglass early if an engaging damage dealer can kill Swain quickly. R becomes more valuable the longer Swain stays alive.
notes.vs-swain-e: E's wave travels forward and then returns. Even if you dodge the first wave, stay out of its path until it disappears completely. If E roots you, its recast pulls you in and leaves you open to follow-up attacks.
notes.vs-swain-q: Q hits with more overlapping bolts up close and fewer from farther away. In lane, stay near Q's maximum range while last-hitting.
notes.vs-swain-r: R stays active only while it drains nearby enemies, and Swain keeps healing during that time. When Swain activates R, leave its range and fight again after his ultimate ends.
notes.vs-swain-melee: Melee champions without a ranged last-hit option lose a lot of CS to Swain's E pressure. As a melee champion without a ranged last-hit option, check summoner spell cooldowns and ward positions to create gank opportunities for your jungler.
notes.vs-swain-mobility: Swain has no dash or escape ability and has low movement speed. Gank or force a fight right after Swain uses E.
notes.vs-swain-sustain: Swain permanently increases his maximum health by hitting champions with abilities and keeps healing with R. Take lane priority early to slow Swain's growth. Late in the game, apply Grievous Wounds to Swain before fighting him.
notes.sylas-combo-basic: Use E's first cast to close in, then hit the second cast to knock the target up. Follow with an empowered basic attack, Q, a basic attack, W, and a basic attack. Each ability cast grants one passive stack.
notes.sylas-combo-q: Q explodes after a short delay where the chains cross.
notes.sylas-skill-e: E has two casts: a dash, then a chain that pulls Sylas to the target and knocks them up. When escaping, use only E's first cast and save the second. When engaging, use E's first cast only if you have an angle to land the second.
notes.sylas-skill-w: W is both a dash and a heal. W's healing scales with missing health. In a trade, land W on an enemy champion after taking damage.
notes.sylas-skill-passive: Petricite Burst's empowered basic attack also damages enemies around the target. Attack speed increases while passive stacks remain. Save empowered basic attacks for trades instead of using them on minions.
notes.sylas-skill-r-mechanic: Use R to copy an enemy champion's ultimate. A stolen ultimate's power scales with Sylas's own R rank and stats. Stolen ultimates with attack damage ratios are converted to ability power ratios.
notes.sylas-skill-r-target: After stealing a champion's ultimate, you cannot steal from that champion again for a long time. Keep several champions available to steal from, and take a different champion's ultimate in each fight.
notes.sylas-skill-r-priority: Prioritize stealing area crowd control and engage ultimates. If your team has no way to engage, choose an ultimate that starts fights. If you need to pick off an enemy carry, choose an ultimate that locks them down. Even if you steal a single-target execute ultimate, it is hard to find an opening to use it.
notes.sylas-phase: Sylas is weak at levels 1–2 because of his short range and tight mana supply. His first power spike comes at level 6, when he can steal an enemy ultimate. He is strongest in the mid game when he has built both ability haste and ability power. In the late game, his short range and low durability make direct fights difficult. In the late game, look for an opening to make an impact with one stolen ultimate.
notes.sylas-laning: His abilities cost a lot of mana, so using them all on the wave quickly leaves him short on mana. Clear minions with Q's explosion, but save one ability cast for a trade. Save W to sustain in lane. Expect to fall behind in farm and plan to make up for it through fights and roams.
notes.sylas-laning-wave: Do not push the wave too hard before level 6. His short range leaves him exposed to the enemy jungler when he stands in front of a pushed wave. After learning R, push the lane and join fights in other lanes or around objectives.
notes.sylas-teamfight: His role in teamfights depends on the ultimate he has stolen. Secure an ultimate with R before the fight starts. When diving in with E, enter second, after an ally has engaged. In a chaotic fight, use W to heal as soon as you have taken damage.
notes.sylas-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is enough to undo your trades, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Build Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.sylas-situational-cc: Against a team that locks you down before you can get close, buy Quicksilver Sash early.
notes.vs-sylas-ult: Sylas uses R to copy an enemy's ultimate. If you have a fight-turning ultimate, use it before Sylas uses R. If you have a fight-turning ultimate, keep your distance so Sylas cannot get in range to steal it.
notes.vs-sylas-early: Before level 6, Sylas is weak because of his short range and tight mana supply. Take lane control and push before level 6 to disrupt Sylas's farming.
notes.vs-sylas-w: The more health Sylas is missing, the more W heals him. If you have a way to reduce healing, use it just before Sylas lands W.
notes.vs-sylas-e: Sylas's E has two stages: a dash followed by a thrown chain. E's first dash deals no damage. If E's second chain hits you, Sylas pulls himself to you, knocks you up, and hits you with a combo. Use mobility abilities and Flash to avoid E's second chain, not its first dash.
notes.vs-sylas-q: Sylas's Q explodes after a short delay where the chains cross. Even if the first chain clips you, move out of the crossing point immediately to avoid the explosion.
notes.vs-sylas-teamfight: Sylas is fragile and most vulnerable just after diving in with E. When Sylas engages with E, crowd control and attack him before he can heal with W.
notes.syndra-combo-stun: Place Q behind the enemy, then push it with E to stun them. Only enemies hit by a Dark Sphere pushed by E are stunned. Using E without a sphere only pushes enemies away.
notes.syndra-combo-wq: Hit an enemy with a sphere or minion thrown by W to slow them. Follow a W slow immediately with Q to make your poke more likely to land.
notes.syndra-combo-burst: Place a sphere with Q, pick it up and throw it with W, push the remaining sphere with E to stun, then finish with R. R also fires spheres on the field. Place as many spheres as possible with Q before casting R to increase its damage.
notes.syndra-combo-self-peel: If an enemy gets close, place Q under yourself or where they will land, then push them away with E to create distance. Against an enemy with a gap closer, be ready to create distance with Q and E.
notes.syndra-skill-q: Q spheres remain on the field briefly after casting. Q spheres can be used by W, E, and R. If a fight is likely, place Q in advance to set up an angle, even if it deals no damage. You can cast Q while moving.
notes.syndra-skill-w: W can pick up and throw enemy minions and normal monsters as well as spheres. You can still poke with W while Q is on cooldown. If mana is tight in lane, throw minions with W to keep trading. If you do not select a target for W, it picks the nearest sphere.
notes.syndra-skill-e: E has a long cooldown. Syndra relies on E to defend herself. Against an enemy with a gap closer, save E for their engage instead of using it to poke. If the enemy has no way to close the gap, actively look for stuns with Q and E.
notes.syndra-skill-r: R fires the spheres orbiting Syndra and those on the field at one target. Place as many spheres as possible with Q before casting R. Once you have enough Splinters of Wrath, R executes targets with low health.
notes.syndra-skill-passive: Gain Splinters of Wrath by putting points into abilities and hitting champions. Each ability gains an additional effect when your splinters pass certain thresholds. Maxing one ability quickly gives you a power spike. Gaining splinters also restores mana. Keep hitting champions to gain splinters and restore mana.
notes.syndra-phase: At levels 1–2, mana costs and cooldowns make it hard for Syndra to poke often. As Q levels up, Syndra gains an advantage in lane. Learning R at level 6 gives Syndra her first chance to secure a kill. Syndra peaks in the mid to late game as she gains splinters and ability power. Syndra is vulnerable when poorly positioned.
notes.syndra-laning: Prioritize safe farming with your long range over risky poke. Place Q where the enemy will step up to last-hit to poke them. Save E for an enemy engage. Avoid fully pushing the wave and giving the enemy jungler a gank opportunity.
notes.syndra-teamfight: At the start of a teamfight, stay at the back and pressure the enemy formation with Q and W. Save E to push away enemies who engage. Use R only on a target you can reliably kill. Place Q spheres before the teams clash to strengthen R. Place Q spheres before the teams clash to set up a stun with E.
notes.syndra-situational-antiheal: Choose Morellonomicon for healing reduction against enemies who sustain through damage. Syndra relies on killing an enemy in one combo. If an enemy heals through Syndra's combo, she must wait for her cooldowns before the next one.
notes.syndra-situational-zhonya: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass sooner to survive their initial engage. Syndra has no mobility ability. If Syndra lets an enemy close the gap, one E may not be enough to escape.
notes.vs-syndra-e: E has a long cooldown. Syndra relies on E to defend herself. Syndra is most vulnerable immediately after using E. Close in immediately after Syndra uses E.
notes.vs-syndra-orb-stun: Syndra's stun comes from a Dark Sphere pushed by E. If a sphere is near you or between you and Syndra, you risk being stunned. When you see a sphere, move out of the path it will be pushed along.
notes.vs-syndra-boots: All of Syndra's abilities work by placing or throwing something without targeting an enemy directly. Buy boots early for the movement speed to dodge Syndra's abilities on foot.
notes.vs-syndra-orbs-ult: R also fires spheres on the field. R becomes more dangerous when many spheres are on the field. If several Q spheres are in an area, either engage and accept the risk of R or move elsewhere.
notes.vs-syndra-maxrank: Syndra's abilities gain additional effects when maxed. Syndra's ability effects change when they reach max rank. When an ability's visual effect changes, adjust your spacing to account for a change in its power or range.
notes.vs-syndra-dive: Syndra has no mobility ability. If your champion can close the gap, check whether Syndra's E is on cooldown before engaging.
notes.tahmkench-combo-stack: Tahm Kench’s combos start with counting An Acquired Taste stacks. Basic attacks and Q each add one An Acquired Taste stack. At three stacks, Q can stun the enemy and R can swallow them.
notes.tahmkench-combo-qr: Press R while Q is in flight to swallow a target with three stacks from range as Q hits. Against a target with two stacks, prepare the Q–R combo and look for an angle to land Q.
notes.tahmkench-combo-allin: In close combat, knock them up with W, build stacks with basic attacks, then stun with Q and use R. After W begins channeling, its landing spot stays hidden from enemies briefly. Hitting a champion with W refunds part of its cooldown and mana cost. Missing W makes both engaging and escaping difficult, so engage when you can land it.
notes.tahmkench-skill-r-ally: An ally swallowed with R cannot be targeted while inside. An ally swallowed with R gains a large shield after being spat out. Swallow an ally with R just before an enemy’s finishing ability hits them. A swallowed ally can leave on their own, so coordinate with them.
notes.tahmkench-skill-r-taxi: You can still use W while carrying an ally, and you briefly gain movement speed. Swallow an ally with R, then use W to carry them out of danger. Swallow an ally with R, then use W to carry them deep into the enemy team. Before engaging with an ally inside, check that you can spit them out where they can fight immediately.
notes.tahmkench-skill-r-enemy: While swallowing an enemy, Tahm Kench is heavily slowed and rooted in place. Use R on an enemy when your allies can kill them immediately afterward. Use R on an enemy when you are somewhere safe, such as under a turret. When swallowing an enemy is risky, save R to protect an ally.
notes.tahmkench-skill-e: E stores damage already taken as gray health, then converts it into a shield. Pressing E with no stored gray health has no effect. After taking heavy damage, use E just before the next burst hits. With several enemy champions nearby, E stores a higher share of damage as gray health. Between fights, let stored gray health restore your health instead of using E.
notes.tahmkench-skill-q: Q is Tahm Kench’s only ranged poke and healing tool. Hitting a champion with Q heals you based on your missing health. If you do not urgently need healing, save Q to stun a target with three stacks.
notes.tahmkench-skill-passive: Basic attacks deal bonus magic damage based on bonus health. Health items increase both defense and basic attack damage, leaving little reason to mix in attack items. In lane, weave in basic attacks to build stacks and deal damage.
notes.tahmkench-laning: When a target with two stacks steps forward to last-hit, stun them with Q. Follow a Q stun with a basic attack. Pressure the enemy only while your stacks remain active. Trading aggressively at close range with no stacks offers little benefit.
notes.tahmkench-laning-bait: Even below half health, Q healing and E’s stored gray health make you tougher than your health bar suggests. Hold on near your turret at low health, then counter an enemy engage with a stun and R.
notes.tahmkench-phase: At levels 1–2, you pose little threat before building stacks. At level 6, learning R lets you save allies. Tahm Kench peaks in the mid to late game, when health items increase both basic attack damage and the amount E stores. Tahm Kench struggles to end games alone at any stage, so stay with your allies.
notes.tahmkench-teamfight: In teamfights, stay beside your allied carry instead of engaging. Do not die early in a teamfight; stay alive to protect your allied carry.
notes.tahmkench-situational-mr: If the enemy team’s damage is mostly magic, fit Spectre’s Cowl between your core items. Because E stores gray health based on damage taken, magic resistance improves how effectively you store it and helps you survive longer.
notes.vs-tahmkench-stacks: After three hits from Tahm Kench’s basic attacks and Q, you are in range of both a stun and a swallow. If you have two stacks, move out of range and wait for them to expire. Tahm Kench poses little threat without stacks.
notes.vs-tahmkench-e: Some damage dealt to Tahm Kench is stored as gray health and returns as a shield or healing. Instead of trading small hits and backing off, engage when you can focus him down and kill him in one go. Grievous Wounds reduces how much stored gray health returns as healing. Buy Executioner’s Calling or Morellonomicon early, depending on your scaling.
notes.vs-tahmkench-r-ally: An enemy swallowed by Tahm Kench cannot be targeted and gains a shield after being spat out. Before using a targeted finishing ability, check whether Tahm Kench still has R. When an enemy is swallowed, keep up pressure with untargeted area abilities. When an enemy is swallowed, also look for a chance to stop Tahm Kench himself.
notes.vs-tahmkench-r-enemy: While an ally is swallowed, Tahm Kench is rooted in place and heavily slowed. If an ally is swallowed, stay together and focus Tahm Kench to interrupt the swallow.
notes.vs-tahmkench-w: When Tahm Kench dives, his landing spot is briefly hidden. When you see the dive animation, spread out so W cannot knock up several of you. Without W, Tahm Kench has trouble both engaging and escaping.
notes.vs-tahmkench-target: Focus untargeted damage on the carry Tahm Kench is protecting. When attacking the carry, account for Tahm Kench’s R giving them another chance to survive if it is available.
notes.taliyah-combo-ewq: Place E, then use W to push the enemy into it and land Q while they're stunned. If you use W before E, you can push the enemy but won't stun them.
notes.taliyah-combo-gank: If the enemy is already fleeing, aim W to push them toward your allies. Taliyah chooses the direction W pushes the enemy.
notes.taliyah-skill-q-direction: Q's shards fly in a line in the cast direction and cannot change direction midflight. Fire Q when the enemy cannot change their direction of movement. If successive Q shards hit the same target, damage drops sharply starting with the second shard.
notes.taliyah-skill-q-worked-ground: Using Q creates Worked Ground beneath Taliyah. Using Q again on Worked Ground fires one slowing boulder instead of shards. Q on Worked Ground costs almost no mana and has half the cooldown. Clear jungle monsters and minion waves with Q shards from fresh ground. Use Q's boulder from Worked Ground when chasing champions or escaping.
notes.taliyah-skill-e: E alone only slows and deals a little damage. Enemies are stunned if they dash or are pushed across E. Place E in narrow passages or entrances ahead of time to stop enemies from dashing in.
notes.taliyah-skill-w-peel: Enemies knocked up by W are briefly unable to participate in the fight. Use W to push melee champions away from your allied marksman. W has a delayed activation, so cast it ahead of time on the enemy's approach path.
notes.taliyah-skill-r-restriction: You cannot use R if you recently took damage from a champion or structure.
notes.taliyah-skill-r-wall: You can use R without riding the wall. During teamfights, use R's wall to separate the enemy frontline from their backline. Block a fleeing enemy's escape route with R's wall. You can immediately destroy a completed R wall by casting the ability again. If R's wall blocks your allies' pursuit, destroy it immediately.
notes.taliyah-skill-passive: When out of combat, moving near walls grants movement speed from Rock Surfing. Plan your jungle routes and roams along walls. Stay close to walls when crossing the river, too.
notes.taliyah-laning-jungle: If Q shards hit different monsters, each deals damage without the reduction. Early on, clear camps quickly to grow stronger instead of forcing ganks. Look for counterganks where you can predict the enemy jungler's route.
notes.taliyah-phase: At levels 1–2, mana costs are high, so conserve your abilities. Your combo becomes available at level 3, when you have Q, W, and E. Your first power spike comes at level 6, when you learn R and can move around the map to intervene. Taliyah is strongest in the mid game as she builds ability power items. Late in the game, letting an enemy engage even once can get you killed.
notes.taliyah-teamfight: In teamfights, stay back and place E on an approach path to narrow the enemy's way in. Place R's wall where grouped enemies are entering to split their formation. Place R's wall along the enemy backline's escape route.
notes.taliyah-teamfight-objective: Taliyah has an advantage in fights in tight spaces, such as the Dragon or Baron pit. In objective fights, place E in tight terrain and use R to block the entrance. Check R's cooldown before an objective fight.
notes.taliyah-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team has a champion who survives through healing, buy Morellonomicon after one core item. Taliyah's sustained damage helps keep Grievous Wounds applied after the first application.
notes.vs-taliyah-e-w: If Taliyah places E nearby, W may follow soon. If W pushes you across E's rocks, you are stunned. When E is placed, move away from the rocks. The space between the rocks and Taliyah is the most dangerous place to be pushed into them by W.
notes.vs-taliyah-q-dodge: Taliyah's Q only flies in the cast direction and cannot change direction midflight. To dodge Q, sidestep instead of moving in a straight line.
notes.vs-taliyah-dash: Before dashing at Taliyah, check whether E's rocks are on the ground. Dashing across E's rocks stuns you. If E is placed, walk in or go around the rocks to engage.
notes.vs-taliyah-squishy: Taliyah has no healing or shielding ability of her own. Taliyah is easily killed when affected by crowd control that prevents movement. Against Taliyah, spend your resources creating an opening to close in on her instead of absorbing her combo.
notes.vs-taliyah-r: Taliyah cannot use R if she recently took damage from a champion or structure. Keep dealing damage to stop Taliyah from escaping with R. If you have not damaged Taliyah yet, chase with the possibility that she may escape using R's wall in mind.
notes.vs-taliyah-roam: Taliyah can quickly reach distant fights with Rock Surfing's speed near walls and her R. If Taliyah disappears from the jungle, back off early in case she is heading to another lane.
notes.talon-combo-reliable: A reliable combo is to close in with Q, cast W, then use a basic attack to trigger Blade's End. Closing in with Q first makes it easier to land both hits of W. Start the combo with Q when you need a reliable hit.
notes.talon-combo-fast: For a fast combo, cast W, close in with Q just before it returns, then use a basic attack to trigger Blade's End. Time W's return hit with Q's landing to complete the Blade's End stacks. In the fast combo, avoid using a basic attack right before Q so the attack after Q is not delayed.
notes.talon-combo-fastest: The fastest combo is to use Q right after W's first hit, cast R during the leap, then trigger Blade's End with a basic attack on landing. Using R to engage spends the invisibility you could use to escape. Use the W-Q-R engage combo only when you are sure you can kill the target.
notes.talon-skill-passive: Blade's End builds stacks with abilities and triggers its bleed with a basic attack. A basic attack on an enemy with remaining stacks refreshes their duration. Keep the Blade's End stacks from W active by weaving in basic attacks before the next W. Keeping stacks active with basic attacks between W casts lets you trigger Blade's End from level 1.
notes.talon-skill-q: Using Q within melee range lands a critical hit without a leap. Using Q outside melee range makes Talon leap to the target. To increase Q's damage, get into melee range first with Flash or E. Killing a target with Q refunds half its cooldown. Use Q to last-hit minions for lane sustain and mana efficiency.
notes.talon-skill-q-aa: Right after a Q leap, the basic attack windup is short, so the attack comes out immediately. Q does not reset basic attack timing. If you used a basic attack right before Q, you still have to wait for the next attack afterward. When finishing with Q, the fastest order is to use Q as your last ability, then follow with a basic attack.
notes.talon-skill-w: W's return hit deals more damage than its outgoing hit. W's return hit applies a slow. Cast W from close range to land both hits. Use W as your main ability in lane. Early on, avoid overusing W so you have mana left for kill opportunities.
notes.talon-skill-e: You cannot cross the same terrain with E again for a considerable time. The restriction on crossing the same terrain again with E is especially long early on. Choose terrain for your escape in advance and save E on that terrain while roaming. E counts as a dash, so targeted tether abilities can interrupt it. You can cross terrain created by allies or enemies with E, and it has the same reuse restriction. E cannot cross terrain that blocks enemy dashes.
notes.talon-skill-r: R grants Talon invisibility. R increases Talon's movement speed. If a basic attack or Q ends R's invisibility, the blades converge on the attack target and concentrate their damage. If R's invisibility ends without a target, the blades converge on Talon's position, revealing his escape direction. Using E during R ends the invisibility early.
notes.talon-laning: Talon is a melee champion with very short range. Do not step forward first in lane. Chip away at the enemy's health with W before engaging. Close in with Q only when the enemy steps forward to last-hit. When trading, trigger Blade's End with a basic attack, then back off.
notes.talon-roam: Talon's greatest strength is roaming across terrain with E. After pushing the wave, cross jungle walls with E to create a numbers advantage in a side lane. Before moving to set up a roaming ambush, clear enemy vision with a Control Ward. When roaming, choose a route outside enemy vision.
notes.talon-phase: Talon deals high damage from levels 1–2. Push the wave quickly and look for an early kill as soon as you reach level 2 first. If the enemy reaches the next level first, do not step forward during that window. Talon's roaming and burst damage peak after he learns R. Talon's impact falls off as the game goes on. In the late game, Talon can easily die where he engaged even if he kills one backline target. When ahead, keep applying pressure to end the game.
notes.talon-teamfight: Choose your kill target before a teamfight. In teamfights, focus your abilities on one target instead of spreading them across several enemies. Engage after the enemy has used their crowd control on your allies. Save R's invisibility for a safe escape. If a frontal teamfight is difficult, flank with E and target the side of the enemy backline.
notes.talon-situational-antiheal: Against an enemy with strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items for Grievous Wounds. Blade's End deals bleed damage over time, making Grievous Wounds easy to maintain.
notes.vs-talon-armor: All of Talon's damage is physical. To reduce Talon's burst damage, buy an inexpensive armor item such as Cloth Armor early. Against Talon, prioritize armor over magic resistance or health.
notes.vs-talon-w: Talon must land both hits of W to complete his Blade's End stacks. Dodging W's return hit prevents substantial damage and the Blade's End bleed from triggering. If W's first hit lands, make leaving its return path your top priority.
notes.vs-talon-r: Talon relies heavily on R's invisibility to leave a fight. Look to counterattack after Talon has used R. Do not chase Talon too far while he has R, as he can use invisibility to evade pursuit and counterattack.
notes.vs-talon-early: Around level 2, Talon deals enough damage to get first blood in a single trade. Around level 2, stay back and farm safely behind your minions. Push the wave first so Talon does not level up before you.
notes.vs-talon-roam: Talon roams very quickly because he can cross terrain. Keep your allies informed of Talon's location. Establish vision along jungle routes to prevent Talon's ambushes. Push the lane to make Talon return to farm. Clear enemy vision with a Control Ward to gather information for a counterattack on Talon.
notes.vs-talon-late: Talon's impact falls off in the late game. In the late game, Talon can easily die where he engages even if he kills one backline target. Group up for late-game teamfights. Layer crowd control as soon as Talon engages.
notes.taric-skill-bravado: Bravado speeds up Taric's next two basic attacks after he uses an ability and makes them deal bonus damage. Bravado basic attacks reduce the cooldowns of his basic abilities. After using an ability, land two Bravado basic attacks. When backing off after a trade, use two Bravado basic attacks on minions to get E back sooner.
notes.taric-skill-bravado-armor: Bravado and E's bonus damage scale with bonus armor. Taric can deal strong damage in early melee trades.
notes.taric-skill-q: Q stores charges, and each Bravado basic attack that hits adds one charge. Q costs the same amount of mana regardless of how many charges you use. If it isn't urgent, save Q charges to heal several allies at once. Don't use a one-charge Q just to trigger Bravado.
notes.taric-skill-w-link: When an ally linked by W is nearby, Taric's abilities also activate from that ally's position. Before a teamfight, use W on an ally covering the side you won't stand on to extend your abilities' reach. Recasting W moves the link to another ally and grants a shield. When moving W to an ally in danger, account for the change in where your abilities will activate.
notes.taric-skill-e: E is a stun that activates after a short delay. Aim E ahead of time where the enemy will be when it activates. Land E as an enemy moves in to last-hit a minion. Follow an ally's immobilizing crowd control with E.
notes.taric-combo-w-e: E also activates from the position of the ally linked by W. Stand slightly apart from your linked ally to reduce the space enemies can dodge through between the two E beams. Use W on an ally about to dash in, then start the fight by activating E from their position.
notes.taric-skill-r: After a significant delay, R makes nearby allies immune to damage. Use R just before a fight or right after E, anticipating where things will stand a few seconds later. R's damage immunity does not prevent crowd control.
notes.taric-combo-engage: Use W on an ally about to engage, then use R, E, two Bravado basic attacks, and Q in that order. Time R's activation to coincide with the peak of the trade following E's stun.
notes.taric-laning: As a melee champion, Taric struggles to reach enemies without E. Use E to start a trade, not to poke. Against a ranged support, don't move forward if you have no opening to land E.
notes.taric-laning-cs: When using up Bravado basic attacks, avoid minions that are about to be last-hit. Use Bravado basic attacks on healthy minions or targets the turret has already hit.
notes.taric-roaming: Taric's movement speed is relatively high among supports, making it easier for him to join fights and roam. When ganking, account for E's delay and aim ahead in the enemy's escape direction. Follow your jungler's engage ability with E. Don't rush toward enemies in areas without vision.
notes.taric-teamfight: If you're at the front in a teamfight, use W on a backline damage dealer. If you need to stay back in a teamfight, use W on an ally who is engaging. Engage when E is ready and you can account for R's activation delay.
notes.taric-phase: Taric becomes strong in melee trades at levels 2–3, when he has both E and Q. Taric is strong in early head-to-head fights because Bravado's damage scales with armor. At level 6, R lets Taric stop enemy dives and explosive engages. In the mid to late game, as he builds armor items, Taric uses that armor both to frontline and to deal damage.
notes.taric-situational-armor: If the enemy's physical damage is high, build Frozen Heart or Randuin's Omen to increase both survivability and Bravado and E damage.
notes.vs-taric-r: Don't pour damage into enemies after Taric's R makes them immune to damage.
notes.vs-taric-r-cc: Taric's R damage immunity does not prevent crowd control. Use crowd control to hold enemies in place while their damage immunity wears down. While they are immune to damage, manage your positioning and crowd control, then attack again as soon as it ends.
notes.vs-taric-bravado: Taric reduces his ability cooldowns with Bravado basic attacks. Kite Taric or knock him away with an airborne effect so he cannot reach a target to basic attack. Manage the wave to keep Taric away from minions and slow down his ability rotation.
notes.vs-taric-e: Taric's E activates after a delay and has a clear warning. When Taric's E is telegraphed, move sideways to dodge it. Bait out Taric's E, then poke and trade from range.
notes.vs-taric-w: Taric's abilities also activate from the position of the ally linked by W. Treat the area around an enemy linked by W as a place where E may activate. If an enemy linked by W dashes in, be ready for E to activate from their position.
notes.vs-taric-early: Taric's Bravado damage is strong from the early game and grows with armor.
notes.teemo-combo-trade: Emerge from brush stealth with a surprise auto attack, follow with Q and one or two autos, then disengage with W. The attack speed boost from breaking stealth makes trades started from brush stronger than those started by walking up. E's poison keeps dealing damage after a single auto, so back off instead of staying close.
notes.teemo-combo-allin: Use Q to block retaliatory autos, apply E's poison with an auto, then throw R into the enemy's retreat path to finish them off. Throw R where you predict the enemy will flee, rather than at their feet.
notes.teemo-skill-passive: Stand still briefly without taking any action to enter stealth with P. Inside brush, P's stealth persists even while moving. Breaking P's stealth grants attack speed. Set up an ambush in brush ahead of time to use the attack speed gained from breaking stealth.
notes.teemo-skill-q: Q's blind only disables basic attacks and does not block ability damage. Use Q to poke enemies who deal damage mainly through abilities. Time Q for the moment the enemy starts their auto attack animation.
notes.teemo-skill-q-monster: Q's blind lasts longer on minions and jungle monsters than on champions. When allies are clearing jungle camps or fighting large monsters, prioritize considering Q on the monster.
notes.teemo-skill-w: W's passive movement speed bonus stops when a champion or turret hits you. W's active movement speed bonus persists even while taking hits. Use W's active to move during fights. Use W to get a favorable fighting angle as well as to escape.
notes.teemo-skill-e: E adds poison to autos, dealing damage over time. Use E's damage over time to repeatedly trade with one auto before backing off. Disengage immediately if a poisoned opponent approaches to retaliate.
notes.teemo-skill-r-bounce: Throw R onto an existing mushroom to make it bounce and land farther away. Use mushroom bounces to place R over walls or in areas without vision without exposing yourself. R uses a charge system. If there is no urgency, save R charges to block a path with several mushrooms at once.
notes.teemo-skill-r-place: Mushrooms placed with R last a long time. R's mushrooms reveal enemies who step on them. Place R around objectives and along enemy jungle routes to provide vision. Use R to clear the wave when you need to leave a side lane and rotate. Avoid spending all your R charges on farming so you have charges left to place where fights will happen.
notes.teemo-laning: Against melee opponents, use your range and E's poison to repeatedly land one auto and back off. In lane, use Q when the enemy starts a retaliatory auto. Teemo is very vulnerable to ganks. After pushing the lane, place R in the river and brush before resuming trades.
notes.teemo-phase: From level 3 onward, Teemo enters his strongest laning phase against melee opponents. Even from level 3 onward, Teemo remains vulnerable in lane to poke opponents with longer range. From the mid game onward, Teemo excels at side lane play and map control through mushrooms. Teemo struggles to serve as a frontline in late-game head-on teamfights. Teemo racks up high damage per minute through damage over time and mushroom damage.
notes.teemo-teamfight: Place R in advance along enemy entry and retreat paths where a teamfight will happen. Once a teamfight starts, attack from the back with autos to apply E's poison. If you expect an objective fight, spend all your R charges placing mushrooms around the area before it starts.
notes.teemo-situational-zhonya: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier to survive while mushrooms and poison deal damage. Teemo has no mobility ability, making it hard for him to survive once caught. Mushrooms already placed and poison already applied keep dealing damage while you survive with Zhonya's Hourglass.
notes.vs-teemo-q: Teemo's Q only blocks basic attacks and does not prevent ability use. When blinded by Q, deal damage with abilities instead of autos or retreat until the blind ends. Auto attack-focused champions should trade right after Teemo uses Q.
notes.vs-teemo-e: Teemo's E keeps dealing poison damage even if you back off after taking a single auto. Stay outside Teemo's auto attack range until you are ready to fully commit. Once you decide to engage Teemo, close the distance in one go and commit to the fight.
notes.vs-teemo-r: Use Oracle Lens to clear mushrooms from key routes. Move as though there are mushrooms in front of objectives and in narrow passages. When retreating, be wary of mushrooms and avoid running through familiar shortcuts. Teemo's mushrooms persist for a long time, even those placed long ago.
notes.vs-teemo-mobility: Teemo relies on W to escape. Push the lane, then engage Teemo with your jungler. Build an early lead to limit Teemo's time to place mushrooms.
notes.vs-teemo-brush: Teemo remains stealthed even while moving within brush. Teemo gains attack speed the moment his stealth breaks, giving him an edge at the start of trades. Go around unwarded brush instead of carelessly walking past it. Wait for Teemo to leave the brush, then retaliate.
notes.thresh-skill-passive: Collecting souls permanently increases armor. Collecting souls permanently increases ability power. You can collect souls from units you did not kill yourself. Collected souls strengthen W's shield. Collected souls increase E's damage.
notes.thresh-skill-passive-safety: Stepping forward to collect souls leaves you vulnerable to attacks. Use W's lantern to collect souls within the enemy's range.
notes.thresh-skill-q: Q has a long windup, making it easy for enemies to see and dodge in open areas. Use Q from brush or angles outside enemy vision. Use Q when an enemy is locked into a last-hit animation or an ability cast. Landing Q grants true sight of the target. Landing Q reduces its cooldown.
notes.thresh-skill-q-recast: Recasting Q sends Thresh flying toward the enemy it hit. Do not recast Q where allies cannot follow up. Once your allies' engage is confirmed, recast Q to close in, then use E followed by R.
notes.thresh-skill-w: An ally must click the lantern themselves to travel with W. Coordinate with allies beforehand on how to use W's lantern. Use W to bring your allied jungler into lane from across a wall. W shields Thresh and the first ally to take the lantern. Use W just before enemy burst damage lands.
notes.thresh-skill-e: E pushes or pulls enemies depending on the direction you sweep. Aim E in opposite directions when engaging and when protecting allies. From behind your allied carry, sweep E outward to peel off an assassin on them.
notes.thresh-skill-e-passive: E's passive grows stronger the longer you wait after your last basic attack. Save your basic attacks until you trade, then use them one at a time. In lane, combine one empowered basic attack with E to harass.
notes.thresh-combo-hook-first: After landing Q, basic attack, pull the enemy toward your allies with E, then use R to block their escape if needed. Chain E as Q's stun ends to keep the enemy immobilized.
notes.thresh-combo-flay-first: Q and E can be chained in either order. Against an enemy already close to you, pull them with E first, then use Q at close range. Q is easier to land immediately after E disrupts an enemy's movement.
notes.thresh-combo-dive: After landing Q, recast it to engage, block the path behind the enemy with R, then push them toward your allies with E. Only recast Q to engage deep when you can immediately bring an ally in with W.
notes.thresh-phase-early: Thresh can initiate in lane and create kill opportunities with Q as early as levels 1–2. Early on, focus on forcing enemies out of lane rather than getting kills. Focus on collecting souls in the early game.
notes.thresh-phase-scaling: Thresh's late-game durability depends on how many souls he has collected. Keep collecting souls after laning by passing through fight locations and around jungle camps.
notes.thresh-laning: Secure brush first to create Q angles hidden from the enemy. If the enemy pressures the brush, back off and collect souls. If enemies pressure the brush, switch to protecting your allied carry's CS.
notes.thresh-teamfight: Choose between engaging and protecting allies based on the teamfight setup. Hold Q when your allies are fighting from the back. When your allies are fighting from the back, use E to peel enemies off your carry. When your allied engage champion goes in first, target an enemy in the backline with Q.
notes.thresh-teamfight-r-escape: When allies are being chased, place R's walls across the pursuit route to slow enemies. When using R to retreat, angle its walls differently than when trapping enemies.
notes.thresh-situational-mikael: Against a composition that locks down your carry with immobilizing effects, include Mikael's Blessing in your core build to remove them. W and E cannot remove immobilizing effects already applied to allies.
notes.thresh-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prolongs fights, buy Oblivion Orb first for healing reduction. Thresh's abilities have ability power ratios, so he can make use of Oblivion Orb's ability power.
notes.vs-thresh-q: Thresh's Q has a long windup. Move sideways immediately when you see Thresh raise his scythe during Q's windup. When facing Thresh, change direction from side to side to dodge Q. When stepping forward to last-hit, change direction once more in anticipation of Q.
notes.vs-thresh-souls: Much of Thresh's armor and damage depends on collecting souls. Trade with Thresh when he steps forward to collect souls.
notes.vs-thresh-lantern: Thresh's W is used to rescue allies in danger or bring in reinforcements. When Thresh throws W, immediately use a finishing ability or disengage.
notes.vs-thresh-e: Thresh's E pushes or pulls enemies in the direction he sweeps. Avoid the line connecting Thresh and his allies so E cannot pull you in.
notes.vs-thresh-mobility: Thresh has limited ways to escape a fight on his own. Close the gap and engage right after Thresh uses Q.
notes.thresh-skill-r: Only enemies who pass through an R wall take damage. Only enemies who pass through an R wall are heavily slowed. Once one R wall collapses, the remaining walls deal no damage. Once one R wall collapses, the slow duration of the remaining walls is halved. Place R to cover both the enemy's escape route and the direction their reinforcements will come from.
notes.vs-thresh-r: Once one R wall breaks, the remaining walls deal no damage. Once one R wall breaks, the slow duration of the remaining walls is halved. If trapped in R, immediately decide which way to escape. The tankiest ally deliberately breaks through one R wall.
notes.tristana-combo-e-reset: E Explosive Charge resets Tristana's basic attack animation. Use E right after a basic attack lands, then follow with another basic attack. Pressing E during a basic attack's windup cancels that attack.
notes.tristana-combo-burst: Apply E, build stacks with basic attacks, use Q to increase attack speed, then detonate the final stack with W. If you jump in, detonate the bomb, and get a takedown, W resets.
notes.tristana-combo-jump-r: Jump over an enemy with W, then use R to knock them toward an ally or allied turret. Only use the W jump-over combo when the enemy cannot immediately retaliate. After jumping over the enemy with W, you remain on their side. You can use R while airborne during W to disengage.
notes.tristana-skill-w-dash: W Rocket Jump counts as a dash. Traps at your W landing spot will trigger. Enemy crowd control can interrupt W while you are airborne. Use W to escape area-of-effect skillshots.
notes.tristana-skill-w-reset: Getting a takedown resets W. Detonating E on a champion at maximum stacks resets W. Before jumping in with W, check whether you can trigger a reset. Manage your mana so you can still use W.
notes.tristana-skill-q: Q takes effect starting with the wait before your next basic attack. Activate Q just before a basic attack. Early on, when you lack attack damage, save Q for fights. Activate Q to take down a turret quickly.
notes.tristana-skill-e-passive: E's passive deals area damage when you kill an enemy with a basic attack. Kill a low-health minion near an enemy champion to hit them with E's damage. When minions are grouped, kill the weakest one first.
notes.tristana-skill-e-charge: If you apply E to a champion, build it to maximum stacks. Do not use E if the enemy is about to escape. Apply E at the start of a fight so you have time to build stacks. Keep attacking the target with E to increase its explosion damage.
notes.tristana-skill-passive-range: As Tristana levels up, P Draw a Bead increases her basic attack and ability range. In late-game teamfights, use the extra range to attack from afar.
notes.tristana-phase: Tristana is weak early because her cooldowns are long and her damage is low. Early on, farm with E's passive and play safely. Her burst remains underwhelming through the mid game until she has attack damage items. Her damage is strong with a completed build, so longer games favor her.
notes.tristana-laning-wave: E's passive naturally pushes the lane. Consciously choose whether to push the lane to pressure the turret and vision or avoid hitting minions with E damage to let the lane push toward you.
notes.tristana-laning-siege: If the enemy is absent from lane, push immediately to pressure the turret. Use Q and E together to damage a turret quickly. Do not start pressuring a turret while W is on cooldown.
notes.tristana-teamfight: In teamfights, use your range advantage to basic attack from the back. Save W to disengage in teamfights. Only jump in with W when the enemy formation has broken and a takedown is certain. After jumping in, use the reset W to reach the next target.
notes.tristana-teamfight-r: Use R to knock away an enemy who jumps on an ally. Use R to interrupt a dangerous cast. R can knock several grouped enemies over a wall. When needed, use R to knock an enemy toward your team.
notes.vs-tristana-early: Push the lane toward Tristana's turret to make it harder for her to last-hit with E's passive.
notes.vs-tristana-e-splash: Do not stand close to allied minions, so you avoid Tristana's E area damage.
notes.vs-tristana-w-cc: Interrupt Tristana with crowd control while she is airborne during W. If Tristana has both W and R ready, engage only when you have crowd control that can hold her.
notes.vs-tristana-w-reset: If an ally falls and your team is losing a teamfight, retreat immediately. When retreating, do not leave a squishy ally in front.
notes.vs-tristana-late: Aim to end the game before Tristana completes her build. Ambush Tristana when she pushes the lane and moves up to pressure the turret. When Tristana disappears from vision, first check whether she might be pushing a turret elsewhere.
notes.trundle-combo-basic: For a basic trade, cast W under the enemy, then auto attack, use a Q empowered auto attack, and auto attack again.
notes.trundle-combo-e-cut: When chasing, use W to catch up, place E ahead of the enemy's path, then use Q on them after the pillar knocks them back. When disengaging, place E between yourself and the pursuer.
notes.trundle-combo-r: Use R right after starting a fight, while the enemy still cannot escape. When engaging, cast W, use R, block the escape route with E, then land a Q empowered auto attack.
notes.trundle-skill-q: Q empowers your next auto attack and reduces the target's attack damage. Open with Q when trading against an enemy who deals physical damage. Do not use Q on a minion before a trade.
notes.trundle-skill-w: In W's area, your attack speed, movement speed, and healing received increase. Cast W where you expect the fight to happen. When engaging with allies, place W around where they will stand.
notes.trundle-skill-e: E creates impassable terrain and pushes enemies directly on top of the pillar away. Place E in a narrow path or beside a wall to block passage. Use E to draw out a terrain crossing ability from an enemy who has one.
notes.trundle-skill-e-gank: If you are in a position to be ganked, place E on the jungler's approach to delay their entry. When your jungler comes to gank, place E on the enemy's escape route. In lane, save E to respond to ganks.
notes.trundle-skill-r: R deals damage based on the target's maximum health and steals armor and magic resistance. Use R on the tankiest enemy.
notes.trundle-skill-passive: When an enemy unit dies nearby, P heals you based on that unit's maximum health. When you are low on health, decide whether to clear the wave to heal.
notes.trundle-laning: As the enemy steps forward to last hit, close in with W and use Q. Using E in a trade quickly drains mana. In lane, save E for ganks.
notes.trundle-laning-wave: Trundle has no area damage ability to push the lane himself, so waves naturally stack up. Keep the wave in the middle and apply pressure from a distance where you can close in on the enemy at any time. Only push the lane and recall when the enemy leaves lane or backs off with low health.
notes.trundle-teamfight: Trundle has no dash. In teamfights, place W in front of your team's formation, split the enemy formation with E, then take down the separated side first. Once the fight has started, use R on the enemy frontline.
notes.trundle-phase: Trundle is strong from the start of lane. Trundle is strong in one on one fights after reaching level 6 and getting R. Trundle is strong in midgame objective fights when his core items come in. In the late game, shift to holding one enemy in the side lane.
notes.trundle-situational-antiheal: If the enemy sustains through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items to keep Grievous Wounds applied with auto attacks.
notes.vs-trundle-w: Do not fight Trundle inside his W area. Back out of W's area and reengage after it expires.
notes.vs-trundle-e: Fight Trundle in open terrain, away from the river and jungle entrances. When Trundle places E, move sideways immediately before its slow makes escape difficult.
notes.vs-trundle-q: Trundle's Q raises his attack damage and lowers the target's attack damage. If you fight with physical damage, back off right after Q hits you and reengage when its effect ends.
notes.vs-trundle-r: The more health and defensive stats a champion has, the worse they fare against Trundle's R. Frontliners should not face Trundle alone. While Trundle's R is active, attack another target or create distance.
notes.vs-trundle-sustain: Trundle heals whenever an enemy unit dies nearby. If you have lowered Trundle's health, capitalize on it immediately or push the lane to force him to recall.
notes.vs-trundle-duel: Trundle is very strong in one on one fights after getting R. Do not face Trundle alone in a side lane. Against Trundle, who lacks area damage, steer the game toward five on five fights at objectives.
notes.tryndamere-combo-allin: When going all in, use W to lower the enemy's attack damage, then close in with E. Once you're close, use W to slow the enemy when they turn their back and start fleeing.
notes.tryndamere-combo-e-reset: Each critical strike reduces E's cooldown, and critical strikes against champions reduce it further. If you used E to engage, keep landing basic attacks to get E back for your escape. Make sure you have enough Fury before engaging with E. If your critical strike chance is low, using E to engage can leave you trapped without E to escape.
notes.tryndamere-combo-r-escape: R can be activated even while under crowd control. When death is certain, activate R, then escape with E and Flash before it expires. When death is certain, activate R, then heal with Q to keep fighting. Plan your escape route first so your health isn't depleted when R ends.
notes.tryndamere-skill-passive: Fury drains after you've been out of combat for a while. Hit minions or jungle monsters to build Fury just before a fight.
notes.tryndamere-skill-q-timing: Q's passive increases attack damage based on missing health. If you can survive, delay Q's heal to keep the attack damage gained from missing health. Q's healing scales with your remaining Fury. Use Q before your Fury drains.
notes.tryndamere-skill-w: W only slows enemies whose backs are turned to Tryndamere. When chasing, use W as the enemy starts to flee. When fighting face to face, use W's attack damage reduction to weaken the enemy's basic attacks.
notes.tryndamere-skill-e-wave: E cuts through every enemy in its path. Using E through a minion wave builds Fury multiple times at once. Just before a fight, use E to engage through the wave and build Fury.
notes.tryndamere-skill-r-bait: Hold R until just before you die instead of activating it early. After making the enemy use their abilities and Flash, survive with R and look to turn the fight. If you activate R early, the enemy can back away and wait out its duration.
notes.tryndamere-phase: Tryndamere has no resource cost, so he can keep using abilities from level 1. Early on, he has no critical strike chance, so his trades are weak. Learning R at level 6 is his first turning point. His one on one fights become stronger from mid game as he builds critical strike items. If your team lacks damage in late game teamfights, create value by split pushing.
notes.tryndamere-laning-farm: Tryndamere ranks among the best in CS and turret plates at 14 minutes. Tryndamere's advantages come from staying in lane and pressuring turrets. Clear waves quickly with E and basic attacks. Attack the turret whenever the enemy cannot stay in lane.
notes.tryndamere-laning-trade: Against ranged opponents, wait until they enter E range. If a ranged opponent stays outside E range, take some damage to secure CS. Against melee opponents, build Fury, then use W to lower their attack damage before going in.
notes.tryndamere-splitpush: With R available, you can survive even if two enemies come for you in a side lane. When an objective is coming up, push the opposite side lane to draw enemy players away. Without R available, you are at high risk of dying in a side lane.
notes.tryndamere-teamfight: In teamfights, approach from the side or behind and target the enemy ranged carry. Enter the teamfight, draw focused attacks, then activate R just before dying and take out the carry. Engage as soon as the enemy uses its immobilizing crowd control on your front line.
notes.tryndamere-situational-armorpen: If enemy armor reduces your basic attack damage, buy Last Whisper or Lord Dominik's Regards for armor penetration. If the enemy builds armor, move up your armor penetration purchase after completing one core item.
notes.vs-tryndamere-r: While Tryndamere's R is active, he cannot die until it expires. When Tryndamere activates R, stall with immobilizing crowd control or create distance. Tryndamere can use R even while under crowd control.
notes.vs-tryndamere-early: Early on, deny Tryndamere last hits to reduce his Fury and Q healing. If Tryndamere builds Fury by hitting minions, create distance before he closes in.
notes.vs-tryndamere-w: W only slows enemies whose backs are turned to Tryndamere. When retreating, walk backward while facing Tryndamere to avoid W's slow. W reduces attack damage regardless of which way the enemy is facing. Do not take a basic attack fight right after W hits you.
notes.vs-tryndamere-armor: Most of Tryndamere's damage is physical and relies on critical strikes. Building armor can greatly change how a duel with Tryndamere plays out. Thornmail exploits Tryndamere's reliance on basic attacks. If you build no armor at all, you will lose to Tryndamere regardless of the item difference.
notes.vs-tryndamere-splitpush: If Tryndamere has R available, sending one person to stop him in a side lane can easily cost you that player. Check Tryndamere's R cooldown before going to take him down. If Tryndamere has R available, trade for an objective or send more players to stop him.
notes.vs-tryndamere-e: To take down Tryndamere, draw him into terrain without minions. Land immobilizing crowd control right after Tryndamere uses E.
notes.tf-combo-pick: For the basic combo, lock in a gold card, move into auto-attack range, stun the target, then use Q and an auto attack. A locked-in card stays ready until your next auto attack. Pick a gold card from a safe position before the fight starts.
notes.tf-combo-ult: When roaming, use R to gain vision, lock in a gold card, then use R to move. Stun with an auto attack as soon as you land, then use Q. Pick a gold card before using R to move.
notes.tf-skill-w-cards: W cycles through blue, red, then gold cards. Use a blue card to restore mana while holding the lane. Use a red card to damage and slow nearby targets when clearing waves or chasing. Use a gold card to stun when starting a fight. Count the card order to lock in the color you want quickly.
notes.tf-skill-w-hold: If you hold a gold card, opponents can see it and back away early. Use a gold card as soon as you lock it in and get close, or pick it outside enemy vision.
notes.tf-skill-q: Q's three cards spread in a fan, and only one can hit each target. To hit a champion behind the wave, angle Q around the side of the wave.
notes.tf-skill-e: E is a passive that increases attack speed and periodically adds damage to auto attacks. After pushing the lane, attack the turret briefly to make use of E's turret damage.
notes.tf-skill-r-vision: R grants vision across the entire map even if you do not move. Even without a good place to move, use R to locate the enemy jungler and mid laner and tell your team.
notes.tf-skill-r-cancel: The teleport on R's second cast is canceled if you are hit by an interrupting effect. Use R to move from a position outside enemy vision.
notes.tf-phase: Avoid direct fights before level 6. Twisted Fate's first strong point comes at level 6, when he learns R. After level 6, push the lane and move to other lanes to build an advantage. In the late game, add damage from the back line and keep moving as you fight.
notes.tf-laning: In lane, focus on pushing the wave before looking for kills. Clear the back-line minions with Q to push the lane, then roam or establish vision. While your opponent clears the pushed wave, create a numbers advantage in another lane.
notes.tf-laning-poke: Against melee opponents, keep poking from beyond Q range. Do not stand in front of a melee opponent when you have no gold card.
notes.tf-teamfight: In teamfights, position at the very back and deal damage with Q. Stun enemies who jump onto your allies with a gold card. When enemies group up, hold your position and look for an angle to land Q.
notes.tf-situational-cc: Prepare Quicksilver Sash against teams with a lot of crowd control that can interrupt R's teleport.
notes.tf-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing keeps undoing your poke damage, reduce it with Morellonomicon. Buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.vs-tf-card: If Twisted Fate has locked in a gold card, stay out of his auto-attack range. You can approach more safely when he is holding a blue or red card.
notes.vs-tf-ult: After level 6, watch for an R roam if Twisted Fate disappears from lane or pushes it quickly. Tell your team immediately when Twisted Fate activates R. When Twisted Fate activates R, retreat under the turret in any lane at risk.
notes.vs-tf-squishy: If you have a dash, close in right after Twisted Fate uses his gold card.
notes.vs-tf-q: Only one card from Twisted Fate's Q can hit a single target. Stand behind minions to reduce Q poke damage.
notes.vs-tf-cancel: Twisted Fate's R teleport is canceled by interrupting effects. If you see Twisted Fate activate R and he is in range, interrupt his teleport with crowd control. If you can predict where R will land, secure vision there in advance and wait.
notes.twitch-combo-burst: Use Q to approach from the side, stack Deadly Venom with W and basic attacks, then finish with E. Throw W at the feet of an approaching enemy. Do not use E when Deadly Venom has few stacks.
notes.twitch-combo-r: Activating R alone does not break camouflage. Your first basic attack during camouflage reveals you. Position with Q, activate R, then start attacking from an angle that lets your attacks pierce enemies.
