notes.twitch-combo-e-finish: E does not target an enemy, so it hits enemies within range even if they leave vision. If an enemy you are chasing with basic attacks is about to escape, finish them with E. Save E during a trade if you have too few Deadly Venom stacks.
notes.twitch-skill-passive: Deadly Venom deals true damage and gains a stack each time a basic attack hits. Deadly Venom stacks disappear after a while. Deadly Venom's true damage is unaffected by enemy armor. Q's cooldown resets when an enemy champion affected by Deadly Venom dies. Check whether you can use Q again right after a kill.
notes.twitch-skill-q: Q grants camouflage and increased movement speed. Q grants more movement speed near enemies who cannot see you. An enemy who gets very close reveals you during camouflage. Use brush and indirect paths when approaching with Q. Start the fight after camouflage ends, while your attack speed is increased.
notes.twitch-skill-w: W has longer range than basic attacks. Enemies inside W's poison cloud keep gaining Deadly Venom stacks. Throw W ahead of the enemy's path. Slow the enemy with W, stack Deadly Venom, then finish with E.
notes.twitch-skill-e: E deals damage per stack to every nearby enemy affected by Deadly Venom. If several enemies have Deadly Venom stacks, finish them together with E. Max E first. Build Deadly Venom stacks with basic attacks and W, then use E last.
notes.twitch-skill-r: R increases basic attack range and makes attacks pierce enemies. Before activating R, move to a position where the enemies line up. R basic attacks deal slightly less damage each time they pierce an enemy. R's piercing damage has a minimum, so targets farther back still take damage.
notes.twitch-laning: Twitch is weak in basic attack trades, but can threaten a kill with E after stacking Deadly Venom. Twitch builds a lane advantage through kill opportunities rather than farming. In lane, gradually chip away at the enemy's health with Deadly Venom. Wait for the enemy to enter E range.
notes.twitch-laning-roam: Use Q to hide in brush or by the river and get behind the enemy. When Twitch disappears from vision, enemies may back off, giving him control of the wave. Q's camouflage lasts long enough to reach another lane. Tell your teammates when you leave lane.
notes.twitch-phase: Twitch is weakest at levels 1 and 2. As E levels up, its damage per Deadly Venom stack increases, creating kill opportunities. Twitch is strong in the mid to late game once he has attack speed and critical strike. Look for early kills, but do not overextend and die.
notes.twitch-teamfight: Do not stand at the front in teamfights. Use Q to reach the flank or backline, activate R, then fire basic attacks through grouped enemies. Reveal yourself after the enemy has used their engage abilities on your frontline. When an enemy dies and Q resets, reposition.
notes.twitch-situational-antiheal: Deadly Venom's damage over time is easily offset by enemy healing. If enemy healing offsets Deadly Venom's damage, buy Executioner's Calling after one core item.
notes.twitch-situational-qss: Consider Mercurial Scimitar if the enemy has persistent crowd control that restricts your movement. If your movement is restricted while attacking with R, it is hard to use your range advantage.
notes.vs-twitch-ward: Use a Control Ward to reveal Twitch's camouflage. Camouflaged Twitch is also revealed if you get very close to him. Go around brush or narrow paths without vision, or reveal them first. Tell other lanes when Twitch disappears from lane.
notes.vs-twitch-e: If you have taken several basic attacks, E can kill you even with around half your health left. Decide when to retreat based on how many basic attacks you have taken, rather than your remaining health. E does not target an enemy, so hiding in brush will not prevent it from hitting you. Move farther away from Twitch to avoid E.
notes.vs-twitch-poison: Building armor does not reduce Deadly Venom's true damage. A spell shield does not block Deadly Venom's damage over time itself. A spell shield only blocks effects triggered through Deadly Venom. Take fewer basic attacks from Twitch to limit Deadly Venom.
notes.vs-twitch-fragile: Attack Twitch when his camouflage ends or while he positions with R active. Focus your team's attacks on Twitch at the same time.
notes.vs-twitch-r-line: With R active, Twitch's basic attacks pierce enemies in front and hit damage dealers behind them. Spread out sideways relative to the direction Twitch is firing with R. Twitch's range increases during R, so he can hit you from distances that are normally safe.
notes.vs-twitch-w: W's poison cloud slows enemies and applies Deadly Venom stacks. Leave W's poison cloud immediately if it lands beneath you. The longer you stay in W's poison cloud, the more Deadly Venom stacks you gain and the greater the risk of E finishing you.
notes.udyr-combo-rotation: After activating a stance, use two empowered basic attacks, then switch to the next stance. The stance effect applies to the next two basic attacks. The next two basic attacks after using an ability gain attack speed.
notes.udyr-combo-awaken: To Awaken a stance, press its key again while it is on cooldown. Awakening resets that stance’s cooldown and adds an ultimate effect. You can use Awakening only once per fight, so choose which stance to Awaken before engaging.
notes.udyr-combo-engage: Approach with E, stun with the first basic attack, land two Q empowered basic attacks, then withstand damage with W. E’s stun applies only to the first attack against each target after activating the stance. Switch to Q right after stunning with E to deal damage.
notes.udyr-skill-e: Awakened E briefly blocks immobilizing and disrupting effects and ignores unit collision. Use Awakened E when unavoidable crowd control is coming. E stance’s basic attack is not canceled by knockbacks or pulls.
notes.udyr-skill-w-shield: The W shield is depleted after defensive stats reduce the damage. Increasing armor and magic resistance lets the W shield absorb more actual damage.
notes.udyr-skill-w-timing: Activate the W shield just before a large hit lands. If you need to withstand damage over time, Awaken W for healing over time.
notes.udyr-skill-q: Q empowered basic attacks deal damage based on maximum health to high-health enemies and objectives. Q’s temporary range increase lets you hit melee opponents slightly earlier. Use Q as your main stance in 1v1s and when clearing camps. Alternate Q and W while jungling to reduce health loss.
notes.udyr-skill-r: R’s storm stance deals area damage over time and slows nearby enemies. Use R in fights where several players are grouped together. Use Q over R in 1v1s. Basic attack a fleeing target before Awakening R so the storm follows them.
notes.udyr-jungle-route: Udyr moves quickly between camps thanks to his high movement speed and E’s speed boost. Path deep into the enemy jungle, alternating between camps and lane ganks. Udyr sustains his health by switching stances, letting him jungle for a long time without recalling.
notes.udyr-ganking: Udyr’s only guaranteed crowd control is his E stun, and he has no ranged way to engage. Start ganks from brush or behind terrain, or go in after an ally’s crowd control. Look for a gank from behind when the enemy is pushing the lane. If Udyr approaches head-on, a single enemy mobility ability can easily foil his gank.
notes.udyr-phase: Udyr puts levels into one ability, making his early camp clears and 1v1s strong. Udyr is strongest in the early and mid game, when jungle pressure and objective fights are frequent. Late in the game, Udyr’s lack of range and area damage pushes him toward a frontline role. Secure your lead through early and mid-game objectives and control of the enemy jungle.
notes.udyr-teamfight: Engage in teamfights when Awakened E can get you past the enemy’s crowd control that stops engages. If you cannot get past that crowd control, stay beside your frontline, keep dealing R damage, and meet the enemy’s engage. Once you reach the enemy, withstand damage with W and body-block the damage dealers’ path.
notes.udyr-situational-armor: Buy Plated Steelcaps early if the enemy’s physical damage is strong. Building armor first greatly increases your effective durability alongside the W shield.
notes.udyr-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing could turn a duel around, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item. Udyr stays close and keeps basic attacking, so he can easily maintain Grievous Wounds.
notes.vs-udyr-e-stun: E’s stun triggers only on the first attack against each target after activating the stance and cannot stun the same target again for a while. After taking one E stun, counterattack or disengage. Udyr’s stun is ready immediately after he activates E stance again.
notes.vs-udyr-w: Pressure Udyr when his W shield breaks to force him to switch stances. After breaking the W shield, give Udyr no time to heal.
notes.vs-udyr-tracking: Place vision at key routes and jungle entrances to track Udyr’s path. Do not step forward in lane while Udyr is out of sight.
notes.vs-udyr-tank: Udyr becomes very durable when he builds defensive items and adds his W shield. Against a durable Udyr, take out his vulnerable teammates behind him first, then use your numbers advantage to kill him.
notes.vs-udyr-mobility: Udyr’s high movement speed and E’s speed boost make him hard to outrun on foot. Save a mobility ability or immobilizing crowd control when facing Udyr. Apply immobilizing crowd control after Awakened E ends.
notes.vs-udyr-range: Udyr must get close to enemies to deal damage. Ranged champions should wear Udyr down before he approaches. When harassing Udyr, save a way to disengage if he gets close.
notes.urgot-combo-basic: In basic trades, weave in basic attacks while W is active. Both basic attacks and W shots trigger leg cannons. In trades, stay close to your opponent and keep firing with W active.
notes.urgot-combo-legs: There is one cannon on each of Urgot's six legs, and each has its own cooldown. If the cannon facing the target is on cooldown, that shot deals no cannon damage. Circle your opponent to point legs that can still fire toward them.
notes.urgot-combo-engage: Slow your opponent with Q, then dash in with E to stun and throw them before dealing damage with W and basic attacks. E stops at the first champion it hits and cannot cross terrain. Slow your opponent with Q first to land E. An opponent hit by E is thrown behind Urgot. To throw an opponent toward your allies, face away from your allies when using E.
notes.urgot-combo-r: Land R, lower the target's health with Q, W, and basic attacks, then recast R to execute them. R's slow grows stronger the more health the target has lost. If the target falls below the execution threshold, R triggers automatically when its duration ends, so there is no need to rush the recast.
notes.urgot-skill-r-fear: R executes the target in front of Urgot and fears nearby enemies at that moment. In teamfights, pull in a target from the middle of the enemy group with R to fear multiple enemies. If you execute an enemy fleeing alone with R, there are no other enemies to fear.
notes.urgot-skill-w-toggle: At max rank, W becomes a toggle that lasts indefinitely. Before maxing W, use it sparingly and account for its duration. Activating W greatly reduces Urgot's movement speed and increases his slow resistance. Turn on W when fighting up close. Turn off W when fleeing.
notes.urgot-skill-w-mark: W prioritizes the champion most recently hit by another ability. To make W fire at your chosen target in a skirmish, hit them with Q or E first. If no champion has been hit by another ability, W fires at the nearest enemy or minion.
notes.urgot-skill-e: E gives Urgot a shield as he dashes. E pushes through targets other than champions, but cannot cross terrain. Against an opponent with a mobility ability, engage with E after they use it. When ganked, use E's shield and stun to escape.
notes.urgot-skill-q: Q has long range and applies a very strong slow. When looking for a kill, save Q to set up an E engage. When holding the lane, use Q to poke.
notes.urgot-laning: Urgot is classified as a ranged champion, but his range is very short. Urgot has an advantage against melee opponents and a disadvantage against long-range opponents. In lane, approach with W active and pressure your opponent by circling to fire your leg cannons.
notes.urgot-laning-wave: With W active, nearby minions are hit automatically too, pushing the wave. To pull the wave toward you, turn off W and only last-hit. Manage W according to the wave state to avoid unwanted pushing and exposure to ganks.
notes.urgot-phase: Urgot is weak at levels 1–2, when Q deals little damage. His trades grow stronger as he puts levels into W. His laning peaks when level 6 R coincides with his first core item. Later on, his short range makes it hard to enter teamfights. In the mid game, secure your lead through lane pressure and turrets.
notes.urgot-teamfight: Before entering a teamfight, look for a chance to pull a target from behind the enemy frontline with E. Damage the target pulled in by E with Q and W, then execute them with R. If the enemies are grouped and there is no opening for E, attack the frontline with W and look for a chance to finish someone with R.
notes.urgot-situational-antiheal: If the opponent's healing is enough to turn a duel around, buy Executioner's Calling after completing your first core item. Dealing continuous damage with W lets you keep Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.vs-urgot-legs: Leg cannons, which account for most of Urgot's damage, deal damage based on maximum health. Each leg cannon has its own cooldown. Stay outside Urgot's short range to avoid prolonged exposure to his leg cannons.
notes.vs-urgot-w: Urgot's movement speed drops sharply while W is active. If Urgot approaches with W active, walk out of its firing range. Urgot gains slow resistance during W, making it hard to keep him away with slows.
notes.vs-urgot-e: Urgot's E cannot cross terrain and stops at the first champion it hits. Urgot's E pushes minions aside as he passes through them. Have your frontline stand in front of your damage dealers to block Urgot's E. Stand near walls to limit Urgot's E engage angles.
notes.vs-urgot-q: Urgot's Q applies such a strong slow that it is hard to escape on foot. When you see Q coming, decide immediately whether to use a mobility ability. If Q has already hit you, judge whether standing your ground and fighting back is better than fleeing. If Urgot's Q hits you, you become W's priority target.
notes.vs-urgot-r: If your health falls below the execution threshold after R hits you, you are automatically pulled in and executed. If you have the R mark, get completely out of Urgot's range before your health reaches the execution threshold. If you have the R mark, immediately use an option such as Zhonya's Hourglass or Quicksilver Sash. R's slow grows stronger the more health the target has lost.
notes.vs-urgot-range: Urgot is classified as ranged, but his range is close to that of a melee champion. Long-range champions can keep their distance against Urgot. Melee champions should avoid fighting Urgot head-on and either take him down with their jungler or farm for the late game. E is Urgot's only way to enter a teamfight. In teamfights, group up to block Urgot's E engage angles.
notes.varus-combo-blight: Blight stacks detonate only when another of Varus’s abilities hits the target. Stack Blight to the maximum with basic attacks, then detonate it with E. Stack Blight to the maximum with basic attacks, then detonate it with Q.
notes.varus-combo-ult: Enemies rooted by R gain Blight stacks automatically for its duration. Start with R, then detonate the Blight stacks twice with E and Q. To increase total damage, use R to start a fight rather than to finish one.
notes.varus-combo-q-charge: The longer you charge Q, the more its range, damage, and Blight detonation effect increase. Varus slows himself while aiming Q. At close range, fire Q immediately instead of fully charging it. If you aim Q incorrectly when no enemies are nearby, cancel it to recover half its mana cost.
notes.varus-skill-passive: A kill or assist makes his passive increase attack speed, attack damage, and ability power. On a champion takedown, the passive’s bonuses are much larger and can exceed the attack speed cap. Varus is especially strong for a few seconds after a champion takedown. After the first kill in a teamfight, keep attacking the next target.
notes.varus-skill-w-cooldown: Detonating Blight on a champion or epic monster reduces the cooldowns of basic abilities. When attacking Dragon or Baron, stack Blight with basic attacks and detonate it with an ability.
notes.varus-skill-w-active: W’s active strengthens the next Q and has a long cooldown. Activate W when the opponent is tied to the wave or in a narrow path, where you can reliably land Q.
notes.varus-skill-e: Along with damage and a slow, E leaves contaminated ground that reduces healing. Place E where a healing focused enemy wants to stand or must pass through.
notes.varus-skill-r: R spreads from the first champion it hits to nearby champions it has not infected. R is most effective when opponents are grouped. Since Varus has no dash, decide whether to use R to start a fight or defend against an assassin.
notes.varus-laning-trade: In lane, stack Blight on the opposing marksman with basic attacks, then detonate it with E. In lane, stack Blight on the opposing marksman with basic attacks, then detonate it with Q. Detonate Blight from basic attacks with an ability before it expires.
notes.varus-laning-safety: Varus has low movement speed, no dash, and relatively low armor growth. Before stepping past the wave to aim Q, check both the opponent’s engage abilities and the jungler’s location. When you lack lane priority, stay back and use your abilities to clear the wave.
notes.varus-phase: At levels 1–2, use the bonus damage from W’s passive to poke and hold on. Once you learn E, you can clear waves and pressure opponents with its ground effect. Once you learn R at level 6, you can start fights yourself. Varus grows stronger as he gets items, but positioning remains important even late in the game.
notes.varus-teamfight: In teamfights, stay behind your frontline and disrupt the enemy formation with Q and E. Use R when opponents are clustered together. Wait until all opposing engage abilities are down before stepping forward to basic attack. Move forward right after a takedown activates your passive.
notes.varus-situational-antiheal: Because E reduces healing, antiheal items are a lower priority even against healing focused opponents. If the opponents have several sources of healing or heal beyond E’s reach, choose Mortal Reminder instead of an armor penetration item.
notes.varus-situational-cc: If the opponents have a lot of crowd control that prevents movement, buy Mercurial Scimitar earlier. If Varus is hit by crowd control that prevents movement, he cannot escape with an ability and struggles to regain distance afterward.
notes.vs-varus-blight: When Varus has stacked Blight with basic attacks, hitting the target with an ability detonates bonus damage based on maximum health.
notes.vs-varus-r: Varus’s R spreads from the first champion it hits to nearby champions, rooting those it reaches. If an ally is rooted by R, move far enough away that the tendrils cannot reach you. The tendrils from R disappear if you move far enough away. Spread out your teamfight formation to keep R from spreading to multiple people.
notes.vs-varus-passive: A kill or assist briefly gives Varus a large boost to attack speed and attack damage. For a few seconds after an ally is killed, avoid fighting Varus and wait for the boost to pass.
notes.vs-varus-q-charge: Varus slows himself while aiming Q. When you see Varus aiming Q, sidestep the arrow’s path and close in on him. When Varus starts aiming Q, hide behind minions to avoid the long range, fully charged arrow.
notes.vs-varus-mobility: Varus has no dash and relatively low movement speed. If Varus’s Flash is down, look for a chance to reach and catch him with an engage ability or crowd control. Prepare a way past the opposing frontline so you can reach Varus.
notes.vs-varus-e-ground: Healing and regeneration are reduced on the contaminated ground left by Varus’s E. If you rely on healing, leave E’s contaminated ground before fighting again.
notes.vayne-combo-condemn: Use Q to line up a wall behind the enemy, pin them against it with E, then build W stacks with basic attacks during the stun. E pushes the enemy away from the cast's origin. Q cannot cross walls. Distinguish between using Q to set up an angle and using it to disengage.
notes.vayne-combo-w: Time your trades around W procs. W triggers whenever attacks or abilities hit the same target a set number of times. Build W stacks with basic attacks, then use a Q-empowered basic attack for the final hit to deal both instances of damage together. Switching targets just before W triggers loses your accumulated stacks.
notes.vayne-combo-r: Activate R, move in with Q's invisibility, then build W stacks with basic attacks. Q's cooldown is greatly reduced while R is active. Use Q sideways while R is active to make your reappearance position harder to predict.
notes.vayne-skill-q: Q performs a short roll and grants an empowered basic attack. Vayne has relatively short basic attack range among ranged champions. Keep Q available to disengage instead of spending every use on closing in. Use Q immediately after a basic attack to cancel its recovery animation and reposition without losing damage. Q cannot cross walls.
notes.vayne-skill-w: W deals true damage based on the target's maximum health. W stacks build separately on each target. W stacks disappear over time. Keep attacking one chosen target to trigger W.
notes.vayne-skill-e: E stuns enemies if it pins them against a wall. E pushes away enemies who get close. Avoid spending E on simple poke in lane so you can respond to ganks. When trading with E, use it on an enemy with their back to a wall.
notes.vayne-skill-r: R increases Vayne's attack damage. R reduces Q's cooldown. Using Q while R is active makes you invisible. Takedowns extend R's duration, but it cannot exceed its original maximum. Use R after the fight starts and the enemy has used a targeted ability.
notes.vayne-skill-passive: P's movement speed bonus only applies when moving toward nearby enemy champions. P's movement speed bonus increases while R is active. Vayne is built to chase quickly but disengage slowly. Check your retreat path before closing in on the enemy.
notes.vayne-laning: Vayne struggles against longer-ranged opponents because of her short basic attack range. Keep the wave near your turret and farm to reduce the risk of ganks. Vayne is weak in the early laning phase. Play to minimize losses early.
notes.vayne-laning-trade: Only start a trade when the enemy steps forward to last-hit. Trigger W once in a short basic attack trade, then immediately retreat with Q. Avoid starting a trade if you cannot attack enough times to trigger W. Save E if the enemy does not have their back to a wall.
notes.vayne-phase: Vayne is weakest at levels 1–2. Q's cooldown decreases significantly as its rank increases. Vayne becomes much stronger in the mid to late game once she has attack speed and penetration items. Avoid falling behind early and secure time to scale.
notes.vayne-teamfight: Avoid initiating teamfights. Enter after your allies start the fight and the enemy has used their engage abilities and targeted crowd control. Draw fights into narrow terrain near walls to set up wall stuns with E. After entering, focus W stacks on one enemy without switching targets.
notes.vayne-situational-qss: If the enemy has lingering crowd control that restricts movement, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items to break free. You cannot use Q while immobilized.
notes.vayne-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing offsets W's true damage, buy Executioner's Calling after one core item to reduce healing. Vayne's fighting pattern centers on attacking one target for an extended time. Vayne's sustained attacks on one target keep healing reduction items' effects active longer.
notes.vs-vayne-wall: Vayne relies heavily on E's wall stun to secure kills. When facing Vayne, avoid fighting with your back to a wall. During the laning phase, position within the minion line or toward the open river. In teamfights, fight Vayne in open areas instead of narrow passages.
notes.vs-vayne-fragile: Pressure Vayne early to force her back. Push the lane to disrupt Vayne's farming and delay her scaling.
notes.vs-vayne-w: W deals true damage based on the target's maximum health. Building armor does not reduce W's true damage. Do not rely solely on defensive items and keep taking Vayne's attacks. W requires a set number of attacks to hit the same target before it triggers. Count the hits you take and move out of range just before W triggers.
notes.vs-vayne-r: Q's cooldown is shorter while R is active. While R is active, Vayne briefly becomes invisible each time she uses Q. Use targeted abilities the moment Vayne's invisibility ends. R's duration extends when Vayne scores a takedown. Keep low-health allies away from Vayne to prevent her from extending R's duration.
notes.vs-vayne-late: Once Vayne has attack speed and penetration items, defensive stats alone struggle to stop her. Vayne becomes harder to deal with as the game goes on. Secure objectives and turrets in the early and mid game, working toward ending the game.
notes.veigar-combo-basic: For a kill, trap the target with E, land W and Q, then finish with R. W lands late, so time it to hit during E's stun. In a kill combo, don't cast W first without E.
notes.veigar-combo-e-placement: E only stuns enemies who cross its edge. To stop an approaching enemy, place E on their path ahead of time.
notes.veigar-combo-r: R deals more damage the more health the target has lost. Use R after lowering the target's health with your W and Q. Use R after your allies deal damage.
notes.veigar-skill-passive: Each time you hit an enemy champion with an ability, you gain Phenomenal Evil Power stacks. You gain more Phenomenal Evil Power stacks when you participate in a kill. In lane, hit opponents with Q when they enter range to increase your ability power.
notes.veigar-skill-q: Killing an enemy unit with Q grants a stack. Killing large minions and large monsters with Q grants many more stacks. Finish off cannon minions with Q. Line up two low-health minions and kill both with Q.
notes.veigar-skill-w: W lands late, and opponents can see where it will land. Use W when an opponent is hit by immobilizing crowd control. Use W when an opponent is trapped by E. Use W when a narrow passage or minions make it hard for an opponent to dodge sideways. As you gain stacks, W's cooldown decreases, making it useful for farming too.
notes.veigar-skill-e-defense: Veigar has no mobility ability. Anticipate the opponent's approach and place E on their path ahead of time.
notes.veigar-laning: To prepare for ganks, keep the wave in the middle and don't push it all the way. When the wave is in the middle, poke from Q range and build stacks. Only step forward when you know where the enemy jungler is. Veigar relies heavily on mana and ability haste. When your mana drops below half, stop poking, farm, and wait to recover.
notes.veigar-laning-roam: After level 6, you can look for kills with E, W, Q, and R. Veigar has no mobility ability, so roaming out and back is slow. If there is no clear kill opportunity, manage the wave in mid and build stacks.
notes.veigar-phase: Veigar is weakest at levels 1–5, when he has few stacks. Veigar's kill potential rises when he learns R at level 6. Veigar's stacks have no cap, so he grows stronger as the game goes on. Early on, aim to get through without losing ground rather than trying to win.
notes.veigar-teamfight: In teamfights, position behind your allies instead of standing on the front line. Use E to cut off the enemy’s approach or block their escape route behind them. When an opponent is trapped or hit by allied crowd control, land W and Q. Save R for an enemy you must kill, especially a damaged damage dealer.
notes.veigar-teamfight-terrain: If you can choose where to teamfight, choose a narrow area. At dragon or Baron pit entrances and jungle paths, E can easily block the enemy team's movement. Avoid teamfights in open areas where opponents can approach from all sides.
notes.veigar-situational-zhonya: If an assassin targets Veigar and closes in, buy Zhonya's Hourglass early. Get Zhonya's Hourglass to respond if an enemy engages after you use E.
notes.veigar-situational-void: If opponents build magic resistance, get magic penetration from Void Staff to increase R's damage.
notes.vs-veigar-w: W deals heavy damage, but its landing spot and timing are visible in advance. When you hear W and see its ground indicator, move sideways to dodge it. When trading with Veigar, keep moving instead of standing still to attack.
notes.vs-veigar-e: E stuns only when you cross its edge. If trapped inside E, move or attack within it instead of running into the edge. If you must cross E's edge, save a mobility ability or Flash until then.
notes.vs-veigar-r: Veigar's R deals more damage the more health its target has lost. If your health falls below half, move out of Veigar's R range. At full health, you can survive Veigar's R.
notes.vs-veigar-passive: Dodge Veigar's Q poke so he cannot gain permanent stacks from you. Veigar's Q passes through only the first two units it hits. Stand behind minions to block Veigar's Q poke.
notes.vs-veigar-early: Keep pressuring Veigar during his weak levels 1–5. Use early pressure to disrupt Veigar's farming and poke. Coordinate your engage order with your allies, bait out E, then gank.
notes.vs-veigar-late: Veigar's stacks have no cap, so he grows stronger in the late game. Before starting a late-game objective fight, check Veigar's position and whether he has used E.
notes.velkoz-combo-basic: Knock the target up with E, cast W under them, then layer Q on top. Cast W the moment E knocks the target up so both W hits land during the knockup. Q takes longer to hit, so layer it in last. One E–W–Q combo completes the Organic Deconstruction stacks and triggers true damage.
notes.velkoz-combo-q-split: You can recast Q to choose when it splits. Q's split beams travel to either side of its original path. When the target dodges sideways, recast Q just before it passes beside them. Against a target behind a wall or close to a brush, split Q in front of the wall to catch them from the side.
notes.velkoz-combo-r-setup: Build Organic Deconstruction stacks with Q or W, then cast R. R deals true damage that ignores magic resistance to targets recently damaged by Organic Deconstruction. Keep R on one target long enough to build stacks, and its damage turns into true damage midcast.
notes.velkoz-skill-passive: Landing different abilities together completes Organic Deconstruction stacks faster. Mix Q, W, and E hits to build Organic Deconstruction stacks quickly. Completing Organic Deconstruction stacks triggers true damage that ignores resistances. Basic attacks cannot add Organic Deconstruction stacks, but they extend their duration. If one stack remains, use a basic attack to buy time, then finish with an ability.
notes.velkoz-skill-q: Q is Vel'Koz's main poke and his only slow. Q has long range and restores mana. Save Q for its slow when you need to keep a target in place. Q splits automatically at maximum range or on hit, even without a recast. When enemies are grouped, let Q travel its full range to hit several of them.
notes.velkoz-skill-w: W has charges, so you can cast it twice in a row. W hits once, then erupts again after a delay. Even one W cast can reliably build Organic Deconstruction stacks. When clearing a wave, save at least one W charge for a fight.
notes.velkoz-skill-e: E is Vel'Koz's only reliable crowd control ability. Do not use E to clear waves or for simple poke. E pushes away enemies who are very close instead of knocking them up. In lane, when the enemy's engage ability is available, prioritize saving E for defense over starting a combo.
notes.velkoz-skill-r: R is a channeled beam that follows the cursor. Vel'Koz is completely vulnerable while channeling R. Before casting R, check whether the enemy has used their engage ability. Before casting R, make sure you cannot be caught from behind. Use R's slow to keep hitting one target without changing the beam's angle much.
notes.velkoz-laning: Vel'Koz support specializes in poke over protection or buffs. Keep hitting the enemy ADC with Q and W to complete Organic Deconstruction stacks. Use the moment the enemy loses health as your ally's signal to engage.
notes.velkoz-laning-safety: Vel'Koz has no mobility ability. Be especially careful when stepping forward to find a poke angle. Poke from behind or beside your ADC, using the edge of your range. Save E as your last safeguard when poking could put you in danger.
notes.velkoz-teamfight: In teamfights, fight from the back using your range. Before a fight, build Organic Deconstruction stacks on several enemies with Q and W. Cast R when an ally locks down the enemy. Move R's beam across the group your ally has locked down.
notes.velkoz-phase: At levels 1–2, you have few abilities and little mana, so your poke rotation is slow. Lane pressure grows once you have both Q and W and can complete Organic Deconstruction stacks in one rotation. Learning R at level 6 gives you chances to finish off enemies. As ability power builds, your true damage and late-game damage increase. Position farther back as your damage grows in the late game.
notes.velkoz-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has an assassin who dives in, get Zhonya's Hourglass so you can channel R to the end. When an assassin dives in, Vel'Koz has no mobility ability and relies on E to push them away.
notes.velkoz-situational-antiheal: Against enemies with strong healing, use Morellonomicon to reduce it. Vel'Koz can easily spread healing reduction by hitting several enemies with wide-ranging abilities.
notes.vs-velkoz-q: Q splits to either side when it reaches maximum range or is recast. Do not dodge Q by moving only sideways. When Q splits, move toward Vel'Koz or behind the beams after they pass.
notes.vs-velkoz-passive: Taking consecutive hits from Vel'Koz's abilities completes Organic Deconstruction stacks and triggers true damage that resistances cannot block. Even if you build magic resistance, avoid taking repeated poke from Vel'Koz. When you have Organic Deconstruction stacks, leave vision or retreat behind minions to let the stacks expire.
notes.vs-velkoz-r: Vel'Koz channels R while standing still. When R's beam starts, prioritize interrupting it with crowd control or by blocking vision. If you cannot interrupt R, move behind a wall or past minions to break vision.
notes.vs-velkoz-e: E is Vel'Koz's only reliable crowd control ability, and he has no mobility ability. Approach Vel'Koz after his E misses. E pushes away enemies who get very close instead of knocking them up. When engaging on Vel'Koz, have a way to finish him after E pushes you back.
notes.vs-velkoz-position: Vel'Koz has no way to escape, so he struggles to survive if caught. Clear vision around the river and tri-brush to create a route to approach from the side. Once you have a route to engage from the side, Vel'Koz has a harder time stepping forward to poke.
notes.vex-combo-basic: Land E's slow, then hit Q. The farther you throw E, the larger its area grows in flight, making it easier to land. Fire Q after E's slow takes effect.
notes.vex-combo-passive: When Doom is ready, your next basic ability fears enemies. To land fear safely, lead with long-range Q or wide-area E. Use W to fear an enemy when they're already close. Clear minions while Doom is down so you don't waste it.
notes.vex-combo-ult: After the R projectile marks a target, recast R to dash to them. If a marked target damaged by R dies soon after, you can use R again. Land the first R on a target you can finish off. After landing from your R dash, use E to lock down nearby enemies and W for a shield.
notes.vex-skill-passive-antidash: Nearby enemies gain a Gloom mark when they dash or blink. A basic ability used while Doom is ready interrupts enemy dashes and fears them. Against champions that engage, save Doom until they go in.
notes.vex-skill-passive-mark: Consuming a Gloom mark with a basic attack reduces Doom's cooldown. Weave in one basic attack against a marked enemy, then back off. Killing an enemy with E also reduces Doom's cooldown.
notes.vex-skill-q: Q gets narrower and faster as it travels. Against close enemies, cast Q right in front of them. Against distant enemies, aim Q where they're moving.
notes.vex-skill-w: W gives you a shield and a close-range shockwave at the same time. Use W as the enemy's burst damage hits. Save W for an engage instead of using it early to poke.
notes.vex-skill-e: E's slow makes the following Q and R easier to land. The farther you throw E, the larger its impact area. If you expect a trade, keep enough mana to cast the costly E at least once.
notes.vex-skill-r: The R projectile marks the first enemy champion it hits. If the frontline is overlapping, shift your angle and fire R so it passes through only the backline. Before going in with R, check whether W and Flash are available.
notes.vex-laning: In lane, use Q to farm and poke while saving E. Poke with Q when the enemy steps forward to last-hit a minion. Use W with Doom when an enemy tries to get close.
notes.vex-laning-vs-dash: Hold Doom and wait for enemies who engage with a dash. As the enemy goes in, use a basic ability to interrupt their dash and fear them. If you spend Doom on the wave, retreat behind your minions.
notes.vex-phase: At levels 1–2, Q's long cooldown makes it slow to poke repeatedly. Once you learn E and can keep cycling Doom, you gain lane control. Learning R at level 6 lets you roam and force engages. Late game, Vex is strongest when kills reset R and let her chain engages. If enemies group up without giving you an R angle, your late-game impact drops sharply.
notes.vex-teamfight: Don't go in first in teamfights. As the enemy engages, interrupt their dash with an ability empowered by Doom. After stopping the enemy engage, use E to lock down the backline. Use R once the enemy formation breaks and you can secure a kill.
notes.vex-situational-zhonya: Against multiple engage assassins, buy Zhonya's Hourglass before damage items to survive after going in with R.
notes.vs-vex-dash: When Vex's Doom is ready, one basic ability interrupts dashes and fears enemies. Delay your dash while Vex's Doom indicator is showing. Go in right after Vex spends Doom on the wave or on poke.
notes.vs-vex-mark: If you're marked, move out of Vex's basic attack range and wait for the mark to disappear.
notes.vs-vex-e: Vex's E grows larger the farther it travels. If you're already within E's range, dodge by moving toward Vex or taking a short step sideways.
notes.vs-vex-r: If Vex's R projectile hits you, it marks you and she can dash to you. If R marks you, move toward your allies immediately so Vex has to dash into their midst. Look for the moment just after Vex dashes with R, when she has no movement ability to escape.
notes.vs-vex-reset: If a marked target damaged by R dies soon after, Vex gets R back. Before starting a teamfight, move low-health allies out of Vex's range.
notes.vs-vex-dive: Vex's only survival tool is her W shield. Get close when both Vex's Doom and W are down.
notes.vi-combo-gank: For a basic gank, charge Q and hit the target, then use an E-empowered basic attack, a basic attack, E, and a basic attack in that order. When Q hits a champion, Vi stops and knocks them backward. Approach from behind so Q knocks the target toward your allied laner.
notes.vi-combo-ult: After knocking the target up with R, charge E while they land, then follow with a basic attack, E, a basic attack, and Q. R targets and chases its target, so use it to start the combo. Using Q first knocks the target away and breaks the follow-up.
notes.vi-skill-q-charge: The longer you charge Q, the more damage it deals and the farther Vi dashes. Fully charge Q to catch or finish a fleeing enemy. If Q is interrupted while charging, you can use it again after a short wait.
notes.vi-skill-w: W activates only when you hit the same target repeatedly. Keep attacking the target you have committed to so your W stacks stay on them. When W activates, it reduces the target's armor and increases Vi's attack speed. Vi gains more from staying on one target and attacking them longer.
notes.vi-skill-e: E turns your next basic attack into an area attack that passes through targets. If an enemy is behind a minion or jungle monster, hit the front unit with E to damage the enemy behind it. Use E's piercing attack to poke when helping a lane or to secure a last hit safely. E stores charges, so let them build up between camps.
notes.vi-skill-passive: Vi gains her passive shield when she hits an enemy or structure with an ability. Before a fight, hit a nearby minion or monster with an ability to activate your shield, then go in. Each time W activates, it reduces the cooldown of your passive shield.
notes.vi-skill-r: R chases its chosen target to the end, so Flash cannot dodge it. Vi cannot be stopped during R, so she ignores enemy crowd control as she goes in. R fails if its target becomes untargetable. Other enemies in R's path are knocked aside and briefly stunned, but Vi keeps chasing her chosen target.
notes.vi-teamfight-engage: Walk close enough for your team to follow, then engage with R. If you use R on a backline damage dealer too far ahead of your team, you will be left among the enemies without allied support.
notes.vi-teamfight-focus: In teamfights, pick off one key enemy damage dealer. Isolate the target with R, then attack only that target until W activates. Use Q to block the target's escape route or knock them toward your team. In teamfights, focus on one enemy instead of alternating between several.
notes.vi-phase: Start ganking at level 3, once you have your abilities. At level 6, learning R lets you reliably catch one target. Vi has low damage per minute early, so she has little impact if she only clears camps. As soon as you have your abilities, help a lane to gain an advantage. Later on, Vi's role shifts toward engaging and isolating targets rather than dealing damage.
notes.vi-jungle-clear: In the jungle, keep attacking one monster to activate W. Activate your passive shield before moving to the next camp to reduce health loss. Enemies other than champions are pulled toward Vi when Q hits them. Use Q to gather scattered monsters.
notes.vi-situational-antiheal: If the target you have committed to is hard to kill because of their sustain, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.vi-situational-cc: If the enemy team can lock you down with crowd control after you engage with R and keep you from escaping, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. R itself cannot be interrupted, so prepare for being locked down after landing.
notes.vs-vi-q-charge: When Vi charges Q, move back or sideways to dodge it. Even if you interrupt Q's charge, Vi can use it again soon, so prioritize dodging.
notes.vs-vi-w: Keep fights with Vi short, then create distance instead of fighting her for long.
notes.vs-vi-r: Use forced movement abilities on Vi after she lands and the knockup ends, rather than during R.
notes.vs-vi-shield: If Vi approaches right after using an ability on a minion, wait until her shield is gone before trading damage.
notes.vs-vi-position: While Vi has R available, backline damage dealers should not go alone into areas without vision. While Vi has R available, backline damage dealers should stay within range of their allies' protective abilities.
notes.viego-skill-passive-possession: Enemy champions who fall near Viego remain as wraiths for a short time. Basic attack a wraith to begin possessing it. Possessing a target heals Viego based on the target's maximum health. While possessing a target, Viego can use its basic abilities and items.
notes.viego-skill-possession-chain: While possessing a target, Viego can use his own R once more at no cost instead of the target's ultimate. After using the abilities gained through possession, use R just before it ends to target the next enemy.
notes.viego-skill-possession-prep: If you do not know the target's ability layout, you will be slow to react right after possessing it. Before a fight, check the basic ability layouts of all five enemies. Prioritize wraiths of enemies with dashes or shields.
notes.viego-combo-basic: In a standard fight, approach with E, stun with W, then use Q. Your first basic attack against an enemy hit by an ability triggers an extra attack from Q's passive. After landing an ability, weave in basic attacks to deal damage.
notes.viego-combo-w-charge: The longer you charge W, the longer its stun lasts. Viego slows down while charging W. Interrupting Viego while he charges W cancels the charge. Against a fleeing enemy, charge W briefly to catch up. Charge W for a long time only when you are sure it will hit.
notes.viego-combo-r-target: R automatically attacks the nearby champion with the lowest percentage of remaining health. Before using R, check which champion it will target. R knocks back enemies other than its primary target. Use R to split the enemy team.
notes.viego-skill-q: Q adds damage to basic attacks based on the target's current health. Q helps Viego damage high-health tanks and objectives. Q's damage speeds up jungle clearing and taking Dragon and Baron. Q's thrust pierces forward and can hit enemies behind minions.
notes.viego-skill-e-approach: E creates black mist along terrain. In E's mist, Viego is camouflaged and gains movement speed and attack speed. When ganking, cast E on a wall along your approach, then follow the mist in. Attacking or using an ability in the mist briefly reveals Viego. While approaching, stay camouflaged in the mist until just before using your first ability.
notes.viego-phase: Viego uses no resources, making his early jungle clear comfortable. A kill in a small fight near an objective can let Viego turn the fight through possession. Viego is strong in the mid game, when he has built his items. If Viego enters a late-game teamfight head-on first, he can easily die before creating a wraith to possess.
notes.viego-laning-gank: Viego's only approach tools are W and E, so solo ganks have a low success rate. Prioritize ganking lanes where your ally has crowd control. If your ally has no crowd control, gank when the enemy pushes the lane near your ally's turret.
notes.viego-laning-objective: Before an objective fight, use E to secure vision as you approach. Even if you lose the Smite fight, killing one enemy lets you heal through possession and look for a chance to reclaim the objective.
notes.viego-teamfight: Viego is not suited to starting teamfights. Enter after the enemy uses crowd control on your allied tank and a target you can kill appears. When you enter a teamfight, secure a wraith for your first possession. If you cannot create a wraith on your first entry, it is hard to keep fighting.
notes.viego-teamfight-window: Possession lasts only a short time, and the moment it ends is dangerous. Before possession ends, kill your next target or retreat to safety. If possession ends in the middle of the enemy team, Viego is easy to kill.
notes.viego-situational-antiheal: If an enemy has strong healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Viego needs to kill an enemy to gain sustain through possession. If he does not kill a target, possession cannot begin.
notes.vs-viego-corpse: If an ally dies near Viego, a wraith remains where they fell. Viego begins possession when he basic attacks a wraith. Do not keep fighting near where an ally fell. Knock Viego away from the wraith or immobilize him so he cannot attack it.
notes.vs-viego-possession: While possessing someone, Viego takes the fallen ally's appearance and uses their basic abilities. Do not mistake a possessing Viego for an ally and turn your back on him. Counterattack when Viego finishes possessing someone and returns to his own body. Keep your distance and hold out until possession ends.
notes.vs-viego-w: The longer Viego charges W, the longer its stun lasts. Viego slows down while charging W. Interrupting Viego while he charges W cancels the charge. When you see Viego charging W, dodge to the side. If you have crowd control, use it to interrupt Viego's W charge.
notes.vs-viego-r: Viego's R targets the nearby champion with the lowest percentage of remaining health. If you are low on health and separated from your team, you are more likely to be targeted by Viego's R. If you are low on health, fall back. If you are low on health, stay close to your allies to make it harder for Viego's R to pick you out.
notes.vs-viego-fog: If you see black mist along terrain, Viego is camouflaged inside it. When you see the mist, place a Control Ward. When you see the mist, take another route around it. Do not push the lane toward the mist.
notes.vs-viego-sustain: If Viego fails to get a kill, he has almost no way to heal. Do not start a small fight you cannot win. Retreat without giving Viego a kill to slow his growth.
notes.viktor-combo-q-aa: Casting Q empowers your next basic attack. After using Q, follow up with the empowered basic attack. Use other abilities while your Q empowered basic attack is available.
notes.viktor-combo-trade: Poke with E. If the enemy approaches, place W under them, then follow up with Q and the empowered basic attack. Use W after the enemy steps forward.
notes.viktor-combo-ult: Place R, then hold the enemy in it with W to deal R's damage over time. You can recast R to control it directly. Move R toward where you expect the enemy to retreat.
notes.viktor-skill-passive: Viktor collects fragments to permanently augment his abilities. Killing minions grants fragments. Siege minions grant especially many fragments. Always last-hit siege minions yourself.
notes.viktor-skill-augment-order: You cannot undo a chosen augment. Choose the augment with the effect you need most at that moment. If you urgently need poke and wave clear in lane, augment E first. If you need to withstand trades and stay close to the enemy, augment Q first. If you need to hold enemies in place during teamfights, augment W first.
notes.viktor-skill-q: Q deals damage and grants a shield. Augmented Q also increases movement speed. When you need to take a trade, use Q for its shield before going in.
notes.viktor-skill-w: W stuns only after the target stays in its area for a certain time. Place W on an escape route or in a narrow passage to set up a stun. Place W on an enemy who is already slowed or rooted to set up a stun.
notes.viktor-skill-e: E hits in a straight line. You choose E's firing direction directly. Augmented E creates one more aftershock along its path. Augmenting E improves both wave clear and poke. Look for an angle to hit the wave and the enemy champion in one line with E.
notes.viktor-skill-r: R interrupts enemy channels when it appears. If an enemy has a channeled ultimate, save R to interrupt its cast.
notes.viktor-phase-early: Viktor ranks among the lowest mid champions in early kill participation. In lane, prioritize E poke and farming for augments over kills.
notes.viktor-phase-scaling: Viktor peaks in the mid to late game with two or three augments and core items. Augments persist through death. Even if you fall behind in lane, keep farming to grow stronger.
notes.viktor-laning-wave: Clearing a wave at once with E builds fragments quickly. After clearing a wave with E, you have time to roam or recall. Pushing the wave leaves you exposed to ganks. Get vision of the river before pushing the wave. When pushing the wave, keep your Q shield and W available in case of a gank.
notes.viktor-laning-safety: Viktor has no dash to escape on his own. If you do not know where the enemy jungler is, do not move past the lane's midpoint. Keep W available to stop ganks and lane safely.
notes.viktor-teamfight: Viktor is a champion who controls the battlefield. In narrow terrain, hold enemies in place with W and overlap R to deal damage over time. Viktor's short range forces him to stand a step forward. Viktor can die quickly if enemies engage on him. Stay just behind your frontline and focus on controlling R.
notes.viktor-situational-zhonya: Buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier to deal with assassins who close in. Once placed, R keeps dealing damage even when Viktor stands still.
notes.vs-viktor-distance: Viktor controls the battlefield more effectively when he is closer to enemies. Q's empowered basic attack is considered close-range. W is considered close-range. Keep your distance from Viktor to limit the poke you take to E.
notes.vs-viktor-augment-read: You can tell how many augments Viktor has by the color of his staff's light. When the color of Viktor's staff light changes, reassess your trades.
notes.vs-viktor-w: W stuns only if the target stays in its area. Leave W's area immediately to take only the slow and avoid the stun. Do not keep trading inside W's area.
notes.vs-viktor-e: E hits in a straight line. Dodge E by stepping to the side. Do not stand in line with the wave, so E cannot poke you as easily.
notes.vs-viktor-dive: Viktor has no dash to escape on his own. When an enemy closes in, Viktor's defenses are his Q shield and W stun. Avoid W's area when closing in to attack Viktor.
notes.vs-viktor-r-interrupt: R interrupts channels when it appears. Wait until Viktor has used R before casting a channeled ultimate.
notes.vladimir-skill-passive: Crimson Pact converts bonus health into ability power and ability power into maximum health. Building health also increases your damage. W and E scale with health, so their area damage grows as you build health.
notes.vladimir-skill-q-empower: After two Q casts, a third Q used within a short time deals more damage and heals more. Use Q twice on minions to empower it, then use it on the enemy champion. Prime Q just before a fight so your first Q is empowered. Q deals damage before healing and costs no resources, making it reliable for last hits. If you need healing, use Q on an enemy champion instead of a minion, which gives reduced healing.
notes.vladimir-skill-w: W briefly makes Vladimir untargetable and destroys incoming projectiles. Enemies in W's pool are slowed and have their health drained. Place W in the middle of the enemy team to deal damage and heal at the same time. W has a long cooldown, so avoid using it first in a trade. Use W just before enemy crowd control lands to nullify it.
notes.vladimir-skill-e: E consumes health while charging and deals more damage the longer it charges. Charging E past a certain point adds a slow. Vladimir moves more slowly while charging E, and it fires automatically after a while. Choose where to aim when you start charging E. Enemy units in front block E, so don't fire it at an enemy champion through a minion wave.
notes.vladimir-skill-r: Enemies infected by R briefly take increased damage from all sources. R explodes after a delay and heals Vladimir based on the number of champions hit. R also amplifies allied damage, so use it early in a fight. Hit multiple enemies with R when they group up or right after an ally lands area crowd control.
notes.vladimir-combo-basic: Prime Q on minions, then when the enemy enters range, charge E until it slows, fire it, and use empowered Q. Slow the enemy with E before using Q to hit them before they retreat out of range. If you use Q first and then charge E, the enemy may retreat and cause E to miss.
notes.vladimir-combo-teamfight: Hit multiple enemies with R, charge E as you move in, land empowered Q and E, then use W when they counterattack. You can use W while charging E. After casting R, coordinate your engage with your allies while its damage amplification is active.
notes.vladimir-laning-early: Early in lane, last hit with Q and stay safe. Before learning W, you have no escape, so avoid standing far up the lane. Last hit waves the enemy pushes in with Q near your turret.
notes.vladimir-laning-health: Farming carelessly with E costs health and gives the enemy a chance to engage. Pushing the wave with E is especially dangerous when you're below half health. When low on health, heal with Q before clearing the wave with E.
notes.vladimir-laning-wave: In patch 26.17 mid lane stats, Vladimir has very few deaths and damage per minute near the top, while his kill stats are in the lower middle. In lane, prioritize survival and growth over kills. Once you can clear waves quickly with E, push the lane and establish vision or join fights in other lanes.
notes.vladimir-phase: Vladimir is weakest at levels 1–5. Early on, W is either unavailable or on a long cooldown, making it hard to escape when caught. Once you learn R at level 6 and complete your first core item, your contribution to fights rises sharply. Because health and ability power increase each other, you grow stronger faster as you build items. Minimize losses early and aim to contribute to teamfights in the mid and late game.
notes.vladimir-teamfight: In teamfights, move between the front and back lines while dealing area damage. Without guaranteed crowd control, Vladimir struggles to start fights himself. Hit as many enemies as possible with R, then move in with your allies when they engage. Engage when W is ready and the enemy has used targeted crowd control on your team's initiator. Hitting more enemies increases your healing, so dive into grouped enemies instead of chasing one target.
notes.vladimir-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team also relies on healing to survive, buy Morellonomicon between core items. Repeated area damage lets you keep applying Grievous Wounds to multiple enemies.
notes.vladimir-situational-zhonya: If the enemy has a burst champion that dives onto Vladimir, buy Zhonya's Hourglass early. Alternating W and Zhonya's Hourglass lets you survive two engages in one fight.
notes.vs-vladimir-early: Vladimir is weakest at levels 1–5. Focus lane pressure and ganks at levels 1–5 to slow Vladimir's growth. As time passes, his health and ability power rise together, making him harder to face.
notes.vs-vladimir-w: Vladimir's W breaks targeting and destroys incoming projectiles. Draw out W with a low-cost ability, then use your decisive ability when the pool ends. Without W, Vladimir has no way to escape if caught.
notes.vs-vladimir-r: While infected by Vladimir's R, you take increased damage from all sources. If infected by R, back away and rejoin the fight after its effect ends. Avoid grouping multiple players inside R's area so Vladimir doesn't heal more.
notes.vs-vladimir-items: Items that deal damage based on maximum health are effective against Vladimir. For magic damage, you can choose Liandry's Torment. For physical damage, you can choose Blade of the Ruined King. Adding Grievous Wounds makes it harder for Vladimir to survive through healing.
notes.vs-vladimir-e: Vladimir moves more slowly while charging E. Enemy units in front can block Vladimir's E. When you see E charging, keep minions between you and Vladimir or move out of range before the charge ends. You can close the distance on Vladimir while charging E slows his movement.
notes.volibear-combo-basic: Activate Q and approach, stun with the empowered basic attack, then use W, a basic attack, and a second W in that order. Q's stun is delivered through an empowered basic attack. Approach with Q, then stun with a basic attack once you are in range. Aim to land W twice during the stun when trading.
notes.volibear-combo-w-mark: Using W again on a target hit by W deals more damage and restores health. Land a few basic attacks after the first W, then use the second W. If you expect to fight a champion, save your first W instead of using it on a minion.
notes.volibear-combo-ult: Leap in with R, then stun with Q after landing and use W and E. Start a turret dive by landing with R to disable the nearby turret briefly. Against mobile opponents, use R when they are immobilized or have no escape route. R grants bonus health, letting you keep fighting after you land.
notes.volibear-skill-passive: Dealing damage with abilities and basic attacks builds passive attack speed stacks. At maximum passive stacks, your basic attacks also hit nearby enemies. Volibear's damage depends heavily on his passive stacks. Hit minions or jungle monsters just before a fight to build passive stacks.
notes.volibear-skill-q: Q's movement speed bonus doubles when you move toward an enemy champion. The movement speed bonus is smaller when fleeing, so use Q to close the gap. If you are immobilized before landing Q's stun, Q ends but its cooldown resets. Use Q first when trying to draw out the opponent's guaranteed crowd control.
notes.volibear-skill-w: W's short cooldown makes it central to farming and trading in lane. W heals more when you have more missing health.
notes.volibear-skill-e: E is Volibear's only ranged ability, dealing damage based on maximum health and slowing enemies. Use E to poke opponents or clear waves when closing the gap is difficult. To hit a moving opponent with E, overlap it with Q's stun or an ally's immobilizing effect. E grants a shield only if Volibear is inside its blast area. E costs a lot of mana and has a long cooldown, so avoid using it out of habit before engaging.
notes.volibear-skill-r: Turrets near R's landing point are briefly disabled. Dive with R when an opponent stays under turret for safety. Save R as a last resort for escaping.
notes.volibear-laning: Farm with W and manage your mana during lane. Trade when Q is available again. Trade when the enemy wave pushes toward your turret and you can catch the opponent nearby.
notes.volibear-laning-ranged: Against ranged opponents, poke with E while securing CS. Approach with Q just after a ranged opponent uses a poke ability or steps forward from behind their minions. Early on, Volibear can usually win trades against ranged opponents if he closes the gap.
notes.volibear-teamfight: After an ally starts the fight and the opponents use their abilities, enter the backline with R. When you enter the backline with R, lock down an enemy damage dealer. Build passive stacks before entering a teamfight to damage nearby enemies too. If the enemy formation is not spread out, hold R, approach with Q, and hold the frontline.
notes.volibear-phase: Volibear is strong in early melee trades. Before learning several abilities, he runs out of mana quickly. Your first power spikes come when W gains ranks and Q is available, and at level 6 when you learn R. Later on, enemy defensive items and healing reduction make it harder to survive on W's healing alone. Secure your lead in the mid game through dives and objectives.
notes.volibear-situational-mr: If your lane opponent deals mostly magic damage, get magic resistance early. Choose Banshee's Veil if an opponent has a targeted ability that could be decisive. Choose Quicksilver Sash if guaranteed crowd control stops your engage.
notes.volibear-situational-antiheal: Buy Executioner's Calling between core items against opponents with strong healing. Volibear can stay close and keep applying healing reduction with basic attacks and W.
notes.vs-volibear-q: Volibear's Q movement speed bonus increases toward enemy champions and decreases when he flees. When Volibear chases you with Q active, use mobility or terrain to break vision, or move toward your allies. Stay outside Volibear's empowered basic attack range to avoid Q's stun.
notes.vs-volibear-w: Volibear's W heals more when he has more missing health. If you cannot finish Volibear when he is around half health, back off and wait out W's cooldown. Use healing reduction items to weaken Volibear's W healing.
notes.vs-volibear-e: Volibear's E lightning strikes after a delay once its indicator appears. When E's indicator appears, walk sideways out of it to avoid the damage and slow. Volibear must be inside E's marked area to gain its shield.
notes.vs-volibear-r: Volibear's R briefly disables turrets near its landing point. If you are low on health and Volibear's R is ready, retreat deeper behind your turret. When Volibear's R leap is telegraphed, use a mobility ability to leave its landing point.
notes.vs-volibear-stacks: Volibear's damage depends on his passive attack speed stacks. At maximum passive stacks, Volibear's basic attacks also hit nearby enemies. Avoid fighting when Volibear approaches while building stacks on minions or monsters. Fight just after Volibear's passive stacks expire.
notes.vs-volibear-lane: Ranged champions should poke while Volibear's Q is on cooldown. Wait out Volibear's Q, then keep poking to take control of the lane.
notes.warwick-combo-gank: Start a gank by marking the target with W and using the movement speed to close in. Before level 6, gank lanes where an ally can catch the target first, then close in with Q and use basic attacks. After level 6, suppress the target with R, then follow with basic attacks, Q, and E in that order.
notes.warwick-combo-r-range: R's leap distance scales with bonus movement speed. Use R while running toward the target with W or another movement speed boost active.
notes.warwick-combo-e-fear: When E expires, it fears nearby enemies. Recast it to trigger the fear early. Recast E to fear the target immediately when they are about to use a mobility ability or an ally needs to land a skillshot. When you need to withstand an enemy's burst damage, let E run its full duration to make the most of its damage reduction.
notes.warwick-skill-q-charge: Tap Q to bite the target, or hold it to move behind them while biting and change positions. Hold Q to move an enemy toward your allies or escape turret range during a dive. While Q is biting a target, Warwick follows them even if they flee.
notes.warwick-skill-q-value: Q deals damage based on the target's maximum health and heals Warwick for the damage dealt. Q's healing is key to sustaining through jungle clears and fights.
notes.warwick-skill-w: W's passive reveals the location of enemy champions below half health even without vision. After a lane trade ends, use W's detection to choose your next gank target. Using W marks the nearest enemy regardless of health. If W detects no target, part of its cooldown is refunded.
notes.warwick-skill-passive: Warwick's passive heals him more when his health is low. Don't leave a fight just because Warwick is at half health. Draw the fight toward minions or jungle monsters so Warwick has targets to heal from with his passive.
notes.warwick-phase: Warwick can start ganking at level 2, once he has Q and W. Warwick reaches his peak power when he gains R at level 6. Warwick clears the jungle slowly, making it hard to gain an advantage through farming. In late-game duels, Warwick loses to damage dealers who have scaled up. Warwick can still suppress one target with R in the late game.
notes.warwick-jungle-path: Choose the lane you want to gank first, then path so your clear ends nearby. Warwick gains more from ganks than from farming.
notes.warwick-jungle-gank: Gank when the enemy has pushed the lane away from their turret. Warwick has no guaranteed crowd control before level 6. Before level 6, if you cannot rely on an ally's immobilizing crowd control, turn toward a camp or objective on the other side.
notes.warwick-teamfight: In teamfights, suppress a key enemy damage dealer with R. Immediately after using R, Warwick is locked in place. Engage with R when the enemy damage dealer is within your allies' range or your allies are ready to engage with you.
notes.warwick-teamfight-dive: Activate E's damage reduction, move past the frontline, then recast E to fear the enemy backline.
notes.warwick-objective: During standoffs at Dragon or Baron, W's passive lets you see enemies who have lost health. During an objective standoff, engage as soon as a W mark appears. Use R's movement speed based range to find an angle from the far side of the objective pit.
notes.warwick-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing could turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Warwick stays close to enemies and attacks for a long time, so he can easily keep Grievous Wounds applied.
notes.vs-warwick-r: While suppressed by Warwick's R, you cannot do anything. Use Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar to immediately remove Warwick's R suppression. If you cannot remove the suppression, focus on keeping the ally caught by R alive. Counterattack while Warwick is locked in place immediately after using R.
notes.vs-warwick-w: When your health falls below half, Warwick can see your location, and his movement speed and attack speed increase.
notes.vs-warwick-e: Warwick takes less damage while E is active and fears enemies when it ends. If Warwick activates E, back off and reengage after the fear triggers. Warwick can recast E to trigger the fear early.
notes.vs-warwick-passive: Don't decide to dive Warwick based only on his current health. Apply Grievous Wounds with Executioner's Calling when finishing off Warwick.
notes.vs-warwick-r-range: Warwick's R leap distance increases with movement speed. If Warwick has a movement speed buff, don't assume you are safe just because you are across a wall or in a bush without vision. During an objective standoff, don't leave the far side of the pit open for Warwick to engage from.
notes.vs-warwick-early: Warwick has no guaranteed crowd control before level 6. Early on, gain an advantage through jungle invades and lane priority.
notes.xayah-combo-root: Set up at least three feathers to root with E. Place two feathers with Q, add one with a passive auto attack, then recall them with E. If you land only Q before using E, it deals damage without rooting.
notes.xayah-combo-passive-weave: After using an ability, Xayah's passive applies to her auto attacks. During trades, weave in a passive auto attack between abilities. An auto attack after each of W and Q quickly adds feathers for E.
notes.xayah-combo-ult: Xayah is untargetable while leaping with R. R leaves a line of feathers when Xayah lands. Dodge an enemy engage or skillshot with R, then immediately root with E.
notes.xayah-skill-passive: Passive auto attacks pierce enemies in their path, reaching opponents behind minions. In lane, poke with piercing passive auto attacks.
notes.xayah-skill-q: Q costs little mana and leaves two feathers in a line. Throw Q so its feathers pass through the opponent for a later E recall. Q feathers that miss to the side fall outside E's recall path.
notes.xayah-skill-w: W increases attack speed and adds a second blade. Hitting a champion while W is active increases movement speed. W has a short duration, so activate it when you can keep auto attacking. W is effective for hitting objectives or taking down turrets.
notes.xayah-skill-w-rakan: Nearby allied Rakan also gains W's effect. Rakan gains movement speed only when Xayah actually hits a target. When Rakan engages, activate W and immediately auto attack.
notes.xayah-skill-e: E hits enemies along the feathers' path back to Xayah. Move sideways to change E's recall angle and bring scattered feathers onto one target. When multiple feathers hit the same enemy, later feathers deal reduced damage. When bringing feathers onto one target, aim for the root over damage.
notes.xayah-skill-e-crit: E's damage increases with critical strike chance and critical strike damage. With core critical strike items in the late game, E can heavily damage the enemy backline even without a root angle.
notes.xayah-skill-r: Do not use R first just to deal more damage. Use R to dodge enemy skillshot ultimates or engage abilities. Xayah ignores unit collision while leaping with R. If cornered against a wall and surrounded, escape with R.
notes.xayah-phase: Xayah is weak in trades at levels 1–2, when she cannot gather feathers. Leveling E shortens the root's cooldown and opens up chances to fight. Learning R at level 6 gives Xayah a way to survive. Xayah peaks in the mid to late game as she builds core critical strike items. Xayah has low movement speed and no escape besides R, making positioning mistakes costly.
notes.xayah-laning: In lane, poke opponents through minions with Q and passive auto attacks. Start a trade when the opponent stands over three feathers. If there is no root angle, save E for farming or disengaging. Do not stay forward with the wave pushed deep toward the enemy turret.
notes.xayah-laning-feather-trap: Feathers remain on the ground briefly. Set up Q feathers at brush entrances or river approaches the enemy may use to prepare a root.
notes.xayah-teamfight: In teamfights, build up feathers with auto attacks from the back, then root enemies with E when they engage. Do not use up E before an engage; keep it to stop melee champions who get on top of you. Use E when multiple enemies are grouped together to root them all.
notes.vs-xayah-feather-count: Xayah's root triggers only when at least three returning feathers hit. If three or more feathers lie on the line between you and Xayah, move off it immediately.
notes.vs-xayah-move: If you fight Xayah from the same spot for too long, feathers pile up under your feet. Keep trades short and reposition so the feathers do not line up along their recall path.
notes.vs-xayah-r: When Xayah becomes untargetable with R, she can avoid engage abilities and crowd control. Engage after confirming Xayah has used R.
notes.vs-xayah-mobility: Xayah has low movement speed and no mobility ability besides R. Pressure Xayah with ganks and forced engages when her R is down or she has not reached level 6.
notes.vs-xayah-e-line: When Xayah uses E, her feathers return to her in straight lines. Instead of moving straight away from Xayah, sidestep out of the line between the feathers and her.
notes.xerath-combo-stun-first: For a guaranteed combo, stun with E, land W in the center, then fire Q. If E misses, save mana instead of following up with W and Q.
notes.xerath-combo-poke: When poking without a kill opportunity, slow them with W, then fire Q. Firing Q first prompts the opponent to dodge, making it harder to land.
notes.xerath-combo-ult: Xerath cannot move while using R. Before activating R, pin the opponent down with E or W. Fire the remaining R shots ahead of the opponent's straight escape path. Activate R only after finding a safe position.
notes.xerath-skill-q-charge: Q gains range the longer it charges. Xerath is slowed while charging Q. Fully charge Q only from a completely safe distance. If a melee opponent is close, charge Q briefly before firing.
notes.xerath-skill-q-aim: Q is easier to land when the opponent moves toward or away from Xerath than when they move side to side. Look for a Q when the opponent steps forward to last-hit a minion. Look for a Q when the opponent retreats to recall.
notes.xerath-skill-w-center: Land W in the center for its full damage and slow. Aim W ahead of the opponent's movement. After landing W in the center, follow up with Q.
notes.xerath-skill-e: E's stun lasts longer the farther its orb travels. Minions can block E's orb. When firing E, choose an angle clear of minions. Save E to interrupt an opponent's dash as self-defense.
notes.xerath-skill-r-cancel: If R ends without firing a shot, its cooldown is halved. If the opponent disappears from vision right after activating R, end it without firing.
notes.xerath-phase: At levels 1–2, Xerath's high mana costs limit how often he can poke. Xerath is very fragile at levels 1–2. After learning R at level 6, Xerath can pressure beyond his lane. Xerath is strongest in the mid game when he has both ability power and mana. In the late game, poor positioning can get Xerath killed instantly when an opponent engages.
notes.xerath-laning-poke: Poke with Q from behind minions, using your range advantage. Don't push the lane unnecessarily. Without a movement ability, Xerath is vulnerable to ganks when his lane is pushed. If you need to push the lane, establish river vision first.
notes.xerath-laning-mana: Excessive poke leaves too little mana for farming or self-defense. Fire Q only when the opponent is in a position where it will hit. If Q won't hit, cancel it to get your mana back. When safe, basic attack the opposing champion to restore more mana with your passive.
notes.xerath-teamfight: Start teamfights from the very back. After your allies engage and pin down the opponents, deal heavy damage with W and R. Save E to stop assassins who reach Xerath.
notes.xerath-teamfight-siege: Xerath is strongest during sieges and standoffs around objectives. Keep pressuring opponents with Q from a safe position beyond a wall or behind a turret. Once the opponents back off, have your team start the objective.
notes.xerath-situational-zhonya: If the opposing team has an assassin who can dive in, get Zhonya's Hourglass earlier. Zhonya's Hourglass can keep you alive if an opponent engages while you are casting R. Zhonya's Hourglass is a safeguard if you get caught while E is unavailable.
notes.vs-xerath-close: Xerath has no movement ability. Most champions can trade damage favorably with Xerath if they close the gap. Close the gap right after Xerath uses E and W.
notes.vs-xerath-ult: Xerath's R has a long cast animation, and he cannot move while casting it. As soon as you see Xerath's R cast animation, start dodging. When you see Xerath's R cast animation, you can also engage on his position.
notes.vs-xerath-q: Xerath's Q travels in a straight line through minions and can hit targets behind them. When Xerath starts charging Q, change direction and dodge well to the side. Close the gap while Xerath is slowed as he charges Q.
notes.vs-xerath-laning: Xerath uses a lot of mana during the laning phase. When Xerath runs out of mana, push the lane and call your jungler.
notes.xinzhao-combo-gank: For ganks, close in with E, activate Q, then knock the target up with an auto attack, W, an auto attack, and a third auto attack. Only auto attacks consume Q's empowered attacks, so using W between them does not reduce the count. W adds one hit toward Determination.
notes.xinzhao-combo-challenge: Mark the target you want to kill as Challenged first. Champions hit by W's thrust or an auto attack become Challenged. E has increased range against Challenged targets. Against distant targets, land W first, then follow up with E. R knocks back only enemies who are not Challenged.
notes.xinzhao-combo-r-timing: Activate R after engaging to survive. Activate R when you enter the enemy team and become surrounded. While R is active, you take no damage from champions outside your spear's range. Activating R just before engaging spends its immunity time on movement, so activate it after closing in.
notes.xinzhao-skill-q: Q empowers three auto attacks and knocks up the enemy on the third. Q's empowered auto attacks also reduce the cooldowns of your other abilities. Use Q freely on jungle camps, too. When going for a kill, time your auto attacks so the third lands as the enemy tries to Flash.
notes.xinzhao-skill-w: W has a slash and a thrust; the thrust deals most of its damage. Aim W when the enemy has trouble changing direction. Champions and large monsters hit by W's thrust are revealed. Use W's thrust to find enemies who flee into brush.
